1. Each player starts with 5 cards of a single color, each displaying a number (Ace = 10) on all four sides.
2. The system randomly determines who goes first.
3. Players take turns placing their cards on the 3x3 grid game board.
4. When two cards are adjacent, the number on the adjacent side of the newly placed card is compared to the existing card:
      If the new card's number is higher, the existing card changes color.
      If it's lower or equal, nothing changes.
5. If a card changes color, the neighboring cards' numbers are re-evaluated using the same rule.
6. Once all 9 squares are filled, scores are tallied based on the colors of the cards on the board.
7. After the match, players keep their remaining hand cards as they are.
8. No rewards are given for draws or losses, and no Willpower is consumed.

<size=42><color=#575757>How to Purchase Bunny Marshmallows</color></size>

<size=42><color=#575757>How to Sell Bunny Marshmallows</color></size>

<size=42><color=#575757>About Leader Impeachment</color></size>
<size=30>1. If the Clan Leader remains offline for 7 days, the impeachment process activates at 0:00 AM the following day.
2. Every active clan member gets one vote, and votes cannot be revoked once submitted.
   To be considered active, members must meet the following criteria: Must be in the clan for over 24 hours and not offline for more than 7 days.
   If a member offline for more than 7 days logs in and votes, the active member count increases by 1.
   New members can vote after 24 hours, adding 1 to the active member count.
3. Criteria for Impeachment Approval: More than half of the active members must vote in favor of impeachment to pass.
4. Once impeachment passes, a new Leader is automatically chosen, with priority given to the Vice Leader. If the Vice Leader is offline for more than 7 days, the most active and contributing member is selected. After a new Leader is chosen, the previous Leader's role changes to a regular clan member.

I. Gameplay
1. Critical Fracture features two event phases each week: Mon–Wed and Fri–Sun.
2. You can challenge stages unlimited times during the event. Each stage offers different rewards and enemy difficulties, but shares the same core mechanics.
3. Starting a challenge doesn't consume items or Pathos.
4. You can deploy 1 team with up to 4 Combatants.
II. Rewards
1. After a challenge ends, you can manually claim the reward based on the total damage you dealt. Reward tiers don't stack—if you meet multiple thresholds, you can only claim one tier. Each event phase allows only one reward claim, which resets automatically with the next event phase.
2. If you don't claim your reward before the event ends, the system will automatically issue the reward for your highest damage tier via in‑game mail. Reward mail is valid for 30 days; once expired, it will be automatically reclaimed by the system.
3. Players with no record or zero damage receive no rewards.
4. When your claim count reaches 0, you can't start new challenges.

Protected by special policies, Catto City maintains its status independent from the major nations surrounding it; and as a result, it has developed into a uniquely open and inclusive, prosperous metropolis. The city maintains pathways and activity zones dedicated for the use of local cats, which contribute positively to the mental health and well-being of its 600,000 residents.\n\nCatto City does not have a particularly long history. Focused on the exploration of the coexistence between humans and Felinians, the city's prosperity stems from the discovery of Pathite, a new energy source developed jointly by both races.

The brightest gem in the dazzling treasure chest that is Catto City is undeniably the Quince District. Here, business, entertainment, technology, and all the latest trends are integrated into the largest commercial area in all of Catto City. Top designers and trendy beverage stops surround the most popular large-scale amusement park and world-famous science museum, in addition to a vibrant College Town and a Gamer City that outshines all others in Catto City...\n\nIn addition to these undeniable draws, Quince District also hosts the once-famous, trendy food destination, Baker Street. With the emergence of Baker's Cafe, the area, which had been in decline due to frequent Anomaly incidents, has begun to revitalize. Can it re-attain its past glory? That all depends on the Cafe.

Once renowned for advanced manufacturing equipment and intelligent engineering, the Southport attracted businesses and investors from all over, providing an vital injection of energy and funds that helped to build growing momentum for the development of Catto City.\n\nWith the recent scarcity of core industrial technology and a stagnant structure for production, however, as well as other factors such as funding and policy restrictions and challenges, Southport has found itself in trouble. This stagnation in development has given rise to a number of problems, not the least of which are the frequent Anomaly incidents which continue to further erode security in the area.

With the land plagued by Anomalies, Yaozhou sent volunteers, traveling great distances to Catto City, in order to bring some relief to that area. Not only did these volunteers proffer assistance, but they also brought their own cultural heritage and shared it freely with the local residents.

Yaozhou boasts a distinctive cuisine, marked by tantalizing and delectable dishes that can make one's tastebuds all but dance. World-renowned auction houses that draw collectors from across the land mingle with unique buildings, whose charming, pitched eaves align in architectural harmony. With streets and lanes adorned with colorful decorations, Yaozhou always has a festive atmosphere...

Walking through the district, one can find unique and ingenious artifacts displayed amidst the scent of fragrant tea, with the lingering notes of a Guqin floating on the air. Here, you can truly find Yaozhou's unique cultural charm.

Once the royal city of Leidsdam Kingdom, Oldtown was settled in a realm rich with history, advanced technology, and a civilization that stood out as a leader in the world. However, the entire land succumbed to contamination by Pathos Particles, when that kingdom fell to Affliction. This place became the last refuge for the people of Leids, but no efforts could reverse the kingdom's inevitable downfall once it had begun.

Once Catto City had been established, the area where the royal city once stood was protected, designated a reserved area for the ruins of Leidsdam, and renamed "Oldtown." As time passed, the conspiracies held by separatists opened a growing divide between Catto City as a whole and Oldtown. This led to the establishment of the Light Curtain, to separate and sever communication between the two sides.

Today, the people of Oldtown continue to resist the development and use of Pathos Technology, preferring to preserve the ancient structures of Leidsdam's royal city. Under the thumb of the Holy Order, the residents remain steadfast in their nostalgic devotion to past glory, finding it difficult to move forward with the rest of the world. Only a few are willing to face reality and actively engage with the outside world, striving to open a new horizon for their district.

The beating heart of Catto City, the Central District houses essential departments and services, including City Hall, the Emotion Remedy Center, and the StormEye Bureau of Investigation, or SEBI. These agencies are responsible for overseeing and maintaining the overall smooth operation of the city.

The most pivotal institution in the Central District, however, is the Ivorus Institute. This research facility has achieved stunning results in the field of Pathos Technology, and it is due primarily to its existence that Catto City stands in a position of leadership, above the world.

With the Tower Institute renamed the Ivorus Institute, it shifted focus to civilian Pathos Technology. In just a few short years, civilian applications developed there brought about a veritable transformation in the citizens and municipality of Catto City.

It should be noted that, for the safety of the public, Central District has certain streets with restricted access. Those wishing to venture to those areas must obtain special permissions, or face consequences.

Located on at the northernmost tip of the city, adjacent to snow-capped mountains, lies the Boreala. Here, vast, frozen marshlands boast the lowest temperatures in all of Catto City, while the contrast of abundant forests in the area create picturesque natural landscapes. 

With pride of place in the district stands the Chausie Stadium - the largest stadium in Catto City. Weekends are filled with a variety of thrilling sporting events that bring droves of spectators to the stadium to watch.

Aside from the beautiful landscapes and exciting sports events, Boreala also serves as both the military and legal hub of Catto City. In conjunction with the courts, prosecutors, prisons, and SEBI in the Central District, this district forms a formidable barrier, safeguarding the peace and security of the people of Catto City.

Political Power in Catto City is shared by a Supreme House and a House of Representatives within the Catto Opinion Bureau. Legislators, members of the House of Representatives, vary in number. Influential groups, as well as the various regions nominate candidates, who are then elected democratically by the citizens. \nIn contrast, the Supreme house comprises only twelve seats - each is held by the founding Lebardmann and Carlson families, as well as the military, the Ivorus, StormEye, and the Catto Electric Power company. The remaining six seats are allocated through elections held among influential organizations and leaders within the city. The Speaker of the Supreme House is then elected by its members. \nThe Catto City Council was initially established to collaborate with the E-System to manage the day-to-day affairs of the municipality. However, over the past decade, the Council has been gradually taking on more authority and autonomy.

An essential organization in which specialized agencies, educational institutions, and research facilities work together to ensure urban safety and security within the city, and to maintain law and order. Within this organization is the Operational Department, whose primary role is to eliminate the various manifestations of Affliction in Catto City, investigate related events, and maintain the emotional safety of Catto City residents.

The Emotional Remedy Center, or ERC, is a comprehensive medical institution responsible for handling Pathos incidents and patients. The ERC receives Pathosis patients, devises treatments plans, and provides Pathos intervention therapy for relatively mild cases of Pathosis. Moreover, the ERC does accept Pathosis patients identified by the StormEye Special Operations Squad as well as certain Anomalies. Researchers also come to the ERC for theoretical and practical scenarios and clinical data.

Once known as the Tower Research Institute, the Ivorus originates from the Leidsdam era and the kingdom's Royal Academy of Sciences. After the infamous Tower incident and subsequent reconstruction, it became the Ivorus. \nAs the official research institution of Catto City, the Ivorus has abandoned biological experimentation and shifted focus to the research and application of civilian Pathos technology, in addition to its existing research duties. This has brought about significant changes within the city.

Jointly founded by the Maine and Golden families, Spangler Inc. was one of the major organizations involved in the construction of Catto City. Over the years, it has expanded its scope to encompass international trade, real estate and Pathos Technology research and development, thus affecting many aspects of citizens' daily lives.\nA decade ago, Spangler Inc. faced a decline through poor management surrounding the Tower Incident. Idego Russell, representing the Maine Family, joined forces with Dahlia Hannover of the Golden Family to drive for bold reforms. Their success pulled the business out of decline and led Spangler to its present prosperity. Under their leadership, it is believed that Spangler Inc. will continue to rise, reaching new heights of development in the industry.

The newly established Fluvia idol agency has soared under the leadership of its founder, Anja Noreen, with Erina Hannover rising to become the most influential idol in Catto City. \nThe agency's management philosophy is famously one of simplicity and elegance. Remaining intentionally small-scale, it has garnered remarkable influence in the entertainment industry through adept public relations and strong connections within the city. These have positioned the Fluvia Agency as a legend within Catto City.

The Furrmeow Detectives, headquartered on Garden Street in the Southport, is headed by the President, Linn, and Vice President, Echo. Other well-known members include Cody and Senshinn. The agency itself grew out of a campus club of curious-minded Felinian students who sought to investigate urban legends. \nAfter encountering and solving various strange and mysterious incidents, the Furrmeow detectives began to gain widespread internet attention. With that fame came more and more requests to open investigations. Guided by interest rather than funds, this non-profit agency only takes on the most challenging and bizarre of cases. \nThrough their investigations of urban legends, the Furrmeow Detective agency has used the truths they uncover to play a positive role within Catto City, avoiding public panic and maintaining social stability.

An offshore data center located on an artificial island in Catto City, the SimuBattle Center is an advanced simulation training center established by SEBI and the Ivorus lab. \nThe central computer cluster is surrounded by several large, seawater-circulating cooling systems, which provide the stable, low-temperature environment required for it to operate. This allows the center's massive computing power to output an incredibly realistic and multisensory, immersive training space.

One of the functional departments within StormEye, the Science Research Division has responsibility for crime scenes, systematically identifying and gathering evidence and neutralizing pathos particles from chaotic scenes. The SRD has its own research institute and independent offices, though it maintains close ties with the ERC and Ivorus Institute, frequently collaborating in the handling of special Pathos events. The SRD's scope of work includes:
1. Clean and maintain Affliction scenes to ensure environmental safety and P-values.
2. Perform on-site evidence collection, recycling, testing, and subsequent restoration and preservation work, with the necessary destruction of hazardous materials when required.
3. Statistically analyze various aspects of physical evidence, including but not limited to appearance, cause, material, structure, and the reason for Affliction, and provide written reports.
4. Maintain combat capability. Provide support in special circumstances when necessary.

At an unknown location deep within the Sea of Despair lies the Wonderland, a faction of Darkrifts, Anomalies, and other Pathos contaminants. The island, once known as Black Heaven, is concealed by the surrounding ocean and accessible only through special means.
The history of Wonderland dates back three hundred years. At the beginning, Darkrifts transformed by Anomaly incidents wreaked havoc in Leidsdam, unchecked. With the establishment of the Felinian Alliance by Naka and Carlson, and their mastery of Pathos Technology capable of effectively combating those Anomalies, the Darkrifts in Leidsdam were quickly pushed into a corner.
Some of those Darkrifts, under the guise of the Holy Order, remained hidden amongst the people of Leidsdam, while the other faction escaped the kingdom and traveled to Black Heaven. Primitive and tainted by Pathos Pollution, the island hosts various Anomalies, some of which have taken human slaves.
The Darkrifts from Leidsdam initially unified Black Heaven, leveraging their advanced technology and strategies. However, the Black King, a local leader, soon led the indigenous people to subdue the Darkrifts and incorporate them into their ranks. Having absorbed their technology and ideas into their own, the forces of the Black King sought to end the chaos of Black Heaven and establish a true paradise for Pathos contaminants. Thus, the Wonderland was formed.

The Catto military is a unique force, formed by an alliance of both human and Felinian factions. With the primary objective of maintaining peace and stability within Catto City, they report directly to the E-System while maintaining the right to autonomous action under certain, special circumstances. Headquartered in Boreala, the military has control over this region, with the Commander-in-Chief doubling as the district chief.\nThough the differing factions within the military each have their own interests, they share the common goal of protecting the city. Believing that cooperation and unity achieve great benefits, the members of the alliance stand united when facing external threats.\nBasing their strategy on defense and counter-attack, the Catto military focuses on the development and research of new technology and weapons, with a comprehensive, strategic cooperation with the Ivorus Institute. Additionally, they collaborate closely with multiple organizations and forces to collectively address threats and challenges in their jurisdiction.

With any conflict come those who wish to profit as mercenaries. The Reaver City originated in a distant, chaotic era, initially consisted of several small mercenary groups near the ruins of the abandoned city of Labus. The descendants of exiles, the population is a blend of primarily humans and Felinians, with Anomalies and Darkrifts as well. Historically, the League was synonymous with chaos and danger, gaining international infamy, shunned and not protected by international conventions.
The current commander, Mamon, unified the entire region with his cunning, exceptional military talent, and the clandestine support of a mysterious benefactor enabled him to sweep through the entire Labus region, establishing a single regime in the form of an independent city-state named the Reaver City, himself serving as the supreme leader.
The City, under Mamon's ambitious reforms, has aligned with various private military contractors (PMCs), primarily performing escort and security services to maintain peace. They provide compensated transportation, carpentry, mechanical repairs, as well as providing food and medical services during conflict for the side they deem just. For over a decade, the Reaver City has played a strong, proactive role in armed conflicts worldwide. In this way, they are fundamentally different from the conventional, pay-driven mercenary groups. Due to this reputation, their international standing has improved significantly.
The League of Outcasts is an international mercenary task platform founded within Reaver City, with branches in all major cities. Within local laws and regulations, the platform reviews employers and potential employees and evaluates task acceptances and participant reputations. With these mechanisms in place to ensure the rights and interests of all parties, the platform has become the largest employment platform in the region.

With the Soothing Power inherited from their Felinian ancestors, the Lebardmann family was originally considered a weaker branch of the Ragdolls, serving primarily as support. However, as the family explored and applied their Soothing Power as the Pathos environment deteriorated, the family gained renown and advanced within society.\nAfter the founding of Catto City by Naka Lebardmann and Corwin Carlson, the Lebardmann family seized opportunities to gain critical influence in the city, quickly establishing themselves as an influential force as the city grew.\nToday, the Lebardmann family is not only the largest and most developed branch of the Ragdolls, but also stands as a leading force in the Felinian community as a whole.

The Eressia Economic Prosperity Commission is a non-profit organization composed of business leaders, entrepreneurs, and government officials. Its primary objective is to promote economic prosperity and development within the Eressia region.\nUnlike the immediate establishment in Catto City of factions from the Yaozhou, Promisedland, and Betulah regions, those from Eressia established themselves in Catto City at different times. Because of this, they never formed a cohesive population that was able to influence the development of the city. In recent years, however, the creation of the EEPC has united the countries in the Eressia region, bringing together resources and making opportunities and benefits available to all with the region. In keeping with this change, the Commission's political influence has increased, securing fully half of the seats in the House of Representatives of the City Council.\nThe current president of the EEPC is Willy Hill, and his son, Harren Hill, also serves as a member of the Council.

Founded by a Mr. K, the Shadow is an old and powerful organization with a presence worldwide. Veiled in mystery and terror, the Shadow's influence has influenced every corner of the world, with members in every field and industry including, if the rumors are true, some of the highest levels of leadership in multiple countries. Technologically, the Shadow seems to be far ahead of its time, appearing to predict and even control future trends.\nDespite widespread acknowledgement of the Shadow's existence, most people only have a vague idea of what it is. Moreover, any member of the Shadow who is revealed as such will face an "accident" soon after their identity becomes known; allegedly to "eliminate imposters" in the ranks.

One of the three major families in the Oldtown, the Black Vulture's members are not bound by blood. Rather, they are an armed, faction-like group stemming from their precursor, the Imperial Eagle, with initial members consisting of refugees from the military of Leidsdam Kingdom. \nOriginally the most prosperous family in the Oldtown, the conservative nature and cautious exclusivity of the Black Vulture, in addition to a tense relationship with the Holy Order, has led to its current status as last among the three major families. Now, they control only marginal neighborhoods on the outskirts of the district.

The true rulers of the Oldtown, once known as Leids Town, are the Holy Order, an organization that originated in the Relief. \nDuring the Affliction in Leidsdam, the leader of the Relief, known as John, was commissioned to come to Leidsdam by Prince Aaron of Leidsdam to come in an attempt to save the crumbling Kingdom. Following his death, successive generations of the sect lost their way to a desire for power, using the trust of the people of Leidsdam as a shield. Manipulating the power of Darkrifts to sow division and a sense of alienation, they attempted to secure control of the Leidsdam region and took on a new name - the Holy Order.\nTo hide their conspiracy to grasp power, the Order took measures to isolate the Oldtown, fabricating the "Sacred Enlightenment" and other legends, disseminating false information and allowing gangs to run rampant to build chaos and fear. Frequent clashes with the city, the orchestration of malicious incidents, and the manipulation of public opinion gradually forced Catto City to establish the Curtain and fully isolate the two regions. Although Oldtown appears on the surface to have gained independence, in reality, it has become a puppet in the hands of the Holy Order. Having long lost their freedom, the people of Oldtown live in abject poverty and have been led to attribute their hardships to the rest of Catto City.

Pathos Energy is generated by intelligent beings during emotional fluctuations. Generally, Pathos Energy generation relies on Pathos Particles. Theoretically, pure, stable, and reliable Pathos Energy does not exist naturally and is only obtained for use through the corresponding purification technology.\nPathite crystals are unique crystalline structures used to store Pathos Energy and which also serve as a standard unit of measurement for it. Although Pathite does occur naturally worldwide, that Pathite contains complex energy with low utility and strong side effects. Additionally, it is rather rare, and so impractical for large-scale collection. Essentially, only those efficient crystals made using patented technology in Catto City are referred to as "Pathite."

Pathos Energy can leak and pool irregularly at specific points throughout Catto City. Such energy leaks, known as Pathos Drop Points, greatly increase the risk of the development of Anomalies in the surrounding organisms, potentially leading to the spread of Affliction.\nConsequently, once new Pathos Drop Points are detected, the Council immediately tasks StormEye to deploy special investigation squads to guard the sites. Moreover, Pathos Catering locations are then established nearby to stabilize the residents' emotions.\nThe origins of such Pathos Energy Drop Points remain a mystery to this day.
Using ingredients infused with Pathos Particles, Pathos Catering uses unique techniques to give their food the ability to help people regulate strong or chaotic emotions.

The unique Pathos Cafe in Catto City specializes in Pathos Catering. These unique cafes incorporate Pathos Particle-infused ingredients with distinctive techniques to create dishes that help regulate emotions. The entire process, from choosing ingredients to final presentation, is strictly regulated by the Council and StormEye.\n\nPathos Cafes are commonly located near known Pathos Drop Points in Catto City, and are established there by the special investigation squads. Moreover, squad members are responsible for both the normal operation of the cafe and the periodic cleansing of the area for Anomalies near the Pathos Drop Point. These ensure the maintenance of stable Pathos environments around these points.

Pathos Armament consists of those weapons created initially by Felinians using Pathos Energy. Felinians resonate with specific emotions, and so can use corresponding Pathos Energy to create personalized combat equipment. Those who resonate with the same emotion may manifest Pathos Armament with different appearances and attributes.
Originally, these armaments were used and understood by individual Felines or passed down through generations, making them harder to control. These were referred to as Primitive Armament. As such technology advanced, Catto City developed Pathos Armaments powered by Pathite, which exbibit greater stability, durability, and precision in comparison with their more primitive predecessors. Newer Armaments are also designed to limit negative side effects of the Patho Particles involved, to better avoid becoming "Darkpaw."

The use of Pathos Armament generally requires authorization by StormEye.

Pathosis can be defined, in a broad sense, as any abnormality related to or caused by emotions. According to the field definition, the normal range of emotional fluctuations in humans is below 40%, and may exceed 50% when facing significant life changes. When humans are exposed to an imbalanced Particle environment for an extended period, and emotional fluctuations persistently exceed the normal range or exceed 80% in a single instance and cannot be self-regulated for recovery, it is diagnosed as Pathosis.

Stages of Symptoms:
If Pathosis does not receive effective treatment, it tends to worsen over time.

Mild:
This is characterized by an increase in the amplitude of Pathos Particle concentration fluctuations, accompanied by symptoms such as mood swings, hair loss, dark circles, insomnia, and acne. This stage can be self-regulated through appropriate rest and leisure activities.

Moderate:
This is characterized by emission of higher concentrations of Pathos Particles, leading to more pronounced personality changes or emotional abnormalities, including but not limited to sensitivity, suspicion, pessimism, and anxiety. At this stage, it is generally recommended that the patient undergo mild emotional therapy or engage in long-term emotional convalescence. Research has shown that interacting with cats can effectively alleviate symptoms of such emotional disorders. If conditions allow, it is advisable for patients to seek timely companion therapy at reputable treatment facilities.

Severe:
Patients at this stage emit a large amount of highly concentrated Pathos Particles, exhibiting symptoms such as mania, violence, and even criminal behavior. Severe Pathosis is also recognized as a sign of emotional disturbance. Patients find it difficult to recover naturally through convalescence and require professional emotional therapy intervention. Therefore, if any of the above symptoms are observed, please immediately contact the Emotion Remedy Center.

In recent years, the development of Pathos Technology and updates in the technical understandings have led to identification of new types of Pathosis. Moreover, fields involved in the research of emotional remedies have grown and expanded.

When a patient with severe Pathosis does not receive timely and effective treatment, they enter the next stage, known as Affliction.

The term "Anomaly" refers to a life form contaminated and transformed by Pathos Particles. These are divided into biological and non-biological Anomalies. Currently, there have been four levels of Anomaly identified: Low, Medium, High, and Darkrifts. Identification of further levels is impossible at this point due to insufficient sample sizes.

For all levels, the basic template for Anomalies is human. Once a human undergoes Affliction, they become a high-level Anomaly, all of which ultimately have human form.

While an Anomaly is transformed by Pathos Particles, it is also influenced by them. Anomalies simpler than Darkrifts are largely irrational, unstable, and exhibiting highly destructive power. Their instability also affects the surrounding Pathos Particle environment, leading to further spread of the Anomaly phenomenon.

Each level of Anomaly can contain only a certain amount of Pathos Particles. As those Particles increase and reach their limit, Anomalies will attempt to evolve in response. If they fail, they will disintegrate naturally. This disintegration in high-level Anomalies and Darkrifts results in a unique phenomenon called the "Pathanthos."

Once Anomaly transformation begins, it cannot usually be reversed. However, new research indicates that this may not strictly be the case in the future.

Currently, the Darkrift is the highest level of Anomaly identified.

Darkrifts have significant control over their own Pathos Particles, which allows them to remain rational and hide within society. However, with the unpredictable nature of life and circumstances, they maintain a risk of losing control when those particles reach a certain threshold.

Darkrifts, while advanced, still fit the common definition of Anomaly organisms. Their bodies, reshaped by Pathos Particles, are essentially aggregates of those particles. 

The lifespan of a Darkrift would reach near-immortality; however, the longer they live, the more Pathos Particles they must consume to maintain emotional stability and consciousness. Ultimately, it is nearly impossible to avoid fate and not become a true monster.

Some scholars hold that Darkrifts can and do evolve further, become those "deities" and "holy beasts" recorded by various civilizations throughout history.

When an Anomaly dies, the large volume of Pathos Particles within them disintegrate at once, and memory fragments carried by those particles will also separate. When there are enough particles released this way, they condense into a tangible form, blooming into splendid flowers that quickly dissipate.

The form of Pathanthos is unique to each individual, and varies for each Anomaly. Moreover, the number of flowers is proportional to the degree of Affliction; a high-level Anomaly generally condenses one Pathanthos upon it's demise.

When a large number of Pathanthos accumulates in a short space of time in one area, it can lead to unexpected consequences.

Catto City, a uniquely open and prosperous, high-tech metropolis, maintains independence from the other major nations due to its historical origins, overwhelming power, and global status.

In the distant past, the kingdom of Leidsdam fell to Affliction, and the entire region became contaminated. Visionaries such as the human scientist Carlson and the Felinian leader Naka recognized the dangers posed by Pathos Particles as well as the importance of strong relationships between humans and Felinians. Joining forces, they launched a collaborative research effort at the ruins of Leidsdam, to purify Anomaly contamination, focusing on Pathos Particles. Rapidly, a city of hope rose around them, created jointly by humans and Felinians on this land tainted by Anomalies.

The foundation for the prosperity and development of Catto City lies in Pathos Energy, a new energy source jointly discovered by humans and Felinians. Using Pathos Particles as a raw material, Pathos Energy is highly controllable and can be stored safely in Pathite.

The cornerstone of Catto City's growth, on the other hand, is the mass production of Pathite, catapulting the world into an era of Pathos technology and spurring on a technological and productivity revolution. From that point, Pathite and its production techniques have become the focal point of international competition, with Catto City firmly in the lead.

The subsequent rapid development of Pathos Technology, based on Pathos Energy, the use of Pathos Particles has increased across the globe.

The Emotion-System, or E-System, is an absolutely neutral city logistics artificial intelligence that serves as the core of Catto City, maintaining the ecological balance of the entire city. Particle Detectors set up throughout the city collect Pathos data in real-time, which is then processed by the Emotion Management Center (EMC) and ultimately submitted to the E-System. The E-System then analyzes the data to make decisions and draft actionable solutions that can be implemented by the various city departments. This helps eliminate potential risks in the city.\n\nInitially developed by Carlson and Naka, the E-System serves as a way to minimize human error and prevent core technologies, such as Pathite production processes, from being leaked.

Felinians are an intelligent species that predates modern humans. They possess physical capabilities superior to humans, including having both human and feline forms. While lifespans typically range from two to three hundred years, certain groups can live for over five hundred years, and their physical appearance remains fixed during their physical prime.

To maintain their forms and abilities, Felinians require a substantial intake of Pathos Particles; prolonged deprivation can lead to weakness and degenerations. Felinians also have the ability to condense Pathos Particles into weaponry.

While early beliefs held that Felinians did not produce Pathos Particles, recent studies suggest that they do, albeit in considerably smaller quantities than they consume them, so it is difficult to detect. Felinians have a high tolerance for Pathos Particles, yet there is still a possibility of Afflictions. Those who have become contaminated are referred to as "Darkpaws."

Felinians exposed to prolonged Pathos Particle contamination can and do transform into what are known as Darkpaws. Compared to Anomalies, they are more covert, with highly volatile personalities and heightened aggression. Using Pathos Armament, they can unleash amazing combat abilities.\n\nUnassuming outward appearances can make distinguishing Darkpaws from other powerful Felinians difficult.

Utilizing the abilities of the Lightveil, Naka has been able to construct a unique space, capable of integrating gathered Pathos Particles. Within the space, Naka is able to decrypt information embedded in them, forming memories from fragments and releasing them in the form of dreams. As such memory fragments scatter randomly across the dream space, sorting out the valuable information requires active exploration and puzzle-solving.

In the early hours of January 2, 2207, a major incident occurred at the Tower Research Institute, the precursor to the Ivorus Institute. Public information states that a series of explosions damaged the main structure of the Tower, causing a massive leak of high P-values from the lab.

In the aftermath, the StormEye responders were able to swiftly contain the scene and prevent further escalation. The severe destruction on the site, in addition to ambiguous evidence of the incident's origin, led the special investigation squad to strongly suspect that it resulted from a research error. There are, however, rumors that the incident was actually a conspiracy orchestrated by Darkrifts.

Since the accident occurred outside of normal work hours, most researchers were offsite and remained unaffected. Unfortunately, all 219 volunteers for classified projects residing on-site were killed. Both the Institute and the City Council, which initiated the project, incurred substantial financial damage as well.

Since the Tower had always been a landmark building in Catto City, the destruction had profoundly negative consequences for the city. Through collective efforts, a new white tower was constructed in just six months, on the same site and renamed the Ivorus Institute, becoming a new landmark for residents.

After the Tower Incident, all projects related to the event were halted, and the relevant records sealed, requiring the highest level of authorization from the E-System for access.

Catos were invented by the former Tower researcher and Babel Tower Award winner Eleanor. A Cato is defined as any cat-shaped digital life form that can carry Pathos Particles. Catos can store a significant amount of Pathos Particles, absorbing negative particles from their environment and releasing neutralizing particles to purify their surroundings and regulate emotions. A built-in processor gradually breaks down Pathos Particles and converts them into Pathos Energy, which it uses to sustain itself in a sort of near-equilibrium. There is, however, a limit to the Particles each Cato can store. To avoid damage and potential Pathos leaks, when that limit is reached, the Cato automatically ceases intake until the purification process is complete.

Due to this limitation, Catos have corresponding limitations in cases of severe emotional disorders or Affliction. In cases of significant emotional trauma or prolonged deterioration, users are still advised to seek immediate medical attention.

Available in civilian and specialized models, the Cato is one of the few research projects unaffected by the Tower Incident. Together with the City Council, the new Institute optimized the civilian version to include various amenities such as material enhancements, greater production, online courses, offline stores, and a Cato community, among others. Catto City also has an adoption promotion plan that offers free Catos to eligible citizens. These programs have made significant contributions towards stabilizing the local Pathos environment.

Specialized versions of the Cato focus on developing special effects for combat purposes and are exclusively available to the military and StormEye.

In their cat form, Felinians exhibit distinct traits, strongly influenced by genetic factors. These traits are commonly known as "breed."

It's important to note that Felinian breeds are not synonymous with domestic cat breeds belonging to the order Carnivora and the family Felidae. Pure Felinian breed is limited to those recorded in Felinian Chronicles: Whispers of Ten Thousand Secrets. Many terms used, such as Chinese Pastoral Cat, Norwegian Forest Cat, and Siamese Cat, are of uncertain origin. Most Felinian historians believe that these terms once represented geographical origins, but existing historical records contain no clues. As a result, Felinian origins are shrouded in mystery.

With the global popularity and growing influence of Felinians, humans started to use the names of Felinian breeds to refer to domestic cats with similar characteristics. For example, the Abundant Sea Cat found in the Steam Islands, due to its characteristics matching those documented in Felinian Chronicles: Whispers of Ten Thousand Secrets, is widely referred to as the British Shorthair Cat. However, this naming convention has not been officially recognized by Felinians.

The Soothing Power is an ability unique to the Lebardmann family; it is capable of rapidly ameliorating any negative effects of Pathos Particles. This power allows its wielder to not only soothe emotions and purify the Pathos environment, but also to heal Pathosis. This is one of the more potent hereditary powers passed down in a Felinian family. In its strongest state, it can purify the Pathos environment over an area of nearly ten thousand square kilometers, healing Pathosis affecting entire cities or even small countries. However, the passage of time has diluted such hereditary powers in Felinians, and there are awakenings only every few generations, with each successive generation weaker than the last. Meanwhile, the cost of using such powers has risen, and those who awaken often live a shorter life than a typical Felinian.\n\nNaka Lebardmann stands as the last member of the family to awaken this power, nearly three hundred years ago, along with the Founding of Catto City and the ascent of the Lebardmann family to prominence. Since that time, the family has fallen into a decline, though there are high expectations that Triss, who has awakened her hereditary power, will lead the family to glory again.

The Lightveil is a conceptually idea human as devised by Pathos scientists - emotionally balanced, able to utilize Pathos Energy as effectively as Felinians and Anomalies, and at the same time, not dependent on Pathos Energy or negatively affected by Pathos Particles. Thus the Lightveil would be immune from Affliction.

From the Particle Reflection Experiment, it is known that a Darkrift who fits the experimental conditions will devour and absorb all Pathos Particles in the environment, thus earning its name. The Lightveil, on the other hand, would be capable of reflecting all Pathos Particles, hence the name. It's important not to confuse these names with simple color theory, as both the Darkrift and Lightveil can emit Pathos Particles of a variety of color values.

The concept of the Lightveil was first proposed by historian Loran Von, and since then researchers have generally believed that Lightveils would be able to utilize Pathos Particles in inconceivable ways, representing hope for all in the fight against Pathos Particles. There have been only two publicized experiments with Lightveils in history, both of which failed.

The Twelve Aspects of the Black King are twelve powerful figures in Wonderland that each correspond to one distinct emotion mask with a formidable power behind it. They serve as both disciples of the Black King and tools with which he rules all of Wonderland. 

The earliest legends involving the Twelve Aspects can be traced back before the establishment of Wonderland itself. During the Primeval Era, the god Krishna fell from the heavens into the world. His body transformed into the myriad forms of earth, his thoughts became sentient beings, and his emotions manifested twelve masks. These were bestowed upon the twelve disciples, allowing them to establish kingdoms and wield divine powers. The Black King is a descendent of the god who fell, and is the sole master of this realm, holding ultimate authority over all, including the Twelve Aspects.

There are always and only twelve Aspects; to become a new member, one must devour an existing mask to create a new one. The title of each mask is defined by its owner, and each it must align with the type of emotion it dominates and is reflective of the owner's personality and beliefs.

Notably, the masks can significantly enhance their owners' control over the corresponding emotion, though those emotions are not forever fixed. Masks can consume each other, which leads to ongoing power struggles amongst the Twelve Aspects. Each successive Black King has encouraged this competition as a way to ensure none gains too much power.

A Pathos Container is an entity capable of storing a large quantity of Pathos Particles without being Afflicted. Pathos Containers are not offensive tools, but rather they are used for the absorption and release of Pathos Particles. The basic Pathos Container comprises a shell that prevents the overflow of Pathos Particles surrounding an internal crystalline structure to absorb and store Pathos Energy. This basic type is not autonomous, and may rupture and release its energy in a burst after reaching its storage limit. In some cases, this can cause Pathos Energy explosions that raise the risk of Anomalies in the area. Advanced versions can be upgraded to increase capacity, add control, analysis, and display modules and limiters, to improve safety and enable precise control of the Pathos Energy inside. All containers can be crafted in various forms and styles.

Broadly speaking, Sacred Relics, Artifacts, Catos, and even Pathite and Pathos Antiques are all technically Pathos Containers.

More narrowly, the technical term "Pathos Container" specifically refers to an invention by the former Tower researcher, Kurokawa Ushio. This invention was nominated for the highest accolade in the scientific community, the Babel Tower Award, but missed out on the grand prize due to its limited range of application.

Ancient legends speak of a sacred item known as the Gift of the Gods, capable of purifying emotional environments and healing Pathosis. Before Pathos Technology was widely adopted, such Artifacts were a crucial method for humanity to combat Pathos Particles, one of the few available means of coping.

Technically speaking, these Artifacts are identified as potent Pathos Containers - special substances capable of containing and releasing Pathos Particles without being Afflicted. Only those capable of influencing an entire civilization are classified as "Artifacts." Names for such items vary, such as Sacred or Divine Relics, or Spiritual Vessels. 

These Artifacts can harbor immense Pathos Energy, able to bring both vitality and destruction. Historical events have demonstrated that the release of such energy by even a single Artifact is sufficient to annihilate an entire nation. The fall of Leidsdam serves as a poignant example.

Artifacts are categorized as natural or artificial based on their origins. Natural Artifacts are unique substances formed naturally, then discovered and utilized by humans throughout time. Each surviving civilization utilizes their own natural Artifacts. With their scarcity, unique composition, and inability to be synthesized, such natural Artifacts hold extremely high inherent value and as such, are regarded as symbols of prosperity and strength.

Crafted by King Igor the First of Leidsdam, the artifact known as the Ring Of Glory uses a natural relic as its main stone. Individuals who resonate with and are recognized by the ring are able to harness its power. Therefore, the ring has been used as one criterion to test potential rulers, passed down through the hands of each monarch of Leidsdam since the first. It symbolizes the king's legitimacy and represents the glory of the entire Kingdom.\n\nAfter the Kingdom fell, the Ring of Glory was lost for a time. The Holy Order, upon taking control of Oldtown, claimed to possess the ring and actively sought individuals capable of resonating with it, aiming to restore the glory of Leidsdom.

The Sensory Space phenomenon circulates amongst the public in the form of an urban legend.

Several witnesses have made claims that, while walking in the city, they found themselves in a peculiar urban space, isolated from their senses of smell, touch, sight, and taste, with only their hearing intact. Meanwhile, the witnesses would hear an unusual song, an indistinct but captivating melody that entranced the hearers. They stated that their sensory deprivation persisted throughout the song, then gradually faded as it concluded, leaving them back in reality, out of the strange space. 

As none of the individuals who claimed to experience this phenomenon reported any adverse reactions and it typically occurred out-of-doors, the StormEye inspectors initially in charge suggested that it must be unrelated to Pathos Drop Points, and has not led to any Anomalies. However, some inspectors speculate that there might be some unforeseen force acting upon these people and resulting in this Sensory Space. While apparently innocuous, the true nature of the phenomenon remains unknown, and that harmlessness may turn out to be deceptive.

Before dawn, Eleanor called again.
"The situation's as I said. With Affliction involved, the Military Defense Alliance needs an exceptional Felinian operative. I recommended you."

Recently, several crew members in the Second Fleet of Catto City have developed Pathosis, which is suspected to be linked to the offshore Pathos Drop Points. I'm getting ready to look into it...
But I could not reveal my intentions to my teacher. Silence was the wiser strategy—for now.

Eleanor, ever prepared, continued smoothly.
"This falls outside the Council's and StormEye's jurisdiction. That's why you're perfect—but expect resistance from within."

Her expression balanced resignation and resolve, her smile carefully controlled.
"In return, the Alliance will grant you the rank of Navy Commander and appoint you Fleet Inspector. During emergencies, you'll have full authority to assume fleet command."
"It's also your chance to expand your influence. My ambitions for you go beyond StormEye."
"..."

The silence stretched between us. On the comm screen, Eleanor maintained that gentle, unassuming expression, patiently awaiting my decision.

I needed support—prestige for the final confrontation.
But I hadn't expected Eleanor to offer it now...
Part of me burned to ask why she still pretended.
To challenge whether this was simply her newest deception.
Yet what would be the point? The truth wasn't something she'd ever freely give.

"What do you want?"
First time speaking without deference, I met her gaze through the screen, searching for cracks in the digital facade.
If I could provoke even a slip in her composure, it might reveal something.
But I was facing the woman who had trained me—who knew me too well.

"I only want to see you reach your full potential."
"I won't interfere. This is merely an opportunity."
"I've always believed in you, Asura. Don't disappoint me."

"Understood."
Whatever your game, Teacher... I'll uncover the truth myself.

The silhouette of Catto City melted into the horizon as the emerald waters darkened—a deep, foreboding blue.

As the surprise Fleet Inspector who just dropped in, I'm under no illusions about my popularity here.
Once, such coldness might have shaken me. Not anymore.

Doubt, wariness, even jealousy—they could be the first steps toward trust. Toward loyalty.
I stood alone at the stern's flight deck, waiting.

"Inspector, what do you require of me?"
Lieutenant Matthew approached—The Innovator's physician, the first to sound the alarm.

"I'd like to speak with you."
His smile was tight, his eyes wary.
"Shouldn't you be interrogating more suspicious personnel? I'm hardly worth your time."

"Relax. I just need your help, Mr. 'Canary.'"
"Me?"
"I'd think you'd be the first to help solve this. But if you'd rather I take this as paid leave... well, you should probably update your resume."
"No—I didn't mean to seem uncooperative. I just... don't follow your logic. What would you have me do? Those men are stubborn. They'd endure punishment before talking. I can't promise they'll tell the truth."

"No need for that."
I handed him the survey.
"Just return this by tomorrow evening."
"What is this?"

It had everything: patient IDs, personal ties, travel logs before and after infection, behavioral shifts—even P-values.
"Why do you need all this?"
"Because numbers don't lie."

As the map lay open, I focused on a small, forgotten mark—Fisher's Flame.
It was a desolate island, too remote to matter, too worthless to govern.

Their existence was a cycle of digging up tubers, hauling nets, and scavenging shellfish from the rocks.
Without proper tools or boats, they were trapped. No newcomers arrived, food ran thin, and for a time, extinction seemed inevitable.

Then came the Catto City's Fleet, their routes stretching farther—and Fisher's Flame, by sheer luck of geography, became a waypoint.
Freshwater, vegetables, fish, and handmade pearl crafts were exchanged for grain and tools, reviving the community and pulling it back from the brink of oblivion.
Yet the island offered little to keep people. The population never climbed past two hundred.

With Echo's help cracking the black box records and the local gossip I'd collected, the pieces finally fell into place.
Every Pathosis outbreak followed The Innovator's stops at Fisher's Flame.
It started with the supply officer who dealt with the islanders, then spread to anyone who'd gone ashore.

The island held the key—I was certain of it.
The timing couldn't be better—a standard supply run would let me search unnoticed.

But first, there was one... complication to handle.

Matthew waited expectantly beside me. My face betrayed nothing as I spoke.
"The records are incomplete. I can't find anything suspicious—"
"I told you they weren't cooperating!"

Watching Matthew's theatrics, I almost felt sorry for him. The poor fool still didn't realize I'd seen through his act.

Every member's dossier, every question on that form—I knew them all by heart.
For someone of his medical expertise and reputation, maintaining complete patient files should have been second nature.
The documents in my hands told a different story: pages out of order, critical records vanished.

"Forgive me."
The sedative needle found its mark in Matthew's unprotected neck. His features twisted grotesquely before going slack.
"Sleep tight."

The equation was simple: remove the obstacles, or become the one removed.

As The Innovator anchored in the island's hidden harbor, it became enveloped in a peculiar fog thick with Pathos Particles, slowly creeping over the shore.
At the port, a group of islanders gathered, their frantic gestures appearing almost welcoming—seemingly untroubled as the fog coiled into their airways and seeped into their skin.
Their skin had taken on a corpse-like pallor, every face locked in the same vacant smile.

And somehow—I was the only one who saw the horror.

"Critical alert. All hands, hold positions. No disembarkation. Islanders will deliver supplies. Execute. Now."

"Bang!"
A squeeze of the trigger, and the shot rang out, severing the boarding bridge in an instant.

"Have you lost your mind?!"

"Bang!"
My next bullet carried a Pathos charge, exploding in a burst that shattered the Pathos Particles' deceptive haze.
The crew had been trained to see what others couldn't. As the Pathos Particle mist thinned, the islanders' Affliction was laid bare—unnatural, unmistakable.

"She's right! Look at them!"
"The physician... the captain... They're Darkrifts!"

Right on cue. Time to move.

"Attention!"
I raised the Military Defense Alliance insignia high, my voice slicing through the panic.
"Emergency protocols are now in effect!"
"She's gone rogue! Don't listen to—"

"Anti-Affliction protocols—activate immediately!"
"I'm your captain! Stand down! Abort all protocols!"

"Remember Lieutenant Matthew. Trust me. Activate NOW!"
"Yes, Commander!"

"Good... Good. I would have welcomed you all... But if this is your choice? Then we burn together! Let's see your precious protocols stop this!"
"All units fall back! Snipers, covering fire! I'll take point."

With the impostor captain defeated, the crisis aboard The Innovator came to an end.
Freed from obstacles, the investigation at Fisher's Flame moved forward rapidly.
Asura uncovered over a hundred and twenty survivors—among them, the real captain and Lieutenant Matthew—hidden deep within a cave.
Had the captain not rallied his people to hold their ground, the island would have fallen long ago, dooming the final battle before it began.

The survivors revealed the truth: during the initial outbreak, the real captain and the ship's physician had tried tracking the contamination's source. But the moment they stepped ashore, they were ambushed.
From then on, The Innovator had changed hands—silently, seamlessly, transformed into the enemy's weapon.
The impostor, wielding stolen identities, had systematically taken crew members for "transformation" experiments. Those who resisted had their minds hollowed out, creating the illusion of an epidemic.

"Reminds me of Wonderland's 'Shadow Jester,' but sloppy. Probably a disciple, not the real thing."
Minami shared her conjecture during the Baker's Cafe's confidential briefing.
"Disguising himself as others? Pathetic."

The revelation allowed Asura to psychologically dismantle the impostor, verifying his connection to the Shadow Jester.
Their plan to use Fisher's Flame as a staging ground for infiltrating Catto City was thwarted before it could begin.

"His acting was unbearable."
"His arrogance blinded him—believing he could impersonate us without even learning our ways. Poetic justice."
In the medical bay, Lieutenant Matthew and the captain reeled from the revelation.
The captain had barely survived, shielding his crew—three broken ribs, a shattered leg. He'd live, but his frontline days were over.
"With you as my successor... and Matthew beside you... I can rest easy."
"If only we had more like you."

After the mission, Asura exchanged brief words with Eleanor over comms.
"How'd you pull it off? Shadow Jester's disciples aren't amateurs."

"Same as always. Called key personnel to my office the night before. The fake 'Doctor Matthew' was there—but he dozed off. Missed his chance to warn his master."
"Humans notice things. The physician's odd behavior had already raised suspicions. Once they saw the truth, acceptance came easily."

"You've grown. Judgment, daring, skill. The Military Defense Alliance is impressed. As your mentor... I'm pleased."

"Gratitude. We're done here."

Asura ended the call, her face unreadable.
Eleanor's approval was never emotional—just cold calculus: results, capability, control.
Respect? Pity? Expectations? Or just another move in her game?
Asura didn't know. Didn't care.

She knew only one thing: The course was set.
And she alone would steer it.

People don vibrant attire, and walls burst with a brilliant array of colors. Welcome to Graffiti District, an area saturated with the free-spirited, individualistic, and rebellious scent of spray paint. As unlikely as it is for me to be here, I now find myself part of this vibrant scene, merely serving as a patrol soldier to prevent any unforeseen incidents.

This armor I wear feels both familiar and foreign. I catch a glimpse of my past self in the mirror, not because of the outfit, but... my demeanor, perhaps?

"Reached designated location. All clear, no signs of Anomaly."

"Wouldn't it be better to call for more patrol teams for this level of activity? Are we really needed here, meow?"

"They're bold enough to attack patrol teams, so it's better to be cautious."

The voices of Echo and Yayoi from the communicator give me a sense of ease.

"Hey! Friend. Don't look so serious, it's the rare time for Graffiti War! Here!"

A can of spray paint comes my way. My initial intent is to catch it and say "thank you". But for some reason, I tighten my grip on the baseball bat I hold, swing it with focused attention. With a swoosh, the spray paint can explodes on the wall, blending with the existing skull graffiti to create a visually striking image.

The silence that follows breaks with even more frenzied cheers.

"War! War!"

The event reaches a new climax. But this feeling, this emotion... What exactly is it?

"All the information about your parents, along with the evidence against them, is right here." A thick stack of documents lies on the table.

"Hmm..." I pick up a few pages and skim through them. They're densely filled with "evidence".

"Although it's not complete, it's hard to overturn the current evidence. And how confident are you that you can refute it?" I can find more evidence, it's just a matter of time.

"These pieces of evidence have extensive coverage and can cross-verify each other. Most lawyers would consider this as the truth."

That's where the problem lies; it's so comprehensive. It's hard for me not to doubt it. After all, it's not perfect evidence, and they have no reason, nor can they do such a thing...

"Plus, the public doesn't care about the truth. Those media and netizens..." I lift the baseball bat and press it on the stack of evidence, scaring her into silence.

"There's too much paperwork. Please send me an electronic copy."

She makes an OK gesture. I know what she's thinking: why bother with all this futile effort. But they are my parents. I know them well. If I don't believe in them, who else can help clear their names...

In my memory, the ocean and the beach are so vast. As a child, I used to often visit this boundless expanse.

In an attempt to hold onto these lingering images, I run towards them. Tiny grains of sand stick to my round toes, only to be swiftly swept away by the tides of time.

Now, I stand here again, in the place of my memories.

Even with my eyes covered, I can feel the scorching rays piercing the vessels under my skin. It's like a volcano waking at the bottom of the sea, building up to erupt—it urgently needs to be cooled down!

"You can do it, Asura!"

"Even though it's not easy to cut a watermelon blindfolded, if it's Asura, there's definitely no problem!"

Encouraged by my companions, I take a deep breath, focusing my attention and steadying the watermelon knife in my hand.

"Am I ready?" I ask myself.
 
"Of course."

I hold my breath, make my move, and slice cleanly through!

—But suddenly, the memories resurface.

"Ah! Nothing beats a chilled watermelon on a summer day, meow!" Echo, eyes fixed on the watermelon still chilling in the ice bucket, sways her tail with a craving she can hardly resist.

"Mind your digestion," I say, though I can't resist the sparkle in Echo's eyes. "...I'll cut some for you later."

"Hehe, Asura, you're the best!" Echo quickly flicks her ears, the faint breeze shaking off the sweat droplets clinging to my hair ends, splashing a tiny spray as they hit my skin. This always happens whenever she has something to say but hesitates.

"Sometimes, Asura... I feel like you're too hard on yourself." Echo begins.

"Like during the last mission—"

I stoically fish out a few chunks of ice from the bucket and suddenly stuff them down Echo's collar.

"Hey, Asura, stop messing around—Ow, it's so cold!" Echo cries out, tail fully erect.

"Asura, you big bully!!!"

"I'm sorry." We know each other so well, sometimes it breeds a certain desire for mischief.

I shake my head, but the memories stirred by Echo's words refuse to leave my mind easily.

"I... won't make mistakes again."

"Ding-a-ling..." As the sea breeze gently brushes past, a soft jingle rings out from the cat collar strapped around my wrist.

"Hm? Asura, you still keep this... Why did you add a bell?" The Inspector sitting beside me turns to me in curiosity. I involuntarily clench the red and white striped band, vaguely feeling the pulse of life.

"To remind myself." The bell jingles.

Three afternoons ago, during a sweltering afternoon, we encountered a troublesome Anomaly on our mission. After the battle, the Inspector sits beside me just like today.

"...Poor thing, its hind leg seems to be broken. Did it accidentally get involved in the battle?" Hearing the Inspector's words, I extend my index finger and gently touch the unnaturally bent hind paw of the kitten in my arms.

The paw remains motionless. Was the nerve severed? The kitten can't talk, it just looks up at me with its teary eyes, its red and white collar dirtied.

"I'm sorry..."

If I have acted faster and eliminated the enemy earlier... or if I have struck more precisely, not giving the opponent a chance to counterattack...

"Asura?" The Inspector's soft call echoes in my ear.

"I'm sorry, Inspector, I... I was lost in thought." I awkwardly lower my head, feeling a gentle touch on top of my head. 

It's the Inspector's hand.

"Asura, you always seem to be afraid of losing something, hence you're always pushing yourself to your limit."

"But you've already done your best, there's no need to blame yourself for the past."

...Oh no. Why is my vision blurring?

"Asura, why do you choose the blade as your weapon?" The Inspector once asked me this question.

Even in my most confused moments, I never forget my answer. One who wields a blade must do so with undivided attention and unwavering resolve.

A blade is powerful, yet it can also be fragile. 

A blade can only confront its enemy head-on. It's rigid and lacks the flexibility of form or the possibility of compromise. It must swing relentlessly until it shatters or nothing stands before it.

If one doesn't want to be weak, they must make themselves stronger, strong enough to overcome anything.

I want to become a blade.

"I want to protect those beside me." 

"Therefore, no matter what obstacles stand before me, I will cut them all down! Even if..."

Even if... it's just a watermelon in front of me.

"Haa!" The watermelon blade smoothly slices through the object in front of me, the sound it makes resembles the frothy rush when opening a bottle of soda.

If you ask what can alleviate the torment of the hot summer weather for my companions... it would undoubtedly be a chilled watermelon.

I remove my blindfold and let out a sigh, my mood slightly improved. "Everyone, let's have some watermelon."

This trip to Platinum Beach is a therapeutic holiday specially designed for Asura.

"Because Asura... she's too upset about the mishap during our last mission." Continuous training without rest can indeed enhance abilities rapidly, but it can also excessively drain the body. Although the intention is to help Asura relax, it seems everyone has underestimated her determination.

Under the scorching sun, on the beach, Asura has her blade locked onto the opponent in front of her. "Ha! Take this, watermelon slice!" Another precise slash, and the crimson juice of the watermelon sprays into the air.

"I-I think that's enough, Asura?" Triss cautiously speaks up.

"We already have too many watermelons, meow!!" Echo screams.

"Once she gets serious, she can't hear our voices..." Even Minami Yayoi can only laugh and shake her head.

Without a doubt, Asura would give her all, even if her opponent is a watermelon!

"But I can understand. Because Asura is such a hard-working fool." Echo looks at the Inspector, who's also looking resigned. 

"She's just trying to convey her gratitude to everyone in her own clumsy way."

Despite the frequent mishaps... it seems that this summer crisis is successfully resolved.

The cascading curtain of rain seems to mute the entire city, leaving only the rapid patter of footsteps drumming in time with my racing heartbeat.

...Not fast enough.

The site of the Anomaly outbreak is considerably far from my patrol area. Being even a second late means an increased risk. I have to move faster!

The shortest distance between two points is a straight line. As for the obstacles on that line, all I have to do is overcome them.

"Clang..." The rusty railing groans under my grip.

Using my upper body strength, I push, and the sky spins before my eyes. Then, my legs land firmly on the ground.

The scattered windows and rooftops in the distance could all be the next landing spots.
 
At this moment, I am once again thankful that I have declined Echo's suggestion of donning a skirt that would hinder my movements. As a Combatant, I have to be ready for battle at all times.
 
Sprinting, rolling, climbing.

Another roll to dissipate the force of the fall from a height. Standing atop a tall building, I finally see my comrades in battle.

I know Echo can defend herself. But seeing the Anomaly creeping up behind her still makes me nervous. The ringing of the sword in my hand echoes the battle cry in my heart, shaking me to my core.
 
"That's bold of you." Leaping from the building, the howling wind is the drum of war, my blood churning inside.

A swing, and a slash.

Light, combat-ready, and travel-friendly...

I blurt out, "Roller skates."

"Roller skates... would be perfect."

Facing Echo's skeptical gaze, I tug the corner of my mouth into a reassuring smile.

...I know what Echo is worried about.

"Asura...! You shouldn't run around the school in roller skates that haven't been checked, meow!" Understanding the concern hidden beneath Echo's clamor, I can only sigh quietly and endure her loud rant.

The black and yellow roller skates lying quietly on the table, now covered in scars from brake failures, no longer resemble their original appearance.

My chest... feels heavy, with a touch of pain.

"So, the brakes can't be fixed?"

"The brakes are worn-out. They should have been replaced long ago!"

"But you truly are one to hold onto sentiment, Asura... these skates are no longer in production, and parts are hard to find."

"None of these will stop me though! I'll ask around after school..."

"...It's okay, don't bother yourself."

"Hey! Are you looking down on me? It's nothing..."

"...The roller skates were a gift from my parents, so I don't want to replace any parts..."

Echo seems to be choked up, her momentum suddenly weakens, and she only mumbles a few words.

"...Alright, but when you decide to repair them, you must let me know."

I didn't miss Echo's concerned gaze, but I only turn my head silently to look out the window.

...I haven't owned a pair of roller skates since I officially became a Combatant. These roller skates represent an empty seat in my heart, forever reserved for their givers.

Sometimes, inexplicable obstinacy is blurred by time in our tightly clenched hands.

Echo's worries are understandable, but as for me, I haven't thought that much.

If I can save more people, why wouldn't I do so?

"How can the equipment provided by headquarters possibly compare to Echo's genius modifications!"

"So, why not leave them to me?"

Echo is doing that look again. It's hard to reject her when she's like this... Even if I refuse, she would have countless ingenious ideas to persuade me to agree.

A surprise from her... I hope it's something good.

"...Alright."

"No wonder, Asura and Echo are quite similar."

"We... are similar?"

"You both don't like to express your concern openly, yet you silently protect everyone, don't you?"

"...Protecting everyone is, after all, the duty of a StormEye combatant."

"Ta-da! Asura's exclusive battle gear, making a dazzling entrance!"

"Mwahaha... Don't be too envious of my modification talents!"

Asura seems not to hear Echo's "boisterous" self-praise, nor does she show her resigned look as usual. She gazes intently at the roller skates in Echo's hand, eyes faintly reddened. Fragmented lights are twinkling in her eyes, as if she's deep in thought, or simply lost in a daze.

"Th-these..." The seat in her heart isn't "empty", but rather filled by more and more other things.

Asura's throat feels dry, and she barely manages to squeeze out a few words.

Echo, as if receiving a signal from Asura, winks mischievously. "Go ahead and try them on, Asura the Serious Combatant!"

"...What kind of title is that?"

Echo, as if suddenly invigorated, impersonates Asura's flat tone with a straight face.

"I most definitely didn't intentionally set the default value of the thruster to the highest..."

"...ECHO!"

"That's enough training for today. It's getting late, head home and get some rest."

The boundless energy of youth can only be exhausted within the pitch. As soon as the dismissal order is heard, the worn-out players immediately spring to life.

"The weather is good today. We should head to the shop for a couple of drinks!"

"Asura, are you coming with us?"

Soon, I'm the only one left on the training field. The sun has long since set, and the distant high-rise buildings have sequentially switched on their dazzling night lights. Those meticulously designed lights flow like a twilight rain, rushing in the direction they must go.

"They'll definitely come to pick a fight when they see a newcomer."

"But don't worry, Asura! Just defeat them!"

"A wrong posture can harm your body and reduce your power."

"You can't rely on brute strength, you'll exhaust yourself quickly."

"This high-intensity sport isn't just about maintaining a steady mindset."

"I have a knack for spotting talent. You've got the physique and mental toughness."

"You're Asura, right?"

"Yes. I'm ready."

In this professional training field, I am different from the team members. This small venue fills with the purest joy of youth. The pursuit of the ultimate glory of being a champion. The exploration of the weight that the trophy cannot bear.

Such focus, such determination for a goal. Can I... also possess it?

Glasses. Gloves. Protective gear. Anti-slip powder. Quick-drying clothes. 

I carefully sort my training gear and stow it back into my backpack.

I... feel like I don't belong in this world.

"Dad, Mom—I want to eat that too!"

"It's late, snacking will make you gain weight. But... let's see, which one do you want to eat, Asura?"

I hoist my backpack back onto my shoulder. It's time to go home.

"Ladies and gentlemen! Let me hear your scream! The game is about to begin!"

"Please look forward to the wonderful performance of our players!"

If these are the only tactics they have... I've seen enough of them already.

"Don't be nervous, remember, you're the best batter!"

And now, it's time to step onto the field.

"I'll burn until the last moment." First, it's the fingertips, then the palm. Asura tightly grips the baseball bat, then, raises it high! 

"I will not, let you down!"

Top of the third inning...

First base, second base... Hit! Score!

Bottom of the eighth inning...

Home run! Score!

"This rookie...!"

"If one hates to lose, then they must fight for their pride until the last moment."

"Sniff..."

"Squawk, squawk..."

the penguins pressed against my feet, nudging me forward, as if urging me on.
