The exploration site was a haze of drifting dust, leaving every face gray with grime—
everyone except me, naturally.

As Ivorus's specially invited researcher—okay, fine, technically just tagging along with the team—I, Echo, was a solid thousand percent sure I'd uncover a new ore vein somewhere in this wasteland.

The old folks back at the lab had already confirmed it: this area sits along a fault cutting through a mineral-rich vein. Sure, years and years had buried the place beneath thick layers of loess, and the rock below was saturated with groundwater...
—which somehow made the conditions here ten times worse than anything I'd imagined.

"We really appreciate Ivorus's support. And we're very grateful to have you here helping with the survey, Researcher... Echo?"
"Trainee Research Assistant, meow!"
I cut the man off before he could finish flattering me.

Researcher. Sure, Mom and Dad are both researchers. But not me. Maybe someday I'll become one too—a researcher in equipment engineering. But right now? I'm still just a perfectly "ordinary" student. Mm-hmm! Absolutely, unquestionably, one hundred percent true!

Of course, being "just a student" comes with its fair share of trouble...
Like academic conferences. Can you believe they won't even let a genius like me attend? Talk about boring!

Same thing this time. They actually tried to keep me off the team just because I don't have qualifications in geological surveying. The nerve, meow!
So I went straight to Grandpa and asked him to let me join the expedition.
All it took was a few tears, a little sweet-talking, and a whole lot of nerve.

And then—
"Guess I'll introduce myself again, meow! I'm Echo, Trainee Research Assistant with the Ivorus Young Geologists Field Team—and the greatest genius of the century!"

Life on-site wasn't nearly the thrill I'd pictured. No daring adventures. No mysterious discoveries. Nothing like the movies—Raiders of the Lost Paw, Secrets of the Sands, or Legend of the Sea of Plenty.
Digging, grading, mapping, reading soil layers... tedious procedures and endless repetition filled one dull day after another.

"That's sandstone, meow!"
"I told you already—we don't need a sample of the schist!"
"Nice work! We'll get this batch of raw ore analyzed right away. Though if you ask me, it's still got way too many impurities!"
...

It took the old hands all of... a week? Ten days? Not long, anyway. They went from eyeing me sideways to coming over to ask my opinion all on their own. Not surprising, really. I mean, I'm a genius—I know my rocks. License or not, one tap and a good look is all I need to tell what I'm dealing with.

And so the days slipped by.
One day, two days... By the time I noticed, we'd already been surveying for a whole month.

"Echo... Trainee Research Assistant."
I turned around. It was one of the older workers—I'd seen him around a few times.
He'd spent years at the mine—long on experience, short on words.

"Mister—just call me Echo. What's up?"

"I... wanted to ask you something."
"Do you really think there's an ore vein here?" 

"Oh, that's all?"
I pursed my lips.
"From what we've seen so far, there's definitely a vein down there..." 

"But at the rate we're going, we're probably never gonna reach it, meow~" 
"We only have two months for this survey, and we've already spent a whole month going in circles near the surface... The mining conditions, the ore quality—it's all ab-so-lute-ly un-ac-cept-a-ble!"
"We might still have a shot if we pushed farther into the valley to the north. But we weren't cleared to survey that area this time."

The old worker fell silent for a long moment.
"I... I see..."
"Thank you, Echo."
He walked away with a sigh.

He was definitely hiding something from me. I could tell.
And once I've sniffed something out, how could I possibly not go poking around?

And just like that, a teeny little plan began to take shape.

Nobody can keep a secret from a genius like me.
It didn't take me long to piece the whole thing together—

Most of the crew were locals. This place had never had much going for it: transport links were poor, the land was barren, and several attempts to bring in outside investment had all fizzled out. So most people here grew up only to leave home, heading for Catto City or one of the neighboring city-states to make a living.

That old worker was one of them.
This time, they'd come home with the same little hope: maybe they really could strike a vein. They wanted to do right by their hometown—if a mine went in here, it might pull in investment, create jobs, and finally give the place a shot at turning things around.

That got me a little grumpy.
Why didn't they just tell me? If they'd said something sooner, I could've come up with a plan already...
Oh, well. Seeing how hard they worked every single day, I'll let it slide this once!

"Echo, your fieldwork's almost over. Think we'll find anything before then?"
The man who was both the "boss" and the foreman around here used to ask me that all the time.
"First of all, it's Trainee Research Assistant, meow! Second, isn't keeping track of overall progress supposed to be your job, Mister? I already sent you all the materials..."
"And anyway, if we expanded the survey area, we'd definitely find something better, meow!"
"Well... there's still plenty to consider, you know. Manpower, whether mining there would even pay off, and..."

I don't really remember the rest.

We only had one month left. At our current pace, there was no way we were going to find anything in time—that much was obvious.

But I already had an idea—the valley to the north. That area wasn't included in our survey permit, but the geology there looked a whole lot more promising.

The older workers would definitely help. No one wanted to strike a vein more than they did. I could pick a few people I trusted and sneak over there during the night shift. The supervisors never wanted to come down to the site after dark anyway, so they probably wouldn't even notice a few of us were gone. As long as we got back before sunrise and covered up the tire tracks, we could pull the whole thing off without anyone ever finding out...

"We're against it."
That was the answer I got.

I blinked at them.
"Huh? Why, meow?!"

"Echo, you're not like us—"
The old worker looked at me gently.
"We've already got one foot in the grave. But you're still just a student... You shouldn't gamble your future alongside ours."

Under that kindly gaze, all my anger just... fizzled out.

"B-but—but this is about whether your hometown ever gets the chance to thrive! That's a big deal!"

"We've lived here our whole lives. Forty years, and this place has barely changed. Who's to say that in a year, or three, we'll suddenly strike an ore vein and everything will turn around?"
"Some things are just wishful thinking. If they work out, great. But if they don't... well, we've gotten by all these years without them. Who mourns something they never had in the first place?"

Just like that, I had nothing to say.

Something about that just sounded so wrong to me.

How could anyone not wish for something just because they'd never had it? Without games, you'd be bored stiff. Without cola, summer would be unbearably hot. Without new parts, new formulas, new discoveries... The whole world would be boring beyond belief!

But they'd simply accepted it. Calmly. Like that was just how things were.

And somehow, that just made me angry all over again.

I'd always thought that once I stepped in, the problem would just solve itself. Find the ore vein. Prove it could be done. Slap the right answer down in front of everyone—and everything would wrap up nice and neatly, just like clearing a game.

So how could something this simple be so complicated to them?

"...I get it."
I lowered my head.

"But—"
"I'm not giving up, meow!"

The following Monday, the foremen found a thick stack of brand-new, fully drafted survey proposals sitting on the records-room table—

"Application for Supplemental Low-Risk Survey of the Northern Valley and Assessment of Ore Vein Potential"

And, in tiny print along the bottom:
—Compliments of Echo, the greatest genius of the century.

Then Echo herself came barreling in behind them, a dirt-caked rock hammer slung over her back.

"Your old report was dumb! I mean, only a total amateur could've written something like that! There are still tons of possibilities out there, and you went and focused on all the wrong things, meow!"

"The fault orientation, groundwater conditions, and surface deposits in the northern valley are all different from what we have here—the conditions there are practically perfect for an ore deposit to form! But if you want permission to keep surveying, you'll need a stronger case and better evidence. Something that tells those important people back in Catto City exactly why this place is worth spending more money on—and why it deserves another chance."
"Right, meow? So I wrote it up for you."

"That's..."

"Oh, and I did a quick check myself—there's sedimentary hematite up there, meow! My guess is it's an exposed deposit—the leftovers of an old basin that dried up ages ago, meow!"

"But can you be sure there's enough ore there to make mining economically viable?"
"Isn't that your job, Mister?"

In the end, the team still didn't uncover an ore vein within those two months.
After an initial assessment, Ivorus accepted Echo's report for further review. Not long afterward, a second low-cost survey of the northern valley was approved.

Whether they eventually found a deposit rich enough to build a mine around... Well, that's another story.

On the day Echo left, the older workers pressed a small pouch of raw ore samples into her hands.

They were gray and dusty—not pretty, and certainly not worth much.

"But they're my favorite pieces in my whole collection, meow!"

The newly bought maid outfit fits perfectly! Ignoring the tightness around my thighs, I fasten the garter belt firmly, taking a satisfied twirl in front of the mirror. The light, fluttering fabric moves uncontrollably with my actions, leaving a faint itch as it brushes against my smooth skin.

Humph, it's not that I've put on weight. The garter belt is fastened tight so the stockings don't fall when I move around. But at this moment, I have too much to worry about to focus on that!

I rush into the Inspector's office.

"Inspector, please, pretty please, let me help you clean the room!" I cup my hands together under my chin, batting my eyelashes in an attempt to squeeze out a pitiful tear, practically using up all my acting skills.

"We can talk about that later. But why are you dressed like this today?"

"Talk about being clueless!"

"To save the coastal cafe Triss invested in, Echo's maid marketing plan is now in action!"

With my hands on my hips, I confidently whip out two specially prepared dusters from behind.

"Inspector, enjoy Echo's first personal service!"

But... housework isn't as simple as I thought. The Inspector was already shocked out of the room by my exaggerated... ah no, by my vigorous cleaning tactics.

I collapse on the floor covered in fresh scratches, my tail twitching uneasily. Hmm, why do I feel a chill down my spine? It must be an illusion! It has to be!

"Echo, could you explain to me how these scratches in the Inspector's office came to be?"

Shiro's voice suddenly echoes behind me. Her emotionless, steady tone, like a devil's chant, sends chills down my spine. Feeling guilty, I avoid Shiro's calm gaze and shuffle my feet, trying to sneak away.

"...The cost of these damaged items will be deducted from your salary next month."

"No, no, no!"

"Inspector, join me and cast a delicious spell on this omelette rice together!☆"

As I hold up the Inspector's hands, my rounded fingertips rub from inside to outside, naturally and stubbornly stuffing the tableware into the Inspector's palm.

I bend over and lift my face, trying to influence the Inspector again with my hopeful gaze.

According to my research, most maid cafes offer such adorable services! I must be right this time, right?

However, in silence, the people around us wear expressions that are hard to describe.

"Hehe, you're so adorable, Echo."

"But no matter what spell the Inspector uses, it won't make this black paste taste good."

"Yayoi!!!"

Well, it's true. It's doesn't look that appealing, but there's no need to be so blunt about it!

"Ahem, thank you, Echo. Hmm... Is this a cat ball drawn on the omelette rice? It's very cute." Hand trembling slightly, the Inspector points at the pattern that I painstakingly outlined with ketchup for an hour.

"It's me! It's me! Inspector, can't you recognize Echo?!" I blink hard, hiding the disappointment in my eyes with a slightly accusatory look.

I failed in housekeeping and cooking... But it was my promotional idea after all, I hope I can help out...

"Hmph, you guys just can't appreciate my culinary art!"

"I'll do more research. When the seaside cafe opens, you will definitely be amazed by my skills!"

I couldn't bear to see everyone's expressions anymore, so I hurriedly retreat into the kitchen with my "failed work". Sensing the concerned gazes from behind disappear, my tense body instantly relaxes, and I take a deep breath in the dim light.

At this moment, I don't want to face either comfort or pity. Let me be a coward, just for a short while.

In the quiet kitchen, the sounds of gears grinding rise as the kitchen waste disposer hummed, grinding the food into smoke.

Should I study a cookbook, or get cooking lessons from a chef? My chin resting on my hand, the whirring and clatter of mechanical parts provide the perfect soundtrack to my contemplation.

"Echo?"

"Meow?!" 

Who... who's calling me?! 

I spin around abruptly. It's the Inspector peeking out from the kitchen door. The warm glow from the cafe outside the door casts a soft halo behind the Inspector.

"Don't be scared, it's just me."

I instinctively tighten my fist, my gaze flinching away from the Inspector's concerned look. 

"Um, I made a mess in the kitchen. It's best if you don't come in, Inspector."

"Cough, actually, I need your help with something." 

My help? The Inspector needs my help... I prick up my ears, setting down the kitchen utensils I was about to clean up. 

"This cleaning robot might need some repairs." 

I look at the seemingly damaged cleaning robot in the Inspector's hand. It appears to be pleading pitifully for help.

I look up at the Inspector again, who's looking hesitated. 

"Cough, I wanted to change its filter, but I accidentally broke it..."

"I'm not good at this, so I came look for you."

"Hmm... Shiro should have been the one to change the filter, she's better at this... everyone has their own strengths, after all."

"Why would a machine in need of Echo's repair show up at this time..." And besides, the Inspector isn't that clumsy. 

All these convoluted actions... they're all to cheer me up, aren't they? 

I blink my dry eyes. 

"You're really something, Inspector. Don't worry, leave it to me!"

The ethereal glow of inorganic light casts a subtle glimmer of sanity over the chaotic lab. I wipe the beads of sweat from my brow, feeding the final trial data into the Terminal.

As if answering the call of 0 and 1, neon lights begin to flicker on the mechanical bodies, cold and unyielding.

"Clean... Clean..."

Indeed, I find more faith in my custom-designed machines than in manual labor.

Eagerly, I send the housekeeping assistant bursting out of the cafe. Confronted with astonished gazes, I confidently demonstrate each function through the Terminal.

"Like this... and then like this... It can simultaneously clean and crush garbage, so you won't have to worry about internal trash overload during busy times."

"When it comes to housework, Echo's mechanical creations are even more adept than Echo herself."

I lift my chin triumphantly and boast with a smirk, "Well, everybody has their own field of expertise."

"But, should I consider applying a maid-themed paint job for them..."

As new inspiration descends, I plunge once more into the clatter of mechanical parts...

The Inspector picked up a menu evaded by the robot, reflecting, "We had to call in the floor-cleaning robot after all. It's a good thing you updated its obstacle avoidance system..."

"Well, we had no choice. The space here is too restricted."

Echo, with one hand behind her back, effortlessly untie the bow at her waist. The swaying hem of her skirt painted a tantalizing wave. She seems entirely drained, her petite figure sinking into the sofa, but she still manages to raise her soft arm, gesturing animatedly.

"When I activated the garbage absorption function of the housekeeping assistant, it gave the customers quite a start!"

"Their expressions were rather amusing, but for Triss's sake, I ordered them to go to the more distant beaches to clean up the trash left by tourists instead..."

The sea breeze stirs Echo's fringe, damp with sweat, her emerald eyes glimmering indistinctly.

"Do you think I went a bit too far, Inspector?"

"Too far?"

You might wonder why I care so much about this particular event. Even though it's just a charity event I did at an orphanage as a celebrity, it remains a precious memory for me.

That day, it seems like the children know I'm coming, and they arrange a stage play especially for my visit. I want to get closer to the children before the production team arrives, so I go to the orphanage early to see what the children are up to.

Despite its small size, the orphanage feels incredibly warm. The children are busy preparing for the stage play, too preoccupied to notice me sneaking in. Seeing their smiling faces, I find myself getting caught up in the lively atmosphere.

Suddenly, a soft whimpering sound comes from a corner, causing an immediate pang of concern.

"Little one, what's wrong?" I find a little girl in the corner, huddled up with her knees to her chest, clutching what looks like pages from a script.

Suddenly, she lifts her head, her face still wet with tears.

"Huh?! Are... are you Triss?" She looks quite surprised, hastily wiping away her tears.

"Hello, I'm Triss."

"May I sit here for a while?"

The little girl doesn't utter a word, simply nodding her head. Without further inquiring, I take the opportunity to sit next to her.

"It's quite lively here today..."

"Mmm, because you're here, Miss Triss. Everyone wants to prepare a surprise for you." 

"A surprise? Is it a stage play?" 

"...Yes. But now that you know, it's not really a surprise anymore..." 

"I'm surprised! I'm happy and grateful that everyone would do this for me." 

"Miss Triss..." The little girl seems to want to say something, but holds back. Her grip on the script tightens.

"Are you also part of the performance?" 

"Yes, I am..." 

"I see. What role are you playing?" 

"Little Red Riding Hood..." 

"That's impressive! Little Red Riding Hood is the lead role in this play." 

My words don't seem to comfort the girl. Tears well up in her eyes again.

"I... I'm so scared. I can't utter a single word when I think of performing in front of so many people..." 

Her voice is trembling, as if she's been holding back for a long time. 

"I'm usually fine, but the teacher said that this time it will be broadcasted on TV. That means my performance will be seen by lots of people..." 

"If I mess up my lines, or if I accidentally fall, what will happen?" 

"Will I ruin the play?" 

So, she's worried about making a mistake in front of the camera... 

Even though she's just a child, she has so many concerns. Perhaps this is part of the troubles of growing up...

"If you're that frightened, why not try to pretend that the camera isn't real?"

"I-I can't do that!"

"Heh... I know, but thank goodness that cheers you up a little."

"I... I know, I'm such a loser...but..."

"What are you talking about? It's perfectly normal to be scared when you're performing in front of so many people for the first time... I've been there too..."

"Really? Miss Triss, you were scared too?"

"Of course, and I was even several years older than you at the time."

"That was my first time singing on stage in front of tens of thousands of people..." Thinking about my past self, I can't help but laugh.

"Back then, I was just as worried as you are about not performing well and losing my place on the stage..."

Because once I lost it, I would have to go back to my family that was like a cage...

"So, how did you overcome it, Miss Triss?" The little girl grabs my hand as if she's found a lifeline.

"How do I stop being scared?"

"I have a magic spell. When you're scared, just recite it in your heart, and you'll be fine!"

"Really?"

"Yes! The spell is..."

"I got it, thank you, Miss Triss!"

Hearing the spell, the girl finally shows a smile on her face, and she runs happily towards the stage.

Although what I tell her is just a meaningless magic spell I got from a comic book, I want to give her courage. After all, what the spell is doesn't matter, what matters is the courage that comes from believing in it!

The curtains swiftly draw and the stage play begins. The girl, adorned in the costume of Little Red Riding Hood, is now a radiant star on the stage.

"She's doing great." Looking at the beaming smile on the girl's face, I let out a sigh of relief.

Just when I think all is going well, the girl suddenly freezes... Mr. Wolf, pretending to be the grandmother, lays on the bed feigning sleep. However, "Little Red Riding Hood" seems hesitant to make her next move.

It's clear; she's still too scared... I quickly make my way to the stage, pulling down the red curtain and draping it over myself.

"Little Red Riding Hood, don't be afraid..." I make my way to the girl's side.

"Tr..." I silence her with a finger to her lips before she can speak.

"Little Red Riding Hood, I am here to help you. The person in the bed isn't your grandmother, but a hungry wolf wanting to devour you..."

"Who... Who are you? How do you know all this?" Thankfully, the girl plays along with my lines.

"I... I am you from the future. I came to help. Don't worry, that hungry wolf can't see me. You just need to do as I say..."

In the end, the stage play concludes smoothly. The thunderous applause from the audience is the best reward for this performance. I stand with the young actors, taking a bow before the audience.

"Thank you, Miss Triss." 

"No worries, if not for this, I wouldn't have discovered my acting talent..."

For some reason, I don't want her to lose that magical spell called "courage". It might seem like an ordinary thing. But after hearing my story, can you comprehend this lingering feeling?

If not for this unexpected turn of events, Triss might never imagine that the story can turn out the way it did.

Her only intention was to help the child out, little does she know it will become a spectacle that everyone discusses fervently. 

"Little Red Riding Hood" is always a universally known fairy tale. Regardless of whether she ends up triumphing over the wolf alongside the hunter or tragically being devoured along with her grandmother, in the eyes of the world, she is forever an innocent, naive child, easily deceived and tricked. It is due to her innocence that her grandmother falls prey to the wolf.

But what's wrong with being naive as a child? That is the essence of that age, after all. 

With these thoughts in mind, Triss adds new characteristics to "Little Red Riding Hood". She portrays a future "Little Red Riding Hood", traveling back in time to the side of the past, innocent and cheerful "Little Red Riding Hood". This is a story she has never read before. But, perhaps it could be a good story. 

A courageous Little Red Riding Hood... sounds good, right?

One day, I received a special letter. It was from a young boy named Alex.

He wrote it on his tenth birthday, a milestone he was told he might never reach due to his terminal illness. The reason for the letter was a promise he made to himself—if he could see his tenth birthday, he would write to express his gratitude.

Alex had spent his entire childhood in the hospital. His frail body deprived him of the carefree days of playing and laughing with friends his age. Instead, his only companion was the TV in his hospital room. Through that small screen, young Alex got a glimpse of the diverse world outside, and I was fortunate enough to be a part of it. He said my singing was like a warm sunbeam piercing through the gloom in his heart, becoming his sole solace. He said that because of my voice, he managed to endure year after year of pain. Since receiving his prognosis from the "Grim Reaper," every day alive felt like a miracle, and he believed that it was I who brought that miracle to him.

By the time I finished reading his letter, my tears had already soaked the paper. It was filled with words of gratitude, yet why did it make me feel so sorrowful? Soon, an unshakable thought took hold in my mind.

Perhaps it was self-indulgent, but who wouldn't be moved by such pure emotion? I wanted to tell him that he created the miracle himself. I wanted to encourage him and do something more for him. Even if it was just to give this child one more beautiful memory before he left this world.

The agent learned about Alex's interests from his mother. She described Alex as a cheerful and sensible child. Apart from listening to music, his main interest was following motorcycle championships. Young Alex had even once said with a smile that he dreamed of becoming a motorcycle racer.

Though I couldn't make Alex's dream come true, I could at least let him witness his favorite kind of race in person. So, I shared all of this with the Inspector and the Baker Squad.

"Oh my gosh, Alex's story is just so sad…"
Eiko was deeply moved by Alex's story and couldn't snap out of it.

"Maybe instead of sad, we should say he's strong..."
The Inspector was the first to say what I was thinking.
"But, how are you planning to hold this race, Tris?"

"Since Alex can't leave the hospital, I plan to use the hospital's open space to create a small track."
"However, it's hard to book professional racers on such short notice, so…"

"You want us to substitute for those racers in the race?"
As expected, the Inspector could easily see through my thoughts.

"Yes, it's the best solution we have right now. Although it's a selfish request, I hope I can count on everyone's help."

"Of course, I'd be happy to."
"Since our esteemed leader has spoken, how could I refuse~"
"Great, as for motorcycles—I've ranked second in the history of Stormeye's practical exams!"
"If you're second, then first must be…"
Everyone's gaze quickly fell on Feitian, who had been silent, and she quietly nodded.
"Oh, that's all in the past! By the way, I can handle the maintenance for this race too!"

How fortunate I am to have such a warm and supportive group of friends.

On the day everything was ready, I went to Alex's hospital room alone. The morning sunlight was gentle, softly illuminating his young face. In the light, the boy bedridden with illness now had eyes sparkling with incomparable anticipation and passion. No words were needed; just the way his hands clutched the bed sheets showed his excitement.

"I never thought I'd get to see you in person, Miss Triss..."
A faint smile spread across his pale face, a slight blush coloring his cheeks. Maybe he was afraid of saying something wrong, or maybe he was just overwhelmed; the sensible child seemed to be trying hard to contain his emotions.

"I never thought I'd get to meet a ‘little hero' who's been bravely fighting against illness for so long."
"I'm a fan of the brave Alex!"
A look of surprise crossed his small face, then he laughed out loud, as if he'd been amused. Who would have thought that such a young, adorable child was already facing the countdown of his life?

"Did you read the letter I sent?"
"Yes, I've read it many times. But the person you should thank in that letter isn't me, it's yourself."
I didn't want to take credit for the miracle Alex saw in me; he needed to know that he was the miracle.
"You survived because you're very strong, stronger than any child I've ever met."

"If even Miss Triss says so, then I must be pretty amazing."
"Of course, I'm your fan. I've brought a belated birthday gift for our little hero."
"Thank you, but you didn't have to go to all that trouble. What you said just now was the best gift for me."

His response was expected. The sensible and strong Alex had already accepted the fact that he was going to die. His thank-you letter, in my eyes, was more like a farewell. So, it couldn't end like this.
"Alex, I want to take you somewhere."

I carefully pushed the wheelchair, guiding Alex to this place. After several discussions with the hospital staff, we managed to set aside this space and transform it into a small racing track. However, since arriving here, Alex's eyes have been glued to the starting line of the track. Four motorbikes of different colors lined up there, harmonizing with the flags and banners on either side of the track. The slanted sunlight cast a metallic sheen on the bikes.

"Triss! You're here!"
Eiko noticed us and waved energetically. Soon, others were also greeting Alex.

"Are they Triss' friends?"
"Yes, they're the ones who brought you this gift. I know you haven't had the chance to see a race in person."
"Well… I used to dream of going to a race when I recovered, but…"
"Medical technology is advancing every day. You still have a chance. Why give up when you're still here?"
"But..."
"Don't overthink it. Watch this race. Maybe you'll feel different after."
After all, the person who told me this is also here today.

"Will Miss Triss participate in this race?"
After a pause, Alex looked at me with concern.

"Though I'd love for you to see me race, unfortunately, I don't know how to ride a motorbike…"
Alex didn't seem disappointed upon hearing this; instead, he let out a sigh of relief. To think, I would be worried about by such a young child.

"But, I'll be joining this race in another way."
I bent down and spoke in the lightest tone possible.
"Alex, want to guess how?"

At the starting line, a striking white stripe clearly marked the beginning of the race. As the countdown from referee White rang out, the atmosphere on the track became tense. The racers gripped their handlebars, feet on the pedals, ready to launch.

With the sound of the starting gun, the motorcycles shot out like arrows, speeding along the track. The air was thick with the scent of rubber and motor oil, and the roar of engines reverberated, making everyone's hearts race and blood boil.

Meanwhile, outside the intense race, Tris stood on a platform in her cheerleader outfit, catching everyone's attention. Her face radiated with a bright smile, her eyes sparkling with determination, filling the entire track with enthusiasm and energy. Waving her pom-poms, Tris loudly called out the names of her teammates on the track, cheering them on.

The racers felt Tris's encouragement, their motorcycles carving graceful arcs on the track. The race was fierce, and it wasn't long before Namiya took the lead with impressive speed. Asura and Echo followed closely, with the investigator slightly trailing behind. But as the race progressed into the middle and later stages, the situation changed. The investigator, with excellent cornering skills, steadily maneuvered through the bends, overtaking one opponent after another.

No one expected the final winner to be the human investigator, whose physical abilities couldn't compare to the feline racers.

For Alex, the outcome was equally surprising. Tris remembered clearly, the boy said this at that moment:
"If I keep trying… will the result change?"

"Humans can achieve the impossible, and you've already done it once, haven't you?" Tris responded with her usual smile.
"We will keep cheering for you… always."

The afternoon sunlight poured through the floor-to-ceiling windows of the music room, casting a warm glow. I set my lyric sheets aside and gently massaged my throat.
"My lady, it's time to rest," the maid, said as she entered with a tray of afternoon tea—fragrant black tea served in delicate porcelain cups, accompanied by an assortment of fruit and vegetable pastries.

"Mary, please prepare some plain clothes for me," I said, turning toward the door.
"My lady?"
"I want to see for myself." I turned back, my eyes sparkling with newfound determination.
"I want to see that other world."

Dressed down in a basic T-shirt and denim with shades and a hat, I stepped into a side of the city I'd never seen before.
Every detail fascinated me: The walls were alive with colorful graffiti, hip-hop beats filled the air, and skaters glided effortlessly by—A world pulsing with rebellious life.
"Yo, fresh meat?" A girl with bubblegum-pink hair approached, casually chewing something.
"Hi, I'm—" The words stuck in my throat—how exactly should I present myself here?
"Call me Candy." She blew a giant pink bubble.
Pop! It burst dramatically before she flashed me a radiant grin.
"Want some gum?"
"Gum?" I accepted the candy she offered, examining its colorful, exaggerated packaging.
"Not just any gum," she said with a conspiratorial wink. "This stuff sticks to your bad moods and pops them away—leaving you light as a bubble."
Skeptical yet curious, I popped it into my mouth. A burst of icy mint flooded my senses.
"Pop!" I pursed my lips in imitation, managing only a pathetic bubble that lasted half a second. The predictable failure should've frustrated me, but instead brought an unexpected chuckle.
"Pfft—you've got a killer smile!" Candy exclaimed, jerking her thumb toward the alley behind her. "C'mon, I'll show you something cool."
She led me to an abandoned warehouse buzzing with kids. I saw graffiti artists at work, breakdancers practicing routines, and clusters of friends passing around treats.
"Welcome to Candyland!" Candy announced, arms wide. "Our hideout—where we stockpile the good stuff and protect every sugar rush in this city!"

"Protect... sweets?" I blinked in disbelief.
"You bet!" A boy in a snapback hopped off his skateboard. "Some cult has been raiding dessert shops, claiming that sugar 'rots your soul' or something ridiculous like that."
"Total nonsense!" A girl painting a donut mural scowled. "Sweets are pure joy!"
"Preach it!" Candy handed me a donut. "The bakery owner hooked us up after we chased those losers away last night."
The first bite sent fluffy bread and sugary frosting melting across my tongue—a stark contrast to the overly refined, lifeless desserts back home.
"So... sweet," I murmured, genuinely touched.
"Right?!" The crew swarmed around me, buzzing with excitement. "Chocolate bars after skating hit differently!" "Strawberry lollipops take me back to kindergarten!" "Macarons cost a fortune, but they can turn a bad day around!"
In this graffiti-covered sanctuary, I felt a surge of unfiltered passion.
While the intricacies of high-society socializing and the finesse of language might escape these young ones, their love for sweets was undeniably real.

"So... wanna join us, Triss?" Candy asked suddenly.
I froze mid-bite and lowered my sunglasses. "You knew?"
"I recognized your voice right away." She shrugged. "But who cares? Here, you're not just 'that rich girl'—you're someone who loves sugar enough to fight for it."
I glanced at the half-eaten donut in my hand, then at the circle of eager faces surrounding me. My answer came naturally.
"Absolutely. I'm in—as a Dessert Guardian."

From that moment on, I started living an extraordinary double life.
By day, I was the distinguished young lady of the Lebardmann family. By night, I traded silk for streetwear, joining my new friends in the quest to protect the city's sweetness and joy.
"Triss, you're incredible at this!" Candy panted, giving me a thumbs-up after we thwarted another late-night dessert shop vandal.
"Years of fencing training finally paid off," I replied, wiping my brow with quiet satisfaction.
We didn't just protect shops—we also handed out candy to street kids. Watching their faces light up with each sweet bite made me realize the true meaning of our mission: desserts were everyday magic that brought happiness.

"StormEye's here!" someone shouted.
I turned to see a familiar figure enter the warehouse.
"At ease—I'm not here to arrest anyone," the Inspector said with a warm smile. "Actually, I came to thank you. We've apprehended that anti-dessert group, thanks to your tips."
Cheers erupted around us. "Woohoo!" "Yes!"
The Inspector approached me and murmured, "Combatant Triss... Never thought I'd find you here."
"Please," I said with a wink, offering the Inspector some bubblegum, "call me a Dessert Guardian now. Thank you for protecting the happiness of the children... of everyone."

Moonlight illuminated the peaceful streets as Triss and her Candyland crew patrolled, dedicated to preserving the city's joy.
As their shift came to an end, Triss leaned against a graffiti-covered wall adorned with vibrant lollipops and donuts, blowing an impressively large bubble.

Who would have thought that this refined noblewoman would find her true self in such a place?
At the crossroads of her dual lives, Triss finally felt whole. Her daytime elegance and nighttime rebellious spirit blended effortlessly—like the freshness of strawberries enhancing the richness of the cake.

She remained the same kind-hearted Triss, but now she understood something deeper:
Every bakery's delightful aroma and every child's candy-induced smile served as reminders of life's small yet precious joys.
Desserts were a form of justice. Protecting that sweetness meant safeguarding all that was simple, pure, and filled with hope.

Even though I have prepared myself, stepping into this place for the first time still sends a chill down my spine.

A gloomy, cavernous room, permeated with a cold, deathly aura. Scattered haphazardly on the floor are dozens of patients dressed in hospital gowns, their faintly rising and falling chests the only sign that life has not yet deserted them. A few others, whose symptoms seem less severe, lean against the walls, sitting or lying down, but the light has already left their eyes. This room, once nothing more than an ordinary ward, had now become a refuge for those deeply afflicted with Pathosis.

"Miss Triss, please save my child!" Not long ago, a mother had found me, unveiling the haunting reality of this place. I was profoundly shaken. To think that beneath the surface of the seemingly serene and beautiful Catto City, patients of Pathosis were being sealed away, their existence concealed.

So, here I am. My mission is simple: to honor a promise to a mother, to rescue her child. All I need to do is to soothe them with my songs.

As the last note of my song faded, I notice a flicker of lucidity return to the eyes of these Pathosis patients. It seems my abilities still hold some sway. I'm tired, yes, but not a hint of regret could be found in my heart.

"What song would you like to hear next?" No matter what has happened, I will use my voice to heal the wounds within your hearts.

Whether it's for humanity or the Felinians, Pathos Particles are a force to be reckoned with. In moderation, they can be beneficial to living organisms, regulating human emotions and providing essential sustenance for the Felinians, even empowering them with manifested armaments.

However, exposure to an overwhelming amount of these particles over an extended period can lead to Pathosis, a condition marked by mental instability and loss of bodily control. In the most severe cases, the affected individuals lose their sanity, transforming into destructive Anomalies.

I possess a unique ability to soothe the hearts affected by these Pathos Particles.

"Thank you, Miss Triss... I feel much better after listening to your song."

"Triss! I can't believe I'm seeing Triss here! Am I dreaming?"

After a period of soothing, those with mild Pathosis symptoms have regained their sanity, and even the severely afflicted have shown some improvement. Seeing this, I feel reassured that my efforts are not in vain.

"Really? Do you truly believe that all of this is worthwhile?"

At some point, I begin to hear strange whispers. But when I look around, there is no one to be found. Perhaps it's due to exhaustion. After all, using my abilities to comfort these patients is not an easy task. But I have no regrets.

A sensation akin to an explosion coursed through my chest, strange voices echoed in my mind.

"You can't save them."

"They are beyond help. They have become captives of Pathosis."

"You can do nothing. And furthermore..."

A figure, shrouded in a white robe, unexpectedly appears before me.

"You will be just like them, ruled by fear and despair, plummeting into an endless abyss."

"You think so? I won't become like that." I continue to offer food and drink to the weakened patients, to soothe the agitated ones, ignoring the figure's ominous words.

"How much are you willing to give for them? They have nothing to do with you." The figure trailed behind me like a shadow. 

"They were doomed the moment they arrived here. Isn't it a form of mercy to let them fade in peace?"

Mercy? I couldn't help but laugh.

"Your so-called mercy, in my eyes, is nothing but cruelty."

"Whether they are human or Felinian, all lives are not to be trifled with."

"Well then, are you prepared to be cast away by the world in your quest to protect them?"

There was no need to respond. I didn't come here to answer such trivial questions.

I begin to sing a soothing lullaby, watching as the faces of the patients gradually softened amidst the melody, slipping into a peaceful slumber.

Yes, this is what I need to do.

"You know, there's no cure for those afflicted by Anomalies."

"But they are not afflicted yet. They're merely suffering from Pathosis."

"Hah, Pathosis? You believe in such a term?"

The figure is approaching me. I only then realize that the phantom, which seems ready to vanish at any moment, has become as real as any person.

"People eroded by Pathos Particles have no way back."

"Impossible! I have witnessed patients cured of Pathosis reintegrating into society..."

"Was that truly a cure? You know the truth, why deceive yourself?"

"What... what are you? Stop trying to bewitch me!"

"I'm you, Triss!"

The white figure in front of me takes off its hood, revealing a face that is both delicate and familiar.

"I am the mercy and despair in your heart. I have always been watching you, hoping you would notice me, but you've always ignored my existence."

"And now, you finally face me. What's your next move, Triss?"

"You're running out of time. Make your choice. Will you accept me, save me, or sever me, this confusing emotion within you?"

"No, you are not me. If you were, you would understand there is no need for a choice."

"There has always been only one path before me." I extended my right hand toward the girl.

"Come, become my strength once again, let's fight together to save the patients here, to save this world."

"Then, everything will be over..."

Upon removing her virtual reality helmet, it takes Triss several minutes to familiarize herself with her surrounding environment.

"Miss Triss, the virtual test was a resounding success!" A Felinian scientist, donned in a white lab coat, can't contain his excitement. He's incessantly swiping through the data on his handheld terminal. 
"If these readings are correct, your abilities could theoretically rehabilitate hundreds of Pathosis sufferers! I can hardly wait to test it!"

"Sorry, but I'm a bit tired." Triss, adorned in her white gown, couldn't hide the fatigue etched between her brows, giving her aura a slight touch of melancholy.

"Miss Triss, pay no mind to this fool." Another researcher, her hair tied back in a ponytail, dismissed her colleague. 

"Even if the scenario was simulated, for Miss Triss it was a real experience. We can wait until next time for any further tests!"

"Oh, wait until next time...?"

"Any objections? Miss Triss offering her precious time amidst her busy schedule for these tests is a blessing we couldn't possibly ask for! It's alright, Miss Triss. Please go rest."

Triss nods at the bickering researchers and turns to leave the room. No one notices the shadowy figure writhing within her silhouette.

"These are the people you've been protecting? Greedy, ignorant, knowing no bounds."

"These lives are not worth your salvation. Your abilities should be directed towards a greater purpose."

"Such as restoring the world back to its original form..."

A flash of bloody light flickered in the young girl's eyes.

"Ah, it's all set. You can give it a try and pluck the strings."
The girl, cradling a musical instrument, seems to be teaching children how to assemble it.
Nearby, an elderly woman was playing, her fingertips pouring out the melody.
"Got it!"

I have no intention to disrupt this harmonious scene. I only savored the melodious tune from a distance.
"Miss, would you like to come and listen?"
The elderly woman Bakeroned me over with her frail hand, inviting me to come closer. 
"Pardon the intrusion."

"This is..."
"A shamisen, a traditional string instrument. I'm teaching them to play in my grandmother's stead."
The girl answered before I could finish.
It seems many before me have asked the same question.
"But compared to music theory, the children prefer hands-on activities."
With that, the elderly woman, referred to as 'Granny', handed over her instrument.

"Why don't you give it a try, miss?"
It's somewhat like a guitar, perhaps simpler. I attempt to play a guitar piece. 

Plin…
Hmm? This tone... It's too different…

"This isn't a guitar, miss. The shamisen has its own method of playing."
The elderly woman gently chuckles as she picks up her instrument and starts to play.
In these few minutes, not only have I come to appreciate the charisma of the instrument, but the elderly woman's passion for the instrument is also clear as day.
A deep and fervent love.

"I've made a fool of myself."

"No, I was too presumptuous. Ma'am, could you teach me to play?"

"Pluck, strum, press, wipe..."
I murmured, jotting down another note here. That should suffice.
With a satisfied nod, I gather the scattered sheets and pens on the table, placing the freshly compiled textbook right in the center. 

"You're still up at this hour, miss?" 

Startled, I see the teacher standing by the classroom door, her face etched with worry.
Hastily, I guided her to sit by the desk, where she spotted the textbook. 

"A textbook..." 
"Yes, a guide for learning the Shamisen,"
I replied, handing over the rough copy to her.

After several days of lessons, I've come to realize that her teaching methods are traditional: imparting knowledge through oral instruction and cultivating students according to their aptitude.
Indeed, it brought out the students' strengths and helped them recognize and fill their gaps.
...At the cost of the teacher's gradually thinning figure. 

The textbook records fundamental knowledge about the Shamisen, techniques for playing, and some scores the teacher has performed.
These are all summarized from the past few days of learning. While it may not be as comprehensive as I'd like, it could at least afford the teacher a bit of rest. 

"Hereafter, you could let the students learn from this textbook. It should help you reach more students at a time," I suggested. 

"Ah... Thank you... Thank you, dear student." 

The word "student" momentarily stunned me.
But seeing the teacher's kind smile, I find myself grinning too. 

And so, within this small classroom, the number of Shamisen students has grown by one.

These days, fewer young individuals find charm in these antiquated relics, with a dwindling appreciation for such performances. Although I've tried to simplify and modify some teaching methods, it feels akin to trying to put out a forest fire with a cup of water.
In my moments of rest, I still get lost in this helpless sigh.

"Triss, is something on your mind again?" 
"Rora, I... I've been thinking about the Shamisen..."
"You mean that instrument you pulled out during your break? What about it?"

I pick up the instrument next to me and pass it over to her.
As she accepts it, she plucks the strings out of curiosity.
The music reverberates throughout the room, lingering long after the notes have been played.

"A shamisen... It's been quite a while since I've seen such an old instrument. Triss, are you thinking about..."
"Rora, can I... host a concert with it?"

I've communicated with my seniors who advocate for traditional culture before. They believe that to preserve our heritage, we must evolve with the times.
Incorporating the performance of other instruments into popular music could diversify its elements, attracting more attention—The crucial first step in promotion...

"How we can blend these disparate elements, and whether this fusion will be well received, is yet another question..."
I've been wrestling with this question for days now...

"Triss, you really need to rest more. Your eyes..."
"Huh?"
Rora's sudden comment caught me off guard. I haven't been sleeping well these past few days...

"Let's set a time to talk with the concert organizer. You, on the other hand... You really need to take a break."

"Yeah. Thank you, Rora."

"How is Miss Triss doing?" 
"She's all ready and waiting backstage."

The director bustles about, ensuring everything is in order before the concert begins.
Tension lingers in the air, palpable even in the green room where I'm waiting.

As an experienced performer, I'm not fretting over my performance.
Rather, I find myself wondering... Can the audience truly embrace this fusion of the classical and contemporary?
Will my mentor approve of my steadfast conviction?
"Will they... accept this revised version of the song?"

"Triss, don't worry. Just like always, hold your shamisen and you'll do just fine."
A familiar and gentle voice echoes from behind me.
A thin, aged hand grasps mine, holding the bow.
"Speak not of mundane affairs, but listen to the Fantasia Fiddler."

"Y-You're here!"
Before I can utter another word, she gestures for silence. Previously, I had mentioned performing with her, but she kindly declined, reasoning that her age has made it inappropriate for her to take the spotlight again.
Still, without gaining her consent, I recklessly planned this concert with my agent.

"Miss Triss, are you ready? The opening countdown is about to start!" The director's voice rings out from the walkie-talkie.
As if she remembered something, she unclasps the hairpin from her head and places it onto mine.

"Enjoy your performance!"

"Oh, another day without any gains. When will there be an end to days like this?"
"Hey, why not unwind with some music? Triss has new songs out at her concert."  
With a flick of a switch, the player starts, and melodies begin to waft through the room. They are tranquil and pure, rustic and melodious.

"Hmm, this instrument sounds familiar. I believe it's called a Shamisen. I learned to play it once."
"Sounds like a really ancient instrument. Can you still play it?"
"There's some muscle memory left. Back in the day, I had a dream of blending it with contemporary music, but alas..."
"Alas, we have all given up something to face life, haven't we?"
A shared smile spread across the faces of the two lounging on the sofa.

"I want to try again. Just like that time I stood on the stage."
"Do you want me to accompany you? Just to be clear, I've almost forgotten how to play my guitar."

This was a late-night conversation in a corner of Catto City. Everyone drifts into dreams amidst the merry discussions.
Here marks the end of Triss's story, but the story of culture doesn't end.
The heritage continues...

The name of the Lebardmann family is known far and wide. Being a part of it, I've been branded with the family's golden insignia since birth.

"Miss Triss, are you ready? The banquet is about to begin."

"Thank you, I'll be right there."

From childhood to adulthood, I've attended countless such occasions. Each time, the butler presents the roster of attendees. My task is to commit each guest's name and status to memory. As a noble lady raised under elite education, it's unacceptable to bring shame to the family by breaching etiquette.

People adorned in opulence freely mingle, dancing under the constellation of lights. The symphony of many instruments softly flows through the entire estate. The hem of my gown, embellished with intricate lace, brushes gently against the carved balustrade.

I converse with them, all smiles.

"Good evening, Lady Lecia."

"It's been a while, Mr. Vanco."

Those present are the social elite of the moment. Money, status, power, connections—they view these as resources to manipulate at will. Yet in front of me, they all sport masks of hypocrisy.

"Miss Triss, may I have the honor of kissing your hand?"

"Miss Triss, your piano skills have greatly improved. If you wish to hold a concert, we would be delighted to assist."

I have no fondness for such hollow pleasantries. Yet, masking one's emotions is another compulsory lesson one must master.

"Miss Triss, your tailor has come for the measurement."

"Please let her in."

This seamstress has skills that are nothing short of exceptional. The attention to detail in her work is remarkable, with precise measurements, meticulous stitching, and the choice of fabric that is both tactile and weighted to perfection. Furthermore, she would never trample the trust of her clients by using inadequate people.

"Miss Triss, it's been a while."

"Does the dress I made last time look short on you now?"

Her smile is warm and inviting, with a glow in her eyes that radiates a comforting light. It's a stark contrast to the endless flattery and fawning found at social events.

"I haven't seen you in a while. Did you go back home?"

"Yes! It's spring there, with dandelions and colorful flowers blanketing the hillsides."
"My two children have grown as tall as Miss Triss..."

Chuckling, the tailor unfurls her tape measure, meticulously taking down my measurements. Her client record sheet, keeping track of my data over the years, reflects a beautiful curve under her annotations.

"Miss Triss, you've truly grown up," she says with a touch of nostalgia, rolling up the tape measure that had just been warmed by my body. "I'm starting to forget what you looked like when we first met."
"Ah, children grow so quickly..."

I have a deep fondness for this tailor. The rhythm of her speech feels like familial chatter. Her stories are a world away from my own, two extremes that could never touch. Those fleeting moments of joy, the scent of fireworks...

"Miss, it's almost time for your class."

"Alright, I'll be right there."

Literature, music, dance, visual arts, languages. Equestrianism, floristry, tea ceremony, incense appreciation, and art connoisseurship.
These diverse courses have become the fabric of my everyday life.

My parents meticulously handpick the finest teachers from each field for me. My teachers, in turn, radiate expressions of satisfaction and awe during our encounters.

"Miss Triss exhibits exceptional talent," they exclaim with sincere admiration or perhaps courteous flattery. To which, I respond with a polite smile.

One day, I unintentionally overhear a private conversation. "Sir, ma'am, Miss Triss possesses the most extraordinary vocal conditions I've ever come across."

"If she dedicates herself to vocal music and receives proper and systematic education from a young age, she could become an artist!"

"There's no need." My father's voice is indifferent, and my mother's, unusually urgent and high-pitched.

"No, my apologies, but there's no need."

"Professor, we merely want Triss to grasp fundamental music theory so she doesn't embarrass herself when expected to perform."

"Anything beyond that is unnecessary, especially vocal music. Please respect our decision."

I let go of the parlor door handle.

I find myself deeply connected with music, particularly singing. I can always hear notes chiming like wind chimes in my dreams. Yet, my parents seem rather unwilling to hear my voice.

My music teacher sighs, but I also... don't want to make my parents upset because of my willfulness.

What I didn't realize then was... fate has predestined the gears of everyone's birth.

As the years unfurl, subtle hints begin to dawn on me. The stringent restraints during my childhood loosen, and my interaction with the world gradually expands.

The familial attention I receive starts to seem not as innocent as I have envisioned. They seem to encourage me to break free, smilingly telling me to "seek the freedom to sing." But to what end?

To "hinder" my aspirations.
To "sever" my dreams.
To "bear" all the pressure.

So it turns out, all these years... 
My parents' sternness was all for the sake of my safe and happy growth. But now, I can take responsibility for my own decisions.

My father, besides his silent care, begins to actively discuss amusing daily trivia with me. In my mother's loving gaze, there's always a hint of an emotion called "heartache".

"Join the music club!"

"Let's start a studio together!"

"Let me think... hmm, how about Triss Studio? It's your name!"

Seeing my senior's hearty laugh, I find myself unable to refuse. Even if failure is inevitable, I yearn to take that step.

Perhaps there are many who genuinely adore my singing? Unrelated to my past, identity, or family honor...

Much like being in a vast private estate, adorned with fabulous neon lights, only the tender moon from the distant horizon seemed to cast a caring gaze upon me.

And if I become a singer...
That person who applauded me that day, saying my "singing was soothing"...
Would they, perhaps, hear my voice once again?

The concierge bows, swinging open the door of the luxury car for the distinguished guest. A pair of slender feet in high heels delicately descends onto the red carpet.

"My goodness, look! It's Triss!"

"Triss! Triss!!"

For Triss, this is a novel experience in her life. The crowd's fervent cheers and the sporadic camera flashes that light up the night are an exquisite treat. The red carpet, broad and seemingly endless, mirrors her future path, stirring contemplation deep within her heart.

Triss Studio's debut music album gains immense popularity upon its release. Triss becomes an overnight sensation.

"Not because of the name Lebardmann, but..."

Letters, flowers, gifts—they pile up like snowflakes in the small space of the studio. Triss picks up these priceless treasures herself, dusts them off, and carefully stores them away.

This is a strange, wondrous choice—a choice she has never envisioned in her life. Thankfully, such a gamble has yielded good results.

There are still many people in this world who truly need me. Even if it requires paying the price of life itself, I am more than willing.

"I hope to be of use."

"Not as Triss Lebardmann, but... just Triss. Everyone's Triss."

"Triss! Look!"
I gently pushed open the door to the backstage resting room, only to be greeted by a gust of wind.
Rora, with her tail wagging excitedly behind her, couldn't wait to approach, holding up her device high.

"Is that... my fan?"

In the center of the screen, a girl from Yaozhou danced gracefully in a flowing cloud-patterned dress, her hair tied high, her movements light.
The music was enchanting, and with every spin and jump, she exhibited a stunning blend of strength and grace.
It was a captivating performance of Yaozhou dance.

At the end of the video, she stood in front of the camera, tears streaming down her face.

"My legs were injured in a car accident, and I thought I would have to say goodbye to dancing. But seeing Triss' determination to move forward gave me the courage to chase my dreams again... I want to keep dancing! Now, I've been admitted to a dance academy, and I will continue on my path!"
"Triss...! Thank you for being the sun that lights up my life."

The sun...

These words, mixed with soft whispers and sobs, left an echoing strength, warming my chest and eyes.
I've heard and seen many such words, yet each time, they still move me deeply.

I never felt I deserved to be called "the sun"... knowing I don't possess that kind of blazing light.
The light that illuminated them always came from the brilliance burning within themselves.
I'm just the moon, quietly reflecting the glow of their hearts.
—Like a dance between the sun and the moon.

If it's a dance, then I must respond to this sentiment!

"Rora... please help me find a Yaozhou dance teacher."

Standing in front of the mirror, I tidied up my messy long hair.
The cumbersome outfit was already switched out for a snug dance practice attire.
The light fabric perfectly outlined the curves of my body, making every muscle-engaging movement crystal clear.

Gazing at my reflection, I took a deep breath, carefully recalling my dance teacher's advice.
Combine flexibility with strength, concentrate on the power in your jumps, and make the spins swift...

"Thud—"

The heavy sound of landing hit the serene air like a weighty note.
I frowned, halting my motion.

That move clearly didn't meet my standards.
It seems that even with a solid dance foundation, mastering the techniques and charm of Yaozhou dance is no easy feat.

Suddenly, the door to the dance studio creaked open.
Instinctively, I looked up and saw a stern-faced Senior Rora in the mirror's reflection, our eyes meeting in the glass, causing me an inexplicable nervousness...

"Triss? I knew you'd still be here, you've almost been practicing all day!"
"Sorry, Rora. The performance list for the next concert is due soon, and I wanted to be prepared before that..."
"Stop, stop, stop—"
In a blink, Rora dropped her serious demeanor, standing with her hands on her hips and sighing loudly in feigned exasperation.

"Alright, I know you too well! Triss always pushes herself too hard. Take a break once in a while, will you? We'd all be worried if you wore yourself out!"
"Here, have some of this! Get some energy before you continue dancing!"
"Thank you, Rora...!"

Gratefully accepting the snack she offered, my thoughts inadvertently drifted.
Push myself too hard...?

Memories are like a meticulously carved scroll, each stroke unforgettable.
The always graceful faces of my father and mother were replaced with anger and worry because of my decision.
It was like a signal, one that tore through the suffocating protective shield like tearing through solid walls, a signal that tore through the difficult and false equilibrium at home.

"Triss, can't you spare us and yourself?"
"Do you really think with that 'Soothing Power' you can become a savior, saving every soul in distress? That's too naive..."
"The world isn't so easily changed, your meager power is but a drop in the ocean to the whole world."
"But to us, you're our only daughter..."

The bitter and conflicting pain nearly numbed my heart, that bitterness seeming to numb my tongue as well as I spoke my heart out.
"...I understand your concerns, but this is something I must face."

The 'Soothing Power' like a predetermined footnote in the pages of a book, from the moment it descended upon me, perhaps the interpretation of my life was already set.

The world is vast, with too many corners even the sun cannot illuminate.
I never fancied saving everyone.

But in the endless night, there must be light.
The moonlight isn't as warm as the sun, and its reflected light seems feeble.
Yet, it can still bring a sliver of solace to those wandering in the dark, offering a moment of peace to their souls.
Even if it means leaving the endless dark seas of the moon to myself, it's worth it.

Looking up, I gazed at my reflection, my eyes deep as lakes filled with resolve.
—I will give it my all.

"Sorry, Miss Triss. We still hope you'll reconsider. From a commercial standpoint, we believe that with your value, just singing a few songs would be very effective. There's no need to choose a high-risk option..."
The concert organizer appeared regretful on the holographic projection, their words forming an invisible seal with no room for compromise.

"I understand. I... I'll think about it again."

I knew their points were valid. Concerts are commercial endeavors, and organizers have their considerations. Switching to a dance routine that hasn't been audience-tested is obviously a hard sell.

Regardless, I wanted to show that fan the dance performance inspired by her.
So, what's next?

My mind raced with countless ideas, only to be interrupted by a sudden presence.
A familiar and comforting presence lingered beside me, as the inspector quietly sat down on the sofa next to me, looking at me with concern in his eyes.
"What's with the frown? Are you worried about the upcoming concert?"

I smiled lightly, trying to ease my brows and eyes.
"Yes. After all, it's someone else's funded event, I can't be too willful."
Perhaps I really should fund a special concert myself...

"Why not do a live stream at Baker's Cat Cafe?"
"The environment might not be as professional, but we'll do our best to make it cozy."

My heart thumped uncontrollably, unable to suppress my smile.

To feel love and support, no matter the circumstances, warm and bright.
As if the sun shines through, melting small troubles in ripples of joy.

Having such a companion is...

"That would be wonderful."

"Yes. It will be."

"Triss! The photography equipment is all set up, come check it out!"
Echo peeked her head out from the training room that had been temporarily commandeered as the stage.

"The backdrop is ready too."
Shiro's head popped up next to her.

With stars for company, the Milky Way for a friend, gentle breezes, and clouds to cuddle, the path under the moonlight is never lonely.

"This will definitely be the best performance."

"Triss… Triss!"
Echo waves a hand quickly in front of my face.

Late night.
Sleep won't come. I turn off every light, pick up a cup of black tea, and walk to the floor‑to‑ceiling windows.

Suddenly I see him again: a man clutching a blood‑red electric guitar, howling his heart out on stage.
Born to press black and white keys, yet his heart belonged to frets and six strings. He lived forever under the gaze of others, knowing he'd never shed those shackles—so he chose to be a moth to a flame.
I can almost hear that sigh in the ashes.

I don't feel I have that right.

My voice—the "Soothing Power" that's supposed to heal anything—why didn't it reach him?

The music I idealize is a carefully brewed black tea—elegant, mellow, best savored in the afternoon sun.
But some people may need something sharper, purer—like… tequila with salt and lemon.
Have I been trapped in a cocoon called "the Triss style," using my self‑assured gentleness while ignoring the shouts desperate to be heard?

…
I don't know.
I want to know.

Another sleepless night.
I start the turntable. Bach's Well‑Tempered Clavier flows out, every note precise as the gears of a watch.

But this time, that perfection makes me feel inexplicably… suffocated.

I swipe through my terminal, rifling aimlessly through folder after folder…
An audio file long forgotten catches my eye—one of the random samples I'd had my assistant collect when I was exploring different styles.
Electronic music I'd once dismissed as noisy and chaotic, unfit to carry any "Soothing Power."

I force my mind to clear, drop my preconceptions, and really listen…

Something shifts.
I touch a restless, surging vitality—a pulse I've never allowed into my own music.

A thought flashes through me.
Is it really incapable of carrying "Soothing Power"? Or have I been trying in the wrong direction?
What if, instead of guiding and calming, I ignite and release—not the hand that smooths with tenderness, but the blade that cuts things open and faces the wound.
"In its own way… that's a different kind of romance."
I murmur, a smile tugging at my lips.

I grab my terminal and text my senior.
"Senpai, I think… I need an adventure."

It doesn't take long before the noise rushes in like a tide.
"EDM?! Is Miss Triss changing her style?"

My decision stirs up a storm. The fan forums are in an uproar.
The studio phones won't quit—partners ring in with cautious questions. Senpai takes call after call until her hand goes numb, and now and then she shoots me a helpless, fond look.
"You owe me dinner later!"

"Triss, I hear you've been dabbling in some… mm, trendier musical forms?"
Mother takes an elegant sip of tea.
"Mmm… a bit of exploration is fine. But do keep up the Lebardmann standard."

"The world of music is wide; I'd like to linger in another garden."
I smile, easy and light. I know the family's worries come from love, but I trust my judgment too.
Doubts do settle like dust now and then, and I brush them away. More than anything, though, there's excitement and nerves… So this is what stepping out of a comfort zone feels like.
My terminal blinks—it's a message from Inspector.

"Triss, the new project is suuuuper cool! Let 'em see the Electro Storm sweeping Catto City!"
A tiny, twinkling tornado emoji at the end.

No speeches—just a simple, teasing cheer, and I can't help smiling.
They get me. They're with me. As always.
That last sliver of hesitation goes still.
"Thanks. It might get a little loud—please bear with me."
I add a playful wink emoji, just like Inspector.

Outside, the sun is perfect. The shadows that clung to my heart feel like they were never there.
This road… is wider than I thought.

I stick to my guns and lock in Boreala's Chausie Stadium. I have Senpai accept every broadcast deal, too.
This song—I want the whole world to hear it.
The 120,000‑seat stadium is packed. I stand center stage, take a deep breath, and tighten my grip on the mic.
"Everyone—before we start, please hear me out."

"All this time I believed gentle music was my calling: to soothe wounds and bring peace."
My gaze sweeps the stands; swaying light sticks merge into a sea of light.
"Only lately did I realize gentleness can't define everything. Some blazing lives are meant to burn on—they should never be cooled."
"Music isn't a single color. There's more than one way to give love and hope. That's why I'm trying something different, why I'm wearing this, why I'm standing here."
"This song is for everyone who keeps moving through confusion and pain, for the souls who never stop crying out—who won't stop until their last breath."

I pause.
A hundred and twenty thousand here, countless more watching the stream… I can feel the world's attention converging on this one point.
"To the wounded. To the departed—'To Every Beating Heart.'"

A wave of electronic sound tears across the stadium. High‑frequency lights rip the night into shifting color. In an instant, Chausie Stadium becomes an ocean of notes and cheers.
We've rehearsed this more times than I can count. I'm not afraid of slipping up; I empty out, as if I am the beat itself.
Release… release! Let it all go!
I knew it. I knew I could.

When the last note dies, I bow to all sides. The roar of applause and cheers feels like it could peel the roof right off.
By chance, I catch a familiar face in the front row—the former bassist of Chautrand.
"Miss, your music is too refined. It doesn't belong with madmen like us."
—That's what he once said to me.

He isn't waving a light stick like the others. He just sits there, meeting my eyes.
"Look at me now—have I stumbled close to your shadow?"
I say to him in my heart.
A moment later, he gives a small, helpless smile, and slowly brings his hands together to applaud.

I smile back.

Weekend. Triss Studio is sweet with the scent of champagne and juice.
Triss suggests a small party at the studio. Along with the staff, the Baker Squad is invited too.

"The #TrissEDM tag has already broken a hundred million!"
"Yep—several new tracks are sitting near the top of the charts."
"Tsk tsk… They found a genius for the arrangement. The synth layers, that second drop, and that long low‑end run after—insane! Ah… but of course, the key is that Triss sings it so well~"
Stars spark in Echo's eyes as she gushes, thumping her thigh—she's always been a die‑hard electronic‑music fan.
"Don't say that. I've still got a long way to go."

"It's about time—let's eat! Oh… right, how about a pre‑meal speech from our superstar?"
"Yeah, Triss, say a few words!"

"Thank you, everyone at the studio, for putting up with my whims. Without your work, there'd be no project. And thank you to the Baker Squad—when I hesitated, you didn't hold back your encouragement, and that helped me take this step."
