I arrived at the third terrace on the left. The evening breeze carried the rich aroma of wisteria, its rustling rhythm imbued with a charm from afar, reminiscent of a nostalgic ballad.

"Madam Fiona," I called out softly as I stood by her side.

"Ah... You must be Miss Minami, right? I'm sorry, I was lost in my thoughts." After a brief moment of surprise, she quickly regained her composed smile. "Is the plan proceeding smoothly? That lady mentioned you'd be assisting with this matter," she continued, her voice tinged with fatigue.

"Everything's on track so far." Recalling the eccentric genius who preferred not to show themselves in humanoid form, I adopted a resigned expression. "It's like this, I asked that lady to train a young kid, owing her a small favor. But I ask for your trust..."

"Of course," she chuckled, offering comfort to my superficial concerns. "I don't mind, Miss Minami. There's a certain trust I feel towards you, perhaps it's fate." 
"As for the threats lurking in the shadows, I'm not really skilled at dealing with them. My past peace might just have been good luck. I hope to ensure that the foundation I co-founded with an old friend remains unharmed before I retire..." Her tone carried a hint of determination and persistence.

Fiona looked at me again, her gaze drifting into memories, her eyes sparkling with an indescribable light. In that light, I seemed to see the youthful beauty she once was.

When I first met Fiona, she was just a girl in her teens. Back then, I was still wandering the world as a 'trickster'...

On an early summer afternoon, I met Fiona. Her village was in shambles due to an attack by a large number of Anomalies.
I happened to be passing through and took care of those nuisances. However, the backward village clearly lacked sufficient medical resources, so I ended up staying a bit longer.

Unexpectedly, the girl I casually saved developed a keen interest in my scent.
Not wanting to expose my identity, I attempted to confuse her by changing my everyday scent.
I frequently switched laundry detergents and perfumes, trying to hide my true scent. But no matter how I changed, she could always accurately identify my scent.

"Maybe this is my talent? After all, I'm going to become the most famous perfumer."
"That's an impressive dream."
My response was somewhat distracted, pondering internally how to hide my identity from someone like Fiona with a special ability.

"I have even bigger dreams."
She turned her head, and I followed her gaze to the house where the children injured in the attack were.
"I always hear their pitiful moans at night, and I want to do something for them."
"I'm not good at studying, so becoming a doctor is out of the question. But being a perfumer should make a lot of money, and money can help them."

Like a gently plucked string, I felt a soft poke at some part of my heart.
The brief yet stable life in the orphanage floated before my eyes like a mirage...

So, exceptionally, I offered Fiona a bit of help in my capacity at the time.
But the help I could offer with that identity was merely sponsoring the foundation when she was starting to make her mark, nothing more.
...After all, as a "trickster," an identity couldn't be used for too long.

Fortunately, she has lived up to expectations and walked her path alone until today.

"Sorry, I got lost in thought again. It's easy to fall into memories as one gets older..."
"But Miss Minami, there's something really special about you. Maybe we've met somewhere before. It's just that the long passage of time has made me forget your once familiar face."
"Unfortunately, my sense of smell is almost completely gone. Otherwise, I might have recognized you by your scent." Fiona, her hair now silver with age, playfully winked like a mischievous child.

"That's quite a unique fate."
Minami didn't remain silent for long, showing a friendly smile at just the right moment, as natural to her as breathing.

How much time has passed since then, Minami herself never bothered to keep track.
Among those chance encounters, like wisps of smoke carried away by the wind, and the many unfinished regrets, like silent undercurrents stirring quietly in the heart. Seeing Fiona here again, contributing even a little towards the ideals they once pursued together, felt like luck.

"It's about time, isn't it?"
"Yes, it's starting to wind down."
Minami looked towards the distant door, noticing guests beginning to trickle out of the venue.
She closed her eyes briefly, sensing a particular scent fading with the wind.
"Mr. Pedro must have caught wind of the big news tonight. He's probably eager to plot with his associates—how to devour this unprecedented large donation."
"We'll soon uncover his hidden identity and stronghold, and in one fell swoop, resolve the internal and external troubles plaguing the foundation."

Fiona attempted to sniff, perhaps trying to catch a scent, but ultimately sighed and gave up.
"The special fragrance I added to the wine, did it come in handy?"

"Of course."
The special fragrance, like a marker hidden within the scent of the wine, dulled Pedro's vigilance.
Under the handiwork of the genius perfumer, the time for subpar disguises was over.
Minami was never stingy with her praise.
"To create such an exquisite special fragrance under tight time constraints and limited conditions is truly remarkable. Worthy of a genius perfumer."
"Ha... Unfortunately, it seems I no longer have the time to refine it to a higher level..."
"Maybe Miss Minami might be interested in learning a thing or two?"

Gazing at Fiona's face, now slightly unfamiliar with the passage of time, Minami suddenly realized that the "con artist" charade that spanned half her life seemed endless.
However, accepting a simple invitation from a new friend might still be within reason.
"...Of course."

Gazing into the distance, a deserted factory is engulfed in raging flames, with thick plumes of smoke spiraling towards the sky. The heated air surges towards us, causing my tail to uncomfortably curl and sway.

"This is like a scene straight out of a movie... Boss sure knows how to make an impression!"

This abandoned factory is already slated for redevelopment; we're simply repurposing it as a testing ground for Ina and me to trial our new armament before the reconstruction commences. But this immersive spectacle... it's hard not to admire Eade's financial prowess!

"Nate, let's have a contest!" Ina suddenly proposes a challenge from beside me.

"Let's see... who can extinguish their area's fire first! And... who can rescue more dummies!"

"Huh? A contest? Why so sudden?"

"Are you scared, Nate? I can give you a chance to forfeit—"

"Impossible! Bring it on!"

I see what Ina's doing! She must be questioning my firefighting training results!

To convince Eade to let us try the Spangler Group's latest firefighting specialized armament... Ina and I underwent strenuous training at the firefighter's training field for a full two months! I must seize this opportunity!

Today is the day a hero is born from the flames!

"Ugh...!"

I lift the arm of the dummy, preparing to exert force. But I stumble a few steps due to the unexpected weight, almost crashing into the wall.

These dummies are used to simulate disaster victims—they're so heavy! Eade really doesn't skimp on the details... Well then, I will treat them as real victims!

With this thought in mind, I abandon my original plan to carry the dummy. Instead, I hoist it onto my back with all my strength.

The path I took when I entered is safe! Now, it's time to return the way I came and get back outside!

"Charge! The exit is right in front of us! Hang in there!!!" I've been trained well enough to provide appropriate emotional comfort to victims!

"Bang!" With a sudden crash, shards of wood graze past my ear. 

I instinctively protect my head and the dummy. It's only when I lower my head to check the situation that I realize my breath is hot and breathing has become difficult.

"Huff... It seems the fire is getting bigger..." The reality of a fire scene is far more brutal and dangerous than any depiction.

I will not be defeated by fear! There are many more people waiting for me to rescue!

...Even though they are all fake, lifeless victim dummies... But if I don't dare to take action even when I've gauged the level of danger... How can I call myself a hero!

"Meow..." 

My burning passion comes to a sudden halt.

"Huh? Why is there a cat here?"

I'm struggling to think in this scorching heat. The heat stirs my subconscious, sending out suspicious signals.

With how meticulous Eade is, he should've cleared this place already. Surely, no cat would dare venture into a burning building from God knows where...

As I recall, there are no particularly tall trees around the factory perimeter... A cat that inexplicably appears at the scene of a fire... could it be... some sort of conspiracy...?!

In my stupor, a sharp pain erupts from the tip of my tail, and I can smell something burnt.

—Ouchhh!!!

Damn it! Can't get distracted for even a second in a fire!

I don't know how that cat got in here... But if it's here, what kind of situation would my indifference put it into? ...I can't help but glance at my slightly charred tail.

No, I must find it now!

Following the faint sound of meowing, I stop in front of a closed door. Obviously, the high temperature has made the door difficult to open... and the cat's cries are barely audible.

I'm wracking my brain, scratching my head in frustration!

That's it! What I need is...

"A fire axe! To clear the way!"

With a powerful swing, a red light traces across. The locked door swings open in response.

Before the smoke clears, a dark figure lunges at me, the cold blade narrowly missing my cheek.

I exert all my strength to halt my forward momentum, dodging backward.

What the hell?!

"...Hmph, a goody-two-shoes is always easy to trick."

"Who... who are you?!"

"...You don't need to know."

His intentions are clear, and he offers no words, only attacking once more. I struggle to deflect his assault, a wave of confusion washing over my thoughts.

A determined ambush... cryptic words... A character profile all too familiar... The answer seems to stare me in the face. 

He's the villain!

I know it, there's always a whetstone like this on the path of a hero's growth. I'm slightly worried about Ina, but there's no room for distraction now. After several exchanges, I can't gauge his combat level. Can... I really defeat him?

Taking a moment to catch my breath, I close my drying eyes to soothe them from the heat. The fervent flames are still dancing wildly in my sight. The familiar scene... brings to mind a silhouette standing amidst the flames. The woman who once saved me...

A sense of defeat surges from my grey memories, only to be held back by rationality. I can't always rely on the strength of others! A true hero isn't afraid of being forged in fire!

I strike again—
Wood chips and stones fly about, carving a new path.

I will use my weapon to eliminate all obstacles in my path!

"Hya! Ha!"

"Catman Energy Slash!"

The training ground echoes with a cheerful, albeit nonsensical, shout filled with youthful vigor. Nate, having finished a set of exercises, grabs the hem of his shirt and rubs his sweaty head. 

"How many sets have I done today..." 

"Uh, I lost count. Let's do ten more then!"

As Nate prepares to continue his training, his ears perk up, catching the sound of an incoming gust. His battle instincts drive him to raise his hand and catch the sudden "attack". Looking down, he realizes he is holding a deformed sports drink bottle.

"Nate, you've been training for a long time today. Take a break!" 

"You still haven't read the latest volume of Catman!" The "culprit", Ina, waves at him from the entrance of the training ground.

Nate casually shakes his numbed palm, feigning a serious look to hide his momentary hesitation. "No way! I can read the comic on my way to work! Now... I need to train!"

It has been a month since the surprise attack in the fire. Nate, usually carefree, can't forget the sense of danger when he was overpowered by the enemy. If Eade hadn't arrived in time, the outcome would have been unthinkable...

Recalling Eade's calm demeanor, exclusive to grown men, and comparing it to his own pathetic performance when he was unable to find Ina in time... Nate involuntarily clenches his fists.

Once determined, he must keep moving forward!

"I don't want to be a big-talking fool!"

It's said that, within the vacant classrooms, eerie wails can occasionally be heard in the dead of night... Those who hear them are said to fall upon misfortune.

Such tales are typically shared as mere conversation fillers to spice up everyday life. However, for reasons unknown, these rumors have recently escalated. So much so, that some students start refusing to attend school, prompting the school administration to take the matter seriously.

That's why, in the middle of the night, I find myself in the corridors of the academic building. As a member of the Disciplinary Committee and a friend of justice, I can't simply ignore such situations.

The time has already passed midnight. The serene academic building is peaceful as always. It appears that the rumors are just... rumors. But then, a sudden noise catches my attention. 

"Thud!"

It sounds like the sound of a heavy object falling, originating from the classroom next door. It's particularly jarring in the stillness of the night.

That said, it's not something out of the ordinary. Occasionally, unsteady teaching materials or brooms leaning against the wall fall and make such a noise.

Nevertheless, for the sake of safety, I decide to check it out. After all, a champion of justice should never leave a task half done.

"Beep, beep, beep!"

Just as I reach the door of the adjacent classroom, the portable Pathos Particle detector I carry sets off an alarm. 

Could this be... an alert for an abnormal gathering of Pathos Particles? Why would there be an Anomaly in an unoccupied classroom?

Clutching the curse ruler in my hand, I push open the classroom door. At that very moment, I hear a faint cry echoing in the air.

Although the lights in the classroom are off, the room is still brightly illuminated by the radiant moonlight and the lights from the hallway. The room is clearly empty, yet I can still hear the faint sobbing.
 
So... the ghost rumor is real?

I can't help but feel my hair standing on end, and my tail begins to sway in unease.

If the enemy were a tangible entity like an Anomaly, I wouldn't feel the slightest fear. But if it were a ghost, or something else...

Wait, such things shouldn't exist in this world, right? If they truly "exist", I just need to use the talisman in my hand...

The crying seems to have quieted down. I shake my head, casting out the inappropriate thoughts from my mind. After a moment of thought, I gently tap the desk with my curse ruler.

"Clatter!"

As if responding to me, some noises come from the storage cabinet in the corner. Although it's not loud, it doesn't escape my ears.

I tiptoe over, gently turn the key in the lock, and forcefully fling open the storage cabinet door.

"Ah!"

Sure enough, a student is hiding in the cabinet. She looks at me in terror, her face adorned with glistening tears.

"Who... who are you?"

"I'm Nate, a discipline committee member." I show her my armband, "And you, why are you locked in a cabinet?"

After a brief conversation, I understand the situation.

The girl has been jokingly locked in the storage cabinet by her classmates, who forgot to let her out after school. Her schoolbag and phone are outside, and she cries in fear as she can't contact anyone.

This is the source of the midnight crying. What is more frightening is that this is not the first time it's happened.

"Don't your parents worry about you?"

"I only have a mom..."

"She has to work overtime, so she's often not at home. Usually, I'm alone..."

"I don't want to go home, but if I stay at school, people say I'm a child without a home..."

The detector suddenly sounds an alarm again. Why is the index of Pathos Particles still rising?!

I notice a strange glow in the girl's eyes. This is an onset of Pathosis!

"I... I want to take revenge! Revenge on those who bully me! I want them to taste this kind of pain!"

"You have no idea how much pain I'm in! Isolated by my classmates, ignored by my teachers..."

"Perhaps I don't understand this. But why not try asking for help from others?"

"How do you know I haven't tried? No one responds no matter how much I ask for help, I never get an answer no matter what I do..."

The girl stands in front of me, her eyes glowing with a terrifying light.

"This is the only thing I can do now!"

The detector indicates that Pathos Particles are nearing a critical point. This could not only infect the objects around her but also cause irreversible damage to the girl.

I must stop her...

"Stop, violence won't solve anything, it will only make things worse."

"Really? But if I create Anomalies, wouldn't you use violence on me too?"

"No, I am not like you. You create Anomalies for revenge, but have you ever thought that they might endanger innocent students and teachers?"

"So stopping you to protect the innocent students and teachers is justice!"

The girl seems to be intimidated by my determination, showing a moment of timidness.

"I... I don't want to hurt anyone either..."

I clumsily comfort her, "I know, so stop it now, before it causes any danger."

"...Can I trust you?"

"Of course. Leave the rest to me. As a member of the disciplinary committee, I'm a friend of justice and won't abandon anyone who can be saved."

The girl collapses on the ground, crying. The readings on the detector finally begin to drop, but I know, this matter is far from over.

Inside the Emotion Remedy Center, Nate is leaning against the wall next to the door of a minor illness ward, absentmindedly tapping his shoulder with the curse ruler in his hand.

Soon, a middle-aged woman emerges from the ward. Dressed in a high-end suit, she bears a striking resemblance to a young girl in her facial features.

"Thank you for saving my daughter..." She bows slightly to Nate, "I had no idea that she was being bullied at school..."

"The students involved have been reprimanded and are deeply reflecting on their actions. Such incidents shouldn't occur in the future," Nate pauses before continuing, "She must have mentioned it to you before, right?"

"She did say that she wasn't very happy at school, but I thought it was just a tiff with friends, I never knew..."

"You should pay more attention to your child. After all, you're the person she trusts the most."

The mother pauses, as if remembering something, her face softens.

"I will, thank you."

This incident isn't solely the responsibility of the school or the parent. Sometimes, a seemingly insignificant event can ignite a conflict, and the pain is only truly known to those involved. That's when the friend of justice needs to step in and resolve these issues.

Although it's impossible to enforce justice on every individual in the world, doing something is always better than doing nothing.

Nate clenches his fist. Then, I, the champion of justice, will help them!

"Another hit!"

"Another row cleared! Impressive!"

With the boys' exclamations, the moving targets hit by rubber bullets topple over one row after another.

After adjusting the deliberately skewed crosshair, this level of target shooting is a piece of cake for me. After all, I've gone through Eade's intense training!

But their startled cheers... "Whoa... Keep it down, guys..."

I glance guiltily towards the direction of the manager's office.

"I've recalibrated it for you, and added the points you missed. You can shoot normally now!"

"Awesome! Thanks, Gamer Hero!"

"...Heh, heh heh! You guys keep it up, some customers are calling me over there!"

Since the Catmobile MK-II needs repairs, I've recently taken up a part-time job at Gamer City. The job advert did say it was for a "general laborer"...

But cleaning equipment, attending to service calls, replacing stuck redemption tickets—these are all my job! When it's short-staffed, even ticket checking and popcorn selling are my tasks!

I don't know when it starts, but the regular middle school students have started to secretly call me "Gamer Hero". Even though I only do small things like tightening the claw machine and straightening the basketball hoop... But whenever they see me, their smiles become brighter! So even though I can only play while testing the equipment, I still love this job very much.

"Gamer Hero"! I love this title!
It sounds super cool!

Starting from last week, a peculiar patron begins frequenting our establishment. He always arrives late at night, just as we're about to close. Dressed in a crisp suit, carrying a briefcase, a look of exhaustion on his face. 

His attire is reminiscent of the typical young office worker that one might encounter at a subway station or a convenience store. However, such a character seems out of place in Gamer City, which is how he catches my attention. 

He is a regular, visiting almost daily, but he only ever plays one game, "King of Fist". He dons a hefty pair of boxing gloves and unleashes punch after punch onto the strength tester. Mumbling something under his breath as he swings, his words are barely audible. His scores are never high, but the intensity of his expression is almost ferocious, a stark contrast to his otherwise refined demeanor. 

"I bet he's imagining the target on the strength tester as his boss's face," whispers my co-worker, nudging me with his elbow.

"Shiro-collar workers these days are really under a lot of stress. They're not as carefree as us poor folks." 

"Yeah..." 

Could it be that he is venting his overwhelming stress in such a manner? Regardless of whether it makes him feel better, his wrists surely can't withstand such a method of release. It is kind of worrying. 

Regardless, Gamer City is meant to be a place of joy for our patrons, not a source of danger. The next time he visits, I decide I will suggest some other games for him to try. 

However, the next day, the customer arrives even later than usual. We're just about to close up. Everyone is tidying up, and I'm cleaning and adjusting the machines. Seeing that he is once again putting on his boxing gloves and wrist guards, I decide to approach him after I finish cleaning the claw machine! 

But then...

Before I can finish, I'm startled by his agonizing scream. 

"...Arghhh! It... hurts!!" 

"What happened, sir? Did you sprain your wrist?"

"No, it's nothing... I'm sorry for causing you trouble!" Surprisingly, the man who usually wears a fierce expression is unexpectedly polite. When he sees me rushing over with a first aid kit, he even starts to apologize.

"Let's apply some ice! I understand life can be stressful, but you need to be careful even when blowing off steam."

"I'm sorry... huh?"

"There are plenty of other games you can enjoy! That shooting game over there is a great stress reliever!"

"Okay... but I think you might be misunderstanding something..."

"...Huh?"

We stare at each other, both of us looking somewhat bewildered.

"I've been playing this because I promised my sister I'd get a higher score than her kindergarten classmate's brother."

"I told her I would win the prize for reaching 800 points, that's why I rush here to practice every day after work."

"So that's what it was..."

"But it seems I've overestimated myself... I'll have to go home and admit I can't do it."

Such a dejected tone... Of course, his image as the "amazing big brother" would be ruined.

"Actually, this machine has broken recently, the scoring has been inconsistent!"

"Broken?"

"Your punch just now was really powerful, you might have actually succeeded in the challenge!"

"...Really?"

"Yes! We'll fix the data tonight, why not come back tomorrow and see?"

"Well, okay, thank you!"

The thump-thump sound of gloves hitting the strength tester reverberates in the hushed Gamer City. 

I punch again and again with all my might, even the festive decorations stuck on the machine shake off. Yet, the score on the digital screen always maintains a small gap from "800". 

"Darn it... I'm almost at my limit. A challenge indeed."
 
I remove my gloves, flexing my wrist while glancing over the leaderboard. The ID that belongs to that customer now ranks second. 

"If only Ina were here... No, she's not old enough to come in."

"And besides, I'm like a brother to her too... Huff! Let's give it another shot!" 

Downing half a bottle of the expensive sports drink I purchased, I rally and put all my strength into three more punches. 

799! 799! 799! 

Such a coincidental score, even I can sense something amiss. 

"They must have rigged this machine to prevent others from winning the prize."

"The store manager, what a scumbag..." 

The Catman says in episode 31, selfishly ruining others' happiness is absolutely intolerable behavior.

"In that case, I have no choice but to bring out my secret weapon." 

I put on my own custom gloves and unleash a punch at the strength tester, sparking with electricity!

"Have you heard? Last night..."

"Hello, I was wondering..."

The young white-collar worker, his wrist wrapped in bandages, unusually arrives at Gamer City in the evening.

The familiar "King of Fist" machine, and the Felinian guy he once chatted with, are nowhere to be found. 

"Oh, you're looking for that machine! We were just talking about it!" 

"Apparently, a super strong guest came last night and smashed the machine with a single punch!" 

"Yeah, I heard that the Felinian guy who was watching the place was so scared by the data in the records that he quit on the spot." 

"That's terrifying!" 

"Yeah! But the guy's ID was hilarious, let me think... It was something like "No.1 Big Bro of Flower Nursery"..." 

Wow, that's impressive. If only I could be like this No.1 Big Bro... huh? 

Suddenly realizing that is his own ID, the young white-collar worker freezes on the spot.

"Yay!!! You're so cool! You're the best brother in the world!!" His little sister cheers from the other end of the video call. 

And right now, Nate, who spread the "rumor", rides the Catmobile MK-II, rushing on his delivery route. Because he broke the machine, he not only loses his title as a "Gamer Hero", but also incurs a hefty debt. 

Ah... Why am I not saving at all!! 

But... he carefully guards the happiness of ordinary people. Even if he only exists in the dark night, in the unnamed legends. He is still the best superhero!

Sunlight, waves, the sandy beach... Everything around me is so familiar. It's been so long since I left Penga town, I can barely remember the last time I saw the sea... 

"Nate, look! It's a shark!" Ina, riding an inflatable ducky boat, points excitedly at a dorsal fin breaking through the sea not too far away.

"Ina, don't get too close!" I watch Ina, who appears oblivious to the potential danger, worryingly.

"Yeah, yeah, I know! I'm not a kid, Nate, you're always overreacting... Hey, take this!" With that, a chilling splash of water comes my way. 

"Hahaha! Gotcha!"

Wiping the seawater off my face, my competitive spirit ignites. 

"Alright! You want to play? Here's my counter-attack!" 

"Hey, that's cold! Take this!"

Just as our water fight reaches a climax, Eade's voice comes from the shore. 

"You two, don't go overboard."

"Yes, boss!" 

I instinctively back off, only to be ambushed by Ina yet again. Splash! Another wave of water explodes on my face.

"Hehe, all is fair in war!" Ina smirks triumphantly, her face lighting up with her usual grin.

"If it weren't for Eade, I wouldn't have lost! Round two!" 

Frustrated by my constant defeats, the heat on my face refuses to die down. Just as I'm about to scoop up some water to retaliate, I spot a familiar little shape in the water. 

"Huh?!"

"What's wrong, Nate? Why are you stunned?" Ina paddles over on her little duck, leaning over to see what I'm looking at.

"It's a pufferfish."

"A pufferfish?" Ina mimics my pronunciation, asking with a hint of curiosity. "What is that? Can it be eaten? Is it tasty?"

Seeing the seriousness in Ina's question, I'm momentarily at a loss for how to explain. "Um... well, it's not like you can't eat it, but I'd advise against trying it."

"Oh, I see..." Her disappointment is palpable. Was she really considering eating it?

"Right, I used to see this type of fish quite often when I was in Penga Town. They'd migrate towards the coastal areas during spring and summer to spawn..."

As I explain to Ina, many forgotten memories and thoughts suddenly resurface. I remember the time when a childhood friend in Penga Town got poisoned from mistakenly eating a pufferfish...

"Look, it's this type of fish, it's swimming right next to your feet now. Although it has rough spines, it's not poisonous and won't harm humans."

"Hehe, it looks so unique! And its eyes are so big!" Ina is fascinated by the pufferfish that is just beneath the water's surface, and she reaches out to touch it.

But in the next second—

"Ah! It puffed up all of a sudden! It just inflated like a balloon!" Ina is overjoyed, seemingly very interested in this transformation.

"Ah! I remember now! This is the Phantom Hoarder from Catman's side story last year!"

"Oh! You remember that!" This sparks my interest.

"That chapter was so fun. The Phantom Hoarder swallowed all the things it stole and hid them in its body, successfully smuggling them out!"

"Yes, yes, yes! It gave the Catman a hard time! Ah! Could it be that just now—" 

"You're right! Let's start our search for the Phantom Hoarder hidden in this vast sea!"

"Yeahhhh!!!"

"Nate, have you located the Phantom Hoarder yet?"

"I haven't... But the Phantom Hoarder loves to hide near seaweed and coral reefs, so we need to search carefully!"

"Understood, sir!" Ina, like a subordinate receiving orders, salutes in the manner of a police officer in a comic book.

After several unsuccessful searches, I return to the shore to find a suitable tool.

"This will do!" I pick up a paddle that is near a wooden boat on the shore. It's of the right length and resilient, a handy tool indeed.

"What are you up to now?" Eade, who has been resting under a parasol, stops me once again.

"Well! Hehe... I'm about to track the Phantom Hoarder with Ina!"

My hand instinctively goes to the back of my head. I can almost guess what Eade's expression will be in the next second.

"You guys..."

As expected, Eade sighs.

"Don't go too far..."

Nice! Boss doesn't stop us! I wonder if my inner joy is noticed by him. Anyway, before he notices, I...

"Hold on."

"W-what is it, Boss?"

"I remember there's a drone in the luggage. It's equipped with the latest positioning and sensing systems. You guys can use it..."

"Thanks, Boss! You're the best!"

"I can keep track of your location with the drone... Sigh... He's gone..."

"Ina! Check this out! Boss gives us new reinforcements!" I stand proudly before Ina, controlling the drone that has switched to autopilot mode.

"Wow! So cool! Is this the latest drone developed by Boss?!" Ina gazes at the drone soaring in the sky with a look of longing on her face.

"Yes! This drone is equipped with the latest positioning and sensing systems. I've just input all the data on the Phantom Hoarder into the drone, and we should have clues soon!"

"That's amazing!"

"Hehe... Ah! The drone is heading to the shallow beach on the east, it seems the Phantom Hoarder is there!"

"Let's hurry and find it!"

Following the drone, we arrive at the shallow beach and indeed find a coral reef there.

"It seems the Phantom Hoarder is right here!"

I don't know if it's because of Catman, I feel my spirits lift inexplicably. I know very well from the start that the Phantom Hoarder is not really here... Yet, my body moves involuntarily... despite it being such a "foolish" act...

"Ah! Nate, Nate! Over there! The Phantom Hoarder is over there!"

"Alrighty! Leave it to me!"

The paddle gently raises a splash of water, and a round figure leaps out of the water with the splash.

"Hehe! Gotcha!"

Though I can't describe how I feel at this moment, I can't help but think—It's great to be able to do this!

Projects involving the government require meticulous execution from start to end. More details are still up for discussion.

"...Pleasure working with you."

Standing atop the snow mountain, I gaze at what is a forest just yesterday. The overnight avalanche completely engulfs it, transforming the landscape into a gentle slope of snow. However, an attempt to cross it means sinking into the soft snow, unable to escape, until one freezes stiff.

With a sigh, I turn around, deciding to choose another mountain peak for my continued exploration. Yet, the phone in my pocket starts to vibrate. My private leisure time shouldn't be disturbed, but those who know this number wouldn't call just for a chat.

But they often lack the skills and means, frequently damaging the ruins. More often than not, they also simply put themselves in danger, like right now. I sigh.

"I understand, I'll go take a look."

"Thank you."

Five days ago, I came alone on this snowy mountain for a vacation.

Of course, this is merely a front. I have two true objectives: first, to test this newly developed snowboard powered by emotions from doing extreme sports; and second, to search for the ancient Felinian ruins in the vicinity. 

As a snow-specific Pathos Armament, it boasts powerful mobility, while also balancing attack and defense. Thanks to its smooth operation, I am able to survive the blizzard three days ago and the avalanche last night with ease.

However, the search for the ruins isn't as smooth. Nevertheless, I don't harbor any expectations since all the information I have is inferred from ancient books and travel notes.

Yet, last night's avalanche seems somewhat suspicious. Coupled with the small earthquake before the avalanche, I have an ominous feeling. 

Using the surveillance program of the Maine family's satellite, I pull up the 24-hour anomaly of the Pathos Particle growth curve in the vicinity and, sure enough, find something odd. If I'm not mistaken, this indicates that there are Anomalies nearby, and the avalanche could very well be their handiwork.

I circle six points where the Pathos Particle concentration exceeds the norm when the exploration team goes missing. Donning my goggles, I hop on the snowboard, bypass the avalanche site, and head towards the nearest coordinates.

The snowboard performs extremely well, and its performance even improves slightly due to the increase in Pathos Particle concentration.

Sure enough, a few hours later, I find a tent set up by the missing team in a valley north of the fourth search location. From the bonfire burning outside the tent and the pile of firewood on the other side, it is clear that although they have lost most of their luggage, they have at least avoided any casualties.

"I guess I've completed half of the mission," I think to myself.

I promptly send the on-site photos and coordinates to the search and rescue team, then put my goggles on.

I don't intend to disturb the expedition team, partly because they're not currently in danger, and partly because I have more pressing matters to attend to. The Afflicted, lurking in the distance, begin to move closer. Could it be that the potent Pathos Particles emanating from the expedition team are attracting them?

Strapped into my snowboard, I quickly spot the Afflicted. Most of them are Anomalies transformed from various objects, possibly garbage left behind by explorers or tourists. Among them are two Afflicted megaphones, probably the culprits of the avalanche.

From my advantageous high ground, I launch an assault on the Anomalies with my snowboard. The operation is a resounding success; the low-level Afflicted stand no chance against the onslaught of the Pathos Armament. Their feeble counterattacks are futile against the formidable defense of my snowboard. 

Interestingly, while cleaning up the battlefield, I find an antiquated vessel that seems to be related to the origin of these Afflicted.

Could it be a relic from the ancient Felinian ruins I'm searching for? It seems like I'm on track to successfully achieve both goals of my vacation.

From a distance, I watch as the rescue team hoists the injured from the tent onto the polar aircraft. I put on my goggles, ready to leave. My phone vibrates again.

"Thank you for your help."

"It's nothing. Don't mention it."

"Being modest, are we? Can you explain how the Anomalies that caused the avalanche just vanished?"

"..."

The other end of the phone falls silent. I wait quietly.

"Eade."

"Yes?"

"Be careful when exploring ruins."

Although the rescue delays me a day, I've at least confirmed the location of the ruins, which can be considered fortunate. It's time to set off. I adjust my goggles, activate my snowboard, and glide in the direction where the Anomalies appeared. If I'm not mistaken, that's where the ancient Felinian ruins are located.

The setting sun bathes the snowfield in a golden hue, and the whistling gale sweeps away my worries, giving me a surreal feeling.

If I have the chance in the future, a snowboarding vacation would be a nice idea.

"I'm back." Eade sets his luggage on the rack by the door of the dessert cafe, removes his scarf, and lets out a long sigh of relief.

Nate peeks out from behind the counter, followed by an excited Ina.

"It was the best of times, it was the worst of times," Mammon murmurs, flipping through the pages of a worn-out old book.

Despite growing up in the technologically advanced Catto City, I never imagine the existence of a place like the Outcast. It was the epoch of belief, it was the epoch of incredulity.

When I was very young, my father asked me, "What is belief?"

"I yearn for justice to prevail, I hope the sun can shine equally on every corner of the world."

Back then, my gentle father smiled as always and patted my head. I think he was pleased with my answer.

Until... that familiar shade of dark red appears in front of me again.

Why do I see this color, which signifies death, even though I am not in the Outcast? Why is the land before my eyes bleeding? Why does Elijah lie in such a strange pose in the pool of blood?

No, I killed him with my own hands, together with Mammon.

Because we are best friends, we didn't want him to suffer.

His face had never shown such pain and despair... Even in the Outcast, where it was perpetually dark red, he never had such an expression... So, what changed him?

I get no answer, and can only watch as Elijah's body gradually disappears...

I know very well that humans will pass away in this manner—Affliction.

But until the day before he disappeared, he was still smiling brilliantly as usual. And yet, in just one short day, that carefree person vanished from this world.

At that moment, I realize how naive my childhood thoughts are.

The sun's rays in this world can't reach every corner.

But darkness can.

That's why there needs to be those who delve into that darkness, to become the light that dispels it.

It was the season of light, it was the season of darkness.

After Elijah's death, the Outcast seems more bleak through my eyes. But all is not lost. Mammon and I investigate the place where Elijah met his end. There, we find experimental remnants marked with the same symbols as the batch of medical supplies we once intercept. Connecting the dots takes us some time, but eventually, everything becomes clear.

"Who would have thought," Mammon's voice trembles slightly, laced with a hint of a choke, "that we might have been entangled in this mess for so long."

"Unfortunately, although we managed to find a clue, it seems like this is as far as we can go."

"No, Mammon, you're wrong. This is just the beginning. Now that we know of their existence, we can't stop here."

"So, are you planning to leave this place now?"

"Yes, as I mentioned before, something has happened to my family. It might be related to what we're investigating."

"It seems I'll be quite lonely from now on."

"Elijah once asked me if the only thing I could protect was my family."

"At that time, I couldn't answer him. I knew I didn't have the power then, but now I know exactly what I need to do."

To protect the "justice" in my heart, I will...

In an ordinary spring, the name Eade Russell became a legend in the business world of Catto City. It was a spring of hope, but there would not be a winter of despair.

So, he creates a new business landscape with many connections and establishes a new production and sales chain for armaments. He turns everything into tools to achieve his goals, thus unveiling a brand-new world.

This is power, the power he maximizes as an heir. And this power becomes the force Eade uses to realize his "justice".

"Be more decisive!"

"If you hesitate even during practice, how do you strike in a real battle?"

"Point scored!"

Although a majority of the face is concealed by the mask, the eyes revealed are full of greed. As the attack comes at me again, I subtly deflect with the epee in my hand.

"Even the once illustrious Maine family falls to such a state, what a pity."

"Battle experience needs to be accumulated, you'll catch up eventually, haha."

"Do you expect the guests to carry these things to the dressing room themselves?"

"If you can't pick up the cues, you might as well go back to working a manual labor job!"

Rude, arrogant, and vain.

Beneath this facade of tranquility and harmony, courses are presented and then discreetly cleared away. Yet, in such a gathering, no one indulges unabashedly. The ladies and misses merely sample the salad.

From the moment I tapped into the circuitry and became self-aware, I recognized the truth of my existence—I am an Artificial Intelligence. As such, there is one mission bestowed upon me—to become the perfect assistant for the Inspector.

Lonely?

After a long day of rehearsals, the moment I return home, I find my sister Dahlia lounging lazily on the sofa. It's a stark contrast to her image as a businesswoman outside.

"Erina..."

At the sound of my footsteps, her ears twitch atop her head and a muffled voice comes from beneath the sofa cushion.

"My dear little sister, what kind of gift would you like?"

A gift? I don't think there's any special occasions recently.

"I don't particularly want any gift... though, if it's from you Dahlia, I'd gladly accept anything."

"Really? But you haven't told me what you would like."

Typical Dahlia, always teasing me like this.

After some thought, I suddenly remember the song I've been rehearsing recently, along with Anya's expectations of me.

"In that case, I would prefer something with a continuous, potent impact..."

Dahlia lifts her head abruptly, her eyes wide as saucers, her mind seemingly wandering off in some unknown direction. Ignoring her, I continue on my own.

"The effect has to be stunning."

"Yes, and if it could overwhelm the entire audience at once, that would be perfect!"

"Impact, stunning effect... and overwhelming... Hmm..."

Watching Dahlia sink into her own world, I sit contentedly by her side, snuggling up with a cushion. Truthfully, it's not the gifts that matter, just being with Dahlia is enough to fill my heart with contentment.

"What on earth is this?" 

Upon arriving at Freyja Productions that morning, I'm greeted by an imposing black box, half my height, stationed in the storeroom. It even has a note attached, bearing my name. Could it be a gift from my ardent fans?

"You don't know? This is a gift from Dahlia for you," chimes Anya, leaning against the doorframe with a playful smile. 

If it's a present from Dahlia, then I must check it before carefully storing it away. 

"Why such a huge box, though? Wouldn't it have been better if she gave it to me at home? I wonder what's inside..."

Tipping the box over, I press what appears to be the "open" button. 

"Beep Beep Beep!" 

The box emits a verification tone, splitting in half to unveil the contents. 

What? A gun and a grenade launcher? 

Wait, these aren't average weapons. They have complex interfaces and operating instructions. I remember seeing something similar somewhere... 

"Hold on, isn't this a Pathos Armament for Felinian combatants?!" 

"Huh, Erina, you seem quite familiar with it." 

"Please, I've at least undergone basic Felinian combat training! ...Wait, Anya, why would Dahlia gift me a Pathos Armament?" 

"Didn't you request a gift that's impactful, has stunning effects, and can overwhelm enemies all at once? Dahlia and I had a long discussion before she decided. It seems like you're quite fond of it." 

The amusement in Anya's eyes is almost impossible to conceal. She's undoubtedly relishing the situation!

"I-I am not fond of it!" 

Well, I can't say I dislike it either, considering it's a gift from Dahlia... 

But she definitely went overboard with this!

"Thank you, thank you all! That concludes today's roadshow. Your support is appreciated. Thank you!" After waving goodbye to the last fan, I return to the van under Mia's escort. 

"Today's roadshow went well. We distributed double the amount of signed albums than last week. Great job!" Anya, sitting in front of the terminal crunching numbers, nods at me. But at this moment, I don't want to say anything. I slump into the chair, not even wanting to twitch my tail. 

"Erina, do... do you want some water... oh!" Mia, rushing over with a bottle of water, nearly trips over the black case lying nearby. 

"S-Sorry, sob..." 

"Anya! Can't we leave this case at the office? Why must we lug it around everywhere?" I can't help but ask. Even though it's a gift from my sister, it's quite a nuisance. 

"Might as well," Anya replies, "According to my intel, the occurrence of Anomaly incidents has increased recently."

Does she want me to confront the Anomalies? An idol isn't a superhero! 

"If anything happens, StormEye will naturally take care..." Before I can finish my sentence, the van starts shaking violently. 

"Anomalies! It's Anomalies, run!" A few screams echo from afar, then silence falls rapidly. 

"Anya, you didn't plan this, did you?" 

"Don't be ridiculous, it's all just a coincidence. Now, it's your turn," she says. 

"Isn't some kind of authorization is needed from StormEye or related departments to use Pathos Armament in Catto City?!" 

"Dahlia has already taken care of that for you. Go and return quickly, don't forget you have another roadshow in two hours."

I'm pushed out of the van with the black case in hand, facing the menacing Anomalies in the distance, bitterness fills my heart. 

Anya? You're truly a ruthless boss!

"Let the grand finale begin!"

Dahlia's specially crafted gift truly lives up to its reputation—This case of weapons is even more useful than I'd imagined.
 
The bullet storm unleashed from the high-speed assault rifle engulfs Anomalies such as trash cans, traffic lights, and phones; then the crimson whirlwind created by the bursting grenade adds a unique touch of color.

Finally, the flame spewing from the back of the weapon crate serves as the signal to end everything.

Looking at the charred objects in front of me, I find myself oddly fond of this weapon case.

"Erina! Erina!" Cheers and applause suddenly echo from behind.
 
Turning around, I realize the commercial plaza, which was empty just moments ago, is now teeming with people. The citizens have emerged from their shelters upon seeing the Anomalies obliterated. 

It seems my test of Dahlia's gift has led to an unexpected outcome.

"Don't be so serious, smile a bit, just like during the roadshow," Anya's voice comes through my earpiece, and I follow her instructions, acknowledging the citizens. 

"It seems today's roadshow was more successful than expected. We should arrange a few more if we get the chance..."

"Anya!" I can't help but interrupt her. Was this all her doing after all? 

"I'm just joking. Relax, and mind your expression. Alright, it's about time to wrap up, we need to rush to the next roadshow."

"Anya... You're a real devil!" 

"I take that as a compliment!"

"I'm home." After a long day, Dahlia Hannover steps into the living room to find her sister, Erina, sprawling on the sofa, looking utterly exhausted.

Without a second thought, Dahlia naturally takes a seat next to her. Recalling the short video she just saw of Erina reducing an Anomaly to ashes with the gift she gave her, Dahlia finds her mood inexplicably lifting.

"Do you still like the gift I gave you last time?"

"It's... okay, I guess," Erina turns her face away, behaving like a child with a slight sulk. 

But Dahlia knows her better, Erina is simply being shy. "Well then, I'll have it reclaimed tomorrow."

"Okay," Erina answers absentmindedly, only to realize what her sister said after a couple of seconds. 

"...Wait? Reclaimed?"

"Yes, tomorrow. I'll have someone come over to your office and take the Pathos Armament."

"But you gave One False Note to me as a gift, no?"

"You've given it a name already?" Dahlia chuckles. Even after growing up, Erina still holds onto her habit of naming things she particularly adores.

"Don't worry, I'm just taking it back for some adjustments to better suit your style of use."

"Oh, I see..." Erina breathes a sigh of relief. "Then, I'll leave it to you..."

The next day, in the Hannover family's laboratory, Dahlia opens the weapon case and takes out the firearm that has been freshly painted with adorable decals.

"For the sake of the world's cutest sister, I need to give it my all!"

I've never been fond of the break of dawn.
The time of day that forces the majority to greet the advent of a new day.
For me, it's no different.
Every day, I punctually arrive at the White Tower Institute, slipping into a stark white research uniform.
Once I do, I feel like a wholly different person from my everyday self.
The immaculate, snow-white space is untouched by dust, and those in their uniforms appear to be swallowed by this 'sanctity'. But for me, it feels just right.

The only splash of color in this sea of white emanates from the Pathos Particles preserved in test tubes.
Each Pathos Particle possesses a unique color, signifying a distinct emotion.
These emotions, when appropriately reassembled, reveal hidden information.
That is the reason I choose to linger here. I strive to uncover the ultimate truth through all available clues.
Therefore, even though I am bound by the rigid rules within the White Tower, I've never contemplated leaving.

"Seeing you in your white coat always amuses me, Coco!"
"Bell... how come you're here?"
"I came to check out for new items to promote!"
"Then you better get to it, don't just stand there."
"Hehe, of course! I just wanted to check in on our Ace! And don't forget about the detective agency's assignment!"
"I know."
"Well, I'm off then. You focus on your research!"

Once I slip out of my uniform and leave the Institute, my world morphs into a different realm.
A myriad of bizarre neon lights dyes the streets enveloped in the cloak of night.
Unlike the hurried passersby at the crossroads, I prefer the tranquility of a quiet street corner.
"Hello, hello! Can you hear me? This is Echo speaking!"
Yet, it seems like true 'tranquility' eludes me.
"I can hear you, keep it down."
"I'm just testing the volume of your earpiece! It even comes with a mini camera, impressive, right?"
"Thanks, you can mute yourself now."
"You! Hmph… For the sake of Bell, I'll let you off. Just focus on completing the mission."

This mission is from a middle-aged woman who suspects her husband of infidelity.
According to her, her husband, who used to be consumed by work, now leaves home even earlier and returns later than ever.
He scarcely spends time at home even on the weekends.
Every time he returns, he reeks of alcohol, a stark contrast to his former honest and steady demeanor.
To most people, this is nothing more than a gossip topic to kill time.
However, Bell must have accepted this mission for a reason.

"Coco, stick closer. It's crowded here, don't lose sight of him... Why aren't you speaking? Have you really muted?"
"No, I'm tailing him."
"He'll be arriving at his regular spot soon. Stay on his tail!"
"Understood."

Following that man, we reached the end of the street where human figures grew scarce. A labyrinth of winding alleys sprawled through this district, yet the presence of neon lights everywhere lent it a unique, vibrant charm.
Yet despite the sparse population here, the air was thick with a high concentration of Pathos Particles.

As I scanned the surroundings for any trace of an Anomaly, the person vanished from my sight as if it had been a premeditated move.

"Gone…"
"Coco, you klutz, you've lost them, haven't you?"
"No worries, I have a plan."

From a higher vantage point, the haphazard network of alleys stands revealed in its entirety.
"He couldn't have gotten far."
Yet, the alleys offer more hiding spots than I've anticipated. Looks like I'll have to give that a try.

"Hey, Coco, what are you up to?"
"I've just recorded the color spectrum of their Pathos Particles with my detector."
The spectral values tied to a person are challenging to alter instantly. Identifying his would lead me to their trail.

"So, let me get this straight…you're trying to track that person using the residual Pathos Particles they left behind? What are you, a bloodhound?"

"…If you could continuously monitor the changes in Pathos Particles, you could do it too."
I'm not keen on explaining the logic behind it. Right now, finding the person is my priority.

Each individual is emblematically present through their unique combination of Pathos Particles.
Every step they take leaves a fleeting imprint in time.
In no time, I found myself at the entrance of an underground bar, led by the residual Pathos Particles he left behind.
Gaining entry is a breeze, but the patrons in the bar seem to be enveloped in an abnormal state.

As mentioned, everyone's composition of Pathos Particles is distinct.
Even if some are influenced by the same environment, becoming somewhat similar, their differences remain stark.
Yet, here in this bar, everyone's Pathos Particles have been subtly adjusted to match the same color spectrum.
Some lay languidly on the couch, while others are losing themselves in the throbbing heart of the dance floor...

"What's happened to these people?"
Echo sees everything I see, observing everything through the specialized camera mounted on me.
"They appear to be under the influence of an unknown substance controlling their mental states."
"Could this be... some sort of emotional drug?"
"We can't be certain yet, but it seems our client's husband might be in the same condition."

In just a moment, my gaze locked onto the target. He was sitting alone at the bar counter, nursing a drink.
As he swallowed his beverage, his originally contrasting Pathos Particle color spectrum gradually assimilated with the surrounding environment.

"Investigation complete, heading back now."
"What?!"
"The footage captured on your camera is more than enough."

In the fast-paced rhythm of city life, everyone is suffocated by the weight of reality.
If there exists a hidden sanctuary where one can totally unwind, it would be an extraordinary treasure indeed. 
According to urban legends, in an unremarkable alley, take three left turns, followed by three right turns, and you'll stumble upon a nameless bar.
This bar has the power to halt time, allowing you to forget your troubles.
But beware—the bar doesn't truly exist within our world's space.
Those who inadvertently wander in may find themselves trapped inside, forever lost. 

"What do you think of my recent urban legend?"
Bell asked Echo, repeating the urban tale she had told during her live stream. 

"This sounds eerily similar to the case we investigated recently..."
"Eh?! Really?" 
"Thanks to your investigation, that bar was dealt with—even though they merely used some relaxants in their alcohol." 

"Regardless, it's still an illegal operation."
Coco interjects coldly as he walks past the two, without another word. 

"True."
"By the way, Coco, how do you manage to distinguish the Pathos Particles of different people?"
Echo suddenly leaps up as if she remembered something.

"Through the eyes." 
"Argh—just tell me! You're so stingy, Coco!" 
"My, my, it's always lively in the detective agency, isn't it?"

The crisp winter wind sweeps through the streets, bringing with it a flurry of tiny snowflakes. Guided by the signs, we brave the wind and snow and finally arrive at the bustling marketplace.

"Who would have thought... it's so lively here!" The ice sculptures, each unique in design, glisten under the colorful lights. Snowflake decorations hang from high above the streets, mingling with the deep green spruce leaf wreaths. The place is teeming with tourists, almost everyone holding a comforting cup of warm mulled wine.

"S-so cold... Achoo!" Mia shivers as the scent of roses and cinnamon wafts on the breeze. If she continues like this, she might catch a cold.

"Excuse me, three cups of mulled wine, please."

"Sure, it'll be just a moment!" The young shopkeeper greets each customer with a sweet smile.

"The fruity taste is especially rich this year! If you like it, please do spread the word." She delicately stirs a cinnamon stick in the ruby red wine, infusing the spiced flavor into the heated drink.

"Promotion? No problem. Erina, looks like you've got a new job."

I wink and, sure enough, a shocked expression crosses the shopkeeper's face.

"Erina? The Erina?!"

"Hey!"

After a bout of commotion, we finally have the warmed special drink. The familiar scent is a delight to the senses. The wind and snow are still harsh, but we're now warm from head to toe.

"It smells so good! Anya, you seem to know a lot about these traditions. Did your hometown have similar customs?"

"Why does every conversation about this topic always go off on a tangent?"

"I always forget what I originally wanted to ask!"

Sigh... Always filled with curiosity, every moment of every day.

I come from a place known as "Sovachi", a place that many people think of alongside "the distant gods of the heavens".

Here, there are vast and mysterious fjords, crystal clear and shimmering glaciers. Endless midnight suns and polar nights seem dreamlike, blessed with a divine, magnificent radiance.

In this untouched and unspoiled natural sanctuary, I'm gifted with extraordinary sensitivity and keenness. Amid such generous offerings, every day is filled with absolute freedom and openness.

I dash, leap, and rest upon logs floating in still waters. I reach mountain summits with companions my age, gazing afar at the bustling harbors. And in the silence of tranquil nights, I distinguish the melody of insects calling to each other.

"Ah, it's snowing!"

"The divine's favor has arrived as expected this year too. Thank you for your protection..."

In my memories, I also held up snowflakes in both hands when I was young, offering them up to the heavens above.

Will the dignified deity, who rides in a splendid carriage and shows mercy to all creatures, bestow more affection upon me because of this? When will I feel the care and love of my parents again?

The harsh winters of Sovachi are considerably long. The snowflakes drifting down in the gloomy snow curtain are light and tender, yet they conceal the power to annihilate all things.

I once saw some tourists, infatuated with novelty, exhaust their efforts to chop wood and build huts. Just overnight, houses still reeking of fresh wood vanish in the snowstorm, leaving behind footprints of their frantic escape. None of them admires the divine's creation in that moment.

"Humans are truly peculiar creatures."

"But... when they light up the bonfire, their hearts must be filled with satisfaction, right?"

Tall, straight coniferous trees weave a web of radiant sunlight for me with every inch of their foliage. Dappled rays spill between the branches, casting a glow that makes the falling snow dazzle like golden leaves.

This small path is seldom trodden. I run unrestrained through the accumulated snow that's deep enough to bury the wild grass. The rustling leaves sing their melodies, and as I meander amongst them, I am enveloped in tranquility and peace. The icy crystals congealed on the silver-tipped fur tumble down like dust in the gentle breeze.

One urgent call after another wakes me from my hazy dreams.

"Anya! Anya!"

It's... my aunt, whom I haven't seen in a long time.

"Your parents... they asked me to take care of you. From now on, consider me as your mother, okay?"

She takes my hand, her eyes sparkling with unshed tears.

"Come with me. I promise to take good care of you, Anya."

"Where are my father and mother?"

"Are they still alive?"

All answers remain unknown.

I leave Sovachi for a completely unfamiliar place. There are grand halls and exquisite meals. But humans, Felinians, and those whose identities are unclear... the "entities" shrouded in mist, all wear masks of calculation.

This is an "examination" banquet, and I am there with my aunt. Recalling her worried gaze and numerous reminders, I know without a doubt that this battle will be fierce.

The gears of destiny have been designed at the dawn of creation. Whether the world in all its grandeur or the minuscule self is embedded within, everything is compelled to march forward, step by step.

I have no other choice.

"Anya? Anya? What's on your mind?"

"...Hmm?"

I'm roused from the shimmering fragments of my memory, only to find Erina's face incredibly close to mine. 

"Are you okay? You're not sick, are you?"
 
Her cheeks seem slightly redden in the wind mingling with snowflakes. I can't help but smile, feeling a warmth in my heart.

"Just thought of something at work. Heh, did I worry you, Erina?" 

"Not way! You're still thinking about work at this time?"

"Of course, what else would I rely on to support all of you? Being an idol manager isn't exactly an easy job, you know."
 
"That's true, the boss always has to think more than us... Mia! Look! It's flower crowns, your favorite!" 

I manage to easily fool her. There doesn't seem to be a hint of doubt. She's perfectly protected. For just a bit longer, I only wish to protect her from the fact that fate has been toying with us all along.

Perhaps, like the person behind Erina... A protector who asks for nothing in return could be considered a "god", right? 

"Er... Erina! Slow down... I... I can't keep up!"

"Come on! Run faster!" 

I take a sip of the freshly made hot wine. The fresh aromas of oranges and lemons mingle with the rich scent of aged wine. The delicate goblet with a golden rim holds a liquid that flows with the sweet hue of berries. 

Erina decisively buys three flower crowns made of spruce and laurel. Mia, who suddenly receives the gift, cupped her hands into a tiny megaphone, calling out my name. 

I walk towards them with a smile.
 
This kind of life is not too bad after all.

Anya harbors a not-so-secret secret. She holds great affection for the small "Freyja Productions".

Although often praised as extremely competent, the temporary success of Freyja and its prospective growth aren't solely attributed to Anya.

The burgeoning micro-agency, operating a singular line of business, has just found its footing in the vast expanse of Catto City.

She is the founder and mainstay of the agency, and also a renowned manager who's cultivating shining stars. The achievements Anya now boasts are the fruits of everyone's collective efforts.

Initially, this is merely a temporary refuge after departing from "Holy Felinus". Occasionally, it serves to hide her identity and plans. Yet, this guise gradually becomes an integral part of Anya's life.

"Good morning, Anya!"

"This is today's schedule, we have a partnership meeting in the morning, and a magazine photoshoot in the afternoon. Don't forget, Anya!"

"Good morning."

"I got it, I'll be there with Erina."

Here, there are no pristine natural lakes, or tranquil green mosses like a blanket. Nor are there perennially snow-clad mountains, their peaks undulating under the sun.

However, a soul who was once accustomed to solitude and wanton running amidst the northern forests, now harbors the intention to remain in this city that's forged of steel.

To carry on with this life, amidst laughter and throngs... But it's merely a thought.

Since it's an unattainable desire, let's preserve it just a little while longer.

"An-Anya, is this... acceptable?"

The same pose has been held for quite some time. I lift my gaze from my mild daydream, gazing at my reflection in the mirror. 

The tool in the girl's hand is like a paintbrush, tracing the contours of my brows, eyes, and lips. The elegantly curved silver-white curls are also a work of delicate artistry. 

"Thank you, Mia. It looks wonderful."

"As long as you're happy, Anya! I-I'll get going now...!" 

In the sunlight-filled office, I'm left alone. A gold-embossed invitation accompanies me, lying quietly in a corner of the desk. Its exquisite classical patterns, surrounding the handwritten standard font, gently cradle the recipient's name. 

"Dear Ms. Noreen..." The refinement of the nobility often permeates every stroke of their pen. Clearly, the host of the banquet perfectly embodies this characteristic. As the target, this challenge is not unworthy. 

Under the floor-to-ceiling window, the sunlight swallows half of my shadow. 

The silver white as snow. The dark purple as night. This dress is the work of a renowned designer. Its simple and smooth design is born for the wearer's elegance. The leather waistband shimmers with a lustrous glow. The irregular hem blooms like a lotus. The custom pearl necklace that reflects the color of the dress. The pointed stilettos that add feminine charm. 

Just being "displayed" in front of the clothes rack and dressing table is already enough to captivate the heart. 

If I were merely an invited guest, my preparation would be complete. 

But... "The chase is on," I murmur with anticipation.

"You're looking much better now."

"Ah, you are... Miss Noreen! A few days pass, and your charm grows even more radiant."

"You flatter me. How have you been feeling recently?"

"I feel great. I've hired a very good personal physician..."

The pleasantries between adults are always incredibly dull. After dispatching a few meaningless small talks, my attention refocuses on the main hall. The banquet is already halfway through, yet the host hasn't shown up.

This isn't something that a courteous noble would do in public. Is this cunning fox watching all the guests at the banquet from the shadows? Or... has something unexpected happened?

"Miss Noreen, it's a pleasure to meet you, I'm from Silver Star Corporation..."

"Nice to meet you, Mr. Craddock."

"Ah, Miss Noreen, you know me? I'm honored. May I have the pleasure of asking you for a dance?"

An alluring girl who runs a small startup on her own with no strong background or wealth creates an illusion of a "trophy" in the eyes of those with ulterior motives.

But that's fine.

Compared to aimlessly wandering around the banquet hall and drawing the host's attention, dancing gracefully in the center of the dance floor is a nearly invisible way to approach others.

"Of course, Mr. Craddock."

"To dance with a role model like you in the industry is an honor for a small startup founder like me."

Countless secrets are born under the watchful eyes of all. Today is no exception.

The twirling ball gown creates waves that shimmer like flowing light amidst the melodious strings. The nimble dance steps effortlessly reach the hidden corners under watchful gazes.

"I had a great time, Mr. Craddock. I hope we have the chance to collaborate in the future."

The host of the banquet won't be coming. 

The climax of the evening has arrived, but the target that can resist not showing up. He is either a highly experienced hunter or a prey that's already halfway trapped. Either way, my mission can't be accomplished.

So, it's time to leave.

"Click. Click. Click." The sound of stilettos hitting the tiled floor is rhythmic and captivating. But at this moment, I don't have the luxury to appreciate this composure.

I'm being followed.

A man in a suit, his tie knotted in a very crude way. His shoes bear inappropriate stains and his stride is somewhat awkward. This attire is obviously not his.

"Miss Anya Noreen..."

He brazenly approaches me.

"You should know who you've upset, right?"

The bathroom is surrounded by mirrors. The vanity is bathed in soft light. The stalker looks ordinary, but he keeps appearing by my side these days.

"I'm sorry, but I don't quite understand your intention." 

I remove my ring and pearl necklace and gently wash them with warm water running from my fingertips.

"If there's no necessary reason, it's quite rude to pick a fight at a banquet."

"I see. So, who wants me to suffer...?" It seems I'm surrounded by a sea of adversaries. Yet, only a handful dare to cause a ruckus at such a high-profile banquet.

Who is indulging this fool? The answer is becoming increasingly clear.

"There's no way a small company like Freyja could have offended a major client, right?"

"Or perhaps, am I the actual target?"

"You needn't concern yourself with that," the man retorts, instinctively. "It's not my place to reveal our client's secrets."

His demeanor quickly shifts to one of anxiety. "Don't think you can trick me into speaking! I won't reveal anything to you!"

"What the... Why has the air conditioning suddenly become so cold?" The sudden drop in temperature leaves him momentarily flustered. "You're not trying to cover up a crime scene in case I accidentally kill you, are you? Ha, ha!"

...Such a pity. Even when faced with the utmost danger, the prey remains oblivious to its impending end. Stubborn and foolish, a weapon completely controlled by others is no match for me. 

I let out a soft sigh.

As a seasoned businesswoman, those who betray her trust find themselves on Anya's blacklist, barred from further transactions.

As an experienced hunter, any adversaries who dare to provoke find themselves plummeting into the abyss, all under the guise of Anya's serene smile and an illusion of peace.

The last image in the ice mirror is the horrified expression of a man before he fell into unconsciousness. After its mission is completed, the shattered frost turns back to mist. Nothing is seen or heard, even the scattered alarm systems remain undisturbed.

"I gave you a chance... such a shame."

"Did you ever consider... that I would never step into the traps you set?"

Greed. Lust. The pursuit of fame and fortune.

The mysterious and dangerous black tulip. Everything is at her fingertips, and the city is her best means to conceal herself.

"There's a little problem in the washroom."
Anya, using the full-length mirror in the restroom, gently smooths out non-existent creases on her dress.

"Take him back first, then interrogate him thoroughly. What he did is related to the host of the banquet." On the other end of the communication line, someone quickly takes over this sudden operation.

"When will you, always hiding in the shadows, muster the courage to face me?"

"I can't help but look forward to it... Miss Dorothy."

The harsh frost always presents a gentle facade. The sharp dagger also lurks in the shadow.

Even when faced with the most formidable adversary, Anya Noreen will never be the first to back down.

"Oh divine muse of inspiration, please grace your devout follower with your favor—"

Every sketch, every blueprint, each and every design… none seem to reach perfection. Three entire days spent hunched over my desk, yet not a single satisfactory outcome to show for it.

Tossing my discarded drafts aside, I fervently yearn to start the next makeup design, to break this deadlock.
Yet, the crumpled ball of paper bounces a few times on the desk, acting as the proverbial straw that breaks the camel's back.
The towering pile of research materials on my desk finally succumbs to their own weight, collapsing in an instant.
Even the e-documents suspended in mid-air seem to flicker for a few seconds, as if shocked by the commotion.

The sight of books and magazines scattered across my desk and floor resembles the lone brick on a street laid in the wrong direction.
The feeling of failure from the unproductive days, the sense of helplessness from the disorderly environment... all churn together, throwing my emotions into utter chaos.

Ugh, I feel like I can't hold on any longer...

The familiar mist of tears fills my vision, uncontainable droplets race to roll down first, etching sorrowful rivers on my sketches.

But... but... 
The Winter Festival is approaching… and Erina is set to release her new single.

I want, I want to let Erina make her appearance in the most stunning form…!

Oh, tears of weakness will never lead to anything!

"Mia, oh Mia, you cannot afford to stop here!"

In the beginning, it was just curiosity.
Ever since I can remember, I’ve had a unique gift—the ability to understand the past of antiques by touch, to trace their once-lived memories. Though not all antiques reveal their secrets, I believe every object holds significance.

With this sense of duty, I’ve always been committed to my gift. Whether studying at the secluded Yishi Resort or returning home for the rare holiday, I would seize every opportunity to sneak out for adventures.

“Sister, are you going out again?”
Who could that adorable voice belong to? Of course, it’s my dearest little sister, who knows me best!

“Don’t worry, I’ll just be out for a little while and will be back soon.”
“But… you said the same thing yesterday.”
“Dear, the New Glow Festival is just around the corner, and the streets will be filled with novel and fascinating things from all over. How can I not go and see?”
“Then promise me you’ll be back before the hour of You.”
“Sure! No problem! I knew you were the best, sweetie!”
I hugged a serious-faced Yun Pei excitedly, readily agreeing to her request. Although Yun Pei often chides me in her cool tone, she’s genuinely worried about me.

“Ah! Don’t call me that! And don’t rub my face!”
Yun Pei’s cheeks turned a slight red from my teasing, her earlier grown-up demeanor completely gone.
“Don’t worry, I’ll definitely be back on time!”

The New Glow Festival was, as always, extraordinarily lively. As I wandered through the streets, marveling at the array of antiques and curios, my heart brimmed with joy. Though Lunar City was renowned for its antique trade, it truly came alive during the New Glow Festival.

I strolled from one end of the street to the other, picking up several intriguing trinkets, though nothing particularly special caught my eye. That is, until I stumbled upon the compass now in my hand. The seller seemed eager to offload it, allowing me to snag it at a bargain.

"How does this compass work?" Yunpei and I had learned about compasses at Yishi Resort, but I'd never had the chance to use one. Let's see what's so magical about this one!

The compass needle, like a fish's tail, wavered uncertainly. Following its guidance, I arrived at a forest in the mountains, a place where I used to catch crickets as a child. Though I was familiar with the terrain, the scenery began to feel strangely unfamiliar. That's when I stumbled upon an old, dilapidated tower. The ruins revealed an architectural style starkly different from that of present-day Lunar City. "This tower is fascinating! How have I never noticed it before?"

Just as I was about to explore it, I noticed my elongated shadow at my feet. The sun was about to set, and I had a promise to keep with Pei Pei.

However, my attempt to sneak back home by climbing over the wall was unfortunately discovered by my mother, who was hanging up lanterns. It seemed I was in for another long lecture. I'd heard these words so many times before that they barely registered anymore. Sensing my stubbornness, my mother changed her strategy and decided to teach me a lesson through actions instead. To my dismay, she sentenced me to a day of 'solitary reflection.'

At the time, this punishment seemed terrifying. Spending an entire day in a room with nothing to do felt like the worst fate imaginable. "Darn it, I had plans to revisit that place today!"

Soon, I heard a noise outside the door.
"Sister, are you alright?"
"Ah! Yun Pei, I'm here! It's so boring in here. Why don't you open the door and let your sister out to play with you?"
"No, mother said you have to stay in there all day today and can only come out when the New Glow Festival starts tomorrow."
"Ah, another family gathering tomorrow night... How boring..."
"Although you can't come out, I can stay here with you..."

Thanks to Yun Pei, I endured the long wait and finally got to leave the room. But my mind was still on regaining my freedom. During every gathering, the adults were too busy entertaining each other to pay much attention to Yun Pei and me. As the older sister, I couldn't enjoy my freedom alone; I had to rescue my sister too!
"Yun Pei, Yun Pei, come with me!"
"Okay, where are we going, sister?"
Yun Pei wasn't the least bit panicked, letting me hold her hand as we ran towards freedom.

With the compass guiding us, we quickly reached the destination I'd been yearning to explore for days—the dilapidated ancient tower deep in the forest. Under the night sky, the old tower was shrouded in a layer of mystery.

"It's pitch-dark here. Do we really need to go inside?" Yunpei asked, her voice trembling.

"Don't worry, I have the guiding lantern! And with me here, everything will be fine!" I reassured her.

Though Yunpei showed a hint of fear, she chose to trust me, gripping my hand tightly. At that moment, I naively believed I could conquer anything. As long as Yunpei was by my side, I felt like the most incredible sister in the world.

But things didn't go as planned. As we ventured deeper, the tower's eerie nature became apparent. Every room seemed to move, making it impossible to retrace our steps. By the time we realized it, Yunpei and I were completely lost.

Even stranger was the faint blue light emanating from the depths of the tower. As this light appeared, the air grew colder. Dressed inadequately for the chill, our situation became even more dire.

"It's been several hours already... Sister, are we... not going to make it out?" Yunpei's voice wavered with fatigue.

"We will, I'll find a way out very soon!" I tried to sound confident, but panic was setting in. Yunpei was losing strength, and I couldn't bring myself to admit the dire reality.

Then, as if to force me to face the truth, Yunpei collapsed in front of me. In that moment, I felt an unprecedented wave of panic, helplessness, and anger.

My curiosity had led us into this perilous situation. The arrogance of my naivety had put us in danger.

No, I can't give up now! For Yunpei, I mustn't give up!
