As she grew older, Yuncan followed the legends of the holy relics and arrived at Leids Town to continue her endless exploration.

Thanks to Yuncan's superb restoration skills, she gradually made a name for herself in Leids Town. In the process of helping the townsfolk restore items, Yuncan also witnessed various precious memories forgotten within the repaired objects.

"Thank you, Yuncan, I now understand why my master entrusted this weapon to me. I won't let him down."

"Thank you, Miss Yuncan... for letting me know why my mother loved this book so much, thank you..."

"Thank you! Miss Yuncan! I didn't know my sister's dress holds such beautiful memories... I will treasure it."

"..."

And today, the smile on An-an's face after seeing the portraits of those good-hearted men and women.

"This brush, though a weapon, can also save others in crucial moments."

Yuncan gently caressed the brush in her hand. "I will use it to protect everyone's inner peace."

As winter gives way to spring, we're celebrating another New Year. 

Could it be my imagination? The festive atmosphere this year feels particularly intense.

I wander through the bustling city streets, beneath neon lights suspended high above, tirelessly changing their hues. A multitude of people brushes past me, laughing and hurrying towards brighter destinations.

"Come have a look!"

"Handmade sugar figurines in traditional style! Freshly made!"

Sugar figurines, huh...

It's been a long time since I've seen these in the streets even before I left Yaozhou. I hesitate for a moment at the sight.

"Would you like a sugar figurine? If you don't like the design we have, we also make cats, dogs, birds, and bunnies!" The shopkeeper is a young girl, with a fluffy white pom-pom affixed to her hair with a bow clip. "Why are you wandering around alone on such a festive day?"

"There were too many people. I lost my sister."

She beams brightly, an authentic sense of happiness shining in her eyes. "I see, you should hurry and reunite with your sister then, but you have to wait a bit for the sugar figurine!"

"A custom-made cat figurine needs meticulous crafting, after all!"

"Alright, I'm in no rush." For some reason, this shopkeeper reminds me of my older sister, even though she appears to be younger than me. Age is indeed a peculiar thing.

Golden malt sugar melts under high heat, transforming into soft syrup. The rich sweetness permeates the air and tickles my nostrils.

Just then—

A blurry figure dashes through the alley, causing the reflected light on a metal storefront to momentarily lose its brilliance as it is blocked by the figure's shadow.

"Hmm?"

The shadowy figure dashes recklessly, uncaring of potential exposure. It barrels through any obstruction in its path, swiftly disappearing into a nearby alleyway.

These streets, I've trodden countless times since my youth. I know that it's a cul-de-sac, a dead end with no escape.

With nowhere left to run, there's no need for relentless pursuit. I quietly lift the fallen lantern light screen, and leave the intermittent hawking of street vendors behind me. The bustling holiday trade keeps the shopkeepers preoccupied, oblivious to these events.

There's nothing but silence and coldness. The atmosphere is starkly different in this alleyway compared to the lively street just beyond the wall. Firework debris, ignored like drifting ash, accumulates here.

"Roar!!!"

An intimidating roar echoes from the Nian hidden in the dark alleyway's shadows. Its form shrinks smaller and smaller, almost merging with the corner.

"Could it really be a Nian..." Not an Anomaly, but a Nian that hasn't appeared in emergency reports for a long time.

"Do you realize the consequences of intruding the bustling city during the New Year celebration?"

"Stay back!" The Nian's voice is youthful, and it seems that its previous roar had exhausted all its courage.

"I-I just wanted to have a look... It's been so long since I've celebrated..."

Despite being a beast that could cause catastrophic disorder, it gives off an impression of being threatening on the surface yet frail inside. Is it... frightened?

"Do Nians... also want to celebrate the festival?" I ask.

"Of course! The streets over there are so lively... with so many delicious foods, and sugar figurines..."

"I love the festivities!"

"Can you bring me a sugar figurine? I swear I won't cause any trouble..."

Perhaps realizing I have no intention to attack, the Nian cautiously peeks its head out from the shadows.

I can't detect any malicious Pathos Particles. Moreover, I spotted the Nian almost as soon as it reveals itself.

I can't possibly resist those pleading eyes.

"Hi, is my cat-shaped figurine ready?"

"Yes, it is! I looked up and you were gone. I was just looking for you. Here, take it."

"Thank you. But... I'd like another one, custom-made."

"Haha, a figurine in the shape of Nian? This is the first time I have such an unusual request!" The young shop owner is evidently taken aback by my demand.
 
"Alright, the customer is always right! Let me think, what does a Nian look like?"

"Hmm... I think it has horns..."

The light veil on the silk umbrella sways gently in the breeze. I return to the alley with two custom sugar figurines. The timid Nian, true to its word, crouches obediently in the same spot.

"Here you go. Is this the type of sugar figurine you wanted?"

"It smells so good! This is it!!"

The aroma of malt permeates the surrounding air. The eager young creature pounces towards me. Its charge is fierce, but its target is clearly not me. Without dodging, I let it clumsily seize the Nian-shaped sugar figurine.

"Mmm, mm! It's so sweet! Thank you, miss!"

"You're welcome. But you might actually be older than me."

The long-brewing snowflakes begin to scatter from the sky in a delicate dance. The Nian and I, who shouldn't be here, unexpectedly usher in the first auspicious snowfall of the New Year together.

"Miss, what are you thinking?" The Nian, seeming to notice my distraction as it delightfully devours the sugar figurine, gently probes.

"Do you hate the snowfall as well?"

"No, it's just... I was reminded of the past." I reply after a moment of contemplation.

"You dislike the snow? Why?"

"There was a human girl who was kind to me in the past. She bought me sugar figurines, and played handkerchief games with me."

"But as I grew larger, her haystack couldn't conceal me any longer. Before I was discovered, I had to sneak away..."

"It was snowing heavily on that day," the Nian responds with utmost sincerity.

Floaty snowflakes land on the umbrella, only to be whisked away by the frigid wind, gently dissipating into the air. The lively sounds from the lantern-lit streets are ceaseless, but in this alleyway, we only have each other's voices.

"I like the bustle. I discovered that the New Year is one of the most vibrant festivals. But humans hate seeing me." 

"They always toss firecrackers at me, plaster odd papers at places I've been to keep me away."

"The New Year Festival always comes with snowfall. Gradually, I too grew to dislike the snow..."

As the golden sunlight begins to dip in the west, the content Nian decides it's time to leave the alleyway. The sky, blanketed with the remnants of snowfall, is perfect for hiding its form.

"...You should avoid those places," I suggest.

"Sure! If humans are scared of me, I won't go," the Nian's moment of melancholy vanishes instantly, and it begins to frolic cheerfully before me again.

"It's nice knowing you! I hope to meet you again at the next New Year Festival!"

As the snowfall ceases, Yunpei finally rendezvouses with Yuncan at the end of the market. Having returned from a treasure hunt, Yuncan, after a bout of bragging, is curious about what Yunpei did as well.

"I've talked so much... Did anything exciting happen to you?" she asks.

"There is, but I'm not sure you would believe me if I told you."

The more Yunpei withholds, the higher she ratchets up Yuncan's curiosity. Bypassing the crowd, Yuncan darts in front of Yunpei, spreads out her arms, and blocks her path.

"You're not going anywhere! Now tell me, tell me! Oh dear Peipei!"

"...Don't call me that, sis."

After leaving Yaozhou, it's rare to have such carefree and playful moments. The setting sun bathes the newly accumulated paper-thin snow with a shimmering glow.

"I just met a Nian that wanted to eat a sugar figurine. I had the shop owner make one in its image," Yunpei begins.

"It seemed quite content after eating and then told me that Yaozhou would have a wonderful start this year."

A gentle breeze blows, carrying small specks of dust wrapped in fine snow, which starts to flutter down again. Yunpei opens her silk umbrella, covering Yuncan under its shelter.

"Even being part of a custom, it was deeply moved by the precious kindness," Yunpei continues.

"So... it wished us prosperity, peace, and good health."

However, Yuncan remains skeptical.

"Such a cultured... Nian? Why haven't I seen one before?"

"Hold on, this isn't what it said, is it? You're making this up!"

"I think you're just fooling me with your nonsense! Hey! Wait a minute, Peipei! Don't leave!"

The sky was high and the clouds were light, with the shadows of the trees mottled and shifting. Occasionally, a breeze would flutter through the pages of the book on the table, yet it never seemed to turn the page. This was the scene I often saw when I returned home and had leisure time.

It was during the celebration of New Glow Festival, and everyone in my family was busy preparing for the festivities. Being just a child, I naturally did not have to involve myself in these tasks. My family, worried about the hustle and bustle in the town during this time, cautioned us not to go out casually. So, I sat under a tree in the courtyard with a book, quietly passing the time.

However, this tranquility was soon easily broken. Yuncan tiptoed through the courtyard, heading straight to the west. I knew what she wanted to do, as usual, and followed her.

As expected, she wanted to climb over the wall again. "Hey, are you going out again?" I asked.

My sister, who was highly focused on climbing the wall, was startled by my voice and froze instantly. However, she quickly realized it was me who called her and visibly relaxed, giving a sly smile. As always, I couldn't resist her stubbornness and just went along with her.

Watching my sister's silhouette as she climbed over the wall, the book in my hand seemed to lose its allure. I don't know when it started, but I always found myself standing there, staring at my sister's retreating figure from a distance...
Strange, why does my heart feel so empty?

Yuncan and I, as sisters, grew up together, yet our personalities are starkly different. My sister is lively and active, while I prefer calmness, even to the point of seeming dull. Because of this, even though my sister is a year older than me, our parents always asked me to look after her. In their eyes, my quietness seemed to signify maturity, while my sister was seen as a child needing supervision.

But I know it's not like that. To me, my sister is a very special existence.

Yuncan, with her free-spirited nature, could never stay put at home. However, she often accommodated me, taking care of me in her own way. Occasionally, I would join her on her outings, but most of the time, I would deliberately distract our parents to cover for her sneaking out. She always promised to return at a set time. This way, I could enjoy my quiet moments and also relish the exciting experiences she shared with me.

Interesting stories, novel toys, delicious snacks, intricate gadgets...
Little by little...
The things my sister brought to me kept increasing.

At first, I didn't pay much attention. Until one day, our father came to me and noticed an inkstone on my desk, asking where I got it from. Worried he might blame my sister, I hesitated to answer and asked why he was interested in it. He told me that the seemingly ordinary inkstone was actually a centuries-old Dragon Tail Inkstone, quite valuable. But my sister was still young, mostly spending her pocket money on snacks, so how could she afford such an expensive antique?

"Of course, by finding bargains! I'm not afraid to tell father the truth, everything I buy is very cheap!" My sister said confidently. With her permission, I told our father about the gifts.

To verify this, our father tested my sister. To everyone's surprise, she could indeed identify genuine and fake items without any tools. The news spread, astonishing our clan members. No one had ever thought that the mischievous Yuncan possessed such an extraordinary talent. Not only that, her abilities grew stronger. Besides distinguishing authenticity, she could also see vague memories related to antiques by touching them.

Perhaps... it's her pure heart that allows her to see more than the average person...
Being always by Yuncan's side, I couldn't help but think so.

As night deepened, the long streets bustled with activity. Tonight, New Glow Festival was culminating in its grandest closing performance. At such times, our family would always gather at the most famous restaurant in town – Lan Yue Lou – for a feast.

However, this time was different. While everyone was still reveling in the festivities, my sister whisked me away from the banquet. "Sister, where are we going now?" I asked. "Hehe... You'll know when we get there," she replied, barely concealing her excitement. I knew she must have seen something special and wanted to share it with me...

What I never expected was that this time, my sister was fascinated by an ancient tower. Even more surprising was that we ended up trapped inside it. It was an abandoned ancient tower, forgotten by time, ingeniously designed with countless traps and mechanisms. The constantly shifting rooms seemed determined to entrap the intruders who dared to enter. By the time we realized this, we had already become 'fish in the net'.

In the darkness so thick it seemed to absorb the light, only the glow from the lamp in my sister's hand offered a flicker of hope. Her rare calmness reassured me, yet also made me aware of the gravity of our situation. As time passed, an undeniable fatigue began to grip me. Watching the silhouette pulling my hand ahead, I tried to keep up with her pace. However, my eyelids grew heavier, and my vision was gradually consumed by the darkness. The next second, I fell into my sister's arms.

If only... I had exercised more regularly...

"Pei Pei... Pei Pei..." In my drowsy state, I heard my sister's call. I had never heard such a tone from her, and I couldn't even imagine what her expression might be like. The sister I knew always had a bright, sunny smile.

What did she look like now? I struggled to open my eyes, only to see her trying hard not to cry. "I'm just a bit tired, sister, don't worry," I said, trying to comfort her, even though I knew such words wouldn't change anything. But to me, my sister's smile was what mattered the most.

I don't remember how I, in my unconscious state, left the old tower.
All I know is that because we didn't return all night, our entire family was searching for us throughout the city.
My mother told me that it was only after my sister carried me, unconscious, out of the forest that we were found and brought back home.
My father was furious and made my sister stay in her room for ten days as punishment.

When I saw my sister again, she had returned to her usual self.
No matter what I asked her, she just smiled and brushed off my questions.
"Alright, alright! It's all in the past, I don't want to recall anything about that dreadful place~"
"But..."

"Right, right, I have something to show you! I found it in that old tower."
As if to divert my attention, she pulled a ring out of her pocket.
"Look... like this, the ring can be split into two!"
She handed one of the rings to me.
"I studied this thing for a long time but couldn't find anything special about it, so let's just keep it as a memento..."

"Hmm... but, sister, your hand... it's injured..."
"Ah, this... I cut it by accident when moving a mechanism! It's healed now, see~"
Her radiant smile now seemed to me a form of endurance.
The wounds on my sister's body silently told of the perils of that night.

In that moment, I seemed to understand—what that empty feeling lingering in my heart was.
Why do I always see my sister's back?
No matter what happens, she always steps in front of me first.
In my eyes, she is always carefree, so reliable... and so I took it for granted and forgot that she too can get hurt.
All along, it was my sister who was protecting me.

"Yunpei... what's, what's wrong? Why are you crying?"
Tears flooded over me, overwhelming my reason.

I was always the one being protected.
What should I do?
How can I protect her?
Back then, I never had an answer...

But now, I think, I can do it.

Unlike her lively and mischievous older sister, Yunpei has always been the sensible and good child in the eyes of her family. Calm and restrained, she loves to learn and possesses a memory superior to the average person, learning to read and write at the age of 3. After starting school, Yunpei consistently maintained her position as the top student, praised by teachers as an outstanding student. She became the pride of her family, admired by all as a "genius". However, her sister Yuncan was the most troublesome child in the entire family.

The sisters' parents, not ones to play favorites, were thus particularly worried about their naughty child. Fortunately, Yuncan's talent for identifying antiques emerged, giving her parents new hope.

They had hesitated to send Yunpei to the prestigious Yishi Resort, fearing it would distance the older daughter from her younger sister. As one of the top institutions in Lunar City and even in Yaozhou Disctrict, Yishi Resort only admits the most exceptional students. Now, with two rare talents in the Yun family, it was the perfect opportunity to send them to Yishi Resort.

After rigorous trials, the sisters successfully passed the selection and entered Yishi Resort for their studies. Yunpei even broke the record for the youngest admittee. The self-disciplined Yunpei remained diligent and hardworking, standing out among the many geniuses. Her serene and resolute demeanor made others keep their distance.

Like an unattainable flower on a high peak, the cold and frosty Yunpei always had a girl by her side who resembled her in appearance but was warm and passionate. The two were always inseparable, like twin lotuses blossoming together yet so different in style, akin to a pair of contrasting ice and fire lotuses.

Upon my first arrival at the affiliated research institute of the Science Research Division in Catto City, I am met with cold stares. This is to be expected. Few people would greet a new leader who shows up out of nowhere with warmth.

Young and reserved, seemingly absorbed in my own world and hard to get along with... the whispers of gossip always find a way into my ears. But such idle chatter isn't enough to break my concentration.

Rusty bronzeware needs to be cleaned with precisely mixed chemical reagents. Pages of books, riddled with holes, require careful disinfection and tweezing for restoration. One after another, severely damaged artifacts are restored. The way my colleagues look at me seems to change.

"Professor Yunpei, these fabrics have completely degraded... If we insist on restoring them, they'll crumble at the slightest touch!"

"This is the latest exhibition schedule for the Catto City Museum. The curator specifically sent a letter inviting you to take a look."

"Dr. Yunpei, a tomb has been discovered in Yaozhou. The excavation work is being planned, and they hope you can participate..."

Every day in the lab, I'm surrounded by such voices. I'm accustomed to scheduling my own tasks, pushing me to complete each one. There must be without errors. This is my trust in myself.

Gradually, people begin to tell me that my presence has become a calming influence in the lab. 
"Sob, Professor Yunpei..."

"Don't worry, let me take a look."

Some people overtly and covertly advise me not to let others become habitually dependent on me. But to me, it seems only right to guide others like my big sister who cares for me within my capabilities.

"Steady hands, stay calm. Even when picking up a single silk thread, your tweezers must not tremble."

"Silks and satins are delicate. Be careful to hold your breath when working up close."

"This is the technique. Seek out opportunities to practice. It's more effective than simply reading books."

"I... I've learned a lot! Thank you, Professor Yunpei! Um, there's someone over by the ceramics who has a question for you..."

"Alright, I'll head right over."

Everyone has problems that are difficult to overcome no matter how much they ponder over them. If it's up to me... this is how I'd solve them.

"Professor Yunpei, you're amazing! Hehe, we thought you didn't like talking before."

"Everyone has their own story, and mine is nothing special... So, I don't really enjoy talking about myself."

"If you don't say anything, it'll only create more distance! People who are too mysterious don't seem to have many friends..."

"...What do you want to hear? As long as it doesn't involve personal matters, we can chat."

"I heard that you have a twin sister?"

"And also, they say that you can learn anything just by looking at it once! Is all of this true?"

"...I do have a sister, but we are not twins. She's a year older than me and is not currently in Catto City."

"As for the ability to master knowledge just by looking at it once, that's just a rumor."

The past that's been labeled as "glorious" no longer needs to be mentioned since it's already in the past.

But for those explorers brimming with curiosity and the desire for knowledge, my name might represent a different kind of life.

Perhaps, it's not entirely a bad thing.

I was born into an antique-dealing family in Yaozhou. My parents had been immersed in the trade for years. This environment, filled with treasures, benefited my sister, Yuncan, and myself. We were raised amidst a pile of precious artifacts, forming a solid theoretical foundation through constant exposure.

Our eyes are trained by priceless treasures. It takes us less than half a minute to identify the so-called "handicrafts" that are deliberately aged. 

"It's a fake."

"Didn't fool you this time either, huh? Ha, where did it go wrong this time?"

"The glaze is dull, the firing temperature wasn't well controlled, it doesn't meet the standard of official kiln productions."

"And the inscription at the bottom. According to 'Records of Ancient Artifacts', all official kiln ceramics produced during this period should have a certain degree of avoidance behavior in their inscriptions..."

"My heavens... Ma'am, she remembered it after just one look!"

"Yunpei, good girl. Come, shall mother teach you mounting today?"

I grew up amidst my parents' praises and the envy of others. While children my age were running and playing in the streets, I chose a different life. But this doesn't bore me in the slightest.

Within the cracks of antiques, lies history that has been silent for a long time. And within the fragments of history, are buried secrets that no one speaks of.

My sister and I seem to have a natural gift for sensing the past of these antiques, for conversing with the long-silent time and space. The antiques neatly arranged on the shelves are my sun and stars.

Few know that within my private collection, there is a metal plaque engraved with mysterious symbols. Our encounter is nothing more than a stroke of fate, and my curiosity is piqued by the enigmatic markings.

If it's an image, the artistic style it presents is unlike any known style. If it's a script, its structure diverges greatly from all known principles of character formation. However, with my work in the research institute piling up, this plaque has to be temporarily put aside.

Yet, every time my gaze encompasses the plaque, a wave of doubt surges within me. Unless something unexpected has occurred, this should be a relic of some civilization. But in this day and age, could there still be a civilization that is completely unverifiable?

...Until one night of the full moon, the plaque suddenly lights up. Dots of deep blue starlight extend and connect, gradually filling in the intricately engraved lines.

The brightness is sufficient to illuminate the dark room as if it were daylight, naturally possessing the power to shock and awe. I notice the anomaly, and as I turn around, I am confronted face-to-face with this unprecedented spectacle.

"What is this..."

I record the date and duration of the anomaly, attempting to discern a pattern. I make multiple rubbings of the strange morphing text, delving deep into ancient texts and documents in search of answers. I compile my observations into volumes, asking my sister Yuncan, who lives far away in Leidsdam, to keep an eye out for clues.

This is no ordinary ornamental plaque.

The secrets it harbors could compel the most passionate scientists to devote their entire lives to it.

And that includes me.

All efforts, withstanding the test of time, often seem futile. But Yunpei never backs down easily. These fruitless attempts only serve to kindle her spirit of exploration.

Mastering a brand-new field of knowledge isn't an overnight achievement. However, by putting forth multiple hypotheses and utilizing all available resources to rule out incorrect answers, the accuracy of the final result significantly improves.

So, let's give it a try.

The brisk autumn breeze sweeps across the land, immersing everything in an almost solemn tranquility. The sky is clear and transparent, stretching out like a vast expanse of azure blue.

The clamor of the world fails to disturb Yunpei's tranquility. Only the white bird, darting across the sky like an arrow, can cause ripples to spread across the calm waters.

The small space and time in front of her can't confine Yunpei's vision of exploration. Looking down from the heavens, it's such a vast perspective. It accommodates the memories, insights, and aspirations of both the Felinians and humans. It accommodates the long river of history spanning millions of years.

There will always be those willing to bend down and scoop up the shimmering water, carefully collecting the floating fragments or strands within. Those scenes from the past are reconstructed and reborn at her fingertips.

The frosty sky remains silent, neatly hiding the battered history. It cleanses, repairs, and nurtures a new vitality. Waiting for the spring to break the ground and see the light of day once more.

Setting out from the northern part of Catto City, passing through the snow-covered mountains and the inaccessible Betula, we finally see the rain-soaked Steam Tri-islands. It's an old nation, once a lighthouse at sea, now loses all traces of civilization.

It's different from the ruins described in newspapers and on the Internet, and it has nothing to do with the place closest to the stars as mentioned by a certain man. 

Here, the warm currents surge, vegetation grows wildly. According to the military doctor's analysis, it can be considered a breeding ground for viruses and Anomalies.

"Major, this is the place," the navigator continues, "A small-scale military base from the opposite mainland... Pathos particles are active!"

"Have they not detected our fighter jets?"

"There's no feedback at the moment, so they probably haven't."

"Probably?"

"...My apologies!"

"I'll go ahead with the recon team. The rest stays in the international airspace and wait for instructions."

"Please allow me to accompany you." The military doctor is always cautious, "We can't currently detect the ground units' specific situation. If they..."

If they have other plans and have set up an ambush for me...

"No worries. There is no one, or Felinian, who can touch me yet."

I'm met with silence.

"Major Olga!" A voice comes over the comms channel.

"May you have a smooth journey. I will pray to the prophets and gods for your safety!"

As an extremely inclusive city of peace, Catto City allows various views and beliefs to coexist, and the military never requires others to change their faith. Although...

"Okay, thank you and your gods."

I don't believe in gods, but I don't agree that science is the ultimate answer to everything.

My mother once spun me a tale of science fiction: A scientist replaced a dying human's heart with that of an animal, thereby creating a new creature, a fusion of both consciousnesses. Of course, it did not reproduce, but rather, met its end as a monster, dissected and reconstructed.

Back then, I was unsure of what she was trying to convey to me through this story.

—The origins of the Felinians, perhaps?

No, the Felinians aren't a creation of mankind.

—The Pathos Particles turned it into a monster?

No, the Pathos Particles played no part in this tale.

—Reckless experimentation may backlash upon the scientist themselves?

No, my mother always supported the continuous innovation of technology.

So, what could it be?

She never had the chance to provide me with the answer, and neither did my father.
They left for the three western islands when I was thirteen, aiding in a war caused by an Anomaly outbreak. 

I learned of their fate from their names listed in the obituaries, and then my mentor came to me. Her sandy blonde hair was still stained with blood, and her green eyes, usually ignited only in battle and accustomed to life and death, were burning with an unquenchable sense of remorse.

"Master," I interrupted her rare hesitation, a sudden realization dawning on me, almost whispering, "I know the answer."

"...Answer?"

In front of me, I see a young boy driven to Affliction by hunger and eats his friend's corpse, an Afflicted wife who wants to die with her normal husband, and an Afflicted old man who bitterly traps his whole family in a dangerous building.

And I, leading the recon team, eliminated them one by one.

"Science hasn't found a way to transform beasts into humans, so," the childish voice from that time still rings in my ear, "I must exterminate all the Anomalies."

I know this is far from what my mother intended, but it is the answer I ultimately found.

At the age of nineteen, I officially enlisted in the military. It was not a surprise, really. After all, I had been tirelessly training, striving to become a warrior capable of defending my family's honor.

On the day, I swear allegiance to the statue of General Snow, a fine drizzle falls on the North District, dampening my tail and eyelashes.

Victor finds it all rather dull.

"At three, one can see what a child will be like in old age. You really turned out just as expected, didn't you?"

"The same could be said for you."

And to think, this guy is my superior.

My mentor, however, has no objections. "I should probably say something to dissuade you, but if this fuels your resolve to grow stronger, then I suppose it's not a bad thing."

"Thank you for understanding." In fact, seeing her like this only reaffirms my path.

Only Zhenxin expresses profound regret.

"But Olga, I thought you want to become a model... what about that dream?"

"I'll continue."

"Continue?"

"I can do it, don't worry."

Exactly. Don't worry. For me, it's never an either-or situation.

The ensuing five years on the battlefield pass quicker than I imagined. Catto City is always ready to respond to external pleas for aid against the Anomalies. My life is a simple cycle of training, traveling, battling, returning, modeling, training, traveling, battling...

Eliminate the Anomalies, then become myself; eliminate the Anomalies, become myself; eliminate myself... eliminate who?

"Is the mission on Tri-islands?" The slender, grey-haired youth approaches me. Truthfully, we haven't spoken much since our adolescence.

He doesn't fuss over the details, much like me, and simply continues, "I need your help."

As I look at the box in his hands, I suddenly realize the nature of the assignment.

The journey is uneventful.

Despite the strange occurrences on the island, the observatory is just as he described it. As agreed, I return the urn containing his sister's ashes to the home they can no longer visit in person.

"(Whimpers)..."

...What is that?

"(Whimpers)..."
