"I'm Stacey, a reservist. Why hasn't my squad application been approved yet?"
"Miss Stacey, your application is currently being processed. Please wait for further notice."
"It's always the same response. Are you a parrot? It seems like you're always free, so why does the process take so long—" 
Oh no, I accidentally said what I was thinking!

The human staff member with short hair stood up immediately, but was held back by the Catkin staff assisting me.
"I apologize, Miss Stacey. The procedure is automatically processed, and we can't interfere manually."
She seemed like a very kind big sister, had I misunderstood her before?
...But I'm not planning on apologizing!
"However, due to the incident involving your previous squad, I'm afraid the approval might be difficult."
I take back my momentary good impression!
"...I'll be back later, until I get a fair response!"
"What, she's coming back again?"

As I turned to leave the office, the murmurs were hard to ignore.
"Who does she think she is, just some brat from a traitor's family, acting all high and mighty..."
Hey, don't think I can't hear you talking behind my back!

Of course, turning around and arguing with them is another story, which ended with security escorting me out of the office.

"Beep beep beep!"
The notification sound from my phone jolted me awake.
Darn it! If it had rung just a bit later, I could have dreamt about walking with President Eleanor!
During the time I was isolated by my classmates due to my background, if it weren't for the President's care, I probably wouldn't have made it to graduation and joined StormEye...

But a message this early in the morning... could it be that my application for the new squad was approved?
When I checked my phone, it was indeed an order, but not for the special investigation team I'd been hoping for. Instead...
I've been reassigned as an Inspector?!
This is clearly a setup! I was once a team leader, and now not only have I been demoted to a regular Combatant, but I'm also being sent to a fringe area like the islands!
What about Aiko! Why is that guy still in the reserves!
This is so unfair! I'm going to complain, I need to go to the administrative office and complain!

"Obey... orders."
When I left the StormEye, those people seemed to breathe a sigh of relief as if they had driven away a plague.
Only Howell patted my shoulder.
"Stacey, I know you're capable and I understand you must be feeling resentful right now."
"But some prejudices aren't something I can change alone."
"It might be a bit chaotic there, but it's a place where you can grow, and you'll learn a lot with Chizuru for a while."
"Once things cool down, we'll find a way to get you back."

Really? I couldn't help but wonder.
...No, this has to be true.
I'm going to make them all see that when it comes to effort, I, Stacey, will definitely not lose!
— It's just a remote island, just watch!

No way! Is this Felinian woman who just walked out of a casino in a sailor outfit — really Trixie, the Inspector?
"Stacey... are you the new fighter?" 
"Pretty impressive resume, how did you end up...?"
"Uh, my knowledge of Felinian history is pretty poor, so I don't know much about family stuff... But anyway!"
"The island isn't as bad as you think, and Howell has already said hello to me."
"Perform well, and I'll take you to some fun places." She said, pointing to where she had just come from.
I know my expression must look forced, but after all, she is my direct superior.
Hold on, Stacey, hold on, this is all a trial from above!

Two months have passed much quicker than I expected.
"Castaway Island Squad member Stacey will be reassigned next week as Deputy to Chief Inspector Howell... initiated by Eleanor."
Trixie looked up from the document.
"It's a shame, I really liked partnering with you. Your fierce expression is especially useful in intimidating others... and now you're going back so soon."
How could she see me like that in her mind! I'm a mature fighter, not a fierce person!
"Ha... just kidding." The superior I briefly worked with smiled, "Congratulations, you can return to Catto City now!"
...
After a long silence, I nodded at her too.
"Although, Inspector, you always tease me, and your methods are always so risky, and you talk in such strange ways..."
"...Eh? Shouldn't the sentence below this be praising or thanking me? That was way overboard with the criticism!"
"..." My expression was still forced as I muttered, "Nope, that was it!"

But... why is there also a secret order sent only to me?
In addition to being a deputy— I'm also tasked with supervising Howell?
Could it be... the chairman wants me to learn from him through supervision?
...
Then perhaps... the next chief Inspector could be...
...
Could I really have a chance to redeem my family's honor?!

"Tsk, so stingy towards Trixie, yet you crack a smile like a child the moment you sneak a peek at your terminal."
"...You're the child here! This is a healthy, sunny adult smile!"

"...That concludes the report on Chief Inspector Howell for this week. The update will continue next week. — Stacey."
After closing the encrypted file on her terminal, the feline woman sitting at her spacious desk closed her eyes, seemingly fatigued, gently pinching the bridge of her nose with her index and middle fingers.

Stacey, born into the Persicat family branded as traitors, faced isolation at school despite her excellent academic performance solely due to her lineage.
If not for the encouragement from President Elf who attended the award ceremony, her fate could have been much bleaker.

Thus, President Elf held high expectations for her.
Upon graduating with top honors, Stacey was promptly recommended to join the Seagull Squad.
Kind-hearted Sachi, highly skilled Kagami, genius Echo, and disciplined Stacey, fighting for honor—on paper, a stellar team setup.

However, personality clashes, inevitably tied to their backgrounds, led to the split of the two.
Neither Stacey nor Echo had matured enough.
Inherent injustices of the world burden the labeled young woman with even harder circumstances following that failure.

Sending Stacey to the remote island was partly to manage the repercussions of a severe injury within the team and partly in hopes of her gaining solid ground and rebuilding her confidence.
Placing her under Chief Inspector Howell was also to see the fruits of her development and to serve as a warning to the increasingly restless Deputy Director of Storm Eye.

Speaking of which, Storm Eye's Director Torahu has been planning to establish a special investigation squad.
Members include Echo, Feitian, Grey Mist, and a novice Inspector.

"It seems a storm is brewing..."
President Elf looked out at the bustling Newsea City and sighed softly.

The moment the middle-aged man in the black suit walks into the bar, all eyes are drawn to him. Maybe it's because his attire and demeanor are so out of place here. As he makes his way towards me, I start to regret taking this job.

As per the arrangement, he takes a seat behind me, a position that allows for hushed conversations without attracting attention.

"I've sent you the target's information," he says.

What? Wait a minute, this idiot! Does he think I choose a rendezvous in the Southport District, where surveillance is minimal, for no reason? All electronic communications are monitored!

"Don't worry, I have powerful backers. No one dares to mess with me."

If you have such powerful connections, why don't you deal with this opponents yourself instead of involving me?

"If we could take action openly, would we need to pay you?" he retorts.

"...In that case, the price is double the initial offer." I counter.

"You're jacking up the price!"

"You've caused me a great deal of trouble."

"You people are so unreliable... Fine, just get the job done quickly," he grumbles.

"And the down payment?"

"Rest assured, you'll get your money once the job is done."

"That's not how it works."

"What a hassle..." the man mutters, tossing me a card.

"That's all for now. I'll contact you once I get news that the target has been taken care of."

So he came prepared? And he made me waste my breath. What a pain.

At this moment, the drink the man ordered arrives. But without so much as touching the glass, he stands up and walks out.

Damn him, good riddance. I pick up the abandoned drink and take a big gulp.

The target is a middle-aged Felinian male, residing in Quince District. Perhaps because the affluent, peaceful Quince District falls outside the client's sphere of influence, he seeks my services. 

Regardless, the Felinian male enjoys a comfortable life, maintaining a healthy routine that includes a forty-minute jog every morning followed by a bath, breakfast, and a day's work. The "work" he does involves cleaning up the messy books of major corporations. 

This is a perfect opportunity for me.

"Good morning!" I, disguised as a jogger, greet the target from afar as he comes along for his morning run.

"Hello, I don't think we've met before?"

"I just moved in and this is my first morning jog. The scenery here is pretty good, and the air is so fresh."

"Miss, you're absolutely right! The riverside park here is all scenic, particularly that bridge over there..."

"Indeed, I just watched the sunrise from the bridge. It was really beautiful."

"Is that so? I'll go and have a look then. See you!"

After bidding me farewell, the target makes his way to the middle of the bridge, slows his pace, and leans against the metal railing, gazing at the rising sun in the distance. I must admit, the sunrise is indeed beautiful today.

Ensuring I am in the blind spot of the surveillance cameras, I draw my bow, nock an arrow, and release it. The flexible arrowhead shoots out at a speed too fast for the naked eye to catch, shattering a previously damaged section of the railing, and without a sound, the target, like a stone, falls from the bridge along with the railing. Below the bridge flows the swift river.

Such a tragic accident. The city authorities should inspect and reinforce all the bridges in Catto City to prevent similar accidents from happening again. With this thought, I pack up my bow and arrow and continue my morning jog.

Upon returning to the bar, I notice the middle-aged man sitting there, as if he's been waiting for quite some time. However, his glass of liquor remains untouched, as full as when it was served. I spot a flimsy card on the chair. I casually swipe my phone over the card, revealing the balance on the screen—it's less than half of the agreed amount.

"The amount isn't correct."

"Heh, that's how the market works," the middle-aged man chuckles deviously.

"You're not planning to honor our agreement?"

"Agreement? Hmpf, you have the audacity to talk about agreements when you've doubled the price at the last minute! Take it or leave it."

"Then there's nothing more to discuss."

Seeing me pocketing the card from the corner of his eye, the corners of the man's mouth twitch upwards. 

"All that talk, and you still took it in the end, didn't you?" He sneers.

"Remember, we've never met, and there was no transaction. Don't bother me again."

"What a miserable place, even the booze has gone off. I won't be coming back!"

With that final remark, he stands up and leaves without a backward glance. Such a detestable character—no one would object if he were to disappear from this world, would they?

Looking down from the high-rise, I see a sophisticated black sedan parked at the intersection. A few minutes later, the middle-aged man who appeared in the bar earlier emerges from the building, accompanied by a Felinian man. He obsequiously opens the car door for the Felinian, a stark contrast to his arrogant demeanor in the bar. He's just like a dog waiting for its master to toss it the leftovers.

I guessed correctly. The Felinian man is the puppet master, and the middle-aged man is just his lackey. If I only make the "pet" disappear, it will be too lonely for him. So, let's hit the road together, you two.

There's no traffic or pedestrians on the road, after all, it's already deep into the night. The sedan starts smoothly and begins to pick up speed. If everything goes as expected, it will make a turn at the next intersection and then completely disappear from my view.

Calculating the timing, I aim at the rivet of an advertising signboard hanging on a nearby high-rise and fire my arrow. The massive signboard, along with its electric sparks, crashes directly onto the roof of the slowing sedan. Subsequently, the explosives I placed inside the signboard detonate successfully. The wreckage of the sedan is instantly engulfed in a raging fire.

If everything goes as expected, no creature can survive such a situation.

By the time the blast wave reaches me, it has turned into a refreshing breeze, faintly carrying the scent of money. The loud noise and flames don't seem to attract much attention, even the pedestrians in the distance simply quicken their pace and quietly leave.

After all, the Southport District is no place for peace.

Pushing open the flamboyant doors to the office, Hailey is instantly enveloped by the dazzling sunlight. The person she's looking for sits in front of the floor-to-ceiling windows of the top-floor suite, his face is almost covered by the unobstructed, harsh sunlight.

"Both sides are taken care of, and there should be no loose ends left," Hailey whispers as she approaches the figure. 

"Well, that's a relief. I can finally get a good night's sleep," Jack Roy languidly replies, propping himself up with his arms and squinting at the sun. 

"Mr. Jack, are you trying to go blind?" Hailey coolly sees through his act and further questions, "Where's my payment?"

Upon hearing the question, Jack Roy chuckles merrily.

"Although no loose ends were left, the time it took was too long. And it seems like you've discreetly raised your price behind my back?"

"I... I have a mortgage to pay off too..." Hailey tries to justify, but Jack Roy disregards her excuse. 

"Therefore, your payment for this job will be halved."

The young girl bites her lip and lowers her head in resignation.

"Understood. If there's no other work, I'll take my leave..."

"Hold on, little Hailey," Jack Roy stands up from his chair. As he turns his back to the sun, she can't help but make a mental comment about his overly dramatic posture.

"Given the current situation, I doubt anyone would dare to mess with us now. Have you considered retiring?"

"Thank you for your concern. But until I've saved enough money, I won't consider it."

Upon hearing her expected response, Jack Roy seems to breathe a sigh of relief for some unknown reason. He takes a few steps, leaving Hailey with his retreating figure.

"I'll leave the rest to you then."

"Good evening, Miss Bella. "I'm your doctor, here to help you heal."
 
Before sunset, I finally arrived in Leidsdam and found the address from the commission letter.
It led me to a yard overrun with weeds, deep in the slums. The wooden door creaked, barely hanging on its hinges as the wind pushed against it.
 
The chilly breeze made me frown as I glanced at Bella, poorly dressed for the cold, standing in the yard.
She looked surprised at first but was now watching me warily.
 
Hmm... I had been upfront about my identity and purpose, so why was she cautious?
Given the time lost on the road today, I needed to start her treatment immediately.
I grabbed the medical kit off my bike and moved past Bella, heading quickly into the house.
 
"First, you'll receive a full-body checkup. For now, I recommend a conservative approach to ease your symptoms, but I'll need a closer look..."
"Hey, I didn't say you could come into my house!"
I looked at Bella, confused, as she raised a hand to stop me, her displeased gaze fixed on the medical kit as if she noticed something specific.
 
"Are you... the witch they say can transform pain into healing?"
"That's just superstitious nonsense. My methods may be unorthodox; some fear them while others have no choice if they want to survive."
Faced with relentless pain, few could truly remain atheists.
That was how this title spread, and I often found myself wasting time explaining it.
 
"Any more questions? No? Then let's get started."
"I never agreed to this treatment, and I can't afford it. It's not like I have much time left, so don't trouble yourself..."
"Wait, why are you pulling out a sedative?!"
 
As I observed the unstable Pathos Particles within Bella, I calmly put on my medical gloves.
 
Patients refusing treatment weren't exactly uncommon.
Perhaps I should just calm her down first?

"I'm afraid your genetic condition is quite serious. Without proper treatment, I'm worried you don't have much time left."
I kept my voice steady as I delivered the test results.
Bella's face, already pale from pain, twisted even more—I realized a bit too late how my words affected her.
 
Oops, I made a mistake.
I was trying to echo Bella's earlier description of her illness, but it clearly didn't ease her mind at all.
Frustration washed over me as I closed my eyes, recalling examples from various social handbooks while I weighed my next words.
 
"There's no need to worry about expenses. I can help relieve your symptoms."
However, I would need to go back to the "family" and retrieve that medical book from the library.
 
That "forbidden" memory resurfaced, sending jolts of nerves through my head as pain raced down my spine like wildfire.
My mind wandered despite my efforts to focus.
 
"The blessing of the Divine Tree—a force powerful enough to change the world..."
The man I was supposed to call "Father" murmured, his voice tinged with anxiety, his eyes burning with a frightening fanaticism.
 
Divine Tree... The Divine Tree...
Was it even real?
 
The quest for proof and the revelations it brought had been sealed away by the immense shock to my mind.
Each time I reached for that memory, a shiver gripped me, warning me to stay away.
The fact that I couldn't even think of it—that alone was an answer.
 
—The "blessing" of the Divine Tree had always been nothing but a cruel joke.
The "wrongs" and "evils" of my family... someone had to pay for them.
I was determined to do whatever it took.

"Ha! You look as pale as a ghost—what a sight!"
"Working on a new patient? Who's the unfortunate soul this time?"
 
S12 finally called in, ready to start the next phase of treatment.
I must admit, she was the most unique patient I'd ever encountered—she set her own treatment schedule.
Yet, I knew she had a good heart.
 
Just like now, she wasted no time expressing her... concern, I guess?
How touching.
 
"Thanks for your concern."
"Huh? Who said I was concerned about you?!"
 
Ah, there she goes, getting mad again.
 
However, I was used to S12's erratic moods; emotional instability was to be expected in patients.
I deftly held her hand in place just as she tried to knock over the medicine.
Considering her past help... maybe I could ask her for some advice?
 
"Patients these days are really a handful."
"Hmm... this should work as an icebreaker, right?"
"What are you mumbling about, woman?"
 
I gave her a full rundown of Bella's condition.
Ancient texts contained methods to ease her symptoms, and with modern science, a complete cure might be possible.
But it all depended on the patient's willingness to cooperate.
S12, who was equally uncooperative, might offer some useful insights.
 
Despite her visible annoyance—frowning with her arms crossed tight—she answered me nonetheless.
"You never thought to ask why?"
"Uh, no."
"If you're not going to use that mouth, you can just give it to me."
"Which part do you want, my lips or my vocal cords?"
"Out... go torture someone else for a change!"
"Thanks for the encouragement..."
"GET OUT!"

"I've done everything I can to ease your worries, and there's still hope for a full recovery from your genetic condition..."
"So, what's still bothering you?"
Over the days we spent together, Bella's anxiety and fear of dying became increasingly clear to me.
 
"Don't worry about me, Dr. Sage. You should focus your energy on helping others realize their potential."
"I prefer to finish what I start."
Bella fell into a long silence.
"The same illness took my love away from me..."
"The promise we made for the next life has only weighed heavier on me since his passing."
 
"...So, he's gone?"
"He... didn't want to hurt me, so he left as soon as the signs of Affliction appeared. I haven't heard from him since. His fate was painfully obvious..."
I recalled the signature on that commission—it was unmistakably her lover's.
The answer was clear—Darkrift.
 
For most, becoming Darkrift was as grim as death, perhaps even worse.
I had seen many who, after their transformation, were too terrified to face their families.
 
"I'm not blaming you, Dr. Sage."
Bella tried to put on a reassuring face, but it didn't come through.
 
I felt as if I had witnessed a similar scene in a script.
After a moment, I picked a line I thought might resonate.
"Maybe he's still out there, just in a different form."
 
For some reason, my response seemed to amuse Bella.
"I didn't expect you, Dr. Sage, of all people, to believe in souls and such."
"No, I wasn't referring to his soul."
"Are you suggesting..."
 
I chose to remain silent. Bella's eyes, catching the soft light, glistened with unshed tears.
"I... I understand now."
"Dr. Sage, please... I beg you..."
 
Her eyes were filled with an intense yearning for life,
a pitiful yet heartbreakingly beautiful sight.

"You're way too arrogant, Sage!"
"The laws of nature—what makes you think a Felinian like you can defy them?!"
 
"Mentor, I'm not a child."
"That's not the issue!"
 
The researcher sighed deeply, a familiar exhaustion washing over them, as it had countless times before.
This talented student was academically brilliant but hopelessly awkward, lacking a grasp of the real world.
The researcher glanced at Sage's blank expression, feeling a wave of helplessness, and finally tossed the manuscript into the shredder.
 
"Your thesis topic is rejected."
"Darkrifts are a forbidden subject, and you still want to research how to turn them back into humans..."
"Aside from the challenge of reconstructing a body deconstructed by Pathos Particles, your goal of reintegrating what society views as monsters will be fraught with obstacles."
"If you want to graduate, you really should consider changing your topic."
 
Sage kept her eyes fixed on the shredder, lost in thought until it finally stopped.
"But after I graduate, I won't have access to research equipment like this. It's too expensive, and I can't afford to continue my research on my own."
"I knew I wouldn't be able to talk you out of it! But did you really have to make your intentions so obvious?!"
"You think I'm just worried about some equipment? It's your future that concerns me!"
 
Sage raised an eyebrow, puzzled by her mentor's words.
"All I want is to find a way to heal them. Nobody else is trying, so I figured I would—and I did."
"Why are you so worried about my future?"
 
"Because others will try to stop you and slander your name, doing whatever it takes to eliminate any dissent."
"Going public with this research will definitely provoke a backlash."
 
Sage slapped her thigh, a look of realization dawning on her face.
The researcher's heart sank as they saw her reaction.
 
"I understand now, mentor! I'll conduct the experiments in secret, away from prying eyes."
"Then why are you telling me this right now?!"

Before I head out each time, there's always someone with a lot on their mind to share with me.
 
"Ms. Akanuma." Asunaro bowed her head. "I'm sorry for falling short. I haven't been able to uncover the origins of that woman..."
She wasn't the same innocent child from a few years ago, standing before her family with a sword. Her voice had deepened slightly, whether from the onset of puberty or from the dedication to her training that had stripped away the softness of her voice. But to embody the persona of an assassin from the Third Group, the girl had started wearing a high school uniform half a year ago, aping the behavior of contemporary students in every gesture—she even played the part in front of me, like a student anxious about a relative's displeasure after receiving poor grades—her hands clasped behind her back, her toes nervously turned inward.
"..."
"Ms. Akanuma?"
Asunaro slightly lifted her gaze to gauge my silence, which only intensified the fleeting illusion.
 
If she weren't part of the Akanuma family, she would likely be living peacefully in some corner of this world as a high school student.
Extremely talented and strong-willed, she would undoubtedly excel in pursuits beyond marksmanship... She would bounce with joy when happy, furrow her brow when in pain, say no to things she didn't like, and be deserving of a circle of friends.
 
"...I've heard that she's become the leader of the First Group and will act as your Seneschal during the upcoming journey to Catto City." She continued, "I wouldn't dare question the master's decision, but to have such an obscure person serve you is truly—"
"Is that what you think?"
"Th-This is what my mother said! Mother said you bear too much weight, and asked me to be your eyes and to share your burdens as much as I can..."
 
As dusk approached, the crows outside the window struck the branches like a sudden downpour, seemingly awaiting my response.
 
"You and your mother have quite the courage."
Finally, a smile played at the corner of my mouth, and my mood eased.
"What are you two to me?"

Victims actually empathize with their perpetrators; this world is far more twisted than I'd ever imagined.
 
Asunaro, originally with the Kishibe surname, faced scorn when she was assigned to the Third Group.
"She is the offspring of that absurd traitor who betrayed Sakura Island and then the rebels..."
"Huh? But isn't she more talented than the entire Third Group put together?"
"With genes that betray for money, she can't be trusted on missions, can she?"
"Well then—" After watching Asunaro silently blend into the crowd, I raised my voice in retort, "Should I send you on a mission right now?"
"...M-Ms. Akanuma! I wasn't aware you were here..." The man immediately dropped to his knees. "Please, don't."
"Are you scared now? Then why would the Akanuma family want someone who's afraid of a mission?"
The Kukurihime blade gleamed as I gripped the hilt—
...
"Always remember, all of you bear the Akanuma name now. Your past is irrelevant."
With a contemptuous look at the man who collapsed on the ground, I turned and left.
"Th-thank you, Ms. Akanuma, for your mercy—I will lay down my life for the Akanuma family!"
The sound of his forehead hitting the ground repeatedly weighed heavy on my heart.
 
—There was a bloodstain on his neck.
This meant that even the Third Group had begun to practice the Akanuma blade techniques... making a clean escape impossible.
The Third Group was always disdained, and among them, there must have been several who diligently practiced the blade techniques in hopes of becoming higher-ranking vassals of the Akanuma family, enduring the curse of eternal damnation... People trapped in destiny are always oblivious, thinking that being exploitable is their worth, and they offer loyalty measured by their very lives to their benefactors.
...Disgusting.
I want to inflict punishment, but I hesitate, considering their plight.
I long to lend a hand, yet my efforts feel as insignificant as a drop in the vast ocean.
What a disgusting... me.
 
I glanced back at Asunaro at the end of the line, who was looking over at me with a mix of gratitude, joy, and indescribable emotions.
...
Perpetrators who consider their victims are asking for trouble.
Didn't I already know that?
Why... am I still making this mistake?

Sugi Kishibe was the supposed strategist for the rebel forces.
Perhaps calling him a strategist was a bit of an exaggeration... After all, on Sakura Island, tightly clenched in the Akanumas' fist, any effort at strategy felt like a wasted breath.
Their numbers were sparse, skulking on the fringes of towns and cities, yet they couldn't slip past the keen eyes of the three thousand crows that served as my spies.
I'd secretly mocked their apparent obliviousness to the rudiments of counter-espionage... only to be caught off guard when I stumbled upon their hidden den.
 
The riverbed was baked dry, the earth lifeless, and the half-buried statue still kept watch behind the time-worn torii gate, its stone speckled with moss.
Moss? Was there a flicker of life left in Shiokawa after all?
The night breeze carried the familiar tang of Pathos Particles, fueling my persistent contemplation of this possibility.
But this was Shiokawa...
"NOW—!"
A whirlwind of steel engulfed me in an instant.
 
With just one foe left, Shiokawa transformed back into crimson.
"You've ruined everything, you overconfident fool."
I'd never been so utterly spent, even the act of lifting the Felinian's head felt like scaling a mountain, and in the end, I chose to rest and sat down beside him.
Sugi Kishibe, bathed in his own blood, met my gaze and managed a bitter smile.
"But choosing Shiokawa wasn't a mistake. You have a profound connection to this land. Our powers were simply inadequate, and in the end, we were like pebbles shattering against mountains."
"We were cornered. Akanuma's First Group had already sealed the coastline, and taking you hostage was the most desperate move we could conceive."
"...My overconfidence has led to the deaths of all the patriots... yet I know, none of them would have second thoughts."
"To see the devil shed tears is... a bonus indeed. Your torment shows you're not invincible."
...
What else was there to say?
Should I mention that I had come alone, before the First Group, with the intent to decimate to aid their flight to the unguarded eastern front?
Should I confess that the Pathos Particles left here on the Crimson Night, fifteen years ago, were enough to devour all my reason?
What should I say...?
Who could believe that Akanuma Ren, the Akanuma clan's most celebrated warrior, no longer craved to take a life?
 
"Akanuma... no, Miss Ren." The man on the brink of death spoke again, "Please spare my wife and daughter... from too much pain..."
"Are you... pleading with me?"
"...Miss Ren, please..."
"..."
"Thank you..."
He actually said.

Pulling up to the Kishibe household, I watched the girl laugh as she waved goodbye to her friends.
That is, until a cry for mercy echoed from her mother upstairs.
We hurried up the stairs, nearly in sync.
The difference was that she was worried about being late, while my mind was adrift, lost in memories.
My recollections were like a slow, steady fire, crackling and unyielding.
 
"Sugi Kishibe was a gambling addict, racking up countless debts."
"He squandered the rebellion's hard-earned funds, lost the trust and lives of everyone in the rebellion..."
The girl, upon hearing this, was seething with anger, ready to lunge at me.
Just days ago, she had been thankful for my intervention in saving her mother from the thugs.
"Asunaro!" The woman shouted, pulling her into a tight embrace.
"...He also lost you two."
Feeling the chill of the scythe's edge, in its reflection, I thought I saw those two figures...
Back then, they were the same age as this girl.
"In recognition of his contributions—starting today, you are exceptionally granted the status of vassals to the Akanuma household."
 
Later, I couldn't shake the feeling that Sugi Kishibe might never have intended to use me as a hostage at all.
When he realized the game was up, he played his final move, selflessly giving everything for a slim chance.
He gambled on the one-in-a-million possibility that... I'd show mercy to his family.
 
And they did indeed survive, barely holding on.
Naturally, I knew that Asunaro, even as a weapon, was too cumbersome.
From her eyes, I could tell that Asunaro's mother didn't believe my words.
But what did it matter?
Marlena and Alara, who had lived in The Ideal City...
They could certainly teach Asunaro, what is the right thing to do.
 
And so, the crows carried my expectations, flying towards the distant horizon.
They flew towards a tomorrow I would never reach.

On the day the girl was born, the sky wept blood-red rain.
—As if everything was fated in the unseen shadows.
She was the silhouette cast by the bookshelf, the tarnish on the sword. She was the angel of the home, and the ghost that haunted it.
Even as a shrine maiden who bestowed blessings, she committed unspeakable sins.
 
If her life had continued down this path, it might not have been seen as suffering.
The mistake was... she tasted the simplest kind of joy.
The kind of happiness that made her want to pour out her soul in the dead of night.
 
It turned out, this was a mistake.
It turned out, I was the one who should have died.
The girl slowly came to understand what she had done, what it truly meant.
But Shiokawa had run dry, and no one would ever scale the wall to talk to her again.
And she grew up, no longer "needing" the occasional care from her mother.
The vast island, like a tomb, entombed her here.
She couldn't drift away or find a shore to rest upon.
 
But Akanuma Ren did not give up.
The ancient texts say that the executioner must carry the weight of the lives taken.
So... with this awareness.
The executioner waits for the day of reckoning.

"Keep away from the moon, shield yourself from its beguiling light."

Thus taught the **Book of Worldly Passage**. Yet, as night fell... the moon rose.

—You must purify yourself, Scarlett.
—Yes, Scarlett needs purification... Scarlett has accrued too many sins.

I began to shed my garments.
Robes are favors from outsiders; flesh is but a facade.
The Divine always watches—
Beneath the seemingly immaculate skin, the filth ingrained in the soul that can never be concealed.

—You must purify yourself, Scarlett.

The "High Prophet" calls to me... with sanctity, with cold springs.

I, in my primordial form, stepped into the dark bathroom, immersing myself in the purifying "Spring of Sanctity."
More fitting than the expansive baptismal font of the past, this place seemed where I truly belonged.
Narrow, tight... able to wrap around me deeply and coldly.

Even in the absence of the Divine, "Cleansing" remains a necessary daily ritual.
Stripping away all worldly adornments from the body, only the true "Primordial" is allowed to soak in the "Spring of Sanctity"—this is "Cleansing."
And Scarlett, burdened by profound sins... therefore, an additional layer of "Penance" is required.

The coiled "Thorns" hissed as they extended their tongues.
The "Thorns" are sleek, the "Thorns" are cold... just like the "Spring of Sanctity."
The "Thorns" wrap around the body, entwining the limbs, tenderly binding my hands, my ankles.
The "Thorns" bare their fangs—
And "Sin" punctures the skin, slowly seeping out.

Crimson, viscous, scalding...
The "Spring of Sanctity" has been tainted and corrupted by my "Sin," no longer as pristine as before.

Behold, how rich my "Sin" is.
Divinity...
For a sinner like Scarlett, can I still await Your "Redemption"?

"Endless calamities surround your self-made prison, your sins have caught up with you."

After intoning the last verse, my father closed the **Book of Worldly Passage** and turned around.

"You must purify yourself, Scarlett."
"Yes, Father—"
"I have taught you—before God, do not call me father."

"Father," holding the thorns consecrated before the holy icon, descended the Oracle Stairs, approaching me. His form was enveloped in auric light, as if it were both cloud and celestial shadow.

"We reside in Him, and He also dwells within us; only you are blind and deaf."
"It is your sin that distances Him, your transgressions make Him turn His face away from hearing you."
"Scarlett, this cleansing—requires an additional layer of penance."

When "Father" grasped the thorns, he ceased to be my parent and became an embodiment of the Divine.
"The High Prophet" sent forth one of His million faces, manifesting within his flesh.
His actions are Divine will; His words, Divine decrees.
This is the "High Prophet’s" expectation... and His mercy for me.

"Yes… please grant me strict penance, High Prophet."

Thorns wrapped around my bare limbs.
The primordial me stepped into the cold baptismal font, immersing myself in the purifying "Spring of Sanctity."

"Scarlett, do you still remember your sin?"
"Yes, I remember."
"My birth killed my mother’s innocent soul, my life defiled all worldly morals."
"As long as I live, He will never cease weeping; He will never return to rest."

Scarlett is crimson, Scarlett is blasphemous, Scarlett is sinful;
But the Divine only wants the pure white, the clean, the sinless.
Scarlett, seeking the Divine's "Redemption."

"The unblemished lamb is the perfect sacrifice."

Night fell, and the moon rose.
Moonlight pierced through the stained glass, and the chapel was as bright as day.
Where the light was born... I saw shadows intertwine and overlap.

"It's you, little Scarlett. I wondered who it was."
"Take your time, don’t rush."

The entwined shadows undulated.
In the flawless moonlight, the 'Patriarch' moved forth in the flesh.

"Scarlett, your sins are not yet cleansed. Your hands are not yet worthy to touch salvation."
He smiled at me, his hand extended, with the moonlight behind him flowing and shimmering in sanctity.

"Or do you so desperately yearn that you wish for me to bestow upon you— the pure white salvation—now?"

I fled the chapel.

Ahead were two diverging paths, one wide and one narrow.
The wide road and broad gate lead to illumination, the narrow path and gate to darkness.
The path is small, the gate is narrow.
To receive 'Redemption,' one must travel the narrow path, pass through the narrow gate.

But having taken the narrow path, I found no gate but came before the statue.
The clouds dispersed, the moon orbited... light descended.
The moonlit statue lowered its inanimate eyes, gazing down at me indifferently.
I knelt before the statue.

Why do you not show me compassion?
Your realm spans the mortal plane, your grace blesses all creatures... yet you cast tainted light upon me.
Is Scarlett not to hope for 'Sanctity'?
Is Scarlett not to aspire for 'Light'?

Is Scarlett... not worthy of 'Redemption'?

"He still lives, breaking through the malicious chaos to stand upon the earth, igniting the thorn fire."

In the same shadowed tale, I first clearly saw "Him."
"On that day, 'He' cleansed all filth and shadow as 'the Brave,' purifying the depraved city of indulgence."
'He' set the thorns ablaze, yet the thorns could not harm 'Him' in the slightest, only cower in fear of 'His' holy might, entirely consumed.
Henceforth—
The world knew no shadows, nor thorns;
There was only the sacred light and the everlasting 'Redemption.'

Will that day, the day of 'Redemption,' truly arrive?

"That day will come, Scarlett," declared the Holy Lady gracing this place.
"Holy Lady… What should Scarlett do?"
I pleaded for guidance amidst confusion and loss.
"…Pray, Scarlett, pray with strength and unforgetting."
"Hidden desires scatter across texts lost in the old days, while the writer of this fairytale prays for a beautiful vision."
"One day, I will restore the glory of Lizdanum…"
Afterward, she departed, never looking back.

Pray…

The 'Thorns' that wander through my body smiled gently and beautifully.
It hissed whispers to me:
Yes, Scarlett, come and pray;
Silently, quietly, like an immaculate white flower, pray.
The day of 'Redemption' will surely arrive. So until then—

Can you endure just a little longer?

When Scarlett fell into a deep slumber, darkness descended upon the night sky, and thick clouds shrouded the land; when she awoke, the mournful moon had plummeted into the depths of her eyes, immaculate and clear. She gazed at the moon through the cold water.
It was a pair of lightless eyes, merely reflecting the moon silently, devoid of sorrow or joy.

The "Thorns" twisted and coiled, embedding their spikes into her flesh, merging with her blood and tissue. Scarlett did not moan.
It was as if her physical body was merely an illusion, filled only with intertwining crimson thorns, but devoid of her spirit.

"…Divinity."
Scarlett uttered a plea.

She wished for the divinity to retract the moonlight that fell upon her. She did not want her sins to be exposed under the light without any cover.

"Divinity."
Scarlett whispered again.

Yet, the "Divinity" was not present here. To follow "Him," one must forsake oneself, constantly bear the thorns day and night, endlessly. Scarlett was born with sin, destined to be entwined with thorns throughout her life.
She must carry the thorns, but there will be no path that allows her to enter through that gate.

...Knowing all this.

Under the moonlight, Scarlett clasped her hands together.
In the darkness, the sinner emitted a faint cry for help.

"Divinity... Scarlett might soon be unable to endure..."
"Please, come to my side sooner..."
"Grant me... my final redemption."

"That won't be necessary. You may take your leave."
In the seventh year of my reign, I finally managed to take my place on the grand, ornate, yet frigid throne all by myself.
This was the same throne my mother had once occupied.
 
"Your Majesty! At your young age, I am concerned..."
Shan'e, the wet nurse I had previously rebuffed, grovelled on the floor, her voice trembling with anxiety.
The vast throne room echoed her unspoken desires for power and wealth.
 
"Are you challenging my words?"
The golden dragon throne was uncomfortable, and I struggled to maintain my posture, having already exhausted much of my limited patience.
 
"I would never dare to challenge you, but have I done something to displease you, Your Majesty?"
Shan'e replied, her body quivering with what seemed to be a genuine terror at my rebuke.
Yet, I could sense that her fear was merely a mask for her fury.
 
Indeed. Just as Mingjin had warned, the wet nurse I once trusted implicitly now viewed me only as a means to her own ends.
A tool—albeit a prestigious one—that had slipped from her grasp; it was no wonder she was enraged.
 
"You have done nothing wrong. In fact, your years of dedicated service are commendable."
 
I feigned benevolence, following Mingjin's advice.
Shan'e was greedy but not particularly clever. Upon hearing my words, a glimmer of delight spread across her aging lips.
The foolish joy that assaulted my senses was reminiscent of the foul stench from a gluttonous serpent—I nearly gagged.
 
"I am deeply grateful for your generosity, Your Majesty. The late Emperor entrusted me with your care, and I could never bear to be negligent."
"Indeed, you earned my mother's trust, and I must reward you accordingly."
 
I briefly closed my eyes. Besides the transient trust, the "Golden Keep" my mother had left me was perhaps the more enchanting treasure.
 
"These years of service have kept you away from your family. I cannot bear to see you separated."
"Your Majesty?"
"Now that I am grown, you should return home to enjoy your twilight years. Your services are no longer needed."
"Your Majesty?! I have never thought of such a thing! I wish only to serve you for life! I beg you, grant me this!"
"Your loyalty is commendable, but I cannot watch you remain apart from your kin."
"But Your Majesty, I—"
"My decision is final. You are dismissed."
 
A foreign emotion filled the air, and it was only much later that I recognized it as resentment.

"Congratulations, Your Majesty. Hereafter, your resolve will be unyielding and unshakable."
Mingjin emerged from behind the curtain, a content smile gracing her lips.
Her presence radiated a soothing fragrance that eased my troubled mind.
 
But what should I do next?
I turned to Mingjin, seeking her guidance.
 
"Your Majesty, as the Emperor, the kingdom's treasures and people are at your disposal. You are free to act according to your discretion."
"But what of state affairs?"
"Your Majesty, your sharp discernment allows you to recognize your loyal ministers. Empower them with governance, and you may reign undisturbed."
 
Reign undisturbed? Reflecting on the history lessons my mother had imparted, I realized that such effortless governance would signify a wise and enlightened ruler.
 
"Furthermore, the blending of the Holy Race with mere humans in positions of power may sully your sacred senses."
Mingjin spoke with genuine concern, prompting me to consider my unique nature.
 
I was born with the ability to perceive the true essence of all living things.
Emotions manifested as voices and auras, ever-present around me.
 
Plants had soft, expansive voices and calming auras.
Insects had distinct, rustling voices and subtle, unique auras.
Beasts carried voices hinting at human speech and complex, recognizable auras.
But the essences of my holy kin and humans were ever-changing, their auras overwhelmingly strong, often unbearable for me.
 
As a child, my constant crying stemmed from being overwhelmed by these emotional currents.
When my mother realized this, she strictly forbade me from speaking of it.
 
After her sudden passing, as an indiscreet young child, perceptive Mingjin understood something was amiss.
She too counseled me to keep this secret, and of all outside my mother, treated me the best, her aura the most comforting.
I trusted Mingjin completely.
 
"How do you wish to proceed, Your Majesty?"
Her gentle voice echoed in the grand hall, and I, enchanted by the sweet fragrance, simply nodded.
 
"I, too, am weary of those despicable creatures. Cousin, you shall handle them for me."
"Your Majesty, you must personally choose your ministers."
"I understand. I shall name you my Prime Minister. Please summon them to me individually, as you see fit."
"As you command, Your Majesty."

Entrusting Mingjin to manage the concerns of the preceding reign, I ultimately found a sense of calmness and respite.
No longer did I have to face those sanctimonious ministers every day or endure the pounding headaches caused by their treacherous schemes and empty platitudes in court.
 
After several rounds of purges, the court had been cleansed, and the ministers were now loyal and patriotic. With effective policies and favorable weather, the people thrived in contentment and prosperity.
Watching the "Golden Keep" steadily amass wealth filled me with great solace.
 
If only my mother could witness this; she would surely be gratified.
 
"Tyrant! Foolish ruler!"
The cries rang out on my fifteenth birthday.
Shan'e, under the guise of offering birthday congratulations, entered the palace, feigning remorse and reverence while bearing gifts.
 
"Foolish ruler, now die!"
In that moment, as the dagger laced with deadly poison flashed towards me, a towering wave of resentment and hatred threatened to engulf me.
I was paralyzed by this unprecedented emotion, unable to move a muscle. It was then I truly understood how skillfully humans could hide their true feelings.
 
Perhaps what the Heavens had bestowed upon me was not a blessing, but a curse.
 
"Your Majesty!"
Warm blood splattered across my face.
Mingjin had thrown herself in front of me, deflecting the fatal blow.
 
My thoughts spiraled chaotically, like countless metal spikes driving relentlessly into my head.
 
"Your... Majesty. I am afraid I can no longer serve you..."
Mingjin's face had turned pale.
"Please... for the sake of my years of loyalty, be kind to... my brother and kin."
 
Over the years, the familiar sweet fragrance had decayed rapidly, replaced by an indescribable fear and the stench of dark corruption.
 
"The Emperor is witless! If the late Emperor knew, she would be furious in the netherworld!"
Shan'e, restrained by the guards, continued her deranged raving.
 
"Remove her from my sight!"
My own voice, shrill and commanding, reverberated through the hall, and the searing headache that gripped me felt as if it would rend me asunder.
In the next moment, I plunged into an endless darkness.

When I awoke, my long-estranged cousin Mingjun, Mingjin's brother who had been away on the military campaign for years, arrived to pay his respects.
It was then I learned the devastating news—Shan'e had been cruelly executed, her entire family wiped out.
 
The pounding in my head refused to subside.
As I closed my eyes, the cherished memories of my time with Shan'e came flooding back, unbidden.
 
"Your Majesty, it grows late. You should retire for the night."
"Your Majesty, I've brewed you a calming red date tea. Please, have some."
"Your Majesty, you've grown taller. I've made you new garments..."
"Your Majesty..."
The earnestness in her voice was tinged with a depth of genuine affection.
 
While new clothes may be appealing, true companions become more valuable with time.
The words my mother once shared echoed in my mind. Without Mingjin's gentle guidance, as I pondered the years that had slipped away, my heart suddenly found clarity.
 
"Why has it come to this...?"
Tears streamed down my cheeks, dampening the satin pillow that Shan'e had crafted for me.
Though faded and despite my growing resentment towards its maker, I had never replaced it.
 
Mingjun observed me pensively for a moment before speaking up.
"Your Majesty, you do not embody the tyrant the world portrays. Surely, you have been misled by deceitful ministers... Forgive my audacity, but the realm teeters on the precipice."
 
So, the peaceful reign I had envisioned, the prosperous era, had already been swept away by the winds of change?
 
"General, what leads you to such a dire conclusion?"
"Your Majesty, Deputy Prime Minister Zhang Rusong has for years deceived and oppressed the common people. Shan'e was but a pawn in Minister Zhang's schemes, which ultimately led to... Afterward, it was Minister Zhang who took the initiative to wipe out Shan'e's entire family. I beseech you, Your Majesty, to heed the wise, shun the unscrupulous, and restore order to the court."
His aura was bracing and keen, a stark contrast to Mingjin's comforting presence.
 
Rumor had it that the previous Emperor, a mere woman, had usurped her brother's longevity and throne, angering the Heavens and meeting an untimely end.
If the world were to right itself, Mingjun would be the rightful heir to the throne.
If I stepped aside and allowed Mingjun to take the throne, he would likely prove to be an exceptional ruler.
 
 
"I see now..."
Mingjin, you know me well enough to understand that I lack both the heart and strength to mend this fractured realm you left behind.
But I have been entrusted by the Heavens—how can I abandon my people and this land?
 
The only recourse now is to yield to the capable.
Yet Mingjun's temperament gives me pause—he may not agree.
 
"Do the people truly see me as a tyrant?"
"Your Majesty, it was the schemes of petty men that led to the nation's ruin..."
"Hmph! I shall not tolerate any slander against my courtiers. Elevate Zhang Rusong to the position of Prime Minister. General Li, you are to return to the border and take up your responsibilities once more."
"Your Majesty? Your Majesty!"
 
As I listened to Mingjun's disbelieving voice fade, a faint smile crossed my lips.
Ah, it seems I am destined to be labeled the tyrant.

The following year, in the autumn of the tenth year of Yonggu, chaos engulfed the realm.
 
The rebel army stormed the Imperial City, and a desperate Zhang Rusong set the Emperor's palace ablaze.
 
General Li Mingjun marched his troops to quell the uprising, only to find two charred corpses among the ruins.
 
News of the Empress and the treacherous minister's deaths spread across the land, and the people celebrated with joy.
 
By the end of the year, Li Mingjun ascended to the throne, ruling for thirty-nine years. He dedicated himself to restoring the realm, earning the title of Emperor Guangwu in the annals of history.
 
What remained unknown to all was that beneath the well behind the bedchamber, filled in and hidden from sight, lay a delicate bronze mirror, called Mirror of Enutrof.
 
Within that mirror, a hidden world awaited.
 
"Prime Minister Zhang certainly knew how to finish off a fallen foe! Too bad he ended up sealing away his beloved Golden Keep."
 
"Who would have guessed the Golden Keep was just an ordinary mirror?"
 
"I assume Mingjun is the Emperor by now?"
 
"With those scheming fools gone, my mind is finally at ease."
 
"But it feels a bit too quiet in here, don't you think?"
 
"How tedious. I suppose I should take it upon myself to inventory the treasury..."
 
All sense of time faded away...
 
Jinque realized she hadn't yet finished cataloging the treasures in the vault.
 
As light once again illuminated the mirror's surface, the cacophony of emotions from the outside seeped through the cracks, stirring Jinque like a cat roused from sleep.
 
"Enough of this noise! Drag them out and silence them once and for all!"
 
But instead of the obedient retainers of old, a sigh resonated like celestial music.
 
"Jinque, I know your mistakes and your story. Would you like to truly live once more?"

Butterflies are naturally drawn to the most exquisite flowers.
In my eyes, those flowers take root in the realm of dreams.
Their growth, blooming, and eventual fading...
All is revealed within the dream.
 
"It's been too long since I last laid eyes on the Inspector—I find myself missing them."
After stretching my stiff limbs from prolonged stillness, I pondered on what to wear to my anticipated rendezvous with my beloved that evening.
Before I could even make a decision, the teahouse door swung open.
"What a delightful surprise! What brings you here at this late hour, Manager?"
Strangely enough, the mere sight of the Inspector's endearing face lifted my spirits instantly.
"Perhaps our hearts are entwined—did you already discern my thoughts?"
"The one who can peer into others' minds... that has always been you, Qi."
The Inspector offered a bashful smile before taking a seat across from me.
 
"Well, if you insist..."
I gazed at the Inspector's countenance until a flicker of unease flashed in their eyes under my scrutiny.
"You entered with a troubled look, furrowed brow, so something must be weighing on you, correct?"
The Inspector chuckled ruefully, prompting me to step closer and gently rest my hands on their slender yet reliable shoulders.
"Come now, confide in me. What has been troubling you? I am deeply intrigued."
"The truth is, I've been having the same recurring dream lately..."
 
Dream?
I, more than anyone, comprehend the profound significance of the Inspector's "dreams."
Furthermore... for the Inspector, these dreams hold a profound and fateful importance.
"Then it's imperative for me to uncover the source of your distress all this time, isn't it?"

"I'm not entirely certain who it is. The dream is always shrouded in darkness."
"I can discern a faint voice amidst the chaos, but its message remains elusive."
The Inspector, momentarily lost in recollection, displayed a rare instance of perplexity.
"Oh, yes, I believe I detected another girl's voice in the dream..."
 
"Another girl's voice? Be careful, Manager, you might spark my jealousy!"
Though spoken in earnest, it carried a teasing undertone.
I narrowed my gaze.
"Fear not; allow me to assist you in unraveling those thoughts."
 
"How do you plan to achieve that?"
"It's quite simple! As a soul healer, I possess unique healing techniques."
With each step she took closer,
I felt my breath quicken.
"Oh dear, don't be so tense; I'm just trying to get closer to you."
"...Is such proximity truly necessary?" The Inspector instinctively took a step back.
"Indeed, building trust with my client is a healer's primary task."
In truth...
No one else would receive such personalized attention as the figure before her.
 
Soon, those hands extended as instructed.
"Relax."
The petite spirit ignited the incense, releasing a calming aroma into the room.
"Good. Now, take deep breaths and sense the energy surrounding you..."
 
Alright... It's time to unearth the source of the Inspector's distress.

The smoke danced gracefully, painting a delicate picture in the air, and imbuing the space with a poetic allure.
All external distractions and noises faded into oblivion,
as if time itself had halted, leaving behind a profound stillness.
 
"Can you try to recall? What was that dream like?"
"Hmm... It was enveloped in darkness, and I couldn't make out anything..."
The Inspector's tension eased, and the turmoil in their heart subsided.
"Are you sensing anything else at this moment?"
"Hmm... I feel... weightless, as if I'm submerged in the depths of the ocean..."
"At the ocean's depths... yet you don't feel constricted?"
"No, not at all. It's akin to being a fleeting mayfly in the deep sea, drifting along with the currents..."
"Would you attempt to swim around?"
"I can, but the darkness is all-encompassing, so the surroundings remain unchanged no matter where I navigate."
"Don't rush; ease yourself into the darkness first... Your sight will soon clarify..."
 
In no time, the Inspector became fully immersed in the trance.
Following a brief silence...
 
"Hmm?! I caught a glimpse of a blurry figure just now..."
"Keep moving closer to it gradually."
"...It's futile; as I approach, the shadow retreats further..."
Furrows creased the Inspector's brow, and their once relaxed hands clenched with tension.
 
Despite my meticulous guidance, the elusive figure's true form remained elusive...
It appears this is not a matter to be taken lightly.

In the vast expanse of the dream-like "ocean," my consciousness drifted akin to a solitary vessel adrift in an endless blue abyss.
Surrounded by darkness, sporadic lights flickered like distant stars, beckoning me forward through the boundless void.
Eventually, my quest for truth led me to enter the Inspector's dream—
a realm that resembled more a cosmic galaxy than an ocean floor, its scale far surpassing my comprehension.
"So, where might our Manager be within this dream?"
I scanned the surroundings under the faint illumination but found no trace of them, and even the Dream Butterflies seemed perplexed alongside me.
 
"Thou... managed to infiltrate this dream?" A voice, genderless and echoing, reverberated around me.
"Forgive my intrusion. Your repeated visits to this dream in search of someone, yet never revealing yourself—"
"I am deeply concerned for our Manager, hence why I sought answers... May I inquire about your identity?"
"Such details are inconsequential to thee."
"That judgment is mine to make."
"Heh... I am not of this realm, existing beyond thine comprehension. I come not to disrupt but to adhere to the law of karma."
"If you are not of this world, how can karma apply to you?"
"Karma's roots were planted eons ago, now entwined within this human..."
"What is your intent concerning our Manager?"
"My spirit's intentions mirror my own. The truth shall soon be unveiled."
"...Are you speaking in riddles with me?"
"No. The manifestation of karma is yet to come."
 
Once more, karma intertwines with our narrative, leading us back to our starting point.
Dear Inspector, is this what captivates me about you?
 
"All that needs to be said is now clear. Thou may depart."
With a brilliant flash of white light, the dream concluded.
 
"Ugh, didn't expect to doze off."
The Inspector rubbed their head, appearing slightly sheepish upon waking.
"I once again failed to pinpoint the root cause..."
"Perhaps the recent workload has been triggering these dreams."
 
Since karma is at play... I shall stand by the Inspector's side and witness its unfolding.

Unbeknownst to the citizens of Catto City, a peculiar phenomenon emerged, catching everyone off guard.
Qi's attention was drawn to this anomaly when Jinque, who had been eager to meet the Inspector, suddenly succumbed to an unnatural drowsiness.
Soon, it wasn't just Jinque and the Inspector—many others found themselves affected by these inexplicable symptoms.
 
The usual explanations like seasonal fatigue no longer sufficed to account for this strange occurrence.
Speculations ran rampant across the Paranormal forum.
 
"It seems like hospitals are filling up with individuals who slipped into profound comas but miraculously awoke after a few days..."
"Yes, indeed! I witnessed someone nod off on the bus and they didn't stir at their stop, eventually being carried away!"
"I experienced it too... I drifted into slumber, had a dream, and upon waking, I thought it was a brief nap, only to learn from my mom that I had slept for three days!"
"Thank goodness this only occurred during our sleep! If it happened while working, we'd be like perpetual drones!"
...
 
Conversations of such nature swiftly inundated the online platforms.
Even scholars have delved into studying the phenomenon, yet no solutions have emerged.
 
Qi, privy to the unfolding events, made the conscious choice to keep the truth concealed from the public.
That realm of half-reality, half-illusion—the enigma ultimately morphed into yet another unresolved urban legend.
However, for those who ventured into that dream realm, those "accidental" connections would remain etched in their hearts for all eternity.

"So, this is all she left behind in the end."
The girl nodded, her expression numb and her eyes red-rimmed.

The photo contained two plastic buttons from a lady's shirt, a small tuft of white fur, and an ID badge stained with dried blood. She was a beautiful and tender Felinian girl.

"We found her, but it was too late."
"Her belongings have all been taken by StormEye, only these... photos remain."

Her demeanor is calm, her narrative orderly.
This was not the relief of escaping a predicament, but the precursor of an impending breakdown.
For a mental therapist, such a seeker of help is more dangerous than those who wail loudly.

"I see. So, what do you need?"
Play it slow. Keeping them calm is the only way to go.
I poured her a cup of tea and pushed it towards her.
"They're gone. Those of us who remain have a much longer journey ahead."

"I... want to forget..."
The girl gripped the teacup tightly as if the burning heat did not exist.
"Forget about that day, the blood, her eyes..."

"She said, the people she recently met were weird, they even knew what she liked..."
"Why didn't I take it seriously? Why... didn't I go with her?"
Her murmurings were like sleep talk, her eyes were dry and hot, filled with bloodshot veins.
"I've been having nightmares every day..."
"...Until one day, I dreamt of this place, the Listening Teahouse..."

"No one but the guilty should be persecuted by their conscience. Know that this was not your fault."
"Besides, the one who guided you here, seeking my help..."
"They wouldn't have done that if they didn't care about your future."

The incense in the stove wafts. The puppet-like girl finally let out a broken sob from her throat.

"What you need is not a stranger's consolation."
"No one knows better than you how she used to bring warmth to this world."

"As for the root of the evil..."
I let out a soft sigh, a laugh carrying a profound meaning within.
What a person in desperation needs is not consolation.
"You should leave it to... hm, StormEye, don't you think?"

The dreams of humanity are often veiled in a mist of varying density.
Not today, however.

Incense is the lure, melody the bait.
The prey lured into the dream is mired in confusion, oblivious to the reality of the moment.

"Oh, have we a guest?"
My smile brushes against the dark red veil, as I extend a hand through the cascading fabric.
"The night is short, my dear guest... Are you just going to stand there, rooted to the spot?"

I hear a gulp.
That's the struggle of a fish hooked, the signal for the hunter to close in for the kill.

"I know, milord, that you are a connoisseur of exceptional beauty, hence your visit," I say, twirling the veil around my ivory fingers.
"Would you like to come over and appraise it firsthand? How else will you appreciate my beauty?"

An unexpected breeze stirs.

That was the snow of many years ago.
It still moistened her soul to this day.

It was then that her father preached.
"Thus did the God of the Earth search for his lost daughter ...mindlessly run the seasons, and the earth has had cold winters ever since."
"...Some say that the child chose to retrieve the memories lost by the River of Forgetfulness, and so became the wife of the King of the Underworld, never to return to earth again."
"......"
"Sylviette?"
"She must miss her mother and father."
"Sylviette..."

Unbeknownst to anyone, the girl later quietly wondered.
"Could it be that ...forgetting is sadder than just dying, than not having a future ...that's why she chose it that way?"

It's a shame.
The best plays are always staged in the dark corners where the dirt is hidden.
The defeated actors are forgotten on the stage where the smell of blood permeates.

As for me.
A 'honored one' who is a good spectator.
I came on stage at the most opportune moment.

"Become my bunny, or become a dead soul."
"Tell me your choice."

I looked down at him, almost unconscious.

"You are ...... that lord!"
His lips, pale from blood loss, trembled.
I admired his fear with satisfaction, like a work of art.

Like every viewer, who wonders about the sublime idea of a work of art.
I guessed with equal interest, what was he fearing?
The atrocity he had just experienced? 
In Wonderland, that couldn't be more normal.
The unknowable future? 
In the presence of implied death, is that not a boon?
Ruthless bystanders? 
Oh, that's too much to my liking.

Time nearly stood still in silence. I waited, somewhat bored, polishing my sword.
Lately, I've been so busy recruiting minions that the neglected sharp edges have lost the luster of being nourished by blood.

The crows stationed on the branches seemed unable to wait, shaking their wings and taking flight.
The paralyzed man was startled and his shoulders cringed.

"I, promise you."
"Hmm. That's really good behavior."

And so
The eyes that concealed fluke and selfishness turned into two round buttons.
The flesh and blood that wrapped covetousness and ambition turned into soft cotton wool.
He became my rabbit.

I watched as he lifted his short hand in a naive manner, cupped the large bunny head, and tried to convey his horror outwardly.
I couldn't help but laugh.

I know all too well the life that this land produces.
There was certainly a small price to pay for wanting to be of use to me.

Wonderland, a giant kaleidoscope.
A gentle turn of the paper cylinder by fate would allow me to witness a completely different world.
 
Once it was silent and black.
When I opened my eyes, I saw a room that was always dark and walls that never let in air.
Like a lowly rat, I lived in fear in a moldy corner.
 
"Remember, Sylviette, we are kin to the Black King!"
"Then why am I not allowed to return to my original form?"
The only thing that responded to me was the silence of my parents.
 
Later on it was a frenzied red color.
Blood gushed from the pierced eyeballs, blurring the figures of the blood relatives who fell in a pool of blood.
Rats accidentally exposed to the sun, drawn into a rampaging orgy by the most evil of men.
 
"Felinian! Heretic!"
"I am not a Felinian! I am a relative of the Black King!"
"Liar! We will bring you to the King's judgment!"
 
Now.
I'm going to be the one to spin the paper cone.
 
"Your Majesty, the Black King, I have done your bidding."
"Sylviette, you have not disappointed me as the most promising descendant of our clan."
"The last position of the Twelve Faces as a reward, you won't mind, will you?"
I suppressed my ecstasy and reverently knelt under the Black King's throne.
 
Power, position, absolute strength.
I reached out to the thorn bushes with my own hands, picking up the variegated flower paper and constructing a new pattern for the kaleidoscope.
 
It doesn't matter if my hands are cracked, the only doom to be feared is falling to the bottom.
I'm going all the way up.

"The end of self-reflection scatters the lingering breath of a glorious nation."
The tedious text is a cryptic and relentless retelling of an era's demise.

I closed the back cover of The End of Love and Lust with a sigh of relief.
To whitewash the history of ignorance with exquisite words and fictional love, is this the kind of civilization mankind thinks it is?
It's ridiculous.

Humans don't care about the fate of mole crickets, and so do I.
If it wasn't for the King's recommendation, I have no intention of learning about these toothsome stories.
My time is precious.

However, it's about that "Smiley"...
What was his intention in recommending this book to Wang?

To let down his guard and confuse the public?
Or is it... a trick of beauty and love?

I closed my eyes fiercely, forcibly erasing the pink bubbles that were born by association in my brain.
Sacrilege! It was simply blasphemy!
That's it, the man's brainwashing tactics!

The king is deeply righteous and indulges that man's ambition.
But I will never allow it! That position can only be ......

"Lo, Lord Deterrence..."
A mumbled voice interrupts the thoughts, and I gather the distorted emotions into my eyes as I slowly look towards the kneeling figure.

The new bunny doll was clearly not used to 「his」 new body yet, and was trembling at an annoying rate.
For no apparent reason, I thought of the two troublesome brats beside Smiley, who wouldn't be trembling and acting like losers!
The accumulated humiliation ignited a violent rage with the force of a prairie fire.

I will not, for long, stay under the thumb of others.
It will be interesting to see what happens when the disguise of a smiley face is torn to shreds.
I look forward to it.

I took the secret letter that the stupid bunny offered with both hands.
Your dear friend, from Catto City.

As an honorable, king's kin.
Alienating traits that resemble those of Felinians is not a difficult task for me.
Although... I don't like this identity.

"Your legitimate identity has been verified, thank you for your cooperation."
The human at the gate smiled knowingly and handed back the ID.
"Welcome to Catto City."
"Alien Felinians will still be required to cooperate with regular screening after entering the city, the process is not exactly cumbersome, so please be aware of that."
 
Heh...
The famous Catto City.
It's actually a sieve full of holes that come and go.
 
I stifle a snort and mimic the human across from me by displaying a polite and sincere smile.
"Of course."
 
Weaving in and out of the tall buildings.
I observed the colorful city like an innocent and curious traveler.
What drama is about to be unveiled on a Stage that stands amidst acclaim and light?
Huh...

"Beep..."
The corner of my coat fluttered, and I instantly sidestepped the high-tech product that sped by.
"This hand is intentionally looking for trouble, crossing the road to see the crosswalk!"
Unfortunately, no one would listen to the curses of an ant.
I raised my hand to gather the hair that had slipped, and my eyes circled around to land on the black and white patterns on the ground.
 
I need a little study time before the good show.

Born in a society where the weak are the strongest.
Weakness is the original sin.

Sylviette, who was sentenced to "death", was whipped by fear all the time.
She was constantly raising weights to force the scales of fate to favor her side.
Desire feeds on her ambition.
 
And Catto City, a utopia far from Wonderland.
The turbulent times will be her best hunting ground.
 
"Talent introduction."
Sylviette thinked about the king's order.
Ever since 'Smiley' had taken his place at the head of the Twelve Faces, the Black King had been extraordinarily fond of the Shinkai vocabulary under his influence.
This was not a precursor she was happy to see.
It was time to make a move herself.
 
Then, let's start from here.
Sylviette looked down on everything here with arrogance and condescension.

Becoming a candidate for the people of Wonderland would be the highest honor of this group of people in this life!
 
"The Fall Recruitment Fair at Pentacity Plaza will begin soon, so please line up!"
"Hello, kid? You don't have your resume? Here's a form for you. It's not too late to fill it out."
"..."
 
Okay.
This incomprehensible city!
Sylviette still needed to spend a little more time preparing the perfect plan.

"Clang!"
The sound of something being toppled echoes from the distance.

Bundles of scrap paper and fallen cans line the path.
The heavy panting of two individuals grows near.
Their breaths are laborious, like the wheezing of decrepit bellows operated by soot-blackened lungs.

"Insistent pests."
They're on my trail again.
Seriously? All that for a discarded chainsaw?

"Get down here!"
I am perched atop a wall, two security guards bellowing up at me with fervor.
One was gasping for breath, his face pale from the exertion. The other was weak-kneed, his legs as wobbly as two fermenting radishes.
"Hand it over... Pay up... Go... Go... Turn yourself in!"

"You can't even speak clearly, maybe you should save your breath."
I dust off my clothes and stand up. Draping the old chainsaw's strap over my shoulder, I tossed it over the roof.
"Dying here wouldn't be a good look, especially since an ambulance wouldn't be able to get in."

"You... bloody idiot, what are you waiting for, call the police!" "I'll... Oh, oh! Right, sorry..."
The man in the shirt may be out of breath, but he still manages to slap his companion on the back of his head.

Such audacity. He must be some kind of boss—no, a leader? That's not quite right.
Perhaps a... "head honcho" would be more fitting.
My guess? He's the type who asserts his presence by finding any excuse to pick on others.

But I've always been a magnanimous person.
As always, I chose to just leave them be.

With a wave of my hand, I graciously let loose a leaf that had just played a discordant lullaby.
The leaf gently danced in the wind before landing on the man's face.

"Pinpoint accuracy, 10/10!"
I vault over the perimeter wall and whistle in triumph.
"Here's a portrait for your troubles. Don't mention it. Ciao!"

"What's this?"
The man grumbles, squinting under the flickering street lamp, finally discerning the scratch marks left by the gravel.

"You bloody scoundrel...!"
The man's rage erupts like a volcano, while I, amid the torrent of curses, hop onto the roof of a single-story house.

What an easy escape. Too easy.
Well, at least there'll be fresh adventures waiting for me tomorrow.
