I'm keeping it.

Welcome to the slums. 
Leaky roofs, moldy walls, and mountains of trash.
Makeshift kitchens line the streets, and not a single communal toilet exists for the households here.

The air here is perpetually foul.
The un-dried clothes emit a damp smell, while the greasy smoke from the eateries and the black water from the factories navigate the alleys.
Cover your nose all you want, the smell will find its way into your eyes.

The people here are eternally ruthless.
Sick elders being cast out of their homes, left to freeze or starve in the harsh cold.
The shrill cries of women and children escaping beatings echo far into the night.

I've grown up here, and nothing surprises me anymore.
But to those who drive luxury cars and live in palaces, this place hardly qualifies as a city.

The dark alleys are too filthy for my liking; I prefer the high ground.
Rooftops, walls, chimneys, grates.
Not just because they're open spaces with unobstructed views and easy maneuverability.
But also because they offer easier access to whatever I desire.

I found a relatively clean rooftop as my new temporary base. Just as I settled on the edge, I heard the lady of the house, stumbling through a lesson with her son.

"Most people live in quiet desperation."
"Mom, what is desperation?"
"Well...for example, after your father has worked hard for a long time, he buys you a delicious ham..."
"Then he hangs it by the window to air out. And when you're hungry and craving for it..."

"It's gone." I answered leisurely, swallowing the last bite of the hardened ham.
Food always tastes better when it doesn't come from your own hard-earned money.

How amusing. 
This child, barely able to recognize all the letters yet, is already learning to accept life's punishments.

"Endure it," I yawned.
"You're still far from escaping all this."

I am accustomed to solitude. In other words, it makes escaping easier.

I need no assistance or aid, and I hate having others meddling in my life.
They're all burdens. That's what it is.

But then, as I sprint across the rooftops and walls...
Someone sneakily opened a window, throwing out several stones to distract my pursuers.
"Run, run!"
A girl urged nervously, peering out to monitor the enemy's movements.

Strange humans, why would they think I need rescuing?
This wall stands as tall as two and a half men stacked together, Even in a fair match, they couldn't possibly catch up.

But at least for now – I don't need to run anymore.
I slung my chainsaw onto my back and jumped off the wall.

Her name is Yvette, still a student at heart.
"We're about the same age, you should be in school too…"
She seems tentative as she speaks.
"Money is not a concern, there are charity funds these days…"

She continues her tirade, but I can't be bothered to listen.
School? Paying to get jailed during daytime feels like a raw deal.

"So, what's your name?"
"I don't know."
"Don't have a name, huh… Can I give you one?"
"Um... the first time I saw you, you looked like you were shining."
"How about Danica? It means morning star. I read that in a book…"

Hmph.
If I wanted to become a star, I wouldn't be scraping by here.
That's not my life. That's just a fairy tale.

"Danica! Our teacher recommended a book today, let me tell you about it."
"Look at this flower I picked on the side of the road! Isn't it beautiful?"
"Danica—meet me at the alley entrance tomorrow, I've got something tasty for you!"

How does she keep this up?
Isn't life in the slums hard enough?
But I couldn't argue with her, and find myself meeting her again and again.

Until one day, I found Yvette curled up behind a trash can, her backpack tossed aside.
She was silent, her chest punctured by a short knife, and the blood seem to have stopped long ago.

I frowned.
It was dark out, what was she doing here? Trying to play the hero for me again?
I've told her time and time again that I don't want that from her. Why do humans love doing so much in vain?

Forget it.
I've seen too many inexplicable deaths like this.
If I had to bury all of them, I'd break my shovel.

But these past few days have been foggy.
The snow can hide the bloodstains, erasing all memories.
I'll keep this hairpin as a memento.

After all… there's nothing left to lament, right?

"Heh... Hah..."
The man's last words came out in ragged gasps, like a bellows with a hole.
"I'll... kill... you..."

Beneath her feet, rivers of fresh blood flowed; before her lay bodies with eyes wide open in death.
In the distance, the glittering sea of lights continues its resplendent display, one firework after another exploding in the night sky.

"I thought you'd be more capable..."
Danica steps on the man's forearm, kicking the switchblade from his hand.
"...But as always, you're nothing but rotten fish."

She wraps an electrical cord around her bleeding wrist and bends down to haul up the electric saw.
It has been fed too many hard objects: steel pipes, fruit knives, moss-covered rocks.
Once a sharp machine, now it's riddled with notches.

The unnoticed vagabond, dragging along an unclaimed, broken electric saw, makes her way towards the end of the alley.
Blood, a sticky mess mixed with grime, is flung from her shoe, splattering onto the dead eyes of the bodies.

Danica is covered in injuries, but she doesn't care.
Humans. Always caught up in self-conflict and self-doubt.
And when they're too hard on themselves? They displace their self-loathing onto others.

This is not provocation; it's revenge.
She has never been one to swallow her anger.
Yvette used to be one. But not anymore.

"You, to the left! You, the other side! The rest, come with me! We're turning this place upside down!"
The coherent sirens tear through the night, awakening the entire slum.
Danica presses her hand to the wound on her side.
Blood squeezes through her fingers, staining her footsteps, leaving a trail of vibrant life in the dark alley.

Even the rats living in the stinking gutter have moments when they want to challenge the cats under the sun. But she was no rat. Those cowardly aggressors were no cats either.

She disappears around the corner of the dark alley, her high-lifted hair tips tracing a flash of flames under the dim street lamp.

Heart-shaped decorations swayed along the streets in the gentle breeze, while the sweet scent of chocolate filled the air. Couples strolled by, hand-in-hand, lost in the warmth of romance.
All around me, the world seemed to glow with a rosy hue—Valentine's Day had arrived.

Across Catto City, festive activities were in full swing, drawing in countless couples and tourists.
To mitigate any potential risks, StormEye had dispatched as many patrollers as possible to various districts, myself included.
To blend in with the crowds, I had chosen one of my favorite dresses that captured the holiday spirit and set out for Commercial Street to begin my rounds.

After checking my equipment, I noticed the candies and chocolates I had prepared.
Originally, I was supposed to patrol alongside the Inspector, but it seemed they were unusually busy today.
"Well, that's only natural—they are an exceptional junior I've mentored, after all."
But in that case... when would be the best time to gift these treats?
"Alright, focus on the task at hand... As a senior, I need to set a good example."
With that thought, I adjusted my beret and began my patrol of Commercial Street.

"Sniff... sniff..."
A faint whimper suddenly reached my ears, drifting out from the bustling crowd.
What was that?
I perked up, straining to listen as I traced the source of the sound.

I pushed my way through the crowd, following the sound, and there, at the street corner, sat a little girl clutching a balloon, softly crying.
"Sniff... Mommy..."
A lost child? With the bustling festival crowds filling Commercial Street, it was all too common for careless parents to lose track of their kids.
"Hey there, little one. Do you need some help?"
I approached her, keeping my voice gentle and warm.
"I... I can't find my mommy..."
The girl looked up at me, rubbing her tear-stained eyes with one hand.

"Now, don't be scared. The StormEye sent me to patrol the area."
I crouched down to meet her gaze directly.
"Can I help you find your mommy?"
"Sniff... Mommy..."
The girl, clearly overwhelmed by being lost for the first time, continued to cry helplessly.

"There, there."
I pulled out a few brightly colored candies from my pouch.
"Here, have some sweets first. Can you tell me where you last saw your mommy?"
"Thank you..."
The girl took the candies, her sobs beginning to subside.
"Mommy said... she was going to buy Daddy some festival chocolates... There were so many people in the store, so she told me to wait outside... Then I saw a balloon cart by the road..."
Ah, so she had been lured away by the sight of the balloon vendor's cart.
"Don't worry, I'll help you find your mommy."
I gently took the girl's hand in mine.

As I comforted the little girl, I guided her in search of the sweet shop where her mother was supposedly buying chocolates.
"The balloon cart earlier..."
Following her gesture, I spotted a small cart decorated with heart-shaped balloons up ahead, the vendor cheerfully calling out to passersby.
Maybe I could ask the balloon seller for directions; it might help me figure out where the girl had gotten separated from her mother.
I approached the vendor and inquired about their recent route.
"Ah, it was that way? Thank you!"
With the location confirmed, I quickly led the girl toward the end of the street.

"Nina! Nina!"
Just as we reached the sweet shop, a worried yet relieved voice called out from behind us.
"Mommy!"

"Oh, you scared me so much! Nina, where on earth did you go?"
"I'm sorry, Mommy..."

Nina's mother noticed me and bowed deeply.
"Ah, it was my duty. No need for thanks."

"Thank you! This is for you!"

"These chocolates... are my favorite! Thank you for helping me find Mommy!"
"Oh, this..."
"You've been such a great help. Please, accept this small token of our gratitude."
Cradling the thoughtful gift, I felt my cheeks warm.

"Well, time to get back to my patrol!"
Seeing Nina and her mother reunited, I carefully tucked away the chocolates and continued my rounds.
"Huh?! Looks like someone's collapsed over there!"

"All dressed up on Valentine's Day... Looks like he's planning to confess, hmm?"
"Ah! Did he get too nervous and faint?"
"Excuse me, pardon me! I'm a StormEye patrol officer!"

"I believe that as long as your words come from the heart, Ruby will feel that."

"I do feel a bit less nervous now."

Burning.

"Mama, Papa, (sobs)..."

I lay there on the ground, helplessly watching my home devoured by the ravenous inferno.

"Tut tut, look at that tear-streaked little face..."

"Come, I offer you chains, chains to control this power."

Everything changed from that moment on.

The only shadow over this bliss was cast by none other than myself.

From the moment I was born, blessings and curses befell my household.
My innate physical defects and strange powers, like a two-headed serpent, tightly coiled around me, coiled around my home.

"Come, I offer you chains, chains to control this power."

A realm of white, my newfound cosmos.

*Boom*

Flames.

"Excellent! Increase the dosage, continue the experiment!" "Injecting Drug C!"
...

Burning.

"Click."

"It appears Subject 760 has reached its limit."
"What a shame… We'll proceed as usual."

"Clang—"

I am alone, collapsed on the cold ground, gasping for breath as I feel my life slowly ebbing away.

"Clang—clang—"
I lift my head. In the dim light, I see two new children in the adjacent cells, like me.

"Hey, hey! Are you awake?"
Once the white coats are gone, one of the taller kids whispers to me. "We… we need to get out of here…"
The other child turns towards us, his back to the bars, resolute in his gaze. "Let's go, together."
Two scorched hands reach out to me.

Struggling, I manage to prop myself up and give a determined nod.

A stifling heat engulfs me.
A surge of intense warmth rudely rouses me from my slumber.
As I open my eyes, a cosmic ballet of stars winks at me from the heavens.

I try to rise, yet my hands sink into a sea of minute grains of sand.
Lifting my head, I find myself in the heart of a desert.
The white room has dissolved into nothingness.

The air carries a distant yet hauntingly familiar scent—the smell of my former home set ablaze.
I look around in a daze, a fierce fire licking at my back.

I stand transfixed, fragments of reality or perhaps dreams materialize in my mind.
After breaking free from the prison, all that greeted us three was the vast expanse of the desert.
The long-absent moon hung high, gently illuminating our path forward.

The sun and the moon rise and set, and we trudge through the desert, our steps growing increasingly heavy and slow.
The desert seems to be slowly devouring us.

*Ting-a-ling*
The sound of distant bells drifts from a far-off dune.
A caravan of camels spotted us, pulling us back from the brink of death.
Little did they know, they were saving monsters.

"Help! Monsters! Monsters!"
"Forget the goods! Run!"
Snapping back to reality, I see the merchants scattering in all directions amid the raging fire.

Much like that blood moon night.
Once again, I am the root of all chaos.
Misfortune befalls anyone who crosses my path.
Would it be a better choice if I were to depart from this world?
A wave of agonizing pain sweeps over me. I lose consciousness and tumble into the abyss of darkness.

"Are you alright?"
A tender voice delves into the abyss, cradling Evelina in its warmth.
"Just hold on, I'm going to administer a suppressant."
A surge of blazing liquid courses through her arm, seeping into her body and permeating every corner.

Slowly, Evelina opens her eyes: white light in a white room.
A silver-haired woman sits on the edge of her bed, her face etched with worry.
"Hush, you're still weak, don't speak."
Evelina parts her lips as if to utter something, but the silver-haired woman gently presses her finger to Evelina's lips.
"I know what you want to say, I know everything about you..."
The woman reaches out, taking Evelina's hand softly in hers. "I'll put an end to them. Your nightmares."
Evelina lifts her head, tears tracing liberal paths down her face. This time, Evelina nods her head firmly. 
...
"Hey, Evelina, have you prepared the training course for this time?"
A staff member approaches Evelina at the StormEye training ground.
"What? The new recruits are starting their training today, of course I've had everything arranged. You got a problem?"
Evelina stands with her hands on her hips, her gaze piercing. 
"Ah, never mind..."
The staff member leaves with a sense of bitterness.

Time whizzes by, and now, Evelina is a seemingly ordinary instructor within StormEye, responsible for training new recruits. "Damn, I was too harsh again..."
Past experiences still subconsciously keep Evelina distanced from others, even if they bear no ill intentions.
This constant struggle troubles her. 

"Hey, are you the new Inspector from Baker Street?"
From this newcomer, Evelina senses something that was long missed. 
"Today, I'll be in charge of your training."
Could this person in front of her be everyone's future?
Like the silver-haired woman once did for her, Evelina reaches out, gently taking the hand of this newcomer Inspector from Baker Street.

"Rustle—"
What was that?
I freeze mid-step, straining my ears toward the sound ahead.
 
Tonight is my first graveyard shift as a physician at the Emotion Remedy Center.
This dimly lit building, nestled in the quietest corner of the compound, has always piqued my curiosity.
 
Day shifts never allow me the time to explore.
So, when the night shift offers a chance, I stray from my patrol route and slip inside.
 
"Rustle—"
The noise draws me forward until I spot a shadow shifting at the end of the corridor.
"An escaped patient? Or..."
Beyond the windows, clouds engulf the moon, shrouding the corridor in darkness.
 
My fingers inch toward my hidden pocket as scenarios flash through my mind.
The adjacent building houses the ICU. If this is a breach, dozens of critical patients could be in danger within minutes. The fallout would be catastrophic—
I edge forward on silent steps, weapon ready.
Whatever lurks in that darkness must be neutralized. Now.
 
Then, as if sensing my determination, the clouds part.
Moonlight spills across the figure ahead, revealing the telltale patient garb—and that unmistakable mark on the chest.
 
"...Oh."
The tension drains from my grip. I exhale, adjust my glasses, and close the distance.
Of course. A child of the stars.

I was once a child of the stars.
Like the constellations above, I felt distant. Untouchable. A world unto myself.
 
"Hey there, little one. Can you understand me?"
Is that voice speaking to me? Understand? Understand what?
Her crimson lips move rhythmically, like a dance. Oh, how I love dancing.
"Dance... dance!"
My own lips twitch in response, mirroring her movements.
"Hmm. You're a special one, aren't you?"
Her mouth curves, as if accepting my silent invitation.
"Dance!"
Let's dance together.
 
That was my first "conversation" with the orphanage Headmistress.
She watched me closely after that, though I had no words for the universe within me.
 
Yet I remained alone.
The library became my sanctuary—quiet, predictable, safe.

I'd pull a book from the shelves at random, press it to my face, and let it open like a treasure chest. To me, the letters and numbers came alive: stick-figure acrobats, birds, kittens.
They pirouetted across the pages, never tiring, never fading.
I memorized each one. They took root in my mind.
I adored them. My only friends, my private cosmos.
 
"You truly love books, don't you?"
Those red lips again, swimming into view. A familiar wave.
"Fairy tales... novels... and arithmetic?"
Arithmetic? The word buzzes in my chest.
"A-rith-me-tic! A-rith-me-tic!"
"So numbers speak to you? Shall I teach you their language?"
I lifted my head and saw a kindly face for the first time, its dark eyes filled with warmth.
 
For the first time, the stars turned their gaze upon mortals below, watching with quiet wonder.

"One... two... three..."
I whispered the numbers under my breath, lining up each utensil with meticulous care.
The Headmistress never pushed, but step by step, she led me from books to helping sort the dining hall's utensils.
161 plates. 158 cups. 171 spoons.
Perfect symmetry. Perfect control. This was how life should be.

A life of quiet routine could've been mine, if only the world had kept its steady rhythm.

"170..."
"Clang!"
The 171st spoon slipped, shattering on the tiles.
"170. 170..."
I didn't know what else to do, so I just kept stacking utensils, my thoughts in a storm.
But the gap remained. A tremor ran through my hands—then a clatter as I jostled the neatly sorted rows.
"Crash!"
The entire rack gave way, a deafening cascade of steel and ceramic. 161 plates. 158 cups. 171 spoons. Gone in an instant.
 
"Holy—someone get the Headmistress!"
"What do we do? We can't eat now!"
"Ugh. It's all that freak's fault..."
Within moments, a sea of young faces had surrounded the disaster area.
"Oh..."
The Headmistress burst in, her smile vanished.
Her lips—those once dancing lips—were sealed tight.
I tried to speak, but my throat felt like sandpaper.
 
Under the weight of dozens of eyes, I turned and fled, making a desperate beeline for the library.
I clawed a book from the shelf, pages fluttering beneath my frantic fingers.
"Stick figures. Birds. Kittens. Where are you—?"
I needed to calm myself. But the words on the page became unfamiliar, twisting and blurring red before my eyes.
My breathing quickened, and my chest felt like it was on fire.
The stick figures, birds, and kittens... they all seemed to ignite.
"FIRE! The library is on fire—"
Someone shouted outside the window. Then everything went dark, and I lost consciousness.

White light, white walls, a white bed.
When I came to, I found myself in a strange, sterile white world.
 
"Ah, finally awake? Welcome to your new home."
A figure in a white coat towered over me, their face concealed behind a mask.
"Spoon...book...Headmistress—"
The words crumbled like ash on my tongue.
"Ah, disassociation disorder. Difficulty connecting with others, yes? Feeling... out of place?"
A figure in a white coat offered me a meal—its contents half-hidden beneath a layer of brightly colored pills.
"Take these. They'll help you... fit in."
 
I longed for normalcy. All I could think was, I need to get back to the Headmistress—I have to explain this!

I swallowed everything. My breathing quickened, and my chest felt like it was on fire.
My mind overflowed with flickering visions—stick figures, kittens, birds—all surging out of me into the room.
They shifted again—reddening, distorting, expanding—until the entire space was clogged with their grotesque forms.
 
"Subject is reacting! Hurry with the data recording!"
A figure in a white coat shouted.

Voices from the past drilled into my temples:
"Your child cannot communicate properly..."
"Get her out of here. I can't even..."
"Hey, where did you come from? What are you saying? You're so strange..."
"Is something wrong with her head? We should just dump her at the orphanage—"
...
Memories flickered like a broken film reel. Waves of unfamiliar emotions crashed through me.
My nerves screamed. Something was peeling me apart from the inside—
 
"Incredible readings—keep going!"
The sterile walls turned red, twisting grotesquely.
"BOOM—!"
With a loud bang, I lost consciousness once more.

"Wake up—"
A woman's voice drifted through the darkness, reaching Hildegard as she floated in the void.
 
"Wake up, child of the stars—"
A pinprick of light pierced the black. Then stick figures appeared, followed by birds, and finally, the kittens. Together, they cradled Hildegard, carrying her toward the growing radiance.
 
The light swelled, until it consumed her.
Blinking against the brightness, Hildegard saw a woman with cascading hair take shape before her.
"Let me light your night sky, little star."
...
"Hildegard! Wake up!"
Hildegard sat up abruptly. The Director of the Emotion Remedy Center stood over her, concern etched on her face.
"I'm sorry, Director. I must have... dozed off."
Hildegard scrambled to her feet.
"Don't worry about it. I just came to tell you your shift is over. Go get some real sleep. These overnight rotations can drain anyone."
Nodding, Hildegard rubbed the sleep from her eyes and turned toward the staff dormitory.
 
"Let me light your night sky, little star."
The dream-voice lingered in her ears. She drew a sharp breath.
That moment had marked her rebirth—the genesis of her second chance.
 
"Director, about the patient I logged last night..."
"Ah, the nonverbal autism case? Yes, she's... quite challenging. Keeps escaping her room, and without any verbal communication—"
"I would like to take her case... if that's possible."
"Really? Well, given our current patient load, I won't refuse..."
"Thank you. I'll review her charts immediately."
Hildegard spun on her heel and marched away.
If no one else would light up her stars, then I would do it myself.

The "Heart's Wish" was far more basic than I'd pictured.
The side corridors were cramped, the inner cabins tiny and low-ceilinged, and the damp, creaky wooden planks beneath our feet seemed ready to give way at any second.
The passengers were packed together like sardines in a tin.
They had no other option.
 
"Miss Shiki." The young man named Hardy inquired, his voice tinged with worry, "Do you really think I can make it to the island?"
His face was gaunt, his breathing shallow. At a glance, it was clear this man was seriously ill.
—But there was still hope.
"Rest easy," I assured him.
In my vision, a gray rope encircled his neck—the end of it curling upwards like a white silk ribbon floating from the heavens.
Upon closer inspection... indeed, it was the Pathos Particles that had given it that grayish hue.
"I believe your previous medical records must have been a false alarm. You're just dealing with a common, mild Pathosis."
"...Please, no more comforting lies."
Naturally, he wasn't convinced.
"But the fact that you're willing to take care of me like this means a lot... Others aren't even willing to offer me a lie."
"Means a lot?" I pondered the phrase. "If lies are what you value, then why choose to board this ship and travel thousands of miles to Sakura Island for treatment?"
"To truly understand my own condition, I suppose..." He offered only a wry smile, "And you, Miss Shiki? Are you returning to Sakura Island to visit family?"
 
Visiting family...
I don't have any real family.
"The person" was right in their investigation—my childhood self was worth no more than a meal to my father, so I ended up in the hands of someone who needed a child.
 
"I apologize, Miss Shiki. My question has put you in an awkward position."
"Not at all. The island holds a similar significance for me."
Guided by the ocean currents, our journey was smooth, and at that moment, I could already see the people of Sakura Island welcoming us from afar.
Their attire was as elegant as "the person" had described.
Finally, a genuine smile spread across my face.
"Because I too wish to... fully understand and recognize myself."

In stark contrast to the lush beauty of Sakura Island, my memories spring from the desolation of a barren isle.
Shou believed this was to prevent us from causing any upheaval.
I gestured back, Only you would bring such destruction.
He paused, then let out a hearty laugh, the chains on his limbs clanking against the floor.
 
...What was this place made of?
Why could Shou not break free, and why could I not see through it?
No one answered our queries, as the only caretaker we dealt with was a low-intelligence automaton.
Her sole duty was to ensure our survival, to prevent our sudden demise.
As for the data from each experiment, it was gathered by silent machinery.
—It was absurd.
Were they afraid I might deduce something? Or perhaps... our keeper had specific reservations.
Of course, these weren't my own assessments.
At that time, I hadn't yet acquired the knowledge to understand what was reasonable.
My interactions with Shou were always a blend of childlike speech and instinctive gestures.
According to the caretaker, we had to wait for a third person to arrive before we could begin synchronized learning.
 
When would she finally arrive?
Shou and I eagerly awaited her, but what we ultimately received was even more brutal experimentation.
That person later deciphered the keeper's intentions.
—The keeper aspired to forge a team with exceptional talents in strength, speed, and intelligence, inseparable from one another.
Shou undoubtedly embodied speed, and after the final experiment, he also gained terrifying brute force.
The reason we were able to escape was that Shou, who endured ultimate agony twice, tore a gap in the island.
 
"Shi, Shi!" Shou, with fewer words and less grammar than me, held up the collapsing roof and excitedly shouted, "Run! Run with me!"
I was disoriented by the deafening noise that had just interrupted the experiment, blood staining my vision in a way I could never cleanse.
Why was there a monster made of blood blocks where Shou should be?
And why, from the caretaker crushed into pieces by him, did a... Felinian aura burst forth?
 
What is wrong with my eyes? Is the world I see real? What will I become...
"Shi." The broken mechanical face of the caretaker emitted another voice I had never heard before, "I'm glad you didn't run away."
It seemed like a sigh of regret, and then it continued.
"It turns out that brute strength is hard to tame... You won't need any more companions in the future; just come directly to me."
 
So, it was the keeper.

The day after Shou's escape, I was recruited into the Guard.
"Demon Gaze" became my new moniker.
 
Initially, my grasp of language was a considerable hindrance to my duties.
"Red, red flesh..."
"Blood?" The captain frowned, deciphering, "A surge in power appears to Demon Gaze as flesh reconfiguring."
"Intriguing." The deputy captain, a talking mass of flesh, chuckled, "If all she perceives is the abnormal, would she even recognize the normal?"
With their guidance, I grew skilled at articulating the world through my eyes.
"A torrent of azure ooze behind the skull, black cords encircling the wrists—he's a severe Pathosis patient, with a history of suicide attempts."
The deputy captain's eyes widened. "You'd be better suited for the Emotion Remedy Center."
And then one day...
"He lied." I accused, pointing at the captain.
The deputy captain seized my collar. "You ungrateful brat! Stop talking nonsense!"
I was perplexed, my brow furrowing in confusion.
"Enough." The keeper's voice resounded from the dome above the Guard. "Proceed as necessary."
 
I never laid eyes on the captain again, but the look he gave before departing was etched in memory.
The deputy captain remarked that the fool succumbed to the ugliness of the human heart.
I was puzzled. What is ugliness?
She scoffed. It's you.
Yet, upon consulting the dictionary the captain had given me, I found the word didn't fit my reflection.
—The Demon Gaze didn't reflect on me, so my appearance remained unchanged since joining the Guard.
No bloated creature, no Pathos sludge in a riot of colors, no flesh reconfiguration, no sudden metamorphoses.
I... am the sole embodiment of normalcy in this world.
 
Or perhaps, this is the very definition of abnormality.

Even without a grasp of common sense, I gradually came to understand.
—As long as I exist, no one in the Guard can keep secrets.
So, it was no surprise when the deputy captain wanted to kill me during the mission.
"Considering the captain used to look out for you, I'll allow you to say your last words."
"...Aren't we supposed to finish the mission first?" I reminded her.
As soon as the words left my mouth, the girl slowly crawling in the yellow sand nearby suddenly fainted.
It was obvious she was pretending; even without the Demon Gaze, it was clear.
The deputy captain glanced at her. "She couldn't do anything... You should worry about yourself!"
 
The battle was exceptionally tough, and though I defeated her, I was left barely alive.
As dawn broke, the small oasis we had destroyed must have been in ruins.
I calmly awaited death, also calmly listening to the sound of that girl crawling through the sand.
From dawn to noon, she gradually weakened.
"Hey... if you're not dead yet, do something..."
"I can't help you."
With half my bones shattered by the deputy captain and my eyes clouded by blood, I could barely sense the passage of time.
Besides... what could two dying people do?
"After the deputy captain, how many more will come to kill me?" She must have reached the water source; her voice was no longer excessively parched.
"If both the deputy captain and I are dead, no one will know your whereabouts for a while."
"So lucky..."
...Lucky?
As a disabled person with a broken wheelchair, she actually believed she could leave the desert.
 
I was pondering this when—
A handful of clear spring water suddenly splashed on my face, washing away the filth before my eyes like a sudden summer rain.
I opened my eyes.
It was then that I suddenly realized the water source was right beside me.
"Well, you'll be my legs—carry me out. In return, I'll be your arms and brain."
That girl was exhausted, yet her eyes were filled with an almost obsessive desire and certainty.
"Since we're not dead, we have to grit our teeth and live for everyone to see—understand?"
 
...I didn't understand, of course.
I didn't understand how someone could have such a strong will to live.
Even with hands worn by sand and gravel until the white bones were faintly visible, she was still scooping up spring water and sprinkling it towards me.
But at that moment, I suddenly realized... this was probably what the dictionary described as beauty.

She was not a child born to the eager eyes of anticipation.
From early childhood through her teenage years, she lived to serve the demands of her "father" and "keeper."
She served as a meal ticket, a watchful eye... always put to the best use.
But her companions were all exceptionally vivid.
Shou carried a primal, yearning impulse for freedom.
And the captain and deputy captain, despite sharing the same keeper, could decisively rebel.
That girl was even more so.
 
"Demon Gaze? That's a pretty unpleasant name, and Shi doesn't really fit you either."
"Why not go by Shiki? If you're just going to 'gaze' without understanding, what's the point?"
"Understand...? Shiki?"
"Let's put it this way: the samurai book I showed you earlier—did you get it?"
I shook my head.
"If you read those samurai texts but didn't grasp the meaning, it's as good as not having read them at all."
"..."
"...Don't look so hurt. If you want to help with my vengeance, you need to read more carefully and truly understand."
 
Yes, revenge. That fragile girl journeyed alone for years, all to take a life from her enemy.
Shiki couldn't fathom why they'd persist in such an 'unreasonable' quest, yet was powerfully drawn to this burning desire.
Enough to follow in the footsteps of the captain and deputy captain, deserting the Guard to become that person's servant.
Though "servant" hardly seems the right word—Shiki is more like a student.
This renowned writer, her understanding of the world far exceeds expectations.
Landscapes, customs, arts... all the beauty of nature and the world, becoming creative fodder
and teaching material for Shiki to learn.
 
"The situation on Sakura Island is dire. If you want to go back and take a look, don't let yourself get killed easily."
"Go... back?"
"...Do you really want to stay by my side forever?" The Felinian with dark hair tied back in a ponytail said, "I'm already sick of you."
She was radiating an aura of deception, Shiki thought.
"That's enough." That girl said before leaving, "I have my own life to live... and you should live yours too."
 
My own life?
The value of life.
She had no grasp of it... if there was anything to pursue, it was only beauty.
Like when Shou shouted for her to run with him, his flesh wrapped in a brilliant glow.
Like when the captain gave her the dictionary, the book exuded a warm, comforting presence.
Like when the deputy captain's eyes burned with murderous intent, a fierce wind swept across her body.
And like that girl who would never give up on life, every time she mentioned revenge, a shimmering starlight that was hard to let go burst forth.
 
...I see.
I see now.
I was born to witness beauty—that is my purpose, my very reason for living.
Shiki finally grasps the truth of her own being.

What does it feel like to fall for someone?
According to the book, it's like a gentle spring breeze on your face or the warm winter sun melting away the chill...
It's sweeter than pudding, puff pastries, tiramisu, or hot chocolate cakes.

"Creak..."
The door opened, interrupting my thoughts.
"Oh, did I wake you, Mandy? I'm sorry."
It was late at night, and Mom dragged her weary body through the door.
"Mom, I know you work hard. Are you hungry? I can whip up some noodles."
Being young, all I could do in moments like this was offer her comfort with a warm bowl of noodles.
"Aw, you're so sweet, Mandy."

"Blub-blub..."
The noodles boiled in the pot. As the clock struck midnight, the only sound in the room was the bubbling water.
"It's so quiet..."
I began to reflect on the past...
When Dad was still with us. I could vaguely recall the joyful laughter of my parents filling our home.

"Mom, the noodles are ready..."
I added an egg and some chopped onions before bringing the bowl to her.
"Oh!"
Mom was staring at the cabinet where Dad's picture hung. She turned away, concealing the sadness in her eyes.
"Mandy is all grown up now."
A smile broke across Mom's face.

"Mom... do you miss Dad?"
"...Oh, you noticed. Yes, your dad was a very gentle man."
She spoke softly, her smile radiating warmth like a spring breeze.
Seeing her happy expression made me wonder...
"What does it feel like to fall for someone?"

"Meow!"
"Meowww!"
As always, Flora and Furball rushed to my side, nuzzling my feet.
"Hey, Flora, Furball. Did you miss me?"
I knelt down to scratch their chins, and the calico and ragdoll cats purred contentedly.
These two were my closest companions, the reason I looked forward to coming to this little alley every day after school.

Mom and I had been living in Catto City for a while now.
Her business in Yaozhou was thriving, and I had made new friends at school.
Life seemed to flow peacefully and happily.
Yet, whenever I woke up at night, I would see light seeping through the gap under the door, knowing Mom was looking at Dad's picture.

"Hmmm... Flora, Furball, do you know what 'falling for someone' feels like?"
They seemed to understand, leaping onto my lap and licking my cheek.
"Haha, that tickles!"
The golden evening glow enveloped us, shining warmly on me, Flora, Furball, and everything in the alley.

"Clatter..."
A sudden noise disrupted my sweet moment with the cats.
I turned to find the source of the sound and noticed some unfamiliar Pathos Particles nearby, glimmering ominously.

Could it be an Anomaly?
Despite being Felinian, this was my first encounter with one.
"Clatter..."
In the shadows where the setting sun couldn't reach, a Trash Can Anomaly peered at us, exuding a sinister, otherworldly presence.

"Flora! Furball! Climb up!"
I wanted to scoop them up and flee from this place, but they hissed at the Anomaly, trying to protect me.
"Clank clang..."
The Trash Can Anomaly leaped toward us, ready to attack.

"Flora! Furball! It's dangerous! Run!"
I threw off my bag and waved my arms wildly.
"Clank clang..."
The Trash Can Anomaly charged toward us.
"Somebody, please help me!"
I shut my eyes, overwhelmed and helpless.

"Watch out!"
Just in the nick of time, someone stepped in front of me.
"Clang, clang!"
In an instant, the terrifying Trash Can Anomaly was smashed to pieces, leaving behind a haze of dispersing Pathos Particles.

"Are you alright?"
"..."
"Don't worry. I'm the intern Inspector from StormEye, on patrol nearby."
Sensing my unease, the person gently explained, reaching a hand down to me where I sat on the ground, shaken.

I grasped the Inspector's hand; it felt warm.
The setting sun cast a golden glow around the Inspector, painting the sky in shades of orange and red. Against the light, their face was obscured.

My heart was still pounding rapidly. I felt my cheeks flush, mirroring the colors of the sunset.
It was as if my heart melted in that golden light.

A feeling I had never known surged within me, tinting my heart with a soft pink.
"I... I am fine. Th-Thank you..."
Unsure of what to do next, I quickly picked up Flora and Furball and dashed away.

"What happened yesterday felt like a dream..."
I gently stroked Flora and Furball, murmuring to myself. The terrifying incident we faced seemed as unreal as a nightmare.
"Meow! Meow!"
In response to my words, Flora and Furball nudged their heads against my palm.

I closed my eyes, recalling the golden silhouette that had shone brightly in the setting sun.
The warmth of that hand and the words of concern echoed in my mind...
"Are you alright?"
My heart raced again, as if something deep within me melted under the evening glow.
"I don't know if I'm alright anymore..."

Since that day, I had visited the alley every day before and after school, hoping to encounter that mysterious figure again.
Days turned into weeks,
weeks into months...
Seasons changed, and time slipped away.
Mom became busier, often staying in Yaozhou for days at a time.
I moved up a grade at school and adjusted to living alone, but I never saw that enigmatic figure again.

Until one day, I returned to the alley once more...

A familiar shape caught my eye... Could it be...?
"Hello? Is anyone there?"
I pressed my forehead against the glass door and peered inside.
This was a new Pathos Cafe that had opened on Baker Street. The interior was fully furnished, and someone was busy preparing for the grand opening.
Hearing my voice, the person turned and approached the door.

"Wow! Are you the Manager? You look so young! I thought we were about the same age..."
Finally, I had found the person I had missed so much. My heart raced, and I started to stutter.

"A-anyway, sorry for rambling... What I mean is, I'm super excited and happy!"
I was being honest—I was overjoyed!
"Please open soon! I'll be a regular customer! But I must be going now."
My face felt like it was on fire, and my mind went completely blank.
"Darn it! What was I even saying?!"
I bolted away in a panic, just like I had the other day.

The breeze brushed against my face, calming my frantic thoughts.
As dawn broke, light flooded my heart.
But the breeze couldn't cool my flushed cheeks, and the light couldn't clear my oxygen-starved brain.
I felt like all my blood had rushed to my heart, making it pound wildly.
"Is this what it feels like to fall for someone?"

"Good morning, Manager!"
From that day on, Mandy became the first customer at Baker's Cafe almost every morning.
"Well... What do you recommend today, Manager? I'd like something special!"
Her tender smile revealed the shyness of a young girl.

"Good morning! How can I help you today?"
As school and work approached, Baker's Cafe began to buzz with activity.
"Ha! The food is just as delicious as ever!"
"Thanks! I can't wait to see you again!"
The Manager waved goodbye to another satisfied customer, surrounded by cheerful praises.
Mandy felt deeply touched by it all.
"Okay, I've made my decision!"

"I want to learn how to cook when I grow up!"
"Huh? What sparked your interest in cooking, Mandy?"
Her mother was surprised but then seemed to remember something, smiling warmly.
"I believe in you, Mandy. You'll make a fantastic cook! That noodle dish you made for me last time was delicious!"

Delicious food and heartfelt smiles always have a way of soothing the heart. This has always been one of Mandy's strengths.
When I grow up, I could help the Manager!
Mandy thought, a bashful yet bright smile lighting up her face.

"Because... cooking brings us joy and comfort..."
That feeling was sweeter than any pudding, puff pastry, tiramisu, or hot chocolate cake could offer.
"I think I'm falling in love with cooking..."
Pink butterflies began to flutter in Mandy's heart.

"This summer, our whole family's going to the seaside… We'll spend days at the ocean park, and there's even going to be a fireworks festival!"
On the walk home from school, my friend chattered excitedly about her holiday plans. I glanced at the photos on her phone—the endless blue sea, soft white sand—and forced a smile, hiding my envy.

When I opened the door, the living room was quiet as always.
"Will Mom get home early tonight…?"
There was a note on the table, in Mom's familiar handwriting:
Dinner's in the fridge. Don't forget to eat. I might be late tonight—no need to wait up.

I sighed, dropped my bag on the couch, and went to the fridge.

Night fell. I sat on the sofa, book in hand, waiting for Mom to come home.
The clock hit ten. Finally, the key turned in the door.

"Ah… Mandy, you're still up?" Mom came in, looking tired and apologetic.
"Mom!" I hurried over, taking her bag. "You must be tired… Let me get you some water."
"Thank you." She sat, rubbing her temples.
"We've had such a rush of orders lately… I might have to work overtime all summer."
"Mom…"
I wanted to tell her my dream: to go to the beach together, to feel the sand under our feet, to watch the sunrise and sunset…
But seeing her so tired, the words caught in my throat.

"What is it? Did you want to say something?" Mom set her papers aside, looking at me with gentle eyes.
"It's nothing… You should rest early, Mom."

Back in my room, I tossed and turned, unable to sleep. Moonlight filtered through the curtains, shining on the piggy bank on my desk.
"That's it!" I shot up in bed as an idea took shape in my mind.
If I earn the money myself, I can help Mom—and save up enough for both of us to go on that trip…
Just imagining her surprise when I handed her my hard-earned pay made me grin in the dark.
Yes, that's what I'll do!

"Welcome! Which ice cream flavor would you like today?"
Sweat prickled on my forehead, but I kept my best smile in place. Summer had only just begun, yet the heat was relentless, and the line outside our little ice cream shop stretched all the way down the block.
"Two strawberries, extra whipped cream…"
"Chocolate-vanilla swirl, with nuts…"
"Three mango, one taro…"
The orders kept coming, one after another. My hands moved clumsily at the ice cream machine—still awkward, still new.
"Why's it so slow…" someone grumbled in the crowd.
"How much longer is this going to take?"
No matter how fast I went, the line just kept growing, a little more restless with every minute.
Sweat rolled down my cheek as I tried to reassure the customers, pushing myself to move faster. "Sorry! Thank you for waiting, your order will be ready soon…"
A little boy finally made it to the front, eyes wide with hope. "Big sis, can I get two strawberry cones?"
"Of course! Just a moment!" I murmured a quiet sigh of relief. Plain strawberry was the easiest—maybe I could catch my breath.
The strawberry ice cream glistened pink and perfect in the sunlight. I handed him both cones carefully. "Here you go—hold them tight!"
"Thank you, big sis!" He reached out with tiny hands, beaming.
But just as he took them—maybe his hands were sweaty, maybe he was just too excited—
Thud—
Both cones hit the ground, pink cream slowly melting into the tiles. The little boy's smile vanished.
For a moment, everything stopped.
He stared at the ruined ice cream, lips trembling. "My… my ice cream…"
He looked down, voice breaking. "What do I do… I don't have enough money for more… I promised Mei I'd buy her some…"

Some customers craned their necks, wondering why the line had stopped. No one said a word, but I could feel the weight of their stares—some full of sympathy for the little boy, others growing more impatient in the heat.

"It's so hot out here…"
"How much longer do we have to wait?"

The boy's eyes were red now. He clutched the last few coins in his hand, frozen in place, unsure what to do.
My heart softened at the sight.

"Hey, don't be sad!" I hurried around the counter, kneeling beside him. "Big sis will make you two brand new cones—on the house, okay?"
"Really? You mean it?" His eyes, still shiny with tears, looked up at me hopefully.
"Of course!" I ruffled his hair gently. "And this time, I'll make them extra big and extra yummy. Wait right here, okay?"
Back behind the counter, I whipped up two new strawberry cones, piling on a little extra sauce for good measure.
"Here you go! Hold them tight this time!" I wrapped napkins around the cones and passed them to him, careful as could be.

The boy's face lit up again, and he bowed deeply. "Thank you, big sis! You're the best ice cream lady in the whole world!"
Watching him clutch his ice cream and run off, grinning, to a little girl waiting nearby, I felt my own heart lighten with happiness.

"Well done, young lady!" an auntie in the line praised.
"What a sweet thing for the shop to do," another customer nodded.
Maybe it was just my imagination, but the restless crowd seemed a lot more relaxed now. Even the summer heat felt a little less oppressive.

"Thank you all for understanding!" I blushed, hurrying back to work.
Strangely, everything seemed to go smoother after that. Maybe it was the warmth in the air, or maybe I'd finally found my rhythm in the kindness around me.
As I worked, I found myself quietly counting: If I keep this up, I'll have enough by next month to take Mom to the seaside, just like I promised.

"Mandy, the forecast says it's going to rain all week…" The manager frowned at her phone. "Sigh… I'm afraid business will be slow at the ice cream shop…"
Sure enough, the next day, the rain poured down, drumming on the shop's awning. The streets were empty—no one wanted ice cream in this weather.
If business stays this slow… my pay will take a hit, too… I polished the spotless counter, nerves twisting inside me. At this rate, saving enough for our seaside trip would be tough…

The rain kept falling for a whole week.
Today, the sky was still gray and heavy, the air thick with humidity. Hardly any customers came in, but I stood behind the counter, hopeful for anyone to walk through the door.

"Big sis! Ten ice creams, please!"
A cheerful voice made me look up—
It was the little boy from before, the one who'd dropped his cones! A whole group of kids followed him, laughing and chattering.

"It's you!"
He nodded, grinning. "Thank you for helping me that day! I got to share ice cream with Mei—she was so happy!"
He turned to his friends. "This lady is the nicest ice cream worker ever! When I dropped my cones, she made me new ones for free!"
"Really? Wow, you're lucky—we never get nice workers like that!"
"Today's our class party," he explained, "and I brought everyone here because you're the best—and your ice cream is the best, too!"

"I want chocolate!"
"I want vanilla!"
The kids all clamored at once, filling the shop with laughter and warmth.

My eyes grew misty. Who knew that a small act of kindness could bring so much back in return?

"Thank you, everyone!" I beamed. "Today, everyone gets extra toppings—on the house!"
Outside, the sky was still gloomy, but inside, the children's smiles filled the shop with sunshine.

The day I got my paycheck, I hurried home early.
I tied on my apron, humming off-key as I bustled around the kitchen: stir-fried tomatoes and eggs, crisp veggies, and Mom's favorite corn-and-pork rib soup…
A warm dinner was soon ready on the table.

The sound of the key turning in the lock. Mom stepped inside, shoulders drooping with exhaustion.
"Mandy? Home so early? …Wait, what's all this?"
She paused in the doorway, eyes widening as she saw the steaming dishes on the table. The tiredness melted from her face.

"Hehe, it's a little surprise for you, Mom… You work so hard every day~"
"And so do you, my sweet girl." Mom smiled, gently cupping my face.

"Come sit down!" I could barely contain my excitement as I led Mom to the table. "There's another surprise for you!"
From my pocket, I pulled out a pink envelope and handed it to her with both hands.

"What's this…?"
"It's all the money I earned at my part-time job this month!" My eyes shone. "I want to take you on a trip to the seaside—just the two of us! We can watch the sunrise, walk on the sand, eat seafood… everything together!"
Mom opened the envelope—inside, a neat stack of bills, my whole month's hard work. Her hands trembled, and her eyes filled with tears.

"Mandy…" Her voice choked up. "Why didn't you tell me sooner…"
"I wanted it to be a surprise!" I threw my arms around her. "You work so hard every day—I just wanted to do something for you, too."

"Mandy…" She hugged me tight, tears rolling down her cheeks. "You're the best daughter in the whole world…"
As the last light of sunset poured into our home, it wrapped us in a gentle, golden embrace.

What exactly is the feeling of "crush"?
It's like a spring breeze refreshing the heart, like a warm winter sun melting away all the coldness. I see this from the book.
It's sweeter than pudding, puffs, tiramisu, or hot chocolate cake...

"Click"
The front door of the house was opened and the creaking sound interrupted my thoughts.
"Oh, Mandy, I'm sorry, did I wake you?"
It was late at night again, and mom came home with a tired body.
"It's okay, Mom. Let me cook noodles for you."
For the still young me, all I could do was to hand my mom noodles.
"It's been hard on you again."

"Gurrrr."
The noodles tumbled in the pot. The clock on the wall was already pointing to 12, and the boiling noodles echoed in the quiet room.
"It's so quiet."
Unconsciously, my mind went back to the long ago past.
At that time, Dad was still around. In my long blurred memories, the house always seemed to be filled with mom and dad's laughter.

"Mom, the noodles are ready."
Adding eggs and scallions, I walked toward my mom with the cooked noodles.
"Ahh."
Mom was looking at the photo of dad on the cabinet and was lost in thought, as soon as she turned around, she quickly hid the hint of sadness and nostalgia in her eyes.
"My girl is getting more and more capable now."
Mom's face was full of smiles.

"Is mom thinking about dad again?"
"You see that? Well, he is a very gentle man..."
Mom spoke softly and slowly, her face looked like a spring breeze had brushed by.
Looking at mom's happy look, but I was out of my mind-
"What kind of feeling does a crush... really feel like?"

"Meow, meow, meow!"
"Meow."
As usual, as soon as Flower and Fluffy saw me, they lightly called out and stuck over, rubbing themselves against my feet.
"Hey, Flower, Fluffy, you've been waiting for me for a long time, haven't you?"
I squatted down and lightly tickled these two cats at my feet, and they responded with comfortable and cozy purrs.
Every day when I came home from school, I always used to come to this alley first to meet Flower and Furball. They were my closest friends.

It's been a long time since mom and I came to Catto City.
Mom's business in the Yaozhou District was slowly getting better, and I had made some new friends in my new school.
Everything in life seemed to be moving forward in such peace and tranquility.
But whenever I woke up at night, and there was a glimmer of light from the living room coming through the crack of the bedroom door, I knew it was Mom looking at Dad's pictures again.

"Flower, Fluffy, what does it feel like to have your heart moved?"
As if they were listening to my self-talk, Flower and Fluffy leapt onto my body and gently licked my face.
"Hahaha, so itchy."
The evening sun in the distance was golden, warmly reflecting on Flower and Fluffy, on me, and on everything in the alley.

"Crash."
An untimely noise came from behind me, interrupting the cozy time I was enjoying.
Following the sound, I looked back, and there seemed to be more unfamiliar emotional particles in the air, shining with an unsettling shimmer.

Could it be... Anomaly?
Although I'm a Felinian, this is the first time I've encountered such a situation.
"Crash."
In the shadows of the alley not illuminated by the evening sun, a trashcan Anomaly was sizing up this way, its entire body exuding a dark and dangerous aura.

"Flower, Fluffy! Come up here!"
I wanted to pick up the cats and hurry to escape from this dangerous place, but they hissed in a low voice in the direction of the Anomaly, trying to scare off the other party and trying to protect me.
"Bang!"
The Anomaly jumped and rushed towards us.

"Flower, Fluffy! Run!"
I took the bag off my shoulder and waved it wildly in front of me.
"Crash."
The Anomaly was about to rush right in front of us.
"Somebody help me..."
I closed my eyes and cried out helplessly.

"Look out!"
In the nick of time, a figure stepped in front of me.
"Clang!"
In the blink of an eye, the dangerous Anomaly was easily defeated by the human in front of me, leaving only Pathos Particles that dissipated into the air.

"Are you alright?"
"......"
"Don't be afraid, I'm a trainee Inspector from StormEye. I am on patrol duty in the neighborhood."
Perhaps seeing my uneasiness, the person gently and softly explained and extended his hand to me, who was sitting on the ground in shock.

I took the Inspector's hand, and it was warm.
The evening sun continued to emit a golden glow behind this investigator, and also traced a circle of golden light around the inspector's figure, making it impossible for me to see the face.

The heart was still pounding. I felt my cheeks ignite and burn like the clouds illuminated by the evening sun.
It was as if my heart was melting into the golden glow.

A never-before-seen emotion crashed around in my heart, coloring the bottom of my heart pink.
"I'm, I'm... fine. Thank you!"
At a loss for words, I picked up Flower and Fluffy, who were still dazed by my feet, and ran away at speed.

"What happened yesterday... are like a dream yet."
I mumbled to myself as I stroked Flower and Fluffy. Everything that happened in this alley yesterday was as unreal as a dream.
"Meow."
As if responding to my murmuring, Flower and Fluffy leaned their heads against my palms.

When I closed my eyes, what appeared in front of me was the golden silhouette of yesterday's evening sun.
That warm hand, those words of concerns.
"Are you okay?"
My heart started to pound again, something soft in the bottom of my heart, melting into the pink evening sun.
"I don't know, if I'm okay anymore..."

Involuntarily, every day before school and after school I would come to the alley to linger for a moment, expecting to meet that figure again.
One day, two days, three days...
A week, a month, a season...
Time passed, and the seasons turned
My mom's business also became busier, sometimes staying in Yaozhou District for days on end.
I moved up a grade and gradually got used to living alone, but I never encountered the figure that my heart longed for.

Until this day, I came to the alley once again.

A strange yet familiar figure flashed in the corner of my eye.
"Hi! Is anyone there?"
I pressed myself against the glass door and peered inside.
It was the new Cafe on Baker Street, which seemed to have been renovated, and there was someone in the lobby preparing something.
Hearing my voice, the figure turned towards the door.

"Eh. I can't believe it's the Manager? So young! I thought it was someone my own age."
Finally I found the person. My wildly beating heart made me incoherent.

"Ah, that, sorry for talking to myself. Anyway, it's really nice of you guys to come! I am super happy!"

"I'll be sure to come back soon! I have to go now!"
My cheeks felt like they were burning and my mind went blank.
"Ahhhhh, what did I just say."
Just like that day, I ran away again.

There was the wind-blown heat in my cheeks, and my brain was so tense that it was deprived of oxygen.
Probably all the blood rushed into the heart to make it beat so fast!
"Is this, what a crush feels like?"

"Good morning, Manager."
After that, almost every early morning, Mandy was the first customer at the Baker's Cat Cafe.
"What kind of cuisine does... Manager recommend today? I want to try it."
The warm and soft smile was filled with the shyness of a young girl.

"Hello, what would you like to order?"
It was time to go to work and school, and the Cafe was getting lively.
"Uh! Manager's cooking is as good as ever!"
"Thank you, and welcome to the next time."
In the midst of the customer's praise, the manager sent another satisfied customer away.
Mandy, who was on the sidelines, watched all of this.
"Okay! I must do this."

"I... I want to learn cooking!"
"Hey? Why are you suddenly so interested in cooking?"
Mom looked surprised, then seemed to have thought of something and revealed a pleased smile.
"But if it's Mandy, you'll definitely be able to make delicious dishes! Mom still remembers the noodles that you cooked, they were really delicious!"

Yes, good food and a sincere smile can soothe the soul. That's what Mandy has always been good at.
And this way, you'll be able to help the store manager in the future, right?
Mandy thought this in her heart, and a shy yet bright smile unconsciously appeared on her face.

"Because cooking can bring happiness and comfort."
It was a sweeter feeling than pudding, puffs, tiramisu, or hot chocolate cake.
"I'm in love with cooking."
Pink flowers stretched and bloomed in Mandy's heart.

"Eh... Ahem! Good morning!"
"Good morning. You're positively radiant today, Miss Felicia!"
"Thank you for the compliment! So, which flowers can I assist you with today?"
"That's a good question. Let me think about it..."
 
Engaging with the early customer, I begin tending to the flowers.
Perhaps due to my advance order, today's flower delivery is exceptional.
The delicate buds cradle within the lush, coiled leaves, while the stem's dew-kissed thorns shimmer.
 
First, I need to trim the branches and leaves, and then immerse the flowers in water to revitalize them. Once those parched veins are replenished, they will bloom anew...
And then, I can transform my shop into a vibrant, fragrant haven of paradise!
 
"My best friend's wedding is just around the corner."
"What flowers should I bring? I also need to ensure the bouquet complements the dress..."
The customer appears flustered.
 
"Hmm, for a wedding... how about using lilies of the valley as the primary flower? They pair beautifully with a light-colored dress."
"It holds a profoundly romantic significance, symbolizing the 'Return of Happiness.'"
"When you present the bouquet to the newlyweds, it will signify their fresh start towards a joyful life!"
 
"Wow! Fresh and exquisite... lilies of the valley it is! Thank you, Miss Felicia!"
"You're very welcome! Your bond must be truly special! A friendship to be admired!"
 
With the bouquet details settled, I bid farewell to the day's inaugural customer.
I then unlatch the quaint picket gate and flip the sign to signify that we're open.

Baker Street bustles with activity these days, boasting convenient transportation links.
The streets are adorned with elegantly designed establishments, ranging from cozy cafes to chic boutiques and cutting-edge tech stores.
Nestled next to a restaurant named "Baker's Cafe" is my flower shop.
 
In no time, I forged a bond with my new neighbors—
a delightful bunch of Felinians, accompanied by a spirited young human.
"Hello, delighted to make your acquaintance! Just call me Felicia!"
 
Right from the start, we hit it off splendidly.
I'd treat them to homemade delights, and in return, they'd bestow upon me charming, whimsical little trinkets.
However, as time passed, I began to unravel some "mysteries" concerning my neighbors—their movements and activities veiled in a shroud of secrecy.
It wasn't just where they went... It was their "true identities."
 
Their cafe attracted a familiar crowd, including notable figures from diverse spheres.
One twilight evening, I even glimpsed...
Ah, yes, I'm quite certain it was... the renowned superstar Triss.
 
As night descended, fans wielding cameras and signs still thronged the streets.
I caught sight of her silhouette through the glass window, I was taken aback!
My initial awe swiftly transformed into concern—what if the fans swarmed her, impeding her escape?
Or worse, what if she became fodder for the tabloids the following day?
 
So I invited her in, suggesting she could stay until the crowd left. However, the gracious lady declined my offer.
"I am familiar with this area. I shan't attract any undue attention."
"I am grateful for your kindness, Miss Felicia. I'm certain our paths will cross again."
With that, Triss bid her farewells and vanished into the night.
 
She possessed an intimate knowledge of the locale, even addressing me by name.
...Is such behavior typical for someone of her stature?
 
...Forget it. Do not pry into matters that do not concern you, and refrain from intervening in affairs that are not your own.
Despite my burning curiosity, those were the principles instilled in me by my parents as proper decorum.

"Oh... it's nearly time to close up once more."
"I still have an abundance of champagne roses... They won't remain fresh until tomorrow..."
 
The sunset tints the clouds crimson, casting a reflection on the shop window.
The hanging cat figurine sways gently, its pink tongue mirrored in the crystal-clear glass.
 
"What should I do with them? Ah, I've got it!"
 
Roses, bamboo baskets, ribbons, floral foam, and nutrient solution...
All these items are already stocked in the shop.
 
Delicately bending the champagne rose stems with pliers, I embed them into the floral foam.
Then, I trim the ribbon and fashion a dainty bow on the basket's handle.
 
"All set! Now they won't go to waste."
Crafting a sign that reads "Feel free to take," I position it in the basket.
Finally, I bring out a pristine white table and place it outside the shop.
"Wishing you an evening filled with romance and cherished memories."
 
Now, regarding the remaining flowers...
Surveying the store, I observe several flowers still in the water buckets, untouched.
While some may endure, others may wither by tomorrow morning.
I can't bear to witness those... forlorn, wilting flowers.
 
"Well, then I'll transform them into desserts!"
"At the very least, you would prefer to be surrounded by those brimming with love, wouldn't you?"
"Thank you for your sacrifice. They'll be devoured in no time!"
 
As night descends upon the city from the horizon,
all the shops on Baker Street light up for the evening.
 
The process of crafting floral cakes isn't overly intricate, but it demands ample patience.
I slip on gloves and secure a cat-themed apron around my waist.
Everything is prepared, and I'm all set to begin—

I begin by preparing the dough and crafting the pastry,
eager to utilize the floral jam that has been patiently waiting in my fridge since its creation six months ago.
The surplus roses are a perfect addition to replenish my inventory.
 
"Ding-dong!"
The doorbell chimes, signaling an unexpected visitor despite my shop being closed for the day.
—Who could it be?
 
"Coming! Just a second!"
I swiftly tidy my hands on my apron, remove my gloves, and make my way to the door.
 
"Pardon me, Miss Felicia, but could I still purchase some flowers?"
"...!!"
 
It's... the neighbor from Baker's Cafe,
the vivacious individual always surrounded by Felinians, scarcely finding a moment of solitude.
 
"We've closed for the day..."
"But since you've asked, I'll see what I can do!"
 
One hand clad in a glove, the other damp with water,
and my apron speckled with flour—
I feel utterly unprepared and a touch flustered.
 
"S-Sorry, I... I'll attend to it right away. Just a moment."
"My apologies for the inconvenience, Miss Felicia. Have I arrived at an inopportune time?"
The youthful neighbor beams brightly, their eyes sparkling as they regard me.
 
I wish to respond, "No, not at all," but find myself...
Struggling to articulate even the simplest of phrases.
 
W-what's happening?
Despite being a grown woman, I am still...
Overwhelmed by a surge of emotions that I could not suppress.
 
"Seems like something special is afoot for you to be purchasing flowers this late, huh?"
"Well, in that case..."
I decided to include some additional small gifts.
 
The mental image of the recipient bowing to inhale the blossoms' fragrance always warms my heart.
As I wrap the flowers in pink paper and secure them with a ribbon, I envision this heartwarming scene.

Felicia, a Felinian born and bred in Catto City,
led a remarkably uneventful life compared to her feline kin.
 
Blessed with a tranquil existence that others envied,
she reveled in a harmonious family where her parents' enduring love shaped her character.
Radiating warmth, Felicia always sported a smile, embodying kindness and optimism in every facet of her life. Her perspective on the world brimmed with compassion and benevolence.
 
Yet, even the most docile cat can feel the allure of the unknown. As she matured, the yearning to venture beyond her familiar surroundings intensified.
The family's boundaries and her parents' deep affection began to feel like shackles hindering her quest for freedom.
 
"I can't continue like this... Perhaps it's time for a change?"
"Might as well take a leap."
 
Summoning the courage to voice her aspirations, Felicia encountered no resistance.
It dawned on her—her parents' love wasn't a restraint but a guiding force propelling her forward.
"Mom and Dad will always support you. Remember to reach out if you ever need help, okay?"
 
With determination, Felicia embarked on her journey towards independence. Though met with initial challenges, she gradually acclimated to her newfound autonomy.
Achieving her childhood dream, she returned to Baker Street and established a charming flower shop.
 
While the shop's profits were modest, every corner exuded Felicia's heartfelt essence,
radiating an eternal beauty and romance that mirrored her inner world.
 
Notably, her neighbors were a delightful addition to her life.
Encountering them before sunset never failed to uplift her spirits for the remainder of the day.
 
"This is quite tiring... What treats should I whip up to express my gratitude?"
"I'll include them with today's bouquet... Perfect, all sorted!"
 
It's the gentle sunshine and the brilliant dawn.
Bright and steady, like hope.
 
This is what she holds onto in her heart.

"Hoo...hoo..."
After finishing the jog, I stood in place, calming my rapid breaths.

Jogging, high knees, speed sprints, juggling drills, dribbling around cones, and finally back to jogging. All done! I can now submit the assignments given by the coach! But for me, this can only be considered a warm-up!

"Hehe~ Now it's my own time! Look~ the ball!"
A round soccer ball, stationed right in the center of the open space. I sprinted at an angle and, using a tricky approach, kicked the stationary ball into the air! Swift shot! Spiraling! Mini goal, shattered from a long distance!

"Wow~! Big sister is amazing! The ball flew so far...!"
Wrapped in thick winter clothes, the chubby little boy looked at me with eyes almost twinkling like stars.

When did my audience appear?! Oops, I completely didn't notice... However, this genuine recognition is making me so happy! In this cold and gloomy winter, there are actually people like me, focusing on sports!

"So envious of big sister's strength!"
"I also want to be like big sister, running in such cold weather and effortlessly kicking the ball so far!"
"Oh, that... it's nothing! I'm still far from those top-notch players!"

Curious and wonderful! His gaze is just like when I first saw that soccer ball blasting into the goal. Well, of course! Who wouldn't love the explosive passion and power on the field!

"If you love soccer, come watch a game! The winter break is almost over, and the league is about to begin!"
His eyes lit up instantly.
"Really? Can I? Can I come watch big sister play?"
"Of course! You must come watch me! My name is Trueheart!"

Fantasy is always so beautiful! But reality, alas, always disappoints...

After the winter break, the soccer field finally witnessed the long-awaited match. However, just as reason had predicted, the audience trickled away, seemingly untouched by any emotions stirred by the game. Even the young boy who trained with me that day didn't appear in the stands. Well, after all, we, like our opponents, are just unknown amateur teams...

"Congratulations! You've secured victory with absolute dominance!"
"So, let's interview the forward combination that also showed outstanding performance in this confrontation~"
"Winning, any secrets? Is it more diligent training, stricter diet, or..."
The microphone was handed to me, and the shivering young reporter in front of me, seriously asked the prepared questions.

"Yes! We usually fully follow the coach and team doctor's plans..."
"—Is there really a need for an interview?"
My voice was interrupted.
"We won't appear in any media at all... Miss Reporter, you should be aware, right?"
"The attendance rate is always so low... Even if we win, no one cares at all..."
The speaker was my teammate, the most reassuring presence in the team. The young reporter lowered her head, slightly nervously covering her intern journalist badge on her chest. The answer was evident, and a sense of discouragement spread throughout the team.

This low pressure continued into the locker room. The pre-prepared confetti and fireworks seemed to be forgotten by everyone. The solemn atmosphere needed to be shattered! And I—Sincerely, chose to be that breakthrough!

"Come on, everyone! Cheer up!"
"Although the audience's numbers are still small, it's much more than before!"
"And as long as we keep winning, we'll encounter stronger teams, presenting even more exciting confrontations!"
"Exciting matches won't come to us on their own, so, everyone, keep running!"
"The next match is on the weekend, we need to train hard!"

Thank goodness, these words had an effect. Everyone's faces were once again filled with determination. Indeed! What's better than a thrilling and exhilarating showdown to vent our emotions! The next game, here we come!

"Vina! Vina! Vina!"
The Lioncat Stadium was packed. Cheers and screams filled the air, drilling into my ears.
They were calling the name "Vina," and I was indeed a member of "Vina."

Ah... I almost forgot to mention!
Due to my outstanding performance last season, I earned a spot in the Vina Football Club.
This spot was voted on by the entire team.

"But Coach... everyone is working as hard as I am! Why... only me?"
"Vina, that's how sports are. Hard work is essential, and so are results. Everyone recognizes you as the strongest, and you deserve this spot."
"Moreover, as long as you shine brightly, our team will attract more attention, giving everyone more opportunities!"
"The stronger you become, the more motivation everyone has to catch up. So, work hard to become an example for everyone, got it, Vina!"
"Yeah! I will show the entire New Sea City that a superstar is born!"

"Vina! Snap out of it!"
Returning to reality, teammates in blue jerseys embraced me tightly!
"Are you nervous? It's normal for newcomers to be nervous. Just play steadily!"

"We've all experienced that mix of excitement and fear!"

Lost in the warmth of care and encouragement, I completely forgot—
I don't even have time to be nervous anymore!
"Yeah! I'll show you guys—the most beautiful goal!"

The time of free-running on the field always passes swiftly. Were it not for perspiration saturating my jersey and the resounding beat of my heart in my ears, I might have forgotten! The match has progressed to the second half, both sides deadlocked, yet everyone's stamina is nearly depleted.

"Really, the opposition has abandoned scoring, focusing solely on targeting us!" During halftime, the captain specifically advised me. "Those fellows are far from being paragons of ethical sportsmanship; you must safeguard yourself. Losing the ball, we can recover, but an injury might mean missing future matches."

"Sunny! Be ready to receive!" Laden with the trust of my teammates, the football, possessed of absolute power, spins towards me. Without room for hesitation or contemplation, I immediately sprint forward and launch a kick! "Hey—!"

Wait! A figure emerging diagonally crashes directly in front of me. A few milliseconds of hesitation, a shift in force, and the trajectory of the ball deviates. — The ball has been intercepted?!

No time for further contemplation, I decisively accelerate towards the football! Yet, another figure suddenly appears, attempting to obstruct my path. "Newcomer, isn't it? Hehe, it's time to experience the cruelty of the field!"

"Thud, thud, thud!" The heartbeat amplifies, time slows down, as if a spotlight has focused on the ball.

Now! It's this very moment! Grant me — a goal~!! In my heart, there is only victory!

"An impeccable goal! From the new player of Vina—True Heart! I have to say, this score is crucial!"

When True Heart came to her senses, the score stood at 4:2.

In the excited crowd, True Heart saw the figures of her former coach and teammates.

In that moment when her body left the ground, True Heart, burning like her blood was on fire, felt a strange dizziness for the first time.

"From an amateur player to a professional athlete, it takes a lot of luck and skill! Can you share with us?"

She was surrounded by countless people, and questions came one after another, like waves crashing over her.

Once again, True Heart saw the reporter who had interviewed her when she was on the amateur team. Now, she had become a sports journalist capable of standing on her own.
Everyone is making progress!

Facing the flashes and microphones, True Heart showed no signs of stage fright.
This was an overwhelming enthusiasm and the best affirmation of her efforts!

"First of all, thank you all for your concern!"
She answered each question methodically.
"Thanks to Vina's favor and the selfless help of my teammates~"
"I was very happy when I played soccer with everyone in the amateur team! Without them, I couldn't have entered Vina."
"My performance... I hope I haven't disappointed everyone who supports me! I will continue to work hard~!"

"Oh, by the way, we heard that Miss True Heart is the daughter of the Lion Cat family?"
"Huh? Oh? You guys even know about that! As a member of the Lion Cat family, I really hope I haven't embarrassed the family!"
"From the first day I started playing soccer, I've always wanted to walk into the sports arena named after our family as an honored athlete!"
