Her future is still a long way off.
In front of the camera, True Heart flashed a radiant smile."

On nights when the moon shines brightly and the stars fade into the background, I find a profound sense of tranquility.
As always, I sit alone in the pavilion, lost in my thoughts, with the moon as my only companion.
Its light is pure and radiant as if it silently watches over me.
 
The cool night breeze does little to dispel the drowsiness that accompanies my mild inebriation.
In this hazy state, it feels as though my body is wrapped in soft fabric.
Warm and weightless, like floating on a cloud.
Might it be that the moon has deigned to cradle me in its embrace?
I know that is merely the workings of my imaginative mind at play.
 
As I groggily open my eyes, I'm met with a face as serene and cold as the moonlight.
"Awake? It's time to return to your quarters, master."
 
"Mmh... Everly..."
Her deep blue eyes shimmer under the night sky, filled with earnestness.
Yet, despite the closeness, I still struggled to read her emotions, just as I often did.
Still, I know she truly cares for me.
"...I'm drunk. Take me back."
I wrap my arms around her slender neck, feeling her body stiffen as she worries about any misstep that might harm me.
I can't help but enjoy putting her in such predicaments; her troubled expression is quite entertaining.
 
"I know you're not drunk. You've never really been inebriated..."
Everly's voice is soft and gentle, like the night breeze.
Unfortunately, after spending so much time by my side, the charming shyness she once had has become increasingly rare.
 
"...Mmh, then I shall rest here. Do not concern yourself with me..."
I pout, releasing her and transforming into a cat, turning away from her.
 
"Pardon the interruption, master."
In an instant, I find myself lifted and enveloped in a warm embrace.
 
You see, she is always so gentle with me.
 
However, the Everly I first met was quite different.

From the rich tapestry of Lunar City's legends, one figure stands apart as a revered, divine being—Loong.
It is said that Loong once wandered through the desolate lands of Lunar City by chance.
Though the visit was brief, the deity became enchanted by the moonlight that illuminated the area.
Determined that all of Lunar City bask in the moon's resplendent glow,
Loong harnessed their powers to channel waterways,
drawing rivers together to transform the barren landscape into a thriving, mountainous region.
 
Everly was born into the Moonkeepers, a clan that devoutly worships Loong.
They revere the deity as the Creator and have dedicated their lives to guarding what they believe to be Loong's sacred dwelling.
 
The reclusive Moonkeepers live high in the mountains, seldom interacting with outsiders.
Their lush, green home nurtures a nearby spring,
and inexplicably, a field of azure evening stars flourishes beside it.
These blossoms possess petals that shimmer like precious gems, but only in the moonlight.
Much like Loong, who seems to cherish the moon above all else,
the Moonkeepers regard these flowers as the embodiment of their deity, with the spring serving as their sacred sanctuary.
 
This too had piqued my interest,
but the opportunity for outsiders to experience it directly is all but unheard of.
Well, typically speaking.
 
Under the cover of night, I skillfully bypassed the Moonkeepers' defenses from above using my Mirror of Myriad.
For them, the lone figure they would anticipate to descend from the celestial realm would be the revered deity...
I ascended against the gentle current of the spring waters.

 Surprisingly, once I had penetrated the forbidden domain, the level of vigilance seemed to have diminished.
They truly hold this place in reverence—a "sacred sanctuary" even their own cannot approach.
This only fueled my curiosity.
 
Not long after, a luminous patch of azure seized my attention at the edge of my field of vision.
I moved with haste towards the sight and was greeted by a vast ocean of flowers.
"So, these are... the evening stars."
 
Their breathtaking azure hue was mesmerizing...
Could there be living beings in this world that radiate such pure Pathos Particles?
It made me wonder if this field was merely an illusion.
 
Compelled by my doubts, I slowly reached out my hand.
Suddenly—
"Don't touch them!"

"I told you not to touch it!"
A stern, icy reprimand cut through the air behind me, tinged with suspicion.
I turned to see a human with hair that shimmered like evening stars,
and a genuine delight surged within me.
The matching pristine Pathos Particle, the identical enchanting azure tone...
"Who are you?"
My curiosity about beautiful things was instantly ignited.
 
"That's what I should be asking. Hmm, who are you... and what brings you here?"
Her voice carried a faint hint of pain, sounding weary.
"Does my identity really matter?"

 Suddenly, her brow furrowed.
Even in her anger, her beauty was striking enough to stir something deep within me.
Yet, this beauty seemed to carry a heavy weight.
As I stepped closer, I noticed beads of sweat glistening on her forehead.
The overwhelming Pathos Particles radiating from her made it clear she was struggling under their burden. 

"You don't seem in a position to leisurely listen to my answers."
"Hah... how would you know unless you try?"
She was more stubborn than I had anticipated.
"Your speed is impressive, but your movements are still unrefined. It seems your body hasn't fully adapted to this power..."
I easily deflected her attack. Strangely, my words only seemed to amplify the chaos of her Pathos Particles.
"At this rate, you'll be completely overwhelmed by Pathos Particles..."
"Pathos Particles?"
A flicker of uncertainty crossed her face.

 Ah, she is completely unaware of what's happening. 

"Don't you feel the pain? Don't you want to know why you've become this way?"
"...What's it to you?"
"Well... it's because of these azure evening stars, isn't it?"
The blade aimed at me hesitated for a moment, confirming my suspicion and deepening my smile.
"What if... I could help you?"

I find joy in sharing moments with beautiful things,
yet the person before me doesn't seem to share that sentiment.

 Following my utterance, her antagonism towards me visibly softened, if only somewhat.
Perhaps my sincere gaze touched her, or maybe she realized I was not someone she could easily intimidate.
Eventually, she hesitated and questioned the truth of my words.
"Can you... really do this?"
"Of course. I never speak empty promises."
Curiously, our family presently a prestigious antique house in Yaozhou, once belonged to a medical clan focused on the research of Pathos Particles.
In those days, they made significant strides in treating ailments caused by these particles, even if they ultimately couldn't overcome the challenge entirely.
The only remnant of their research is the sealed Time-bending Hourglass, buried beneath their ancient manor and left untouched.
While their studies may have been set aside like that of Hourglass, they were not without merit.
 
Obtaining the Moon Stones as a birthday gift kindled my curiosity, driving me to explore the family's ancient texts.
It appears they created the Time-bending Hourglass to treat Pathosis, inspired by their discovery of Moon Stones.
 
These Moon Stones are unlike ordinary gems.
They exhibit varying luminescence based on the Pathos Particle composition of the bearer.
More importantly, they seem to regulate the P-value.
For Felinians, they serve as stable amplifiers for their abilities,
while for regular humans, they act as an "elixir" that maintains Pathos Particle equilibrium.
 
"What is this?"
she asked, intrigued as I presented the Moon Stones.
"Look, this is the moon I've brought for you."
I pointed to the waning crescent in the sky, its shape mirroring that of the Moon Stone.
"..."
"Hehe, this can help you. Hold onto it, and you'll soon understand." 

As she grasped the Moon Stone, it began to emit a soft, azure glow in her hand.
Undoubtedly, a fair beauty paired with a magnificent gem—the gem only serving to enhance the allure of its wearer.
 
"...Huh? How is this possible?"
"Does it hurt as much anymore?"
"...Is it really alright now?"
"No, this will only ease your pain. Your transformation into a Darkrift is irreversible."
 
"A Darkrift?"
She seemed completely unaware of this...
"Yes, but before I explain further, you should at least tell me... your name."
 
"Everly."
"Haha... how fitting for this particular evening."

The fateful encounter between Celena and Everly began on a moonlit night when the blue evening stars were in full bloom.
Celena had come here out of mere curiosity,
never anticipating that she would cross paths with Everly.
Likewise, Everly could hardly have imagined being rescued by this seemingly carefree Felinian.
 
Later, Everly recounted the events that unfolded around her.
On the night of the year-end full moon, the Moonkeepers performed a purification ritual known as the "Lunar" rite.
Under the cover of darkness, everyone would descend into the river below the mountain springs to bathe in the moonlight,
cleansing themselves of the impurities accumulated over the past year in hopes of welcoming the new year.
 
After the purification ceremony, the Chieftain would select a newly matured maiden to become the "Moonkeeper Star" of "Loong," destined to enter the divine realm.
However, Everly remembered that those chosen as "Moonkeeper Stars" who ventured into the divine domain never returned.
The clan accepted this without question,
as the Chieftain claimed that those who disappeared had been chosen by "Loong" to remain by their side.
And they would be bound to the deity's presence forevermore.
 
Year after year, the Moonkeepers faithfully upheld these purification rituals.
This time, it was Everly who was chosen to become the "Moonkeeper Star."
 
Upon entering the divine realm, at the Chieftain's command, Everly plucked an evening star revered as a "sacred plant."
The Chieftain informed her that consuming the evening star would allow her to hear the true words of the deity.
 
Following the instruction, Everly consumed the flower.
Almost immediately, she felt a raging power surging within her—
one she could neither suppress nor control. The overwhelming agony caused her to lose consciousness.
Just before slipping away, she heard the Chieftain's exasperated sigh, as if lamenting,
 
"Ah, the deity has opted not to make an appearance yet again, I see? And we have gathered so many..."
 
When Everly finally awoke, she found herself in an unfamiliar mountain cave.
There was no time to comprehend what had happened or how long she had been unconscious.
Lacking the strength to move, she could only remain in the cold cave, praying for her body to recover before it was too late.
As time passed, she suddenly heard a woman's voice.
 
"I was the one who brought you back to consciousness—I can't help but feel quite pleased about that!"
Each time Celena revisits this memory, she finds herself unable to resist a playful taunt.
"Back then, you truly were an intruder."
Everly responds at a leisurely pace.
 
"But even I was surprised. You, who had just obtained the Moon Stone, unpredictably awakened your abilities."
"It was less a matter of abilities and more one of wish fulfillment..."
"Oh? A wish, you say? What manner of wish compelled you to expend your strength in sealing off that divine realm?"
 
Everly maintained her silence, but Celena grasped the core of her unspoken wish.
It was a straightforward wish—to prevent such tragedies from happening again.
Nevertheless, what Celena failed to grasp was that—
as the last "Moonkeeper Star," Everly had already found her "deity."

"Another gift, is it?"
Before my young eyes lay a stunning snake-shaped golden bracelet, embellished with vibrant rubies.
 
"This exquisite piece comes from the ancient kingdom once known as the 'Golden Desert.' With your 10th birthday approaching, your father..."
The servant dutifully presented yet another rare treasure my father had acquired from distant lands.
 
While the intricately crafted bracelet was undeniably beautiful, I couldn't shake the feeling that...
Its allure had been marred by the greed of its acquisition.
To me, it had transformed into nothing more than beautiful refuse.
 
"I see... Please put it away."
"...As you wish, milady."
 
I certainly appreciate all forms of beauty.
As the heiress of an antique house, I've encountered countless so-called treasures.
Yet, what I truly treasure is the pure, unique "luster" that emanates from the Pathos Particles within these objects.
I often find myself pondering their origins and the transformations of their radiant, variegated essence.
 
To capture these Pathos Particles, I frequently use a Mirror of Myriad, preserving them as wondrous gemstones.
 
I never grow tired of admiring these stones.
Over time, I've realized that...
Be it the heartfelt sentiments embedded within these items or the artisanal fervor in their crafting,
the 'obsessions' ingrained in their essence are what unveil their true beauty.
 
It's a pity my father seems unable to grasp this, merely assuming I'm enamored with rare trinkets.
I have no desire to elaborate further.
To someone so consumed by family and business, my words would likely be dismissed as mere whimsy.
 
"If you would, please inform my father that he is not expected to send such things anymore."
"But..."
The servant's countenance betrayed a troubled look until another voice unexpectedly chimed in.
 
"Now, what's troubling my darling daughter?"
"Nothing, it's just... I already have plenty of such things."
"So... you're dissatisfied with the gifts I've brought?"
"—Just tell me what you desire, and I shall spare no expense to acquire it for you.."
 
"Really...?"
Overcome by a mischievous impulse, I pointed towards the moon above, intent on teasing my self-assured father.
"Then why not pluck that moon from the sky and give it to me?"
 
Father paused, clearly taken aback by my response.
But soon, he burst into laughter.
"Haha! Very well, I shall fetch the moon for you."

A new gift was personally presented to me by my father just a few days later.
"These are the Moon Stones, presenting nine distinct pieces, each representing a different phase of the moon."
As I marveled at the jade stones, I found myself captivated, barely registering his subsequent words.
 
"They're stunning..."
That was the only thought I could muster at that moment.
Though the stones appeared unrefined, not a single flaw marred their surface.
They were breathtaking—pristine and ethereal, like immortal maidens captured in a painting.
Neatly arranged on sapphire silk, they emitted a soft, gentle glow reminiscent of moonlight.
Faced with such breathtaking beauty, I struggled to find words that could express my feelings.
...It was quite disappointing.
 
"Well? Are you pleased, my dear?"
Snapping back to reality, I pulled my hand away just before touching the Moon Stones.
"Thank you for the gift, Father. I love it, but I'm curious about where they came from..."
 
"These were unearthed by our ancestors as natural gemstones."
"Natural gemstones? So the Pathos Particles within formed naturally?"
 
"Yes, it's hard to believe, I know, but it's true."
My father, mid-speech, retrieved a Moon Stone from the box, holding it up as if to display it.
"Additionally, the Moon Stones have the remarkable ability to change in accordance with the holder's inner state."
Before long, delicate green motes emerged within the Moon Stone's luminous glow,
akin to fireflies flickering in a summer night sky.
"Cee, why don't you give it a try?"
 
As I grasped the Moon Stone, the previous "fireflies" vanished,
replaced by a deep crimson hue enveloping the stone.
"It really changed... These stones are incredible."
At that moment, I couldn't tell if I felt surprised or delighted.
 
"But the wonders of these stones don't end there..."
"Don't end there?"
"Perhaps it's still too complex for you to grasp right now. When you're older, I promise to explain.
"How can you say that when you haven't told me anything yet?"
"Haha, why, the knowledge you'll uncover as you come of age is boundless..."
 
"..."
Once again, I felt that familiar frustration—my father always seemed to expect me to mature while withholding information.
"Then why give me this Moon Stone? It's hardly just a simple birthday gift."
 
"The Moon Stones represent the position of Family Head, which you will one day inherit from me. That is why I present this to you now."
He handed me the box containing the Moon Stones.
"For now, just consider it a gift."
 
This was one of those rare "gifts" that lingered in my memory.
Yet at that time, I didn't fully understand the deeper "meaning" behind this "gift."

Naturally, he had plans for me to assume some responsibilities in the family's antique business.

"You must never enter Hydora Manor without my permission."

"The Time-bending Hourglass is, in reality, just an ordinary disc."

"This is an inescapable fate and duty for anyone born into this family."

"I understand you are still young and carefree. I don't mean to burden you with everything at once..."
"Father, you're still so full of energy. Isn't it a bit early for me to take on the family business?"

"I see..."
I responded absently, fiddling with the beautiful jade stones.
 
"Ah, right..."
My father suddenly seemed to remember something important as he looked at me with intention.
"I believe I entrusted you with something significant on your 10th birthday..."

a cruel twist of fate indeed.
I had to admit, it was a clever tactic.
Though I tried to hide it, my hesitation revealed my inner conflict.
The smile on his face was infuriating.
 
If guarding the Hourglass was a given, I might as well use it as my "bargaining chip" for freedom.
After all, the Time-bending Hourglass held greater importance than the family business.
I refused my father's initial request for me to inherit the business, proposing that the Hourglass be my condition.

"You may avoid the business, but as the future Family Head, you can't afford to fail."

For a long time, I had dreamed of a secret trove—
a sanctuary to hide all the beautiful things I cherished.
I envisioned it as a place where I could gaze at the moon, a kind of fairyland.
Yes, it would be a fairyland...
My treasure trove, both real and imagined.
Only the things I hold dear would be allowed to enter.

In Lunar City of Yaozhou, whispers of a captivating legend have circulated for ages.
It is said that when the moon rises high above the treetops, a mysterious place materializes along the cloud-draped shores of Stellar Lake.

The so-called "celestial realm" turned out to be a treasure trove filled with countless rare and extraordinary riches.
Its shelves shimmered with exquisite gems and jewels, each one more dazzling than the last.

their worth transcended mere currency.
 
Yet, the most captivating of all amidst these riches of immeasurable worth—
were the stones—
rumored to grant any wish...
...
 
Thus,
the "Antiquities Atrium" rose to legendary status, a dreamlike vision reminiscent of flowers reflected in a mirror.

patiently awaiting the footsteps of those who sought their desires.

Ugh, damn it all...
Why are you wretches staring at me with those accusing eyes?!
What mixed blood? What taboo?!
I won't let you filthy pests trample on me and mock my existence!
Begone! All of you, just die!
 
My memories are like shattered shards of a mirror, flickering in the darkness but never forming a complete picture.
Dim, sordid fragments appear clear one moment and hazy the next, like an old film reel looping in my mind, each frame piercing me with icy coldness.
Whenever I try to focus on them, a thick fog clouds my vision.
The jeers and taunts echo in my ears, leaving me with the crushing weight of despair.
 
Aaaagh, I hate this!
At some point, I started recalling snippets of the past.
That girl keeps appearing in the fragments—she looks similar but feels so unfamiliar...
No, that's not me...
Her mind is consumed by thoughts of death...
It's likely because yesterday, today, and tomorrow are all unbearably wretched, making the end feel inconsequential.
 
But why... why do I see her memories?
Fuzzy and fragmented, utterly irritating...
Whenever I try to delve deeper, an invisible force tightens around my head, the pain intensifying, like thousands of needles stabbing my skull or an unseen power tearing my thoughts apart.
 
Why concern myself with the past?
That tattered, worthless relic—do I truly need to retain any memory of it?
To me, those hazy recollections are but meaningless scraps,
superfluous trash better off forgotten entirely!

The past holds no sway over me now. I live with a freedom and boldness that surpasses all others.
This "family" I now have, who truly care for me...
It is all thanks to the grace of my master.
So I'm willing to give everything for my master,
for the "family" that loves me.
 
Night has fallen, and the once-bustling port now lies silent.
The salty sea breeze drifts through the abandoned docks and ships.
From high above, I pursue the "pest," destined for its demise.
 
The flickering port lights cast everything below in a sharp, diminished glow.
I tread lightly, making as little noise as possible.
My heartbeat syncs with the night—a sensation I know well.
 
Despite knowing their fate is inescapable, the pest continues to flee in utter desperation. What could they be so stubbornly clinging to?
"Haa—Haa—"
The fleeing man gasps for breath, occasionally glancing back at me.
His face is a complex mix of sweat and fear, eyes filled with primal terror of the unknown and a fierce instinct for survival.
I can sense that the man has reached his limit, both physically and mentally.
Soon, the one who ran into a dead end stumbles, collapsing in disarray.
 
"What's wrong? Giving up on running?"
I land gracefully, approaching step by step.
The pest can only shuffle backward into the corner.
"Wh-Why... Why are you here? Where's that gentleman?!"

"Aagh, my leg!"
The pitiful cries echo through the silent port.
At that moment, I realized the sickle in my hand had already pierced the man's left leg.
 
This won't do—it'll get messy.
 
I quickly retract the blade, wiping away the stains with care.
"Hmph, you? You're not worthy of seeing my master..."
 
"Stay back! Stay back!!!"
Despair morphs into anger.
A feeble, flickering attempt to fight back.
Soon, this weak "pest" finds himself cornered among the clutter.
With nowhere to escape, he instinctively lashes out, throwing anything he can grab—old boards, ropes, even sharp nails—at me with all his might.
 
"Damn, can't you just let me finish this peacefully?"
His desperate struggles have drained my patience.
With a flash of the blade, his life is swiftly extinguished.
Blood gushes as he finally falls still, the anger in his eyes fading away.
 
"Ah, finally some peace and quiet... I should've done this sooner."
Completing my task for my master lifts my spirits.
But now,
I face a pressing question—how should I dispose of this "trash"?
Glancing toward the calm sea, I make my decision.
"Hmm, got it! Into the ocean!"

Beyond just cleaning up "trash" for my master, I have an even more important duty—
escorting homeless children to their rightful place.
The Pathos Energy within them will fuel the detonation of the Pathos Drop Points, and I'm responsible for ensuring my master's plan unfolds seamlessly.
Each time the Pathos Drop Points explode, I feel the bone-deep pain of the blast,
but I can endure it—I won't die...
Haha... only I can do this.
My master says this is a task meant for me alone.
 
Ah, to be so needed by my master... it gives me purpose.
  
"Waaah, where are you taking us?"
Suddenly, the childish cries shatter my tranquility.
 
"Ah?!"
The unexpected interruption makes me lower my voice, glaring at them to be quiet.
The child immediately freezes, eyes wide with fear.
But at that moment, a strange, blurred face seems to overlap with theirs—
one I've never truly seen yet somehow recognize.
Just like those damned dreams, the moment I try to focus on it, a sharp pain throbs in my head.
"Dammit..."
 
I don't need this.
I only need my master, my "family"...
 
As the pain subsides, my vision clears.
"Shut up and come with me obediently!"
I realize I've been too lenient with these brats, allowing them to be so noisy.
 
Yes, I just need to follow my master's instructions and take them to the designated place.
All that matters now is serving my master...

All that matters now is serving my master.
Somewhere along the way, this singular notion has come to dominate Mink's every thought.
Born of mixed blood, part human and part Felinian, she lacks the ability to transform like other Felinians.
The flaws in her body serve as a constant reminder of her parents' forbidden union.
Such unconventional behavior should never have occurred.
The people of Catto City are meant to live in the light, rejecting even the slightest impurity.
Consequently, her parents abandoned both their conscience and their daughter, who bore the burden of their sin.
 
To survive, Mink had to scavenge for scraps from the trash.
Ostracized as an outcast, she not only lacked a "family" and "friends" to care for her,
but she also endured relentless ridicule, abuse, and deception during her wandering years.
Eventually, she began to believe that—
no one would ever love her.
 
Mink ultimately gave up on seeking "love."
She distanced herself from all humans and Felinians, allowing herself to fade away.
But fate had other plans. A trafficker, searching for weak Felinians, discovered the dying Mink on the street.
Treated like mere merchandise, she was shoved into a damp, dark underground cell, muzzled and chained for resisting.
No sunlight, no warmth—only cold walls and endless despair.
Until that "false light" came and pulled her from the depths...
 
This person claimed to be her "family."
For the first time, Mink felt genuine warmth in someone's words.
Yet, as she interacted with him more,
she realized their "family" bond was not rooted in pure care—
"exploitation" was a more accurate term.
That light that "rescued" her might be leading her into an even darker abyss.
Perhaps this person sensed Mink's growing disillusionment.
 
Under his guidance, Mink underwent a "treatment",
which involves daily injections of unknown drugs and therapies, subjecting her body and mind to unimaginable torment.
Yet, miraculously, she survived.
Her body transformed—
she could not only shift forms like a regular Felinian but also possessed physical defenses and recovery abilities far beyond the norm.
However, the cost was the shattering of her psyche.
Her memories became a jumbled mess; even the slightest recollection brought her immense pain and burden.
The only thing that never faded was her longing for "love".
Perhaps because this desire stemmed not from memory but from her very instincts.

"Identification complete. Welcome home, dear Miss Dorothy."

This is my secret garden, my little kingdom of love and beauty.
No one knows. No one is disturbed.

"Hello, Miss Jasmine. How are you?"
The windmill jasmine wrapped around the window gently swayed, answering me with its lush leaves and fragrant flowers.
 
"Good evening, little Rose, so glad to see those pesky bugs didn't make you sick."
I curtsied slightly and lifted the hem of my skirt, which was hooked by the flower thorns.

"It's been a long time, Ms. Nightingale, Dorothy sends her regards."
The nightingale's crimson lips opened and several cries escaped from its throat.
However, the vocal machinery had fallen into disrepair over the years, and the song, which should have been smooth, was unusually hard to hear.

I moved closer to check the parts of the device on her beautiful body.
"Well,. your vocal cords are a bit abnormal. Is it broken?"
Bright red gems adorned the Nightingale's chest.
In the pupils that had lost their luster, I looked into my own focused and worried expression.

"It's pitiful. It's okay, Ms. Nightingale. I'll fix you."
My voice was soft and comforting as I probed my fingers into the birdcage to straighten the curls of her hair that fell over her shoulders.
Then full of love, I touched the snow-white, cold, and massive plumes on her back.

This is the best downfall a disfavored plaything can get.

As the owner of the garden, I have a lot of heavy lifting to do.
Watering the flowers and plants, with a precise configuration of nutrient solution, careful protection of the branches, leaves and rhizomes, and especially not damaging the flowers.
Butterflies have to be wiped down with the lightest duster, and the temperature and humidity of the room have to be kept at the right level.

Immersed in this kind of work, I always feel peaceful and cozy.
It's as if I've returned to the cradle and become an unsophisticated infant again.

My garden.
My hidden treasure.
My dreamland.
That's what I always call it.

Starting with the first flower I met, I have described the details of this place to every visitor without fail.
As would any proud owner of a carefully crafted work of art.
 
Similar to Ms. Nightingale, each of my most valued visitors must have loved the garden as well.
Here, they will receive the most favorable treatment.
Until I lose my fondness for them and my patience wears thin.

Unruly struggles will be fixed into graceful shapes by long nails.
Filthy blood, too, slowly drains away like a depleted river.
 
"Beauty" and "Obedience"...
I was once told that these are the most beautiful qualities in the world.
And I took those virtues and gave them back to them generously.
 
Well, your guests should feel contented as well, right?
 
Live in never-ending joy with such a beautiful and vibrant little world.
To be a part of this place for a long time is probably exactly what they want.

I turned on the old sounding machine.
Follow the images in my memory and try to recall the way to make it ring.
"Buzz..."
The turntable begins to spin and the metal needle etches with it.
The black vintage record is grateful for the gift of the needle's tip, its skin gifted with a ring of etched marks.

"Dear, please wait for me."
The piano is euphonious and sincere, the chords romantic and bouncy.
Apart from being a bit hoarse, this is a familiar tune adapted from a hometown song.

"If you're going to forget me, I'd rather die a million deaths.."
I couldn't help but hum it softly, and even wanted to dance to it in such a wonderful mood.
But the atmosphere of a solo dance was uninteresting, and I was in desperate need of a considerate partner.

As I looked around, the secret garden was as silent as death.
Even Ms. Nightingale's singing came to a screeching halt when the mechanical clockwork reached its end.

"Alas."
What is to be done? I cast my troubled eyes towards the figure on the sofa.

"Can you bear to see me alone like this? Ms. Vautrin."
The skeleton on the couch, who had gracefully settled down, was indifferent to my invitation.

Well, well.
This reaction was certainly within my expectations.

Ms. Vautrin was never like that, quiet and polite, like a machine with its initial program set.
Even when confronted with a dirty rat scurrying out of the slums, she would never show the slightest hint of disgust.

But she had also been a young lady with a strict family upbringing, surely she wouldn't have brushed off a lady's request a second time.
... only right?

"Good lady, will you please dance with me?"
I looked pleadingly into her eyes, cupped her hand, and prayed for the mercy of this true aristocrat.

The smile should be gentle and blushing enough. The tone of voice to be sweet and dainty enough.
Such an invitation would be sincere and would not be met with a cruel refusal.
"Ms. Vautrin - may I? Please."

The kind Ms. Vautrin didn't say a word and just looked at me.
Then she took my hand and placed her white arm around my waist.

The flames that burned in the center of the carpet reflected a whole dance floor for us.
The light blazed my fluttering skirt and outlined the invisible gown for Ms. Vautrin.

"Our dance is joyous. The end of our lives will be happiness."
"Oh young lovers, forget yourself."

Stale ballads chanted through the phonograph, and the single pendulum of an antique clock joined the orchestra's accompaniment.

Ms. Vautrin was gentle, her steps steady and fluttering.
I stepped to the accents of the music under her skillful guidance, my lace-adorned skirt fluttering lightly.

We danced happily through this spectral time together.
Until the beeswax-coated white bones became too much to bear and the bone spikes used to hold them in place came loose with the dance.
Her head rolled off, firelight looking at me from empty sockets.

"Ah, Ms. Vautrin."
I sighed softly.
"It turns out that when it comes to this day, it is even you who will break your word."

"I promised to stay with me until the end, but it's okay, I'll forgive you."
"I guess you're already tired, right? Soon someone will take your place."

"Dorothy has picked her next target."
Anticipation and excitement leaped in the young girl's pupils illuminated by the firelight.
The extreme pleasure of the imminent capture of her prey made even her bones tremble.
"My prey has a pure soul and the most beautiful heart..."

The golden shadows of the setting sun were cast in through the skeletonized clock that took up the entire wall.
Snow-white bones were stacked on the carpet, long, slender fingers folded back against the femur.
Dorothy reached down and carefully cupped the skull that lay dormant by the fireplace.
 
She gazed into the pair of warm sockets and placed her palm over her eyes.
 
"Sharp needles piercing the skin, long nails buried in the bones. That will be Dorothy's finest work, a miracle in the end."
"I'm going to make it, aren't I? Ms. Vautrin."
The young girl's murmur faded to a whisper. Dorothy embraced the snow-white skull and fell asleep in the pile of broken bones.

"Dear, dear. please wait for me."
"We shall meet at last. in dreams."

The old memories that litter the dusty coño will be overturned in a new glory.
The demons buried in the shadows will finally get what they deserve.
 
The vines in the garden sprinkle in the spring breeze, and the firewood in the fireplace burst into starry sparks.
It was a warm goodbye, a loving word of affection.
Or perhaps, Ms. Vautrin's approval.
 
She will stay with you. Sleep in peace, Dorothy.
In endless dreams, in eternal agony.
 
Until the moment when the. needle tip pierces "its" heart.

I'll take all the bags except for these two!

I want to shop too! Ahhh—

yet Linn, unfazed by the noise, appears to be in high spirits.

...D-don't try to butter me up! You always resort to this tactic...

In this field, results are all that truly matter.
In highly structured disciplines, this simple principle carries even greater weight.
 
In the relentless pursuit of results day after day, time seemed to stretch under an invisible force.
Outside the window, whether it was the first light of dawn or the deepening dusk, it felt as if the outside world couldn't penetrate the fortress built from science and ideals.
Soft lighting from the ceiling bathed each lab station in a gentle glow.
Every sway of the test tube and every drop of solution felt like part of a meticulously crafted design.
 
In this environment, the success of the experiment depended on every single detail.
I believe that anyone who could thrive in such a high-pressure setting must possess an extraordinary passion for this research.
 
For now, I could only watch from the sidelines, lamenting my inability to experience it firsthand.
Fueled by my passion for Pathos Technology, I graduated with solid grades and joined the Tower Research Institute.
As an inexperienced newcomer, I worked as a research assistant, helping others log data and track progress at each stage of the experiments.
The repetitive, mundane tasks seemed endless, yet they couldn't shake the determination that brought me here.
The road to truth was always meant to be like this.
 
To me, the process has always outweighed the results.
Every aspect, from pre-experiment preparations to meticulous record-keeping and post-experiment cleanup...
Every little task, every single step, I strove to perfect.

Of course, I knew there would be people who disagreed with me.
"There she is again, staying late. Who's she trying to impress?"
"Her again? Ugh, what's her name? Ivy? Elle?"
"How am I supposed to know!"
"Wait, aren't you on the same team?"
"That one always acts superior and won't talk to anyone."
"Yeah, no surprise there. I heard she was at the top of her class in some prestigious school. I guess being just an assistant doesn't sit well with her."
"She's always the first to arrive and the last to leave. Even though we only need to log hours, she insists on updating every ten minutes. Not even a robot would work that hard!"
"What's she trying to prove? She's totally overdoing it..."
"Who knows? Looks like our star student is just craving some attention from above, hahaha..."
 
Those thinly veiled jabs disguised as casual remarks were something I had grown used to.
I always responded with silence.
I wasn't doing this for anyone else; every step of the research was vital.
No detail was overlooked, and no record was taken lightly.
There was a certain peace in repetition, persistence, and attention to detail that I appreciated.
I never expected anyone to understand me as I truly was.

Realizing I wouldn't engage, they walked away, visibly frustrated.
The lab settled back into its quiet rhythm, and I returned to my work.
The air was filled with a faint scent of reagents, the silence broken only by the soft hum of instruments and the gentle clinking of test tubes.
 
"Are you not going to say anything back?"
A soft yet steady voice cut through the quiet, making my heart skip a beat.
"Huh?! Professor Lebardmann?!"
My reaction seemed to catch her off guard. I hadn't noticed Professor Naka Lebardmann approaching, and now she was looking at me with a subtle smile.
 
"Oh, did I startle you? My apologies! I honestly didn't think anyone would still be here at this hour. But don't be nervous; just call me Naka."
"Alright, Professor Naka."
 
"Heh-heh, you're so diligent and obedient... Be careful, or someone might take advantage of that!"
She gently flicked my forehead; to her, I probably looked like an innocent, naive girl.
"Let gossip like that slide, and soon enough, it'll become the truth others believe."
 
"I understand your point, Professor, but I can't control what others think. I'm just doing what I should, laying the bricks that build who I am each day. Whatever others may say won't sway my beliefs."
 
Maybe my unexpected outburst surprised Professor Naka; she let the topic drop and reached for my experiment log instead.
"You did all this by yourself?"
"Mmm."
 
"I guess I misjudged you; maybe 'logical' is a better word to describe you."
Professor Naka smiled as if she had just thought of something.
"Oh! Right! Would you like to see the new lab team I'm putting together?"
 
For some reason, my eyes felt a bit misty.
Perhaps it was because this was the first small recognition I had received since I arrived here...

Although the process was a bit cumbersome, I successfully completed my experiment and, as I had hoped, joined Naka's new lab team.
In fact, that team was something Naka decided to create during our conversation.
Looking back, it was that very conversation with Naka that changed everything.
 
Years passed, and to this day, Naka and I maintain a mentor-friend relationship.
Though I rarely see her due to her hectic schedule, my respect and admiration for her have never diminished.
 
Long before I ever stepped foot in The Tower, I had heard whispers of Naka and Carlson's "legendary feats."
I never doubted those stories.
But it wasn't until I witnessed the experiment firsthand that it truly felt real to me.
—Perhaps geniuses really do exist.
 
I knew there were countless others out there who outshone me.
What fascinated me was how the term "genius" often made their achievements seem predetermined.
I used to think of it as a term that belittled others' hard work, almost dismissive in nature.
However, once I grasped Naka's perspective, I realized that some individuals could indeed bypass the grind and uncover truths swiftly and accurately, even amidst chaos.
I came to understand that I had underestimated the true meaning of "genius."
 
"Having you here gave me the confidence to proceed with this experiment."
I was puzzled by her statement; my role hadn't accelerated the process or altered its outcomes.
 
"Don't take it so seriously. Until we have solid proof, it's all just speculation."
"Actually, you remind me a lot of Carlson. Ever since he left, I've been stuck in my research."
"If it weren't for you, I doubt I would have found the courage to restart the experiments. These data are a real headache!"
 
A true genius, yet grounded in logic.
Although I had never met Carlson, I sensed we shared similar thoughts—
Someone like Naka could undoubtedly change the world.
 
—And I would be there to witness the entire process.

Yet, the facade of respectability had already crumbled, revealing the desperation beneath.
Just gamblers, nothing more.
No amount of euphemisms or justifications could conceal their true nature.

His true adopted son had been afflicted by the Anomaly, requiring an enormous sum to ensure his son's future well-being.

the Spades, Clubs, Diamonds, and Hearts—what were we to him?

It felt grossly unjust.

the lead human said with a weary sigh, wiping the distasteful blood from my fingertips.

"My friends ensured they're living well in Catto City! They're safe for lifetimes to come!"
