His mind, long dependent on my sleight of hand for gains, forgot the art of deception. The humans subdued him swiftly, cutting his rant short.

"Stop deceiving yourself,"
the human stated calmly, delivering the unvarnished truth.
"You've gambled away even your friends. You're just a penniless, failed gambler."

The owner, confronted with the evidence that Stacey presented, had no choice but to comply with the demands to integrate into Fish Market and submit to official oversight. Yet, he couldn't fathom how this young girl, so well-versed in the rules of gambling, wasn't the Ace of Spades lying in wait. 
More puzzling was the idea that the Ace of Spades would relinquish a life of guaranteed victories.

Rumors circulated that 'Poker' met his end during a special StormEye operation.
Following that, Mr. Poker, the notorious boss, disappeared without a trace, and his trusted lieutenant, the Ace of Spades, lauded for her devious skill with a deck, was detained and sent for reeducation due to her youth.
"She must have been eliminated; someone so dangerous," they said, "capable of executing feats of theft."
Others speculated, "She must have been exploited; such a talented child deserves to have her talents harnessed."

At most, she transitioned from one 'Poker' to another 'Poker.'
After all, she was just a child with a talent for gambling—or so people believed.

Only Trixie noticed something amiss. The human who cleaned the blood from her fingers after she had "aggressively" confronted Poker had not only the expected pity and reluctance in his eyes but also... admiration.

The Felinian Combatants led Poker away.
The human spoke, "Are we done here?"
"Oh dear..."
Trix dropped her facade of helplessness, reclining languidly against the chair.
"I've always known Poker's claims of having foster children were false. I mean, there's no reason anyone would serve such a despicable man forever out of loyalty—I'm not naïve."

The human laughed, relaxing his posture, and that's when Trixie noticed the name on the lead interrogation document on the table.
"Ethan… so, are you also looking to gamble with me?"
Ethan shook her head, then nodded, her smile fading as she met Trixie's gaze directly.
All these years, Trixie remembered... her teacher's eyes were always so bright.

"I'm not a gambler. But I bet you're a good kid."

"The legendary summer festival, and the wish-granting Wishing Tree…"
It all sounded like a story made up just to attract tourists~
Humming a tune, I strolled into the island's liveliest beach bar as the last light faded from the sky.
I was supposed to be investigating Fragrance Island, but with two days left before the festival, why not enjoy a bit of vacation first?
After all, in every good adventure, the bar is where the real stories begin~

A seat had just opened at the bar. I hopped up, my tail curling elegantly around the stool.
"Hey, gorgeous, here alone?" I barely had time to order before a cologne-drenched beach boy swaggered over.
His arm almost landed on my shoulder. "A beautiful catgirl, drinking alone—how tragic. Let me buy you a drink—"
"You're quite the charmer~" I slipped out from under his arm, producing a deck of cards that fluttered between my fingers. "Since you're so eager, why don't we play a little game first?"
His eyes sparkled. "What kind of game?"
"Just a simple guessing game~" I spread the cards across the table, flashing a mischievous smile. "If you win, I'll drink with you tonight. But if you lose—"
"If I lose, what?"
"If you lose, you'll have to accept a little punishment~"

As I expected, the beach boy was utterly defeated. His face burned bright red, and I had to hide a smile—just a hint of suggestion and a few simple card tricks, and he lost everything.
"That round doesn't count! …You must've cheated!" he snapped, scattering the cards in a fit of anger as he leaned in, trying to intimidate me. "Don't pretend to be all innocent. I've seen plenty of feline girls like you in places like this—"
"Ah—!"
He didn't stand a chance. In a heartbeat, I twisted his wrist behind his back.
There was a sharp smack, and down he went.
I leaned in close, whispering sweetly in his ear, "Well, little brother~ Do you know who I am now?"
"This… these moves…" he stammered, voice trembling. "You're… from the StormEye?!"

I let go, and the beach boy scrambled out of the bar, tripping over his own feet.
"Nicely done!" called the bartender, polishing a glass with a knowing grin.
"Oh, I'm just here to have a bit of fun, not to stir up trouble~" I replied, slipping back onto my stool. I was just about to ask about the festival when a loud commotion erupted at the next table.
"I win again!" crowed a sharply dressed young man, raking in a pile of cash.
His opponent, dripping with gold chains, looked every inch the rich boss. He clutched his face, lamenting, "Why is my luck so terrible tonight…"
Even as he complained, he threw secret glances at his companions, signaling beneath the table. The young winner, swept up in his joy, didn't notice a thing.
I narrowed my eyes. So, they're running a scam… Even on this Castaway Island, the stench of casino tricks lingers.
I drifted over, quietly approaching their table.

It only took one round for the tables to turn. The guy stared at his cards, pale with disbelief. "H-how could this happen…"
"A bet's a bet, friend." The "boss" who'd been whining over his losses had already changed his tune.
"Yeah, rules are rules!" chimed in the two shills.

"No! One more round!"
He lunged for his lost money, but the shills pinned him down.
I slipped behind him and slid into his seat. "Wow, what an exciting game! Mind if I join~?"
The three cheaters exchanged wary looks. I pulled out my wallet and placed all my cash on the table. "No worries, I'm here to play for real. I heard the best card sharks gather here, so I had to see for myself~"
The "boss" looked me over, greed flickering in his eyes. "Well, if you're that eager, let's play."
The game began. With a glance, I caught every trick—palming cards, switching, marking, signaling… Tsk, such old hat. Did they really think they could get away with this here?
Once I had their routine down, I unclasped my pearl necklace. "This round, let's raise the stakes."

"Straight flush,"
I said lightly, revealing my cards and collecting the pot.
"Impossible!" The "boss" shot to his feet. "You cheated!"
"Cheated? Boss~ It's not nice to blame others just because you lost~" I tilted my head, feigning innocence. Then my tone sharpened, "But speaking of cheating, didn't you switch cards on the third draw? And that tiny crease on the ace of spades—when did you mark it? Oh, and your little hand signals—three taps for a big card, a pinky circle to fold—it's cute, really."
"You… you're just making things up!"
All three turned ashen.
"What's even funnier—" I twirled the cards in my hand, "on Castaway Island, small-time crooks like you wouldn't even get past the casino doors."
"Brat!" The conmen dropped their act and lunged.
It was no contest. A few swift moves, and they were all down. I pulled out my communicator, voice casual, "Hey, can you send a squad to the beach bar? Got a few fraudsters caught in the act. Yes, it's me—Trixie."

The young man who'd lost his money earlier finally realized what had happened. He hurried over, gratitude etched on his face. "So it was all a setup… Thank you for exposing those cheats!"
"Take this as a lesson," I said, returning his money. "Don't let gambling cloud your mind. Next time, you might not be so lucky."

By the time everything was sorted, the moon hung high above the sea.
Silver light spilled across the sand. I found a food stall and treated myself to a bowl of the local seafood soup.
The aroma of spices mingling with the salty sea breeze made the night feel especially peaceful.
"I just wanted a break, but ended up working overtime…" Trixie sighed to herself. "Still, that last game was pretty entertaining."

For Trixie, a "vacation" never truly meant rest. As her teacher Ethan used to say—
If you want to survive in this world, you need the ability to become the villain.
To protect others, you have to know the shadows better than anyone.
Scammers prey on the weakness and greed in people's hearts. As an enforcer, her job is to make sure those who exploit others pay the price.
After all, if you want to fool the eye, you have to fool the heart first. And if there's one thing Trixie's good at, it's seeing through people.
"Tomorrow, I'll keep investigating that so-called miracle Wishing Tree…"
Trixie stifled a yawn.
"Tonight, after some unexpected overtime, I'll let myself relax—a moonlit beach, a bowl of steaming soup, and nothing more to worry about."

"Remember this, you are Ace of Spades, Seven of Diamonds, Four of Clubs…"
The strong humans commanded us condescendingly. 
I followed his pointing finger to look at each one—the "seniors". 
They were five or six years older than us, masters of their craft.

Four of Clubs was very kind, often bringing us tasty treats that would stop the dizziness once eaten. 
However, Seven of Diamonds complained that she only brought candies, unlike the protein-rich foods he found… Whatever 'protein' was, it apparently made you strong and kept you from getting tired easily.
At that moment, Ace of Spades would cough, and then they'd all stash their goods away.

I secretly asked the Four of Clubs why, if their numbers were higher than that of the Ace of Spades, they still listened to her?
Four of Clubs just smiled and said, "The Ace of Spades doesn't only represent 1. It also represents 11. That's the ace card."

The three idiots wouldn't believe what I said, even though each one of them is quite a bit older than me... they just don't get it!

"Only one person can be the ace, the wildcard." 
I waved my index finger in front of them: "That's what the seniors told me."
"Really?" asked the biggest idiot.
"She's always lying," the second idiot retorted.

"Pfft! You'll understand on Selection Day." 
I wasn't upset: "By then, one of us will be chosen as the new Ace of Spades."
The little idiot scoffed: "The new Ace of Spades... Doesn't that mean the current Ace of Spades is going to be replaced? I remember, she mastered all the gambling techniques, no one could beat her."
"Eh? Dodge, you knew about this?"
"..."
"But is that really fair?" 
The big idiot continued: "Even a wildcard, as powerful as it is, can only substitute for one card, right?"

Those damn brothers, think they're so great because they outnumber me?
I put my hands on my hips and stressed: "This is a game, having one more or one less card makes a big difference, you know!"

"This is a game where having one card too many or one too few makes a big difference!" cried Seven of Diamonds.
I saw his palms were bright red, his wrist twisted into an unnatural position...
The surrounding bodyguards whispered among themselves, saying he was now 'useless'.

"Do you really think so?" The man loomed over him, his oversized hand gripping the boy's head.
"As a result, Ace of Spades had to be executed by an angry guest because of your failure, and Four of Clubs was sent away as compensation... Wouldn't things be better without you?"

Seven of Diamonds was no more.
The peers around me began to fear me... because I, were a Felinian, known for the strength to crush a skull with one hand.
Only the three idiots remained unchanged.
But later, those beef bits that had mysteriously disappeared were once again rewarded to me by 'my own kind'.

"The so-called saviors die because of their own delusions... You are no different from Ace of Spades." Dodge said calmly, looking at my hands.

"Four of Clubs and Seven of Diamonds often swipe snacks from the guests, I know that, and I don't forbid it," the tall male Felinian said gleefully on the same day. 
"But I remember he took beef bits, and she took candy... After spoiling you little rascals, there should have been nothing left."
...
"Good kid, it was you who gave all the beef bits back to your brothers and sisters, wasn't it? How did you manage that?"

His head blocked the light source above, completely enveloping my world in shadow.
It was like the depths of the casino we lived in... perpetual darkness, with only the narrow paths controlled by the dealer showing any light.
And before stepping completely into the spotlight—a time not long ago but felt like ages to me—Ace of Spades told me that the ace wasn't always held till the end.
As a wildcard, it should control the timing itself, deciding when the critical moment is.
And then, act without any regrets.

"It's not hard at all… but this is a technique only I use." 
I finally responded to the man's question—with conditions.
"So, let me help you turn around all your losses..."

The essence of gambling is sacrifice.
If you think that gambling can grant you some freedoms, you are also sacrificing other freedoms. 
It took years and meeting her "Teacher" for Trixie to fully understand this.

As a child, she was merely a gambler raised for the purpose, not even having a proper name.
The "adults" worried that too much knowledge would breed wisdom and that capability would lead to independence.
Because understanding that one can define oneself leads to true aspirations.
At that time, she and her friends couldn't even grasp the order of poker cards; they were merely used for basic gambling games that took advantage of their small statures.
Hiding in secret passages as echo chambers, lurking in corners as petty thieves. What they awaited was merely 'sunlight' made of lamplight.

Yet, after a certain incident, she suddenly rose to become the new Ace of Spades. 
Her name echoed across the isles, even attracting overtures from overseas tycoons. But from the day she sat at the table, it seemed Trixie could never leave it again.
Her skills—she had long realized they would be coveted and exploited, and her abilities, hidden for years, were continually milked by those people. 
Yet, she felt that her specialness was precisely because she was meant to shine eternally at the gambling table.

Until the day the "Poker" organization completely vanished.

Salt. Nothing but salt.
That's all that remains for me—clinging to the shattered plank in this endless, uncaring ocean.
The sun beats down mercilessly. My skin burns, my lips crack. I think there's blood, but I can't taste it anymore.
"Papa... Mama..."
The words tear at my throat, lost in the wind.

The storm came without warning, swallowing our tiny boat whole. My parents vanished into the black waves, leaving me clinging to the last splintered piece of the plank.
How long has it been? A day? Two? Time has blurred into nothingness.
Above me, unknown birds circle—patient, waiting for my body to still.
I try to shoo them away, but my arms won't obey.
"I'm sorry... Papa, Mama... I can't hold on..."

Just as my vision fades, a shadow flickers at the edge of my sight.
A hallucination? No one else could be out here.
"You poor child."
The voice is soft, distant, as if carried by the wind. Then—Hands grasped me, pulling me from the drifting plank—their solid presence proof I wasn't hallucinating my salvation.
"Do not be afraid. From now on, I will be your mother."
Her arms are comforting, yet something in her touch sends a shiver through me. Maybe it's just the cold of the sea still clinging to my bones.
"Thank... you..."
The words slip out before darkness takes me. When I wake, the world has changed.
Later, I learn this place has a name—Wonderland.

"Hilda, come here."
The woman who had pulled me from the sea—the one I now called Mother—stood waiting in the training yard.
Three months in Wonderland, and my body had fully healed.
"Yes, Mother."
I forced my feet forward, pulse quickening. She had given me food, shelter, knowledge—everything. But her lessons... were unlike any other.

"Today, we swim." Her smile was calm.
My muscles turned to stone.
Just the thought of that ocean—the one that took my parents—made my whole body tremble.
"I... I don't want to—"
"Crack!"
The sharp crack of a slap burned across my cheek. Yet when I looked up, Mother's eyes were still soft.
"Do you know, Hilda? Real love hurts." As she caressed my burning cheek, she whispered, "Remember this—true love comes with pain, and this pain will make you invincible."
"But—"
"Why did your parents die?" Her voice turned to ice. "Weakness. Unless you grow stronger, you'll share their fate."
The words lodged in my ribs like a hook.
...She wasn't wrong. If I'd been stronger, maybe I could've dragged them both to shore.

"I understand, Mother."
And so the true training began. From dawn till dusk, I fought the waves until my lungs burned and my legs gave out. Every flinch, every gasp for air, earned the kiss of her whip—each strike a whispered mantra: "This is love. The deeper the pain, the purer the love."
And in time... I learned. Pain wasn't the opposite of love. It was the heart of it.

"Hilda, I have a mission for you."
Years later, grown but kneeling as always, I marveled at Mother's ageless beauty—time's cruel touch had spared her completely.
"Your orders, Mother?"
"Travel to Catto City and serve as Menace's personal assistant," she said, that cryptic smile playing across her lips. "Attend her every need. Observe... everything."
"Understood." My forehead nearly touched the floor. "Her every action will be documented."
"My clever girl." Her fingers carded through my hair like they had when I was half this size. "No matter where you go, you'll always be my darling daughter."
 When I reached Catto City, I finally met the legendary Menace—regal, ice-cold, yet bearing a faint resemblance to Mother.
"Lady Menace! Hilda of Wonderland, reporting for duty!"
She barely glanced at me. "On this nation's soil, you may call me Sylviette."

I threw myself into every task Sylviette assigned—while secretly reporting her every move to Mother.
Yet somehow, I kept messing up. Nothing I did ever pleased Sylviette.
"HILDA!" "I asked for mistletoe, not the entire cursed forest!" Sylviette snapped.
Once again, I found myself bending at the waist to apologize to Lady Sylviette.
"Apologies, but... your exact words were 'take it all'..."
I lowered my head in apparent shame, while mentally drafting my report to Mother.
"A... gift from Lady Venus. For the Snow Festival."
The box nestled in the mistletoe branches came with my perfectly timed declaration.

The night was deep when I quietly slipped out of my quarters and made my way to the meeting point.
"Mother." I murmured into the communicator, keeping my voice low.
A familiar tone responded, "Tell me, my child—how do things stand?"
"Lady Sylviette accepted Venus's gift, just as we planned..." My thoughts drifted back to earlier. "But when I—when I delivered those 'orders' from Venus... Sylviette's aura became even more menacing."
Once again, I relayed every detail of Sylviette's movements to Mother.

"...Good. Continue your surveillance. Never forget, Hilda—Wonderland relies on this. I rely on this."
"Yes, Mother."
The call ended, and I slumped against the wall, exhaling hard. A quiet doubt crept in—Was deceiving Sylviette truly the right path?
The cold bite of her sword at my throat—the moment she caught me forging Venus's commands—flashed through my mind. My body trembled at the memory.
Yet, Mother's will was my purpose. I had no choice.

"Hilda!"
The voice sliced through the silence behind me. I jolted, nearly leaping out of my skin.
"L-Lady Sylviette!"
"Care to explain why you're lurking about at this hour?" Her gaze sharpened, probing.
"I—I was just—! The moon! Look how bright it is!" I stammered, thrusting a finger upward.
She tilted her head at the blanket of clouds overhead and smirked. "Impressive. You must have vision like an owl."

Midnight winds stirred as the clouds reluctantly dispersed. Moonlight spilled through the cracks in the heavens, painting Hilda's troubled face in silver.
That devouring sea still lived in her bones. The merciless waters hadn't just claimed her parents—they'd stolen the future she was meant to sail toward.
Being saved by "love" might have been her redemption. Or perhaps it was merely trading a quick drowning for a slow suffocation.
Wonderland taught her a cruel lesson: Pain became affection, obedience turned instinctual, and betrayal served as loyalty's testament. This perverse wisdom dragged her deeper with each passing day, an inescapable riptide of the soul.
She chose the seafaring life despite her fear of the sea, served Lady Sylviette while secretly watching her, and sought belonging where only lies could give her place.
She was a living paradox—a girl shipwrecked between devotion and despair.
Before Sylviette, Hilda's smile never wavered. The perfect mask.
How long could this charade last? She didn't know. Mother's doctrine was clear: true love is measured in suffering. The greater the agony, the purer the devotion.
When the reckoning came, she'd lose everything. But for now...she still had Mother. Still had that twisted "love."
Like that splintered plank from her past—flimsy, fragile...but all that kept her from sinking.

For a solitary cat, Castaway Island was an ideal haven.

I roamed among the reefs, feeling the salty sea breeze ruffle my fur and the waves crash against my paws.
Most days, I easily caught more than enough fish among the coastal rocks.
On the rare bad days, I would dive beneath the waves; with enough effort, I could always find something.

The ocean nurtured the fish, and in turn, it nurtured me.

Whenever I had the chance, I would sit on the beach, watching the ebb and flow of people and the sun as it rose and set.
The waves rolled in a tireless rhythm, as if the ocean itself were breathing.

I knew my secrets lay hidden deep within the ocean...
...the past that remained shrouded in mystery.

No one seemed to notice me. I was just an inconspicuous stray cat.
Only the ocean and the distant wind whispered stories I couldn't comprehend.

As night fell, the villagers returned to their nests like weary birds.
The aroma of cooked food wafted through the air, calling home the children playing in the fields.

Sometimes, a thought would cross my mind: there had once been a home for me in that little village.

I understood that the ocean wasn't always bountiful and gentle.
It held the power to destroy everything. In the face of nature's overwhelming force, life felt fragile and insignificant.

I was the lone survivor of a catastrophic shipwreck, now stranded on this island.
I had lost all my memories and everything I once had, but this island welcomed me.

Abundant rain replenished the lakes and creeks, providing an endless supply of drinking water.
The vast ocean and forest offered a diverse array of food.
Thanks to the warm climate, the sea never froze, and a rocky cave provided perfect shelter.

Aside from the unbearable loneliness, I lived a fairly good life here.

Though I had forgotten everything, a deep-seated fear kept me away from the local settlement.
Yet, my longing for a home often compelled me to transform into a cat and approach the village cautiously.
I became accustomed to sneaking into the village under the cover of night, hiding in the tall grass to observe their joyful lives.

In the moonlight, those ragged cottages resembled silent, looming temples.
Light spilled through the gaps in doors and windows, like sacred flames that flickered endlessly—both warm and mysterious.
Each beam of light told a story of life within those homes. Sometimes, I would see a family gathered around the dinner table; other times, a mother singing a lullaby to her children.

Slowly, I began to uncover the village's secrets.
What I didn't realize was that someone was also discovering my secrets.

"FiFi!"
I made a signaling sound by blowing air through the small gap between my lips and teeth.

Before I could react, I found myself ensnared in a soft net.

"Meow—Hiss—"
I struggled to break free, but my wounds hadn't healed yet, and I ended up hurting myself further.

The window creaked open, and for the first time, warm light from inside the house poured over me.
I couldn't clearly see the owner's face against the brightness. Their excited voice sent chills down my spine.

"Good job, Howell! I've lost so many things lately. This cat must be the thief!"

I hadn't stolen anything. I always hunted for my food and never took from anyone.
But there was nothing I could do to prove my innocence; all I could do was bare my teeth and hiss in desperation.

"We lost a big fish today. People have seen this cat sneaking around the village—who knows how many homes it's raided!"
"What a shameless criminal. Let's make it pay!"

That was absurd! They had only one fish, which they cooked into a stew and ate.
I had caught that fish for them when I heard their daughter was ill, even injuring myself in the process.

Why? Why were they lying?
That family had seemed so friendly. Was it all just my imagination?

"Hmph. Stop lying! You took her fish. I saw you do it."
"What are you talking about? I... I found that fish right at my doorstep!"
"She dropped it there, and the next moment, you picked it up. You call that finding it? Was this cat supposed to deliver fish for you?"

Yes, I had delivered that fish on purpose, but now I was starting to regret it.

"I don't know what you're talking about! It's late. Just stay away from my house!"
The window slammed shut.

A girl gently lifted me up.
"Don't be scared. They just moved in. Everyone else in the village likes you. We won't believe a word they say."
"Yes, you're hurt. We just want to help."
"Let's head back. Mitchell must have some medicine and bandages ready. We can talk later."

Before I knew it, they had made me part of their family.
Mitchell and Howell were orphans, just like me.

The girl who carried me was Emelyne, the village head's daughter and Mitchell's fiancée.
She was the first to uncover my secrets. By claiming I was a distant relative, she convinced the whole village to let me stay.

"What's your name?"
I couldn't remember my name, but I recalled the sound they used to call me.
"FiFi!"
"You mean Fifi? Is that even a name?"
"Shut up, you little rascal! Fifi is our sister now. Don't worry; you'll be safe here."

"Understood!"
Once again, I had a home. In that moment, I truly believed it.

Night enveloped the island like a dark shroud, casting a shadow over the village.
The villagers, rooted in this land for generations, seemed to have their emotions trapped here.

Seagate Village, the most remote corner of Catto City, was the oldest fishing community on Castaway Island.
This place held many secrets, and today, one more was added.

"The target is dead, master. There are two other casualties. Only a villager named Howell survived, but he's in a deep coma with serious injuries."
"Just injured?"
"We discovered that the target has lost all her memories. None of the villagers know where she came from. They took her in out of kindness, completely unaware."

"Lost all memories? What a coincidence."
"Yes. She was just unlucky. Unlike me, I met you after I lost mine, and you gave me a second chance. I vow to repay you with everything I have, master!"
The vague figure behind the car window cast a complicated and eccentric look at the subservient subordinate.
There was a mix of surprise and self-satisfaction.

"So, you think Howell is more valuable alive than dead?"
"Yes. Howell witnessed the entire transformation of the villagers into Darkpaws during the black tide and their battle with the target. He would make the perfect witness."
"You did well. This matter is concluded. You can return to handle business at sea. The previous captain was incompetent. From now on, that ship is yours. You are the new captain."
"Yes, master!"
"Do not disappoint me."

The car drove away, and the arrogant master didn't notice how tightly the newly appointed captain clenched her fist, turning her knuckles white.
"Lost all memories? Hmph... You're so confident, aren't you? To think you'd have me do something like this..."

The shock helped her recover most of her memories, but she felt so intimidated that she could only scream silently in her heart.
"Fifi... I couldn't protect you. But I will avenge you!"

The captain didn't see the weak and exhausted brown bobtail cat hiding in the bushes nearby, her dirty and tangled fur a testament to her struggles.
She was Felinian but had lost the ability to transform into a human due to her serious injuries.
Those wounds had triggered fragments of forgotten memories.

"Quick, go underwater! Escape from beneath! Don't let them see you!"
"Don't worry. We're born to dive. You can do it!"

She remembered her parents dying in a shipwreck. They had been much better divers than she was, so why...?
That was all she could recall; the rest of her memories sank to the ocean floor like the wreckage, impossible to retrieve.
Once again, she began her life apart from others, determined to uncover the truth of her past.
Without her human form, she evaded detection, blending in as an ordinary cat.

She would sneak into the village under the cover of night, lingering only around the old house she once called home.
Years had passed, and the once-vulnerable child had grown into a capable adult.

One day, Howell brought a ten-year-old kid back to the old house.
"This was our home..."
"But... where are my father and mother?"
"They're gone. Let's move on. From now on, I'll take care of you."

Howell seemed to have moved past the pain, but Fifi knew he was still searching for answers. That was why he had left their hometown to join StormEye.
He didn't want the child to carry the heavy burden of "vengeance."

"Meow..."

"We're family now!"
Fifi thought, holding the kid's face in her heart.

"Sorry, child. You'll have to face this new world on your own now."
 
No matter how many times she entered "slumber"—
The first memory that surfaced upon awakening was always her mother's face, filled with regret in those final moments.
 
Before her stretched the so-called "new world," an endless expanse of barren land.
Behind her lay the massive, fractured "home," bearing the heavy burden of survival.
 
"Child, this is a pure, untainted new world."
"The future of the Felinians rests in your hands now!"
"Remember to observe! And extrapolate!"
 
"Don't be afraid, child. Death isn't the end. I'm simply going to the home of the stars."
"When that day arrives, I will return to your side."
 
"At the perfect time... in the safest moment..."
"Our new home..."
"I can't wait for that day... to..."
"See you again..."
 
But...
 
At the end of the stars, I found nothing but the stillness of oblivion.
Everything moves along its predetermined path, heading toward the long sleep of the end.
 
The stars would eventually fade, their light consumed by darkness.
 
I alone bore the mission of survival—imperfect and broken as I was...
Where could I possibly go from here?

I was born aboard the Ark.
One of the exiled children drifting between the stars.
 
My homeland had long since vanished; the Ark had become my new home.
 
That night, the Veil of Time, which glimpsed into the future, flickered with a faint glimmer.
My mother shed tears of joy—it was the first time in millennia of wandering that the Veil had illuminated.
 
"Time to land!"
My mother declared, making a decisive choice.
 
"Our home won't survive another ten millennia—this might be our only chance!"
No response came from the empty cockpit.
 
Hundreds of thousands of supercompressed Pathos Vessels lay stored in superimposed states within a pristine spacetime chamber.
Just like silent gravestones.
 
These vessels contained the last remnants of our kind—our only survivors.
 
As the chosen spark of hope for the Felinians, My mother had wandered alone for tens of thousands of years.
 
Thanks to Pathos Technology, her lifespan was nearly infinite.
Yet, her will, much like our shattered "Home," could not withstand another ten thousand years.

Pathos is the fundamental particle of the universe.
 
These Pathos Particles possess the power to create anything.
But they can just as easily unmake everything, reducing it to nothingness.
 
The Felinians once misused the power of Pathos, leading to their own downfall.
 
The light of our home planet was completely extinguished, vanishing from the star charts.
 
Yet, it was also the Pathos Particles that enabled us to leave our homeland and cast ourselves into the cosmos.
 
Only the finest among the Felinians were chosen to be the spark.
They'll guide those of our kind—now compressed and stored in Pathos Vessels—in search of a new home.
 
I once ventured into the Veil of Time to explore the past.
In that chapter of history, which I had not lived, destruction arrived with brutal swiftness.
 
When the Pathos Particles on the planet exceeded their threshold, the once-tamed forces suddenly became dominant overnight.
 
That was the first moment the Felinians truly heard the "voice" of the Pathos Particles.
 
And that voice carried only one message:
 
"DESTRUCTION!"

The star chart was a painting long frozen in time.
Each spark of life, along with its inevitable demise, was fated from the very beginning.
 
If destruction is the ultimate truth of the universe, then the future is already sealed—how could those bound by its rules ever hope to defy them?
 
The "New World" was barren yet pristine.
 
My mother entrusted the hope of the New World to me, surrendering the only chance at "eternity."
 
There were countless Arks, but only one "Veil of Time."
 
It was also known as the Tomb of Time.
 
All matter inevitably succumbs to decay. Yet, within the vast timeline of oblivion, Pathos Particles endure eternally.
 
Each time death approached me, my mother would lay me to rest within the Tomb of Time.
After she chose to embrace death herself, I took on the Veil of Time.
 
My Pathos, "asleep" in the endless light, was guided by will, taking form and finding its way back to the realm of matter.
Revived, I embraced a new life.
 
Beyond the veil of time stretched a timeless chart of stars.
Here lay the buried light of all stars.
 
Light represented both time and space.
 
I held this light to illuminate the path ahead, yet all I could see was the endless black at the edge of space and time.

Fata hailed from a distant star, long extinguished and hidden beyond the clouds.
Everything on this planet lay within her grasp.
Yet she cared little for the material world; her thoughts were fixed on a far-off future.
 
What truly defines a worthy "new home"?
 
At first, Fata hesitated to step into this pristine world.
She lived aboard the Ark, searching for a way to liberate her people from the grip of Pathos Particles.
 
But that was as impossible as asking fish to survive without water or humans without air.
"The timing isn't right just yet."
 
Following in her mother's footsteps, she entered the Veil of Time, hoping to glimpse the future and discover how to bring her people back.
But all that awaited her at the end of time and space was a dead, silent void.
 
It was painfully clear.
 
This also explained why Dr. CC—the creator of Fata—had spent ten thousand years gazing at this desolate ruin from day one.
 
Gazing into the past, Fata recalled that fateful moment.
 
The light was so faint it almost seemed like meaningless space debris.
Or perhaps just an illusion conjured by her fatigue-clouded mind.
 
Back then, she was merely a black cat with a hint of red, a lucky emblem on her home planet, unable to utter a single word.
Her focus had been on the flowing hem of the Veil of Time, imagining herself chasing a non-existent mouse, completely oblivious to the glimmer surrounding her.
 
"Maybe... my mother's will has already run dry..."
 
Fata mused to herself.
Moreover, at the final moment, Dr. CC resorted to ancient methods to create the Felinians, sacrificing half her life and consciousness for Fata.
 
"In bloom, she's not a flower. Hazy, she's not a mist. That's my favorite line of poetry."
"If your gaze falters in the mist, perhaps it's best not to look at all, right?"
 
With a smile, Fata meticulously designed every detail of the new world until another out-of-control Ark collided with hers, severely damaging her body.
Could she have held on a little longer?
 
"Again and again, my eyes wander to the past, but the future offers no answers to my searching gaze."
"For the vast universe, a Felinian's life is so insignificant it can't even find an anchor..."
"We can't gather the materials needed to repair this body anymore. I refuse to taint this pristine new world with Pathos Particles."
"So, I'll have to transform you into a new Felinian..."
 
"Meow?"
Fata tilted her head. She couldn't understand a word.
Yet, she felt the overwhelming sadness and frustration—were they running out of cat food?
 
"Meow!"
It's alright. I can skip a meal or two. This place looks vast—there must be something to hunt here.
 
"Sorry, child. You'll have to face this new world on your own now."
 
The old spark was extinguished, and a new one was born.
 
Life as a Felinian spared her from hunger, but the survival of her kind became her burden.
It was as absurd as asking a crawling baby to join a space expedition.
 
But Fata was a good cat—obedient and responsible. By observing the pasts of others through the Veil of Time, she absorbed all she could.
 
It was then that Fata sensed the Pathos Particles filling the world.
 
It made sense—there was more than one Ark. Whether by accident or design, the inevitable happened: the Pathos Particles leaked out.
Clinging like a malignancy. Small as they were, they heralded this planet's doom.
 
"Escape this planet and find a new home."
 
But the Ark had already sustained damage.
 
"If I can't see the future clearly, then I'll simply stop trying to look any further."
Fata resolved to repair the Ark while gathering unique Pathos.
Perhaps a solution would present itself when she reached a new home.
 
Closing her eyes to the material world, Fata immersed herself in the past within the Veil of Time.
The rare glimpses of the future she caught still filled her with despair.
 
Until one day, the Veil of Time flickered with a faint glimmer once more.
In that moment, she realized her mother had been absolutely right.
Anyone who had stared into the darkness for tens of thousands of years could instantly recognize that extraordinary, unique glimmer.
It was a light that didn't belong to this star chart.
 
"A shooting star! That's a shooting star!"
"What kind of future will you create for this world?"

For reasons I couldn't explain, my earliest memories were a blur.
To be more precise, they felt almost non-existent.
When I say "non-existent," I don't mean they were erased or missing; it was as if they had never been there at all.
No matter how hard I tried, I couldn't grasp the overwhelming, blinding white. What could it possibly mean?
 
In the days I do remember, I spent most of my time in a vast jungle.
The happiest moments for me were when sunlight filtered through the canopy and warmed my face.
Though we didn't have many friends, I cherished my life in the jungle.
We danced and played, relaxed in the shade, and shared our dreams.
Yet, despite the joy, we wore locating devices that resembled shackles at all times.
The people around us claimed these devices were for our protection.
Since we all possessed different powers, we needed them to monitor our status.
As someone who could control explosions, I was often the center of attention.
After all, even the smallest spark could pose a significant risk to the jungle.
 
Days like that repeated endlessly, with the seasons changing around us.
But I didn't care about that.
At that time, I hadn't yet developed a curiosity about the outside world.
The jungle was my entire universe—
My friends were here, and everything I knew was here.

Then one day, my caretaker announced that my vitals were unstable, and I needed to be placed in solitary care.
So every night, they locked me in a small room.
 
"Hmph! I'd rather be in the jungle!"
Staring at the empty walls, my boredom quickly morphed into anger.
I clenched my fists tightly, trying to keep my emotions in check.
 
But reason couldn't hold back the flood of feelings.
With a deafening crash, the lone chair in the room toppled over, screeching against the floor.
 
"You've said that 501 times..."
A calm, emotionless voice came from outside.
"Ah, I'm sorry! Did I wake you?"
"No..."
 
I peered through the small opening in the door, trying to locate the source of the voice.
I'd tried talking to the people in the nearby rooms when I first got here, but no one had responded.
I realized everyone in this area was in solitary confinement... and this was the first time someone had spoken to me!
Might as well try to get to know them.
 
"Great! I thought I'd be the only one stuck in here today!"
"...."
"Hey! When were you brought here?"
"..."
"I'm Garfire. What's your name?"
"..."
"Hello? Are you asleep? Are you there?"
 
Was the one who answered me a ghost or something?
 
"I'm not a ghost."
"Huh? Did I say that out loud?"
"No... I'm Zoe."
 
"Zoe? Zoe... Zoe! What a beautiful name!"
"Stop repeating my name. Are you dumb?"
"No, I'm Garfire!"
"..."
 
She fell silent again.
It seemed my new friend wasn't much for conversation.
That was okay; I could always try to engage her!

Separated by a narrow corridor and two doors, Zoe and I could only communicate at night.
During the day, I roamed the jungle as usual; otherwise, I'd be bored out of my mind.
Meanwhile, Zoe was taken to the largest library in the base to study.
After much effort, I began to understand her better,
and I gradually accepted that she often fell asleep while we talked.
But there was something Zoe kept to herself, something she never shared with me.
I knew I wasn't the brightest, but I was certain of my feelings.
 
Eventually, my suspicions were confirmed.
One day, Zoe unexpectedly brought up the topic herself.
 
"Have you ever wanted to see the world beyond here?"
"So, do you want to explore the jungle with me, Zoe?"
"...."
"What? You don't?"
"I mean outside this base, this jungle. There's a much bigger world out there..."
Zoe explained that she had read about the entire world in books, and it sounded far more interesting than my experiences in the jungle.
 
"Are you saying you want to leave here, Zoe?"
I asked, even though I suspected I already knew the answer.
"Yes."
Her voice came softly from the other side of the door, but it hit me like a heavy blow.
Before I could fully process my feelings, my body acted on its own.

"I want to go with you!"

"What did you say?"
It was unusual for Zoe to use that tone—intrigued yet confused.
 
"I said I want to leave here with you."
I blurted it out on impulse, but I didn't regret it.
Everything is more fun when you have someone to share it with.
 
"I thought you liked it here."
"But if you leave, I'll have no one to talk to. I'd be so bored..."
"Do you really believe I can escape from here?"
"Of course! You're so clever!"
"..."
I realized I might have said something foolish, which is why Zoe fell silent.
What did I say this time?
Then I heard a soft chuckle.
"Hehe..."
"What's so funny, Zoe?"
"It's nothing. I just have this feeling... maybe I really can make it out of here now that you've said it."
 
"Absolutely! If you need my help, just call out!"
"I do need your help. In fact, it's essential."
"R-really?"
"Yes, and what I need you to do is quite simple."
She lowered her voice, even though the guards monitoring us couldn't hear.
"We have a ruse in Yaozhou called 'creating a diversion.'"
"What's a diversion?"
"..."
 
Zoe didn't seem surprised by my cluelessness anymore. She calmly explained her plan.
I didn't fully grasp what she meant, but I understood what I needed to do.
When she learned about my abilities, she even taught me how to control my Pathos Particles to manipulate explosions more effectively.
It wasn't as easy as she made it sound, but I eventually got the hang of it.

"Let's see... I think we need this, and this... Oh! Zoe said we also need this!"
I gathered all the components I could find.
"I made a bomb! Zoe was right about this!"

I thought everything would go according to plan, but what happened next was beyond anything I could have imagined.
The project I had so eagerly undertaken became the spark that ignited the destruction of my jungle.

In the land of Mannava, which lagged behind in science and technology, many secrets lay hidden in the vast jungles.
This place was meticulously enclosed, protected by barbed wire and sturdy fences that created an impenetrable barrier, isolating everything inside from the outside world.
Deep within the jungle...
After countless lives had been sacrificed, Garfire emerged as a "product" of sorts, gaining the ability to control bombs at will.
Because of this, she had the chance to meet Zoe.

Zoe's plan involved Garfire destroying the heavily guarded room at the center of the base while she was out in the jungle.
Once that was accomplished, chaos would ensue throughout the base.
All the guards and staff would rush to the explosion, leaving the "lambs to be slaughtered" in shackles unnoticed.
Through observation and study, they learned the layout and security arrangements of the entire base. Zoe even figured out how to remove the shackles, which was crucial for Garfire's mission.
In the midst of the chaos, they planned to meet at the side entrance of the courtyard and escape together.
 
However, at the exact moment Garfire triggered the bombs...
A massive surge of energy erupted from the labs.
Garfire was caught off guard.
A black mist engulfed everyone like a ravenous beast. Those affected lost their sanity, frantically trying to attack Garfire.
The once peaceful and beautiful jungle turned into a hellish landscape.
Eventually, it lay in ruins.
 
When Garfire opened her eyes, she saw a smiling face.
"Good! You're awake! Finally, we have a survivor."
"...W-what? Where's Zoe?"
"Wow, you seem pretty spirited. Is Zoe your friend? I've been searching for a long time, but I'm sorry to say there's no one else."
"No. It can't be! Zoe can't be dead! She's so clever! How could she just...?"
"Alright, if you don't believe me, you can look for her later. But for now, you need to come with me."
"...And who are you?"

The beautiful woman flashed another perfect smile.
"I'm Delilah, a diplomat from the Elis Guild."

My memories felt like slivers of light slipping through a narrow skylight in a vast, dark prison.
Dust motes danced in the light's path, swirling in silent unrest, turning the dim images into a tangled blur.
I tried to pick apart the visions, but all that emerged was the manor, scorched and reduced to ash.
 
"I'm sorry... Sis Qi. "I still don't feel anything..."
 
"It seems the curse from before is still affecting your memory."
"Don't stress—just take your time. Patience has always been our strength at the Whispering Teahouse."
 
A warm and elegant older sister stroked my head and handed me a calming cup of black tea with milk.
"That's enough for today. Drink up and get some rest early. Oh, and don't forget to brush your teeth, alright?"
"Alright, Sis Qi."
 
—I'm not a child anymore...
I gave a polite bow, holding back the rest of my thoughts.
 
As stated in the New Canon decreed by Oephilos, the old holy city:
All women must remain obedient, modest, pious, pure, and unquestioningly loyal.
This is the code every lady must strictly follow.
Any violation will result in divine punishment, bringing shame upon her family.
 
Granny Taya and Aunt Pollyanna had no faith in the new gods.
I couldn't remember who had given me that New Canon...
I didn't know when it started, but some voices had been haunting the corners of my mind.
 
"Aphros, you haven't met the god's expectations—you're a bad girl!"
"Aphros, what you're doing will bring humiliation to your family."
 
On that fateful night, as the tragedy unfolded, I couldn't help but think...
Maybe it was my inadequacy that brought the gods' punishment upon Granny Taya and Aunt Pollyanna.
 
Sis Qi has been nothing but kind; I can't let her suffer because of me.
And also... the Master who freed me from the curse and gave me a fresh start...
 
Sis Qi said the Master is the Chief of StormEye, the hope of Catto City, and someone truly significant.
I will never bring harm or trouble to the Master!
 
I'll behave and become a proper lady!

Qi once said that Lord Ashen Mist was drawn to deep, agonizing emotions, but I didn't think I possessed any of those.
 
"I'm really lucky!"
That belief had always been a part of me.
 
Without luck, I wouldn't have survived the flooding of the Lange River when I was just an infant.
Nor would I have met the kind-hearted Granny Taya.
 
Thanks to her devoted care, I lived a worry-free life until I turned fifteen.
When Granny Taya could no longer care for me, she entrusted me to Aunt Pollyanna, whose kindness matched her own.
 
If it weren't for luck, I wouldn't have made it through the fire at the manor and the curse that followed.
I was truly blessed to receive so much help along the way...
 
In contrast,
those who lost their lives because of me—my parents, Granny Taya, Aunt Pollyanna, and others—were the real victims of misfortune.
 
Someone like me, who survived by sheer luck, has no right to claim anguish.
I closed my eyes, effortlessly blocking out the memories, and prayed for a dreamless sleep.
 
The darkness flowed like a river, swaying and rippling endlessly.
I surrendered to its waves, drifting aimlessly.
 
"Do we really have to do this? It's flood season—throwing her in could kill her!"
"She's better off dead than staying here. I know in my heart she'll survive—luck will guide her! She's not an ordinary child; she won't die easily!"
 
"You mean... the experiment worked?!"
"No abnormalities so far, and her energy is rising quickly—she's the mature subject they've been searching for all this time."
 
"The Darkpaw who won't lose control... Those wicked individuals will hunt her down, subject her to vile experiments, or force her into committing unimaginable atrocities..."
 
"You do realize that if anyone finds out about this, we'll both be executed, right?"
"That's why we need to send her away now before it's too late! Plus, when she's older, she won't slip past the nets anymore..."
 
"...I see. Let's do this. No, not us—just me. Leave now, before it's too late..."
"No, I'd rather die by your side."
 
"Sorry, sweetheart. We couldn't protect you—we have no other choice..."
"Forgive us for our powerlessness. Luck will carry you forward—you must survive, no matter what!"
 
The river's currents, like strong arms, safely bore the Felinian infant into the unknown.

The gods blessed me with an extraordinary memory but cursed me with the inability to forget.
 
It wasn't until much later, after I secretly learned Shyriitrikan, that I could grasp the true meaning of the haunting dialogue from my dreams.
 
"That... was my mother... and father?"
 
I struggled to sift through the scattered fragments of memory.
 
When Granny Taya brought me into her home, she hurriedly burned something in fear.
It was my swaddling, or rather, an old, ragged bedsheet.
 
Something was written on the inner side of that bedsheet. I strained to recall and pieced together its essence.
 
"Thank you... kind stranger. The child's identity... must remain a secret... It's too dangerous..."
"I'm sorry... for dragging you... into this trouble..."
"Please, if possible, don't mention this to... the child... or you too... will be in danger."
"If you can't look after her... bring her to ...rudo..."
"Mino... will offer a reward."
"I beg you, keep this secret... Do not tell... my deepest gratitude!"
 
So, that was why we moved houses so often— from the Shyriitrik Federation to the Bocanya Kingdom.
That also explained why Granny Taya, though proficient in Shyriitrikan, only ever taught me Bocanyan.
It clarified why she forbade me from revealing my abilities or attending school...
 
"God, forgive me—I lied to her; I had no choice."
"Maybe she'll understand one day, but I can't be the one to tell her—it's too painful..."
"My sweet Aphros, her heart is as flawless as crystal—I can't ruin that; I just can't..."
 
Every sacrifice Granny Taya made was for me...
My parents, who gave everything, likely lost their lives because of me...
 
"Aphros, you can't act like a child anymore."
With that thought, I made a promise to myself—I would hide everything about myself!
 
After learning Shyriitrikan, I never used it again.

A few years of quiet living had lulled me into a naive belief that the danger had passed.
I thought we were just moving again, as we had in previous years, but then Granny Taya hurriedly sent me to Rose Manor.
 
"Make yourself at home, Aphros. Aunt Taya has gone back for some family matters, but I'll take good care of you until she returns,"
Aunt Pollyanna said with a soft smile.
I noticed the sadness hidden behind her forced calmness, and in that moment, I realized the truth—but it was far too late.
 
The fireflies gliding through the valley carried the news—an old woman had fallen by the river for good.
Aunt Pollyanna's pet mynah, Abu, revealed that Granny Taya had come by a few days earlier.
 
It turned out that the one place meant to shelter me had been corrupted. For over fifteen years, Granny Taya had single-handedly kept me safe from pursuers.
It wasn't until last month that they came after me again,
and this time they were far better prepared. With no one to turn to, Granny Taya had to risk seeking help.
 
"The lord of Egarudo, Minotara, is a powerful Felinian. Perhaps this was where her parents hoped to send her."
"Thanks, Pollyanna..."
"Don't worry; it's safe here. Lord Minotara won't allow them to wreak havoc in Egarudo. You and Aphros can stay here without any concerns."
"...Alright then. "I'll bring Aphros here in a couple of days."
"Huh? What about you..."
"I... I've been poisoned, and I don't have much time left. They don't dare to openly attack nobles yet. Their intent was likely to kill me quietly with poison, so no one would stop them from taking Aphros away..."
 
"What?! I'll get a doctor right now—"
"Don't bother. There's no antidote for this poison. I'm a pharmacist myself, remember? Otherwise, I wouldn't have realized I'd been poisoned so quickly..."
"I'll leave quietly. Please, keep this from Aphros. She's sharp; if I stay here, she'll definitely notice. I don't want her to worry."
 
"But she'll figure it out sooner or later..."
"Ease her into the truth. Just say I caught a cold back in my hometown or something like that."
"Don't cry, Pollyanna. Without that child, I would have died fifteen years ago. She's kind and pure-hearted—you're going to love her!"
"I-I'll take good care of her. Aunt Taya, don't worry—I'll treat her like she's my own."
 
"That's what they said, squawk! Abu doesn't understand, but Abu remembers every word, squawk! Abu's the best! Squawk!"
"Huh? Aphros, why are you crying, squawk?! Come on, no tears! You can understand us—that's almost as good as me, squawk! Abu's never met anyone like you before, squawk!"
 
From that day on, I never asked to leave the manor again.
 
Two years later, Aunt Pollyanna told me that Granny Taya had passed away after catching a cold.
 
I remained calm, knowing already that Aunt Pollyanna had buried Granny Taya on the manor grounds.
I planted an acorn by her grave, and it was already sprouting fresh leaves.

The manor had been reduced to ashes years ago, its grounds forever haunted by the curse of Pathos Particles.
In these cursed lands, a Felinian seeking help encountered the former Catto City Inspector, now Chief, who offered assistance.
 
Qi, who quietly coordinated the aid, was engaged in a lively conversation with Minotara, the ruler of the land.
 
"So, you really knew Aphros's parents?"
Qi looked at Minotara, a faint smile on her lips.
 
"Yes, they were powerful. I never imagined they would fall victim to the Divinus..."
"I heard they intended to leave Aphros in your care."
"Pollyanna and I discussed it, and I thought she would be a better caregiver than I could be. Now, I believe you are the best ones to look after Aphros."
 
"Heh! Lord Minotara, you truly underestimate Aphros."
"With her extraordinary memory, her ability to communicate with animals, and the immense power she unleashed in crises to stand against Mr. K's curse..."
If it weren't for Aphros dragging the curse into her dreams to contain it, it would have spread everywhere before you could seal it."
"And let's not forget that she has the power to bridge reality and dreams. That big cat guarding her—if I'm not mistaken—is a manifestation of a dream she created."
"Rather than thinking of it as us taking care of her, I feel privileged to have her with us."
"Her years in the shadows have helped her hone her powers. A reliable and stable Darkpaw—Mr. K would be green with envy if he heard about her, haha!"
 
Minotara remained silent, but the weight of her expression deepened.
"If that's the case, I trust you'll address the latent threats within her."
"Absolutely. The curse has clouded her thoughts, and Lord Ashen Mist will handle it."
"The girl believes she was responsible for the fire at the manor. Although K pulls the strings behind both The Shadow and the Divinus, his main target this time was me—and Egarudo."
 
"He almost succeeded. If Pollyanna hadn't been so cautious and used a fake gem, the curse would have imprinted itself on your contract gems, directly eroding both your souls through the bond."
"Mr. K is a master manipulator—sending a down-and-out noble to sway the manor servants into betraying their master and setting the manor ablaze... But he underestimated the power of the mind."
 
"It's a shame I arrived too late to save Pollyanna... Once I rebuild the manor, I'll bring Aphros here—I'll make a contract with her. The manor and its lands will belong to her."
"Oh, wow! It looks like Aphros is going to be a manor owner! Lord Minotara, you ensure the reconstruction is flawless, and I'll do my best to cleanse the curse's impact on her."
"...Beyond cleansing the curse, I want her to regain her sense of self. She's never had the chance to truly be herself, unable to fully realize who she is. That's the greatest pain she carries."
"That's beyond my abilities, I'm afraid. But I know just the right person for the task! I promise Aphros will be in good hands!"
"With that person, Aphros will surely rediscover her true self!"

A beam of light pierced through the darkness.
It expanded and enveloped my perception.
After what felt like an eternity, a face slowly emerged from the white glow, watching me with somber eyes.
He looked familiar... but who was he?

As the light dimmed, my vision sharpened. An overhead light flickered from the gray ceiling above.
I found myself lying on a pink-and-white hospital bed, surrounded by a myriad of beeping machines. Their rhythmic sounds called to me, lulling me into a sleepy haze.
"Lily, look! Daddy has some new candies for you."
With dark eyes and a forced smile, Dad approached my bed, shaking a bottle of medicine.
"You'll feel better after you eat these candies."

"Daddy Panda" donned white gloves, opened the bottle, and carefully placed a pill onto a spoon, as if performing a sacred ritual. He fed me the medicine, followed by a spoonful of water.
It was a struggle, but I managed to swallow the pill. Daddy Panda's frown eased slightly as he held my hand tightly.
His hands felt like a warm hearth in the dead of winter, thawing my ice-cold fingers.
"Lily is the bravest girl... Daddy... Daddy will make you better..."
Something glimmered in Dad's eyes.
"Lily must be bored lying here for so long. Would you like me to tell you a story?"

I wanted to reach out and touch his face, but I lacked the strength to lift my hand.
"Daddy..."
I called in a faint voice. Suddenly everything brightened again, melting Dad's face into the white light.

I woke up.
Sage explained that this was called a "dream."
But I was just an AI robot. According to my database, only living beings could dream. Why was I dreaming?
"Because, Lily... that was your life... when you were human."

"Sage, I don't understand. Do AI robots have memories of their past? Do they have parents?"
I sat up straight in the backseat, addressing Sage, who was driving.
"Lily, you are special. You're unfortunate, yet lucky at the same time."
"Unfortunate and lucky? I don't get it."
With a screech, the car halted in front of a dilapidated house.
"Lily, an unfortunate child just like you once lived in this house."
Sage stepped out, grabbed the med kit without a word, and knocked on the discolored door.
"However, she never had the luck you possess."

Inside the crumbling house, a bed with only three legs leaned against the wall. An ill Felinian girl lay on it.
"Will I... get better?"
"I'll do my best to make sure of that,"
Sage replied, removing her medical gloves and jotting something down in a notebook.
The girl's eyes dimmed, her sorrowful expression and dark gaze reminding me of my father.

Just like him, I approached and held her hands tightly. Her hands felt small and shriveled, just like mine.
"Hi, I'm Lily. Miss Sage is a great doctor..."
I tilted my head, recalling the words that once gave me strength.
"You're a brave child. Miss Sage will help you!"
"And... if you're bored, I can tell you a story."

"Haha, look who we have here—such a precious little one!"
It was late at night when Delilah stumbled home, clearly intoxicated, and wobbled toward me.
"Oh, my dearest Lily!"
Delilah collapsed into my arms, her fingers tangling in my hair.

"Delilah, you're drunk again."
I jolted awake, rubbed my eyes, and helped her onto the couch before pouring her a glass of water.
"Here, quickly now, you need to rehydrate after all that drinking!"
I pursed my lips, feigning annoyance.
"I've told you countless times! This isn't good for your health..."
I racked my brain for all the medical advice I'd learned from Sage and began my familiar health lecture for the inebriated Delilah.

"...and that's why you can't keep drinking like this. Do you understand?"
Channeling Sage, I pretended to adjust a pair of nonexistent glasses and offered her some "doctorly" advice.
"Alright, alright... My dearest Lily cares about me. I get it."
Delilah gazed at me with hazy eyes, pinching my cheek with a smirk.
"I promise... I'll drink one less glass next time."
"What? Just one less? That's unacceptable!"
"Fine, one and a half glasses less..."

After a bit of playful banter, Delilah settled down, gently stroking my face, reminding me of my father.
"Lily... there's something really important I need to tell you."

"Lily, are you happy being with me?"
"Absolutely! I love spending time with Delilah!"
"That's wonderful to hear."
Delilah lowered her gaze, no longer under the influence of alcohol. She seemed lost in thought.
 
"Do you remember what Sage told you about your dad's words?"
"Yes. Sage said my dad wanted me to be safe, happy, and to grow into a great person."
"Exactly. But what I have here... and what Sage has... they aren't really the best places for you to grow up."
Delilah gently stroked my head, as if she had come to a decision.
 
"Lily, do you like Baker's Cafe?"
"Baker's Cafe? Is that where Shiro and the Inspector—I mean the Chief—live?"
"Yes. I was thinking... if you like it, you could live there."
"I really enjoy being with Shiro and the Chief! But..."
I tilted my head in confusion.
"Why do you want me to live at Baker's Cafe, Delilah? I don't understand..."
Besides, Delilah's life wasn't healthy enough. How could I leave her like this?
 
"I care about you, Lily. But I want you to have a better life... better than here..."
Delilah leaned closer, her cheek brushing gently against mine.
"Sometimes I have jobs to do, and I might not have the time to take care of you... But Shiro..."
"Shiro told me last time that if you wanted, you could stay at Baker's Cafe. Whenever you like... What do you think, Lily?"

What do I think?
I closed my eyes to ponder, but soon my sleep mode kicked in.
Once again, fragments of memories from my past began to surface.

"This... is the core of my dearest daughter, Lily's consciousness."
The man in the hospital bed cradled a spherical crystal in his hands, speaking his final words to the white-haired woman beside him.
She accepted the sphere, holding it delicately.
"There's just one step left... You need to install Lily's consciousness into Prototype No. 7512..."
He poured out his last secrets, fearing he wouldn't have enough time for his life's work to be recognized and preserved.
"Please... keep Lily safe... and help her grow into an exceptional person..."

The sphere in the woman's hands shimmered with a soft light, radiating warmth like a sleeping baby.
"I...promise you."
"Thank you..."
The hospital room fell silent. A beam of setting sunlight illuminated the man's pale arm, guiding him to the afterlife.
"Lily... I wish you a happy and fulfilling life..."

...
...

"Shiro, I'm back!"
A girl dressed in pink and white bounced into Baker's Cafe, her energy infectious.
"I've prepared a new daily health schedule."
Lily was here for the Inspector... the current Chief.

Sage, Delilah, the Chief... everyone important to Lily. She wanted to ensure they were always healthy. She never wanted to relive that past in any of their roles again.
"In the coming week, I will help the Chief adopt a healthier lifestyle."
This was what brought Lily the most joy.
Just leave everyone's well-being in her capable hands.

"You mean the lady who came today was... Delilah?"
"I've never met her, but her beauty is well-known."
"Her status as a socialite is just a facade. In reality..."
 
The unrestrained, familiar chatter spilled out from the private room, unclear if it was their typical rudeness or a desperate need to assert themselves.
The server leading the way had a fleeting look of embarrassment and indignation, seemingly wanting to barge in and put a stop to them.
I gently pressed my hand on her shoulder, offering a reassuring smile as I smoothed her crimson hair ribbon.
Ah, the girl was blushing. Such an innocent demeanor is truly...
I felt compelled to say something to comfort her.
 
"Don't worry."
But my words barely made a ripple in her heart. Malice and prejudice were merely reflections of others' thoughts; she didn't need to carry that burden.
What we needed to figure out now was how to turn their arrogance to our advantage.
 
"Gentlemen, it seems you have some rather unique opinions about the Elis Guild's operations."
"Did you come to this neutral ground, managed by the Guild, because your houses are in decline and you can't exert your influence over the expansionists?"
"If your discussions with the Elis Guild—our potential cooperation—are based on such views, I'm afraid you'll be disappointed."
The people in the room, startled by the sound of the door opening, or perhaps feeling guilty, fell silent and turned their gaze to the "culprit".
His face flushed with embarrassment as he tried to argue, hoping to salvage some dignity.
 
But I wasn't interested in a debate. I needed a victim to send a warning to the others, so I decided to finish the show quickly.
I didn't want to delay my spa appointment.

"I must say, Miss Delilah is not only stunning but also highly capable. That's truly admirable!"
"With such an exceptional socialite, I believe the Elis Guild has a bright future ahead! We look forward to working together to bring peace and prosperity to Mannava!"

The "mastermind" had already left the meeting, and the talks concluded smoothly. I navigated the formalities with ease, as if the earlier unpleasantness had never happened.
 
Personal feelings should never interfere with the greater good.
The noble houses they represented had drained their lifeblood in endless political disputes and military conflicts. Meanwhile, the Elis Guild remained in control of the only demilitarized zone in Mannava, desperately needing power and resources.
 
The peace they touted... Hmph... It's nothing more than them seeking tranquility after losing the capital to compete. Of course, we welcomed their request to join us. In a land scarred by war, every contribution mattered.

After seeing off the last Ambassador of Peace, I strolled to the parking lot, humming a tune out of tune.
Worn out by three hours of political maneuvering, I longed for a long bath and a facial spa.

In the shadows, behind a loathsome silhouette, a familiar scarlet ribbon swayed.
"Don't get too comfortable. You were just lucky today. I was having a bad day. Normally, women of your class wouldn't even get the chance to keep my company."
 
Hmph, that's disgusting.
His frivolous attitude and arrogance reminded me of a memory I'd rather forget...

My home was my first glimpse into the world beyond.
The wall around the window was mottled with cracks, where a few stubborn plants managed to grow. Yet, they did little to brighten the gloomy atmosphere of our household.

With my father's bruises still stinging my lips, I clutched tightly to the alcohol he'd demanded I bring back, returning to stand under that window, feeling the scrutinizing gazes upon me.
Their eyes held a mix of awe, but more so, greed.

"The girl must be their daughter... She looks just like the mother who ran away."
"She's beautiful, but that'll attract too much attention. Not a good thing..."

I lowered my head, doing my best to ignore the constant prying and envy.
 
Ignoring them wouldn't shield me from my father's wrath, though.

On my 13th birthday, I received the first gift of my life—a sweet treat called ice cream, its rich, sugary flavor far surpassing the icy icicles of winter that couldn't even be preserved into summer to provide relief from the heat.

Was that a gift too? Or simply the price for it?

As if trying to make up for the compliments he had never given me, he told me my looks had brought him great fortune.
Maybe I should be thankful for the neighbors' gossip. Even if I didn't understand it then, I instinctively knew it was something to fear.

But what could I do?
I would be beaten. It would hurt. I would go hungry. My life felt like a nightmare.

Perhaps if I just accepted it all, it would be easier than futile resistance.

That night, I was moved to another room with a new window to gaze out of.
The wall surrounding this window was adorned with exquisite wallpaper, but all the luxury in the room felt irrelevant to me.

Ominous sounds echoed from outside the door. I curled up in the corner, waiting for whatever fate had in store.

"And then? What happened next?"
"Ah... I'm sorry. I shouldn't have pressed you. If you don't want to share, that's perfectly fine..."
The server with the scarlet ribbon gasped, her voice trembling, as if she had completely forgotten the danger she had just been in.
 
Mr. Culprit lay on the ground, his face swollen and bloodied, sound asleep and utterly oblivious to our conversation.
I shot him with another dose of tranquilizer and quickly called Garfire, urging her to come clean up this mess.
Honestly, a delicate socialite like me shouldn't have to deal with such a dreadful situation.
 
"Don't worry. You can tell me everything."
"The noise at the door? That was just a mischievous child trying to pick the lock."
Recalling how we first met under the moonlight made me chuckle.
"That's not how an Ancient Felinian princess should act! She was a few years older than me, yet she whined and begged to hang out. She even dragged me away—or should I say, saved me—by sheer force."
 
"Whew, that's a relief. I thought you... I'm glad you're okay."
"Hey, wait! You mentioned an Ancient Felinian princess? The one overseeing the demilitarized zone?"
 
"Isn't it obvious? I just reported to her that we might have some new recruits for the guild."
"...But I need to consult with you first."
 
"What? Me?" The joy in her eyes faded, replaced by disappointment.
"I heard that the Elis Guild plays a crucial leadership role in the peace buffer zone in Mannava. I figured you'd need someone far more capable than me—like those you were just talking to..."
What a sweet worry. She's got a heart purer than any of them, yet she sells herself short for no reason.
 
"Come on, you took this guy down pretty handily. That's quite a talent in my book."
"Ah! I almost forgot about him. I'm going to get fired for this!"
"And that's why..." I leaned closer to her, locking eyes with her earnest gaze.

"I formally invite you to consider joining us. I'll be waiting for your answer."

"The girl you brought back the other day has great potential. She dominates the training grounds."
Glancing at a picture in the message, the crimson hair ribbon was still vividly bright, just like its wearer.
Delilah quietly chuckled as she typed out her response.
"She's much braver than I was back then."

"Different soil grows different flowers."
"What's the status of the Code N investigation?"
 
"Going smoothly."

Delilah recalled everything that had happened since meeting the Inspector, a broad smile spreading across her face.

Irresistibly drawing one in, closer and closer.

Sigh...
Delilah sent another heartfelt message.
"Love is a hand that reaches out but then withdraws."
 
"Huh?"
"Focus on your work."
"Hmph! Miss President, you're not half as cute as you were as a child."
Delilah smiled and replied,

"Okay. Next time you come back, I'll introduce you to that person. You'll like them."

"Unicorn, sweet unicorn, did you eat to your heart's content?"
 
The unicorn remained silent.
This is terrible—there's a note on the unicorn saying I'm going abroad soon—and I haven't packed at all!
Stressed, flustered, and sad, I pouted, straining to remember what I had seen before...
My mind was a complete blank!
 
I was overwhelmed—Viola's to-do list seemed never-ending.
I couldn't recall things from just one glance, and I wasn't allowed to keep a journal...
If only Shiki were still here; she'd give Viola another note as soon as she finished something... Shiki, where have you gone?
I was so upset that tears welled up as I rubbed my eyes.
 
"Didn't I tell you not to cry so much?"
Gasping for air and leaning my head back, I suddenly noticed a note stuck to the chandelier.
How on earth did I get that up there?
Oh, and the note had a big arrow pointing toward the side of the mirror.
 
"There's a work visa in the cabinet behind us. We'll be special screenwriters for the Stars Group from now on."
Special... What?
But the name Stars Group sounded familiar to Viola—she had mentioned it earlier.
Humming a cheerful tune, I opened the cabinet and pulled out a small notebook.
—Viola knew the rule: anything not pre-packed into the unicorn had to go into her pockets!
But beneath the notebook... "Approved by the Catto City Immigration Office"...
 
Catto City? Haven't I been there enough times? Why is it so important now?

Deep-toned furniture and walls fitted with armrests.
Finally, the curtains had been drawn as they should be... Well, that's progress. Maybe a little praise is in order.
Feeling surprisingly upbeat, I scooted my chair over to the balcony.
Through the misty crimson gauze, the city's glowing silhouette emerged beneath the setting sun.
As always, the staff at the gate stood rigidly, their vigilance unwavering.
 
Is "that person" still staying out of this?
If this continues, finding Mr. K will feel like chasing a mirage.
But the power "that person" displayed... If I can't harness it soon, how will I ever step into this illusory city?
With no influential backing, no extraordinary combat skills, and not even the ability to walk...
No, I shouldn't think like that.
I made this choice when I first left home—I will do everything I can to see this revenge through, no matter how hopeless it seems.
Closing my eyes, I took a deep, calming breath... and began to shed the weight of my burdens.
 
"Good evening, S12."
The intruder barged in uninvited, speaking with blatant disrespect.
"I recently saw a patient as far gone as you—what a stroke of luck."
 
That patient you saw was me, you despicable hack.
My grip on my emotions began to slip.

When I first met Sage, I had learned to handle Viola quite well.
It might sound a bit strange, almost as if I'm not really Viola...
That's how she chose to differentiate us—she called herself Viola and me... well, me.
At six years old, I was a puzzle even to myself.
Still, an innocent child is infinitely better than a vengeful, hate-driven madwoman, right?
After all, even Shiki once said that being around Viola was easy.

Though we still don't know who made us this way, she diligently follows my instructions to fulfill my wishes.

"Viola doesn't want to go—it looks really dark over there..."

"Going to another country? Viola hasn't even properly seen this place..."

What's more, she would often feel tired.
"So tired... Viola... needs to rest..."
But this time,
I didn't say a word.
She knew that if she fell asleep somewhere unsafe, I'd be left defenseless when I took over the body.
 
Viola accepted "me" wholeheartedly, without complaint, as if "I" were entirely myself.
That's how we've made it this far.

"Is this really how it ends?"
I spoke half-heartedly about the finale I had just witnessed.
"Thumbelina, with sheer will and the help of friends, escaped the mire... A fairy tale ending, indeed."
 
Sage, her hands resting on the nerves of my leg, seemed to have let go of the topic she had insisted on, drifting into quiet contemplation.
I had grown accustomed to this habit of hers and, surprisingly, found it soothing.
Forthright and dedicated, her lack of social awareness and inability to read the room oddly felt just right to me.
So many people probed into my past, questioning my emotions. While the Pathos outbursts caused more damage than I could ever inflict, everyone still judged me—a stranger with mere physical impairments.

But Sage was different.
She treated me regularly at my mother's request but never delved into my identity.
S12... "S" was shorthand for the category she assigned, and "12" identified me as the twelfth patient within it.
