Everything became data and poured into my senses.
What millions of eyes saw, what millions of ears heard—converted, streamed into my system.

For a moment, I was the city's consciousness—crowned with a trillion neural links.
I was everywhere at once; with a breath, I could be anywhere.

"Did… we do it?"
I tested screens and speakers and spoke my first words as Digital Naka.

"Congratulations, Professor. From now on, you and this city are one."
Cauvin stood just in the cameras' blind spot. I couldn't quite see his face.

Long ago, Lebardmann was just a small offshoot of the Ragdoll kin.
Our chieftain led fewer than a hundred of us in a coastal port of Eressia, assigned to trade with the humans our people despised.
From the start, I was the odd one out—maybe in all the Felinian—too curious about humans and their tech.

What makes humans different from us?
Why don't they have ears and tails?
Why do they get Affliction—can Felinian get it too?

I loved to sprawl on sun‑hot stone steps, watching the big human freighters glide in, drop anchor, and lower the gangplank.

Crew in strange outfits bustled, unloading crates—machine parts we'd never seen, gleaming crystals, and odd objects with no obvious purpose.
The air was brine and rust—and something else… the smell of faraway places.

When I got lost in it, my mother would come stand beside me.
She never dragged me away—just sat, following my gaze.
"Naka, what do you see this time?"

I always pointed at whatever shone brightest—
Maybe the anemometer spinning on the mast, maybe some odd device being assembled on deck.
"Do those shining things… take pain away, like the Soothing Power?"

She froze for a heartbeat, then smiled and ruffled my hair.
"Maybe. Humans don't have what we do, so they find other ways. But you, my darling—your power was born with you. It's a gift from our ancestors."

"Naka, stop wasting time on this nonsense. And stay away from the human institute."
The chieftain yanked the crude microscope from my hands, shaking with anger.
"The Soothing Power is a rare power close to our ancestors. Hone it, and we might join the Ragdoll clan's core!"

"But I love research… and it's not useless…"

Some human firearms rival an adult Felinian.
Airships fly faster than our quickest runners.
Microscopes reveal structures so small even awakened Felinian eyes can't see…
And anyone can use those tools—our gifts are rare.

"I'm not listening to that twisted logic. Our people survived on bloodline, not on human trinkets!"
"But, Uncle Chieftain, weren't we sent here to trade for what humans have and we don't?"

He fell silent.
"I'll train the Soothing Power, I promise. But I want time for what I love too. Please?"
Humans can do many things Felinians can't—but Felinians can do plenty humans can't, too.
If each has strengths, why shouldn't I learn both?

After training the Soothing Power every day, my power did grow—but the crash hit harder each time. Barely a month in, I blacked out mid-practice for the first time.

"That's normal with the Soothing Power. I told your chieftain: it's powerful—almost enough to heal any Black Blight, and it works on human Affliction. But it burns the user's life force."

"If it's for healing, fine. But you knew it drains her life—and you still had her practice aimlessly?"
As far as I remember, that was the first time my parents ever lost their temper with the chieftain.

"It's just life force. She likes humans, doesn't she? Our kind lives over three hundred years. Burn a hundred—two hundred—she still outlives them. With talent like hers, she has a duty."
"Duty? You want her to trade her life for hollow glory?"
"Then I'd rather leave this family behind!"

After that, my parents took me away.
"I'm not afraid to die… I just don't want to die for nothing."
My mother stroked my hair.
"Silly girl. Death is a long way off. That's not your worry today. From now on, do what you love."

Everything after that started on that day.
Much later, I learned that everything has a price. The one called "ideal" is the heaviest of all.

The warm morning light streamed through the window, spilling over my little desk.
The girl in the mirror looked bright and cheerful. The band-aid on my knee from yesterday's tree incident didn't bring me down at all.
Mom leaned in to tie my sailor scarf, adjusting the ribbons with care.
"My, don't you look lovely today, Asura? Just like a little princess."

"I don't wanna be a princess!" I protested, shaking my head and sending my pigtails flying.
"Mom, I'm the boss of the Resilient Paws! We stand up for what's right and send all the bad guys packing!"
I reached for the tabby cat plush on my pillow and held it up high. "Back me up, Top Cat!"

"Sure, sure, our little hero. But it's your birthday. Let's try to stay out of trouble today, okay?"
Dad said with a smile, smoothing down my tail and ruffling my hair.
"Yeah, yeah, deal!"
I said the words, but my mind was already made up.
The Resilient Paws doesn't take a day off just because the boss has a birthday! This definitely didn't count as trouble!

Once my parents were out, I dashed to the window and whistled. My team, lounging in the grass, perked up immediately.
Quick check: Gray, Ginger, Tuxedo... All present and accounted for!
"Usual spot. This afternoon. Big one!" I hissed, giving a quick signal.
Gray responded with a sharp "Mrow!" and a paw lick. Now that's a solid vice-captain!

I can't wait for this afternoon... Catto City is counting on us!

Mom and Dad were out shopping. Perfect!
I slipped out of the house and made my way to our secret base in the alley.
"Resilient Paws, rally up!" I announced, holding up Top Cat as my team gathered around.
Gray nuzzled my leg while Ginger swished her tail patiently. Everyone was ready.

Then I heard it—a faint sound of crying carried on the breeze.
I signaled for silence and followed the sound. There, huddled against the wall, was a little boy in overalls, wiping his eyes.
"What's the matter?" I asked, mimicking my dad's comforting tone.
"I can't find my mom..." he whimpered, looking up with tear-streaked cheeks. He was definitely younger than me.
"Don't worry! I'm Asura, the head of the Resilient Paws. It's our mission to help those in need!"

I turned to our sharpest agent. "Vice Captain Gray, you're in charge. Lead us to the community police post!"
The boy blinked away his tears. "You... you can really command cats?"
"Absolutely!" I replied confidently, taking his hand. "Just leave it to me! I'm a professional!"

Gray guided us through the familiar backstreets. I kept the boy entertained by telling him about how we scared off that bully bird from the nest last week.
He hung on every word, his worried expression gradually turning into a grin.
Yeah... this felt right. The world could always use more smiles!

"...and then Gray went flying—"
A loud, menacing bark cut me off.
A massive dog barreled into the alley, teeth bared and eyes fixed right on my cats!
"MEEEEOW!" Gray let out a sound I had never heard before. Her fur puffed up, and she leaped onto the wall.
Ginger and Tuxedo were so terrified that they scrambled behind a trash can, shaking in fear.

"Go... go away..." I could barely manage to whisper. My whole body felt like it was trembling.
The dog growled and advanced closer. It was almost right in front of us now.
The little boy clung to me, tears streaming down his face.
"Stop!"
I shouted as loudly as I could. I was crying, but I couldn't move.
...
I can't run away!
I'm the boss...
I... I have to protect everyone!

"GO AWAY!"
Fear took over, and I reacted without thinking. I threw Top Cat—my very important commander—straight at the dog.
The soft toy soared through the air before landing in the dirt.
The dog seemed taken aback and paused. Just then, its owner rushed over and grabbed its leash.
"Sorry! Sorry! It got away from me! Are you okay?"
My mind felt completely blank. I just shook my head.

Once the dog was gone, all my courage evaporated.
I looked at Top Cat lying on the ground, then at Gray perched on the wall, and finally at the others still hiding. I felt overwhelmed by fear over what had almost happened and guilt for what I had done.
I hadn't protected anyone. I threw my friend and got it all dirty...

I fought back tears as I picked up my muddy Top Cat and hugged it tightly.

"Look who it is, our hero... Hey, what's going on? Did something happen?"
Mom knelt in front of me, her hands steadying my shoulders as she spoke softly.
I started crying, the words tumbling out between sobs.
"Mom... I was really scared... I threw it away. I feel like a failure as a boss..."
I buried my face against her, sobbing too hard to say more.

"Asura, you've got it all wrong."
After a moment, Mom gently wiped my tears with her thumb and locked eyes with me.
"True courage isn't about being fearless. It's about being terrified but still finding the strength to stand up for others. And that's exactly what you did today. You held your ground even when you were scared. That's the greatest bravery of all."
Her words wrapped around me like a warm blanket. My tears began to slow, though my nose still tingled.

"But... I still threw Top Cat. It's all dirty now..."
My voice trailed off into a whisper, weighed down by guilt.
Dad took the dusty Top Cat from my hands and gently brushed it off.
"It's just a little dirty. It's not broken, and it's still with you."
He crouched down beside me, ruffled my hair, and smiled.
"It saw your courage today, Asura. I'm proud of you."
"Mom... Dad..."
Oh no, I could feel the tears threatening to spill over again.

"Meow~" A familiar cry came from the window.
I turned to see Gray leaping gracefully onto the sill, its gem-like eyes warm and inviting.
Soon, Ginger's fluffy head appeared, followed by Tuxedo... they were all here.
My team hadn't abandoned me. They weren't angry.
They... were still waiting for me.

A huge weight lifted from my heart.
I sniffled, took Top Cat from Dad, and hugged it tightly to my chest.
"Yeah, I get it now. Next time... I promise I'll do better!"
The Resilient Paws never stay down for long!

Even much later, Asura often found herself reflecting on that birthday afternoon when she was eight.

The warmth of the sun, the dusty air, the nervous sweat on her palms, and the seemingly permanent stains on her Top Cat's fur... The memory wasn't always vivid, but the way fear gripped her heart just before she forced herself to step forward—that was a feeling she would never forget.

Understanding came much later, after she had witnessed fights far more brutal than any childhood game. It was then that the young woman truly appreciated her parents' wisdom. Her eight-year-old self, scared and shaky, had still chosen to stand as a shield. That small, trembling spark of "protection" was a glimpse of the path her life would follow.

The "Resilient Paws" might be long gone, but the sweet, simple memories remained. When her parents went missing and her normal life shattered, it was these echoes of a happier time that carried her through the long years of despair. She still loved to take out that old, stitched-up tabby cat plush. While she didn't carry Top Cat around anymore, it always had a special place in her gear— a quiet trophy of her first promise and a reminder of the reason she fought.

Deep down, she was still that little girl in a blue sailor dress, with band-aids on her knees, shouting about fighting for what was right.

She was. And she always would be.

A while ago, the Inspector started asking everyone to share their first impressions of each other. Since it seemed to help with team bonding, I had no objection.
I simply declined to participate.
I had already made my assessment of the Inspector perfectly clear: "lazy, scatterbrained, chronically late to meetings, and altogether half-baked."
The Inspector, somehow, was not satisfied.

—Of course, that wasn't all of it.
I still felt lost.
Even through the eyes of the future, I couldn't see clearly.
I had already reached those answers, yet I still didn't know how to put them into words.
Naka couldn't tell me. And neither could the Inspector.

So, every now and then, I find myself wondering—
that future beyond the countdown... can it really be changed?
Everything that happened...
...No. Not yet. It still isn't time.

When that day truly arrives, I'll tell you the rest.
All of it.
So until then—
Thank you for staying by my side, all this time.
Thank you, "▆▆▆▆."

When a life comes into this world, it takes from the one who bore it more than flesh and blood.
A faint glimmer of that soul, too, is etched into the new life.
And so, bearing that sin, the child who once arrived in tears spoke:
"Thank you for giving me a lifetime to live."
"Even if it is filled with hardship and tears, I will walk forward with a smile."
"—Thank you, Mom."

For the past few nights, the Inspector had been taking walks with me around the streets near Baker's Cafe.
"This is my first time in Catto City... and my first time ever leaving Divinus. Could you stay with me a little longer?"
"..."
The look on the Inspector's face was exactly what I expected. So was the answer—
"Alright. But you haven't fully recovered yet, so we're not going too far."

A shrill, agonized cry rang out from the alley. We hurried over, but all we saw was a shadow slipping away into the dark, with a few tiny shapes huddled nearby.
They were alive. At least, they were still moving.

"Those are... baby sparrows."
Something in the Inspector's voice sounded strangely strained.
I stepped closer, and only then did I see them clearly: four nestlings lay scattered on the ground, each small enough to fit in my palm. Some had their wings torn off. Some had their bellies ripped open. But they were so tiny, there was hardly any blood.

"They're all going to die."
Ah... I shouldn't have said it like that.
My tone must have been too cold. If I could say it again, I'd make myself sound a little more regretful.

"Yeah... If we'd gotten here a little sooner."
The Inspector gently shook their head, a look of regret on their face.

"Inspector, who do you think did this?"
"Probably a cat or dog. But it could've been a snake, a raptor... or even a person."

"A person? But people don't eat sparrows. Why would they kill them?"
"Because... well... maybe they just hate sparrows. Maybe they wanted to destroy their nest. Or maybe it was just for fun. It's hard to tell..."

"Most humans kill with intent, while animals don't understand the meaning behind their actions. Which do you think is more contemptible, Inspector?"
"Killing is killing, Ulthar. I don't think one is more vile than the other. But if I had to choose, I'd say humans are worse. At least animals don't dress it up as something justified. Humans invent all kinds of 'necessary' reasons for killing, and in the end, they convince themselves they were justified in taking a life."

A textbook answer. Just as expected.
It didn't disappoint me. But it didn't surprise me, either.

I watched as the person before me crouched down, took off their light coat, and gently wrapped the four dead chicks in it.
"It's not just humans. All sentient beings are prone to forgetting that a life is a life—not merely 'a sparrow.'"

I stood to one side, watching as he filled the small pit with dirt.
"Do you always do things like this?"

"Like what?"
Inspector paused and turned to look at me, a hint of confusion on their face.

"Death is always near, Inspector. There's no shortage of it in this world."
I gestured toward the tiny, unfinished grave.
"If you keep doing this, it'll wear you down."

"Oh, this? It was nothing, really. I just happened to be here. If I'd had something more important to do, I wouldn't have bothered."
Inspector covered the grave with the last bit of dirt, then patted it down with the back of the shovel.
"True, there's no shortage of death. But I still want to hold on to a basic respect for life..."
"I'm afraid of going numb—afraid that one day I'll stop taking death seriously and end up like those I hate."

"...Huh?!"
"U-Ulthar?"

I slipped my arms around the one who had, somehow, started to occupy my thoughts.
"Inspector... do you hate me?"

"Hate you? Of course not. Why would you think I'd hate you...?"
Good. The voice above me was a little stiff, but at least I hadn't been pushed away.

"I crawled my way out of a pile of corpses. Maybe... I'm exactly the kind of person you were talking about. Someone numb to death."
Inspector's body was warm. I held them a little tighter and felt the slightest tremble in my arms.
"That's not your fault, Ulthar. If anyone's to blame, it's the people who did this to you."

"Then... may I stay by your side from now on? I'll hold on to you, remind you, keep you from falling any deeper... and you can teach me, little by little, what it means to respect death."

The only answer I received was silence.

By the time I got back to Baker's Cafe, it was already late into the night.
Inspector said I should get to bed early. Mm... then I will.
For now, I should be a good kid.

...
Again.
That room—one I know all too well.
That cold, acrid smell never fades, in stark contrast to the calming scent of Baker's Cafe.

I stood in the middle of the room, surrounded by countless versions of "me" floating in tanks. Tubes were pierced into their brains, mouths, noses, limbs, and spines—pumping in nutrients, draining waste, and flooding them with information.
It hurts. I know. Like shards of glass being pressed into your head, one piece at a time.
And there, among rows of identical tanks, I found "myself."

I pressed my fingertips against the outer wall of the tank. "I" opened my eyes, lips moving faintly as a trail of tiny bubbles slipped free.
I knew what "I" was trying to say. At that moment, there was only one thing "I" wanted to say—
"Save me."

Poor kitten... you didn't even have a name.
No one loved you. No one cared about you. And, of course, no one was ever coming to save you.
But back then, "I" didn't know any of that.
Even in the darkest moments, with death only half a step away, "I" still naively believed that all suffering would one day come to an end.

"Raise your head. Look at me."
Whenever I return to this "dream," I always speak to "myself."
Though I know it's nothing more than a phantom of the past.
It can't change what has happend, nor can it touch the present.

And yet, I still speak.

"See? I'm right here. You know me, right?"
"I" responded with a small nod. Good girl.
"You may cry, but you're not allowed to die."
"Not until you become me."

...
I woke from the dream. A chill crept over me.

"Come in."
I opened the bedroom door.

"Ulthar? It's late... couldn't sleep?"
"Mm. I have a bit of a headache."
"I see... There should still be some stabilizer in the fridge. I'll go get it for you."
"No need. If you don't mind, Inspector, just let me stay with you for a little while... I feel a lot better just being with you."

Inspector agreed, just as I expected.
Good.

Curled up beside Inspector, I noticed a cut on their right index finger—the same hand that had once laid those sparrows to rest.
"When did you get hurt?"
"This? I cut it by accident while cooking earlier. Just a tiny cut, no big deal."

Inspector lifted their hand and held the finger out to me, as if to reassure me it was nothing serious.
Almost by instinct, I gently closed my lips around it.

"...!"
Inspector snatched their hand back as if they'd been shocked, a thin, glistening strand stretching from their finger.
"Ulthar… don't."
"Sorry... I overstepped. I just thought it might help the cut heal faster... I… I'll go now."
—Ask me to stay.

"No... I mean... you don't have to do that. Relax—this is Baker's Cafe, not Divinus."
"Then… why didn't you answer my question earlier, Inspector?"

Inspector looked like they wanted to say something, but hesitated.

"Once we're better prepared, we'll be leaving for Leidsdam."
"As you can see, staying by my side is dangerous. And besides… you only just got out of Divinus."
"Like I said before, I want you to have a normal life from now on—to grow up in the light, far away from all that mess in your past."

"There's no getting away."
"I can't escape it—and you know that as well as I do, don't you? If we don't put the past to rest, sooner or later it'll come back for us."
"You saved my life. I want to do something for you… please. So at least let me go to Leidsdam with you."

I turned away from Inspector and walked toward the door, keeping my head lowered the whole time. I couldn't let anyone see the smile on my face.
"My head doesn't hurt much anymore. You should get some rest too, Inspector. And thank you... for tonight."
What a pity. All I could hear behind me was the faint hitch in Inspector's breathing—I couldn't see their expression.
It must have been fun.

The storm is coming, my dear.
Come with me—to the very heart of it.

It had been raining in Quince for days on end.
At dusk, Ulthar slipped out alone, the lights of Baker's Cafe fading behind her.
She had an excellent memory. After a few turns, she found the alley without much trouble.

The alley was quiet, no different from countless others. In a busy district like Quince, no one would ever give a place like this a second glance.
Ulthar stopped where the sparrows had died, then crouched down and ran a hand over the ground, lowering her head for a closer sniff.
No blood. No trace. Not even the faintest scent. It had probably been washed away by the rain, and whatever was left had been carefully cleaned up afterward.
—As if nothing had ever happened.

She left the alley and headed toward the small grove.
The weeds seemed thicker than before. Ulthar wandered in circles for quite a while before finally finding the little dirt mound, almost flattened by the wind and rain.

"Miss, it's pouring. You should get under cover."
An elderly man hobbled past under an umbrella, likely one of the local residents.
Ulthar stared straight ahead and shook her head expressionlessly.
"What are you staring at that patch of ground for? You'll catch a cold if you stay out here..."
Seeing that the girl had no intention of responding, the old man finally took the hint and shuffled away.

Ulthar stood there for a long time.
"What's dead is dead. No one will ever know… It's no different from before."
She murmured to herself.

"Maybe that's for the best. A clean death isn't so bad—better than what some others got."
She slowly raised her right arm. A massive, pale hand appeared in midair, a blood-red eye in its palm.

"Boom!"
The hand slammed down, then dissolved into threads and vanished.
As the dust settled, the little mound disappeared into the surrounding ground.
At most, a passerby might complain about the uneven path, but no one would ever notice this place again.

She turned and left, never once looking back.

Let me think... where should I begin?

Perhaps with the mist.

Mist lies year-round over the sea-lanes of the Sea of Plenty.
The handful of records that survive speak of sails that once crowded this route—shadows, half-seen.
But for me, and for most of my people, that age is so distant now it has passed into legend.

These waters were once awakened by lamplight and the cry of steam whistles. They have long since gone lifeless.
Rustfire Isle lies mottled with rust—as do the steel bridges, pipelines, and bones of steamships that once joined it to the other two islands. Now it is home to little more than wheeling ravens and a few Anomalies drifting along the shore.

It is no place for the living to linger.

The great works of that bygone age of industry were sealed away in the Cataclysm, and Pathos Particles settled over everything—the islands, the sea, and all that lies beneath.
Plants swelled to monstrous size; insects grew shells like tempered steel; and strange things out of the deep, trailing eerie spines of bone, came to prowl the misted waters.
Every trace of what was once called civilization was scoured away.

The survivors fled the land they had once called home, leaving only us—those who scrape a living among the islands.
I came in with the tide, born of these churning waters.
Tidemark Tabby—that is our name.

My people hold fast, proud and stubborn, to the last untainted ground among the reefs, stringing the scattered havens together with our small boats.

We do not believe ourselves mere survivors.
In the teachings of the Earth Mother, every one of us is a warrior—and every one of us will, in time, become a god.
The flesh is only a vessel to ferry the soul across.

Death, then, became something to strive toward. No birth among us is truly a beginning; each is an ancestral spirit treading the warrior's trials anew.
For one day we shall cross the sea again, and set out on the voyage home—to the ancestral land.

The sacred office I inherited is that of the Mourner.

To be precise, I am charged with guarding the Necropolis of Heroes.
I receive the departed, and make certain that souls still possessing an anchor of will may find their way back to the ancestral land.
And so it goes—day after day, year after year. Until the living I have known return to the Earth Mother's embrace, and the dead are born anew beneath the Throne of Heroes.

At some point, I could not say when, my people began to call me the Plume of the Tide.

Perhaps because my wings were never meant for flight.
Perhaps because my ravens bear away the souls that have not yet found their way home.
Or perhaps only because they needed a name for the things they could not easily explain.

—It makes no difference.
My calling is simply to raise this lantern. Nothing more.

The Necropolis lies deep in the Sea of Plenty, out along the rim of the shallows that ring the Steam Islands.
It is an unmarked stretch of water, far from any sea-lane. To look at, it is only a surface of perfect stillness—no whitecaps, no birds—a flat blue-green that mirrors the ever-gray sky.

"Once you pass into the Necropolis of Heroes, you can no longer hear the tide."
That is what I used to tell the poor sailors who strayed into those forbidden waters.

I need not have said anything at all, but the oracle had summoned me there, and perhaps one among them carried a heroic soul waiting to be reborn.
A heroic soul makes no distinction of race, yet most outsiders do.
The living are so easily beguiled by appearances, turning against one another over outward differences, forgetting the will they first carried.

It falls to me to receive these lost souls and wake the heroic will within them.
Sadly, no ancestral spirit has yet worked a miracle through an outsider.

The salt wind always clouds a lost sailor's judgment, yet it is not only the wind. Woven through it is the world's dark will, dragging the living down into the realm of the dead.
That, I cannot prevent.
Even the finest navigators and helmsmen of the civilized world, once they draw near the Necropolis, slowly forget the course they were holding. As if bewitched, they sail deeper, and deeper still—

And then the hidden reefs swallow every channel a ship might take, leaving wreck after wreck of those who wandered too far.

And so this place has another name: the Dead Sea.

Only the Tidemark Tabby can cross the Dead Sea.
Only I can guide a ship back out.

Most who are lucky enough to escape go on to boast of their own courage; few ever come back to thank me.
Just as well—I do not mind.

Now and then, someone will speak in terror of "the floating ones."

And they are not wrong. Beneath the Dead Sea, the dead drift in multitudes.
Below the Necropolis lie humans, Felinians, Anomalies, and sea-beasts so ancient no one can name their kind. They hang suspended in the water, yet never decay.

Those are the heroic souls. Their bodies sleep here for eternity, and from them, gods are born anew.
This is the planet's Necropolis of Heroes
—and the ancestral land of the Tidemark Tabby.

As for my own work... I give names to the remains that cannot rest, and watch over the heroic souls still waiting to be reborn.
The ravens are always with me, and I am always with the heroic souls—my own kin and strangers alike.
I simply stay there, waiting quietly for the sea to carry away the last longing each soul clung to in life, and to part it from its empty shell.

And so, to me, the Dead Sea holds no terror.

My weapon?
Ha… surely you jest.
As befits the Mourner's divinity, I was born of a prayer for a valkyrie; yet I take no part in the quarrels of the living… and so it would be presumptuous of me to call any weapon truly mine.
For a long while, at least, that is what I believed.

You see, all I carry is this one lantern.
Though it takes the shape of a long scythe, it is only a small light to guide the dead—nothing more.

It was only later—when people saw the ravens gathered at my back, and the still water break into black feathers—that they began to imagine otherwise.
Seeing the heroic souls answer my call, they mistook this lantern of mine for a weapon, and me for one who possessed the power to command the dead.

There—please, do not be afraid.
It is only the heroic souls, answering me.

...Why do I not correct them?
If such a misunderstanding moves the living to hold a little more reverence for death, then I think it does no harm.

"Souls of the Einherjar"—that is its other name.

Yes, just as you suppose: in a sense, it is no single object. More precisely, it is the gathered echoes of every heroic soul across all the ages of the tidal civilization—and the authority it grants is what binds me to the Throne of Heroes.

Among my people, there is an old saying...
Outsiders tend to take it as judgment, as though the Dead Sea punishes the souls who were not brave enough, not pure enough, not loyal enough, and I am the one charged with dragging them into the deep.
But I do not see it so.

In truth, until I heard it told that way, it had never once occurred to me that I might have the right to judge anyone. 

A heroic soul, I think, is neither a victor nor one without fear.
It is simply someone who understands their own purpose—who lives quietly with it, and does not turn away from the end that awaits them.

I do no more than raise the lantern, and put my question to those wills that lie sunk beneath the Dead Sea.
If they choose to answer still, their answer becomes my sword and shield—
the road that leads them home.

I was never meant to leave the Dead Sea.

I was meant to keep my watch at the edge of the Necropolis of Heroes, to guard the waters where the tide makes no sound.
This was the sacred office I inherited, the duty my people laid upon me.

And yet, in the end, I left.

The command came from Nornveil.
But the resolve to obey came from the Dead Sea Codex as Skuld read it—and from the oracle that Verdandi placed in my hands.

"The light of salvation kindles in the east, and breaks westward through the clouds."

By the time those words surfaced upon the Codex's pages, Skuld had gone several nights without sleep.
Verdandi, who governs the Present, had meant to deliver the oracle wrapped in some small jest, so the mood would not sink wholly into deathly silence—yet that goddess, who had always had such a gift for putting others at ease, could not in the end bring herself to smile.

I remember being silent for a long while.
Nornveil would never ask such a thing of me lightly.
The goddess who holds dominion over Fate understood, better than anyone, what it means for the Necropolis of Heroes to be left without its Mourner.
And so they all understood—
there was little time left.

The ancestral land was sinking. The Dead Sea trembled.
The islands the Tidemark Tabby depended upon were no longer safe.
Our numbers dwindled, rebirths grew ever more frequent—and yet the Necropolis only grew more crowded.

So for a time I entrusted part of the Dead Sea's authority to the sister who presides over Birth, and sealed the Necropolis.

It was not an easy thing.
Or rather, I had never once imagined I would leave that place of my own will.

Before I left, I asked Nornveil:
"And if there is no light in the east?"
She did not answer.

She did not know what words could answer such a question, nor whether any answer existed at all.
It was Verdandi who stood before me then, but I knew that Skuld, who is always with her, had surely heard it too.
Neither of them spoke. They only looked at me.
There was guilt in Verdandi's eyes.

But that was never what I intended.
I had no wish to leave her, or Skuld, anxious on my account.

So I continued:
"Verdandi—I will carry the lantern there."
"Until the light comes."

For such is my fate.

"Fate will light the way for you."
That was the last time, before I left, that I saw Nornveil smile.

Outsiders find the fate of the Tidemark Tabby hard to grasp.
They do not understand why the Tidemark Tabby would enter the Dead Sea of their own accord, nor why death should be where their lives begin, nor why a people on the brink of extinction would presume, here of all places, to speak of the fate of the planet.

The truth is, few know what "the planet" even means.
Even the Tidemark Tabby, who have read both past and future in the weave of fate, cannot say why the ancestral spirits called this world "the planet."

Fewer still ever come to understand Vingrakka.

She has the look of an envoy of death.
In a sense, that is exactly what she is.

Seen from a distance, she is usually ringed by ravens; her soul-lantern sways, and black runes flicker faintly across her pale skin.

Perhaps it is the authority of her divinity—but wherever she goes, even the triage ward of the Emotion Remedy Center, at its most frantic, falls quiet for a moment as she passes.

Yet she rarely uses her authority, and never speaks of these things.

She does not like the word "oathbreaker."
The way she sees it, most souls have not forsaken their vows—they have only forgotten the way home, lost in suffering too long endured.

She has seen remains adrift in the Dead Sea for centuries; seen heroic souls worn down to hollow shells, still reaching to grasp the long haft of her scythe; seen warriors once mighty howling in meaningless agony as the corruption consumed them.

She cannot save everyone.

The oracle once said that all life holds the potential to become a warrior. But Vingrakka knows, better than anyone, that not every soul can reach the ancestral land.

Many lose their way, and more still have never so much as heard of the anchor. They scatter into the flood of Pathos Particles, and vanish without a trace.

This is why she keeps her silence.

She must go on lighting the lantern, go on ferrying the dead, go on setting every soul whose will still endures upon the road home.
Though fewer and fewer return. Though the Dead Sea grows ever more crowded. Though the ending has long since been foretold...
Though one day, she too will sink beneath this tideless sea.

Still, she is there.

"To sink is not the worst fate."
"The worst is for no one to remember what you once lived for."

So she says, and raises the lantern once more—
as though, deep in the dead water, countless heroic souls were once again raising their own "anchors."

Nice work, everyone!

"Here's to a smooth launch!"

That would be me.

I duck into the restroom, where the door at least muffles the noise outside.
Water streams between my fingers, cold enough to sting.

I wish I could just get out of things like this.

Not that I dislike my colleagues. They're all at the top of their field; a few are honestly funny, and the project lead is gracious and generous... It's a far friendlier workplace than I ever imagined.
I'm just no good at this part. The mingling.

I never cared much for socializing, not even as a child. That's why I went into communications engineering in the first place.
In a world where Affliction can disrupt the internet at any moment, local network clusters have become the standard solution.
And each of those digital islands has a quiet corner or two—long forgotten, long unwatched—where a few kindred spirits can find one another.
Underground idols. Amateur sleuthing. Hacking... There's always something.

So much of the world I know has been made possible by the work I love. I've seen Catto City's first mainframe come online. I've watched a dedicated transoceanic communications link go live. I should be thrilled by all of it.

Even as everyone outside talks excitedly about where the project is headed, I still feel empty.

Urban legends. Strange phenomena. Rumors.

Nine times out of ten, I know exactly what they are.
Clickbait. Hearsay. Lies dreamed up by people with too much time on their hands.
Countless threads like these appear on the forum every day, and just as many are forgotten.

It's still fascinating, though.

Their curiosity and fear are what make the stories real.

What's it like to believe?

The ones who post on the forum. The ones who refresh the page over and over in the middle of the night. The ones who take something they can't explain, spin it into a few hundred words, then sit there waiting for a stranger's reply—
What did they see?
Why do they believe stories like these?
And once they do, what does the world look like to them?

I haven't watched them nearly enough.

"If only I could make a place that was truly free. Somewhere all that curiosity could run wild, with nothing to hold it back."
The thoughts keep circling.

Something wells up inside me—something I've never felt before.

Curiosity. The urge to pry. Delight.

The Last Cross hauntings have attracted considerable attention lately, but our research has yet to yield any definitive conclusions.
What we can say for certain is that this is a composite urban legend—one that only emerged after internet ghost stories became widespread.

According to recent news reports, a construction error at Niihara Station inadvertently created a hazardous Pathos Drop Point.
Those who wander into it often experience hallucinations, which are believed to account for the panic and cases of Pathosis reported in the area. This phenomenon is also widely considered the basis of the urban legends surrounding Niihara Station—or, as it is known in the stories, Last Cross.

Stories currently in circulation include "The Girl at the Window," "The Train That Never Stops," and "The Station That Shouldn't Exist." These accounts differ in detail but share a similar tone and style, and are generally believed to draw on Sakura Island folklore and the Castaway Island train accident.

Tracing these stories back to their earliest source has proven far more difficult. A search of our database indicates that they only began appearing in our records within the past two months, though they may have been circulating online for another month or two before that.
This has led some to speculate that the stories first spread among students near Niihara Station.

According to our findings, an anonymous chatroom saw a brief surge in popularity within the past six months. During the same period, the number of urban legends and ghost stories about Catto City appearing online increased dramatically, with several particularly notable entries preserved in our archives.

However, the chatroom's server has since shut down, and much of the material associated with it has been lost.

In our next installment, we will explore the urban legends surrounding the anonymous chatroom itself.

As Black Tea gazes out the window, her response to Milk is soft, her thoughts drifting away.
 
Her earliest memories transport her to a small land blanketed in R. rubus blossoms.

The field of flowers in her mind now exists as a distant "dream."

Milk's usually detached demeanor softens as she speaks.

Alone in the empty courtyard, Black Tea closes her eyes, still lost in thoughts of her homeland.

when she wakes once more, the world before her will shift irrevocably.

I always find myself in the role of protector,

I believed that as long as everything was within my gun's reach, I could ensure its safety.
This balance of closeness and distance feels just right to me.
 
My earliest memory takes me back to a grand palace, forever surrounded by blossoming flowers.
It was the imperial city of a small, forgettable kingdom, so insignificant that even its name has been lost to history.
Perhaps its small size shielded it from the world's turmoil.
 
As the sole Gourmandian here, I served the ruler of this nation.

But... I was always there with her.
I vowed to protect her and the country she cherished,
a promise I had the power to uphold.
She once mentioned that my presence brought happiness to all here.

With the arrival of spring, the blooming flowers would be harvested to decorate the celebrations.

The wind danced around us as we leaped from the tower, landing in the bustling festival streets.

leading me through the throng until we reached a shop's entrance.

New clothes?

"Absolutely, it never fails to impress."

"Here, I had Mr. Lewis tailor it to your measurements."
She pushed the dress into my arms, leaving me no choice but to accept it.

"I've been wanting to surprise you with this. Today seemed like the perfect occasion."

"This is my first gift to you since I became queen. I can't keep giving you trinkets that only children would enjoy, can I?"
"...Thank you, Camellia."

—I lost everything I was meant to safeguard.

Camellia's desolate gaze and her former smiles... They torment me, blending in my mind.

"Please, stop."
A white arc of light materialized before me, enveloping me in a warm embrace.
It felt like a bubble, cradling me gently on the precipice of darkness.
 
The following events blurred, and much remains hazy in my memory.
My sole recollection is that Milk rescued me from the brink of full "Fallmorph" on that pivotal day.
It was Milk and her partners who restored my sanity.
Through our interactions, their abode, Satan Café...
It started to feel like another haven worth protecting.
 
But can I safeguard it this time?

propelling her to take that courageous first step forward.

Deep Dream is akin to the vast, pitch-black seabed spanning thousands of miles, where not a single delectable fish can be spotted, only an endless expanse of silence.
 
"Hello, is there anybody...?"
"Master... everyone..."
Where exactly is the way back home?
I continued to stir the seawater, yearning to swim around.
With each passing second, my panic mounted, my heart burdened so heavily it felt as though it would pull my body into ever deeper trenches.
 
In this foggy state of mind, a sudden warm touch gently caressed my head, and a soothing voice seemed to break through the sea's surface, reaching the frigid seabed.
"Chocola? Wake up... Chocolate...!"
 
The lapping sound of the sea gradually receded from my ears.
I jolted awake as if emerging from a brush with death, the world appearing blurred. The fingertips that had been resting on my head now tenderly brushed my cheek, wiping away the tears brought on by drowsiness.
Finally, I discerned the figure standing beside me. It was Vanilla.
　
"I noticed you were sleeping restlessly on the sofa, so I woke you up."
"How are you feeling now?... Did you have a nightmare?"
 
"Uh... Vanilla..."
For some inexplicable reason, a wave of sorrow washed over me.
Without hesitation, I threw myself into Vanilla's embrace, burying my head in her neck and frantically seeking solace, trying to sense her breath against my skin.
 
"Good girl. I understand. Are you feeling homesick?"
Vanilla gently enfolded me, patting my back with her right hand, the bond between twins swiftly helping her grasp my unease.
"Mmm."
I bowed my head and replied softly, sensing the hand behind me tighten slightly as Vanilla hugged me close.
　
"My feelings mirror yours."
"Before discovering the way back home, we must learn to regulate our emotions. Only then can we confidently forge ahead..."

"Shiro's skills are absolutely amazing—!"
 
I cheered, raising the silver spoon holding the last bite of the delicious strawberry cream cake, and bringing it ceremoniously to my lips. My tongue eagerly savored the cream, filling me instantly with joy and sweetness.
 
"Mmm..."
"Ah, my earlier gloominess vanished in an instant! That's the wonder of Pathos energy, isn't it?"
 
"It's not just the magic of Pathos food, you know."
"Eh?"
I looked at Shiro with a puzzled expression, not fully grasping her deeper message right away.
 
"You have the ability to uplift and drive happiness within yourself, which is a precious quality."
"Is that so...? Hee-hee..."

"Engaging in other activities..."
I repeated Shiro's suggestion softly, suddenly having a realization—!
 
"Eh!!? How do you know what's troubling me..."
"Because you wear your heart on your sleeve. I mentioned it before. There's no need to hide, they will surely notice."
Vanilla, who had been quietly eating, finally set down her spoon and glanced over.
The feeling of being noticed made my ears warm, momentarily unsure how to react, I instinctively turned my head, pretending to be engrossed in observing the guests at the nearby table.
 
I truly didn't want you to worry about me.
After all, I am a mature little cat, and it would be too embarrassing if you found out I was secretly shedding tears in my dreams due to homesickness!
Unexpectedly, Shiro's thoughtful advice addressed the unspoken confusion.
 
But what should I do?
I looked at the travel magazine the neighboring guest was reading, and suddenly had an idea!
 
"—I've got it!"
"Just like traveling! In a fascinating place like Catto City, we must bring back some souvenirs, right!"

"Ugh... Feeling a bit overwhelmed..."
I found myself standing at the entrance of the mall, my eyes inevitably drawn to the vibrant array of signs, while a tinge of confusion crept into my heart.
What gift could truly capture the essence of Catto City and evoke that delightful "meow" sensation in everyone's hearts?
 
Clutching my purse tightly, which held the funds Vanilla had set aside before our journey.
The operation of the shop and our daily expenses demanded resources, leaving only a meager budget for souvenir shopping. This money even accounted for the future purchase of dried fish for the next ten days.
Thus, I clenched my fist, reminding myself repeatedly—not to squander recklessly!
 
Navigating through the shops, I marveled at the diverse range of goods. From exquisite handicrafts to delectable treats...
I discreetly raised my arm to cover my lips, ensuring no drool escaped—
each item leaving me in a state of indecision, meow!
 
As the first traces of dusk lit up the tiled floor, I instinctively glanced up at the darkening sky outside, only then realizing the weariness seeping into my legs.
Perhaps, it was time to call it a day... Vanilla and Cacao awaited my return at the shop for dinner.
 
Just as I was preparing to depart, the moment I passed through the entrance—
an electronic beep echoed in my ear, rekindling the waning flame of enthusiasm.
 
"Your emotional state is in excellent condition, please continue to maintain it. Wishing you a pleasant day."
 
In an instant, I turned eagerly toward the emotion-monitoring device stationed at the entrance.
How did I not think of this earlier! Isn't this the quintessential gift from Catto City? It even cares about everyone's emotional well-being, meow!
 
"Sorry, the emotion-monitoring device is not available for public purchase."
"They serve a specific purpose and are only allocated to designated locations. Moreover, acquiring one requires multiple layers of approval."
"Is that so... Thank you!"
 
I mustered a smile and bid farewell to the helpful staff member who addressed my queries.
Exiting the mall, I slowly hunched my back, bowed my head, and made my way home under the waning sunlight.

I found myself quietly nestled by the window, my gaze absentmindedly tracing the bustling reflection of Vanilla in the glass as a sense of disorientation crept in.
Upon my return, Vanilla astutely picked up on my subdued mood, without hesitation guiding me to the couch and shouldering all post-closing tasks herself.
It seemed I had inadvertently burdened Vanilla... my tail twitched anxiously a few times.
 
Suddenly, a furry little head leaned in from my side, almost brushing against my cheek, its warm and moist touch passing over me like a silent reassurance.
I turned to meet Cacao's amber, clear eyes, her pink tongue still out, poised to draw nearer.

"Are you worried about me?"
"Mew..."
"Haha... Alright, no more licking. I feel much better now!"
 
"You rarely appear so down, Chocola."
"Did something go awry in selecting souvenirs?"
Vanilla, having completed tidying up, also took a seat.
Struggling to contain the lingering feeling of sadness in my heart, I snuggled with Cacao into Vanilla's comforting embrace.
 
"Just a bit..."
"That's the most suitable souvenir I could come up with!"
"I never imagined it would be an unattainable goal... Every subsequent idea is inevitably compared to it, and I'm left unsatisfied, meow..."
 
"Chocola, you're being silly."
Vanilla gently grasped my hand, giving it a slight pinch, almost teasingly.
"Remember, the purpose of souvenir shopping is to uplift your spirits. Why make yourself more despondent instead?"
"The sentiment behind the gift holds more significance than the gift itself. If the recipient knew it troubled you, they would fret."
 
Soft, soothing whispers resonated in my ears...
"Cheer up, Chocola."

"First, we need to... Then, we can... Finally, we will...!"
 
Chocola gripped the piping bag, murmuring with a rare seriousness between her lips.
Despite her intense focus, the cream that squeezed out still bore a slightly clumsy and imperfect shape. Yet, the fragrant, sweet cream, akin to clouds in a clear sky, piled generously on the cupcake's rough surface, embodying the sweet intentions of a young girl.
 
"Success! Come taste it, meow..."
 
*Ahoo*—
Before the words could fully dissipate, a nimble, mint-colored figure leaped from the counter, already snatching two freshly baked cupcakes.
 
"Hey, Cacao! That's risky!"
"Uh... Mmm. Nom nom..."

"Chocola's culinary prowess is quite in demand."

"This marks the 8th recipe Chocola has learned from Catto City. I've been diligently documenting every step of Chocola's growth."
 
"Hehe. Fantastic! With my exceptional culinary skills, I'll surely amaze everyone!"
"Oh my! Bestowing Excellent Chocola as a gift, wouldn't that be too perfect?"
Whether influenced by the present joy or hopeful anticipation, a blush subtly bloomed on Chocola's cheeks.
Vanilla playfully raised her finger, lightly tapping the girl's forehead.
 
"Enough, getting carried away already."
"..Regardless of Chocola's path, she remains a unique and cherished gift to all."

"That's a wrap for today's VLOG. Stay tuned for the next update. I'm Linn, and don't forget to subscribe to my channel!"

As the video nears its end, the screen gradually dims, leaving only a black background.

"Chocola."
"Meow—!"

We exchange a glance and shout the name in unison.

I stay quiet, slowly zooming the camera in on the enthusiastic Chocola.

"Vanilla, your cake..."

"Well, in that case, let me suggest some exciting spots in Catto City for you."
Chocola's eyes sparkle at Shiro's offer, and I immediately sense her strong anticipation!
"Thank you so much, Shiro!"

A sun-kissed breeze dances across the expansive sea, where the soft sound of waves caressing the boat seems to be the only noise left in the world.

*Plop.*

"You're nearly halfway through your itinerary, right?"

The words "fish" and "feast" send my mind into an irresistible daydream. Instinctively, I start drooling.

"Don't rush around like you're out of time. Everything has a turnaround; don't let a yet-to-come end become your shackle. We're all here, so enjoy the present. Like now... why not cuddle and take a nap with them?"

"Alright..."

"Wait, Vanilla, are you suggesting we prepare gifts for everyone at Baker's Cafe?"
After a brief pause of confusion, Chocola suddenly stands up, realization dawning on her face.

"Oh! Vanilla, you're always so thoughtful!"
"It's all thanks to their care that we can live here in peace! Our recent VLOG adventures in Catto City must have caused them a lot of trouble... We have to get them a great thank-you gift!"
"We should definitely send them a copy of our VLOGs as a memento. What else can we give them..."

I watch Chocola pacing back and forth, deep in thought. An instinctive urge to chase rises within me, my tail quivering with anticipation. Then I jump at Chocola, and we both fall onto the soft carpet.

"Hey! Vanilla! Stop interrupting me! It's already so hard to think of a gift! Meow!"
I cuddle up to Chocola in silence, observing her thoughtful face with interest.

Chocola suddenly sits upright, her gaze fixed on me, as if looking for something unusual in my face.

Uh... Seems like she's seen through me. The twin telepathy between us works a little too well.

"I knew it! You can't fool me, Vanilla, you already have an idea, right?"
"Come on, tell me now, please!"

My intention was to see her putting on a cute act, and now I've achieved my goal.

"The secret is in our camera, you know."

"Oh wow—this is a photo of us with the food critic!"
"It's thanks to his promotion that La Lune became so popular."
Taking the photo from Chocola, Vanilla flips it over, applies glue to the back, and carefully sticks it in the scrapbook.

A few photos are meticulously collaged together with hand-drawn illustrations interspersed. Beneath each photo, two lines of childlike handwriting, one in blue and one in red, delicately narrate the story behind it.

The collection of photos centers around a single theme: the three catgirls and their friends from Baker's Cafe.
Vibrant and lively, the images capture the laughter and joy they shared.

From the triumphant poses after defeating an Anomaly in the simulation training ground with Asura, to the victorious smiles following a gaming victory at Gamer City with Echo; from their hungry expressions watching Minami skillfully slicing fresh sashimi, to their astonishment at Triss's extravagant shopping spree at a luxury mall...

"What photo should we place on the final page?"

Vanilla and Chocola exchange a glance and smile.
As if by silent agreement, they both point to the same photo—

It's a rare group picture, taken under the dim stage lights after Triss's concert.
Standing side by side, they beam brightly at the camera, resembling shining stars with an enduring glow.

How should we caption this photo?

Vanilla takes the pen without consulting Chocola. She knows they are in sync.

"Don't forget us."

"To the brightest stars in our hearts, our lifelong friends."

It's time to close the shop.

I gaze quietly at the sign hanging on the door handle.
When night falls, the red letters should face outward... Chocola says that means "closed."

But today, no cat has come to flip it.

I approach the door, rising on my toes, reaching out to touch the wooden sign.
It starts to wobble, just out of my grasp...
Meow, it almost feels like it's teasing me.

I focus on the swinging sign and leap suddenly.
My paw finally lands on the rough wood, giving it a firm swipe, causing the sign to spin in the air, now displaying "Closed."

But...

Upon landing gently, my surprise is met with the sight of the umbrella standing by the door toppled on the ground.
Seems like I accidentally stepped on it during my jump.

Feeling perplexed, I instinctively perk up my ears, lower my body, and tuck in my tail!
My instincts urge me to wait... but for what?

The calm surroundings are interrupted by voices from the lounge.
I move silently closer, peeking into the lounge through the slightly open door.

"Ow! Vanilla, be gentle...!"
"If we skip massaging those sore muscles, you'll suffer more tomorrow, Chocola."
"Alright... It didn't seem like much when everyone helped. Now that we're on our own, I realize how challenging running a shop can be. There are still some raw materials left to move; let's continue tomorrow!"

Chocola is utterly drained... She truly needs assistance...

I blink, my ears twitching ever so slightly.

Hee-shoo!
I bound onto the stool that Chocola set up for me, finally getting a glimpse of what was on the counter.

That big bowl seems to have something sticky in it... maybe egg whites?
I recall how Chocola used a peculiar metal claw to mix it, turning the egg whites into marshmallows...

Let me give it a try.
I spot the familiar gadget on the counter and, mimicking Chocola's actions from before, I press the switch—

*Buzz—Boom*!
"Meow—!"

A strange vibration tingles through my paw, as if I'm facing a formidable foe, prompting me to hurl the device back onto the table.

"Cacao!? What happened, are you okay?"
Chocola rushes over upon hearing the commotion.
As I gaze down at the spilled egg whites on the floor, I nervously clutch at my shirt hem, feeling like there are fifteen buzzing iron claws in my chest, all jittery and unsettled.
Suddenly, a shadow looms over me, causing me to instinctively retract my neck, bracing for what's to come... A scolding? Instead, I feel a gentle warmth enveloping me, devoid of any reproach.
I raise my head in astonishment, only to meet Chocola's reassuring smile.

"Alright! No need to be frightened! Let's clean this up!"
"Curiosity is natural for young kittens, but remember the kitchen can be dangerous—be cautious, okay?"

...It's not just about curiosity...
But...

Observing Chocola's slightly disheveled hair from the day's activities, I quietly nuzzle into her palm.

The shop exudes tranquility, accompanied only by the gentle melody of the afternoon breeze.
I hear a soft, calming breath beside me, prompting me to open my eyes slowly.

On the sofa, Chocola and Vanilla are already lost in peaceful slumber.

Perfect.
I rise cautiously, sneaking back to the kitchen.
Memories of the bustling morning rush flood my mind. I was like a mischievous sprite, more hindrance than help...

I must do something.
The determination grows stronger despite the initial setback.

I fumble my way to the storage cabinet and eventually locate the mop.
Having closely observed Chocola's technique and with the restaurant still in need of cleaning...
I am convinced I can handle it.

Surveying the cafe, I assess the remaining cleaning area.
Finally, I lowered my aching arms—Clang!
I winced in pain, holding my throbbing forehead, glaring resentfully at the handle—only to realize it was my own grip that had faltered first... I despondently sank back to the floor, tail curled in defeat.

Was there another way...
Hmm...?

I cast a glance at the mop on the floor, then at the clothes entangled within it.

"Cacao! Cacao?"
The call from the outside seems muffled... as if passing through a veil.

Who could be calling me...
My eyelids stubbornly cling together.
I wag my tail, surrendering to a dream filled with savory fish treats.

*Click*—
"Thank goodness...! I thought Cacao was missing..."
A sudden flood of light invades the dark, cramped space.

"Uwah—! Cacao, what's that wrapped around you?! A rag??"

Upon hearing about my "secret equipment," a sense of pride wells up within me.
Observing Chocola's puzzled expression, I decided to showcase my "achievement."
Recalling the cleaning process from earlier, I lower myself onto the floor,
initiating a series of rolling, crawling, and scrubbing motions seamlessly.

"Oh, my... goodness..."
Chocola's lips move in silence, while Vanilla articulates their realization.
"So... Cacao, it was you who cleaned the floor."

"Uh-huh." I rub my stiff neck, a result of all the rolling around.

Did I succeed?
As they rush over, their surprise and joy evident, the thirty miniature versions of me in my mind finally ease into relaxation.
Perhaps I did it right in the end... I suppose?

"This... should be good, right?"
"What an unexpected twist."

where a vibrant, dazzling set of lifelike cleaning toys for kids lay.

"Meow..."

The night wind suddenly picked up, carrying the ambiguous scent from the nearby neon lights.

Squirt—Squirt—

'She's the one who's sick!'

"What... what are you going to do?!"

A Dragon Li cat is always cool as a cucumber, but can be aggressive when offended. They are territorial and like to think about the goals of life, maybe something like taking over the world. After much consideration, they have decided to start by claiming the home sofa.

The Norwegian Forest Cat is a master at socializing. They can be found either making new kitten friends or embarking on exciting adventures. When it comes to playtime and mealtime, they take their activities very seriously. Monotony is not their cup of milk, as they are always in search of the next exhilarating experience. In fact, they have even persuaded other kittens to form the Extreme Cat Sports Association.
The Social Butterfly Cat - A true lover of play and food.

The wise Devon Rex is driven by an insatiable curiosity about the truths of the world. With an unquenchable thirst for knowledge, they are determined to unravel the eight greatest unsolved mysteries of the feline realm. When they sense unexpected thoughts in the minds of other kittens, their curiosity is instantly piqued. Once they establish a friendship, they will eagerly involve their companions in deciphering the secrets of the cat universe.

The Moo cat's inner world is incredibly rich and vibrant. They find joy in doing things that other kittens may consider strange. Their range of hobbies is vast, but they tend to lose interest quickly. Renowned as the "Wise One" in the feline world, other kittens often seek their assistance with problems. However, whether they decide to lend a paw or not solely depends on their mood.

The Siberian Forest cat, with their exceptional affinity for cats, often becomes the center of attention in any feline gathering. They radiate happiness on regular days and can remain joyful for an extended period of time, even from a simple compliment from fellow kittens. They never miss the regularly held cat parties and contribute to the vibrant atmosphere by bringing forth various joyful topics.

The emotionally abundant Abyssinian cat naturally possesses a gentle strength. They experience sadness when something they have cherished for a long time gets damaged, seeking solace in music and books. However, due to their gentle nature, when the Abyssinian cat desires to rely on other kittens, they also fear becoming a burden to them.
Gentle and stable, patient and mysterious.

The peace-loving Scottish Fold cat avoids conflicts at all costs. When they make a mistake, their tear glands produce a crying cat face. They have their own imaginary world, filled with flowers and sunshine every day. Occasionally, they yearn to participate in the regularly held cat parties, but often miss them due to their tendency to oversleep.
Gentle and charming, intelligent and resilient.

The quiet-loving Australian Mist cat finds solace in the company of a good book and a cup of hot tea. It is challenging to provoke their anger, but when they do get angry, it can be quite intimidating. They pay attention to detail and excel at meticulous arrangements. Taking care of other kittens brings them a sense of accomplishment, making them a reliable member of the Cat Rescue Station.

Not even the Pathos Detector crafted by the StormEye can penetrate the depths of your heart (unless you're merely choosing randomly). Welcome to Cat Fantasy, a realm brimming with infinite possibilities. May you find your favorite feline companions here and forge lifelong bonds.
System error, please try again later.

The peace-loving American Shorthair cat possesses a warm and generous heart. When faced with a hungry feline, they willingly share their treats, even when they are hungry themselves. As a cat that loves to assist others, they are already planning to turn the next cat gathering into a charity dinner.

The Ragdoll cat with an artistic soul is always filled with ethereal inspiration. When surrounded by nature, they feel complete, and their creativity breathes life into collected cat hairballs, transforming them into renowned works of art in the feline world.

The responsible Calico Cat is efficient and meticulous in their work, earning the trust of the cats around it. A chosen working cat, they are the true master of multitasking. Even during their downtime, they may be teaching other cats how to effectively manage the stockpile of cat food.

The ambitious Leopard Cat is bursting with self-assuredness and determination. They possess strong self-motivation and strive for success and personal fulfillment. With their natural leadership qualities, they always have followers, passionately discussing ways to make you the CEO of the feline world.

The naturally food-loving Domestic Shorthair Ginger Cat always seeks out delectable treats. Don't be fooled by their adorable appearance, for they are adventurous and fearless. They may get lost in the jungle in pursuit of their favorite food. But who cares? Adventure is the spice of life!
Standard food lover with contrasting traits.

The perfectionist Maine Coon cat adheres to its own internal order. Strong-willed and serious, they can resist even the most irresistible attempts to be cute. Though they may seem composed and unapproachable, their elegant tea-drinking posture at regular cat gatherings has captivated many little felines.
Calm and reliable, with outstanding charm.

The enthusiastic Golden British Shorthair cat possesses strong empathy. When they see a teary-eyed kitten, they shed tears alongside them and do everything to provide comfort. Like a little sun, the Golden British Shorthair cat may occasionally experience a slump and feel inclined to take it easy in its feline life, but it always manages to find the beauty in life and bounce back.
Brave and alert, with a passionate personality.

The Siamese cat possesses an insatiable desire to share and loves befriending all kinds of kittens. Hedonistic and living in the moment, they are masters of creating surprises even when none exist. The words "dull" and "monotonous" have no place in the Siamese cat's vibrant life. Their favorite pastime is snuggling up with their close kitten companions.
A vibrant and versatile presence, like a dog among cats.
